articleTitle: 60 GHz High Gain Planar Antenna Array for Millimeter-Wave Industrial Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a high gain and compact antenna array is designed using a parallel feed network at 60 GHz license-free band. First, the design of a single microstrip patch element is improved to achieve a high realized gain of 9 dBi. Then, a 16-way parallel feed network is designed for the 16 element array. The peak realized array gain is 18.56 dBi at 62 GHz, with −10 dB impedance of 10% (57.9 to 64 GHz). The proposed antenna array is suitable for millimeter-wave industrial applications and works on various 60 GHz protocols such as wireless local area network (WLAN) IEEE 802.11ad/ay, wireless personal area network (WPAN) IEE 802.15.3c, Wireless HD and ECMA-387.

articleTitle: Mid-Infrared Surface-Enhanced Spectroscopy Enabled by 3D Printed Metamaterial Absorbers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, surface-enhanced mid-infrared (IR) detection based on a 3D printed plasmonic meta material absorber (MMA) is presented. Leveraging the strong field enhancement effect in the 3D meta-atoms of the MMA, we have experimentally demonstrated that a series of molecular fingerprint vibrations of glycine can be significantly enhanced. In addition, our experiments show that, due to the capillary effect, the microscale 3D printed features can lead to selective analyte deposition, providing an additional knob to control surface-enhanced IR detection.

articleTitle: An Innovative Graduate Education Course - Lean Canvas for Invention
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The Lean Canvas for Invention (LCI): A Team Based Framework for Research Development and Mentoring is a bold, new, and trasformative approach to STEM graduate education and training. In this project, we are piloting, testing, and validating the effectiveness and feasibility of the Lean Canvas for Invention framework, hosted within a course for research students within the College of Engineering at the University of Utah. This course is 1–3 credits, meant to be taken in the first year of a graduate student program. Content includes research development (including business-oriented evaluation of technology), career development, and mentor/network development. This paper describes our first year experience teaching the class twice, lessons learned, and plans for next year's developments.

articleTitle: Wearable Radiofrequency Metasurface for Smart-Bandages
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Chronic injuries are a major health concern affecting worldwide population. In this context, smart dressings can be an effective solution to monitor the wound inflammation state. This paper presents a radiating system to be integrated into the wound bandage as a low-cost and high-sensitive sensor. The proposed hardware configuration consists of an actively fed RF probe and a planar 2×2 metasurface made of double-layer spiral resonator unit cells. This particular design allows to enhance the retrieved signal and, thus, the overall system sensitivity. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed configuration, full-wave simulations incorporating a biological layered phantom were carried out to compare healthy and inflamed tissues. The identification of the inflammatory state is performed by analyzing the amplitude variations of the input impedance recorded by the fed probe. The numerical results verified the proposed approach, confirming both the ability to determine the presence of the inflammatory state and the position of the disorder. Consequently, the proposed sensor is a promising alternative to evaluate clinical issues and allow better treatment decisions in wound healing.

articleTitle: Space-Time-Coding Metasurface for Direction-of-Arrival Estimation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Direction-of-Arrival (DoA) estimation is essential for wireless communication and radar applications. This paper presents a DoA estimation system by leveraging the space-time-coding metasurface combined with a single receiving antenna and related radio frontend devices. The least mean squares (LMS) adaptive digital filter is applied to adaptively estimate the DoA, which makes the system more robust and reliable. A simulation is performed to demonstrate the proposed DoA estimation system successfully.

articleTitle: Dielectric Screen Loading for Low-Complexity Static Reflectarray Prototyping
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Reconfigurable arrays used in RIS deployments require integration of biasing circuitry to control active elements to configure phase distribution. While their size increase, complexity, time and manufacturing cost rise. For the prototyping stage, we propose to get rid of biasing line and surface mounted elements integration to allow a static configuration using a dielectric screen covering the array without modifying its unit cells original design. The array can be then configured by different static screen configuration.

articleTitle: Evanescent-Mode Filtering Antenna with Tunable Stopband Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A compact waveguide filtering antenna operating in evanescent-mode with tunable stopband bandwidth is presented. The evanescent-mode waveguide is loaded with a dual-mode dielectric resonator that allows parallel coupling paths to generate both reflection zeros and transmission zeros in the filtering response. The two transmission zeros created at the upper side of the passband are responsible for specifying the stopband bandwidth of the filtering antenna. The locations of transmission zeros are, in turn, controlled to achieve 23% stopband bandwidth tuning for ripple level of 30 dB. The proposed filtering antenna operates at <tex>${f}_{{0}}={8.15}$</tex> GHz with a 10-dB return-loss bandwidth of 1.26% and a gain of 3.6 dBi. The small aperture of an evanescent-mode filtering antenna yields wide beamwidths of 129° and 74° in E- and H-planes, respectively. Moreover, the filtering antenna is fed by a standard propagating waveguide, making it suitable for high-power radar and phased array applications.

articleTitle: Near-Field Synthetic Aperture Radar Utilizing a Commercial V-Band MIMO Radar Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Millimeter-wave imaging can provide visibility through multiple materials for security screening, non-destructive testing, and goods inspection. One traditional challenge with millimeter-wave imaging is associated with the high overall system cost due to the need for multi-element apertures. Recent advancements in radar technology have made multiple off-the-shelf radar boards available which can be used for millimeter-wave scanning of goods and security screening. In this paper we discuss a synthetic aperture radar architecture that scans a V-band multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar in a small number of locations in space to synthesize a larger radar aperture. We show experimental measurements using a 20TX/20RX 62–69 GHz MIMO radar sensor.

articleTitle: Combination of Measurement and Simulation for Fast Virtual Drive Testing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Virtual Drive Test (VDT) is an area of great interest for both scientific research and industry. The objective of VDT is to emulate a real-world communication testing by approximation of defined conditions. VDT can be performed in measurement facilities with over-the-air approaches and channel emulation techniques [1] [2], by simulation-based software-in-the-loop tests [3] or by combining measurement and simulation [4]. For all possible solutions, the challenge of the scientific community is to look for an automated, controllable, repeatable, and reliable procedure, which can considerably reduce testing time and costs. In this paper we present a new VDT technique to evaluate the V2X communications performances based on the combination of measurement and simulation. In particular, the radiation performance of a DUT representing the antenna under test installed on a vehicle is tested in a measurement facility, the radiation pattern (vehicle equipped by the antenna) is integrated in a simulation of a realistic scenario to reproduce a real-world communication testing. The accuracy of the method is validated by comparison with results of measured data from Field Operational Test (FoT) of LTE links [5] [6].

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of a 5G mmWave 2×2 Antenna Array Using a 3D Printed Hemispherical Lens
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The manuscript presents a 5G mm-Wave 2×2 patch antennas array with high gain that is further enhanced using a 3D printed hemispherical homogenous lens. The array operates at 27 GHz, and it is fed by a microstrip lines network, using proximity coupling. The gain on the compact 2×2 patch antennas array is 13.8 dBi and the addition of a hemispherical 3D printed lens enhances the gain by more than 9 dB. For the lens implementation and integration with the antenna array, additive manufacturing in used. The support structure and the lens itself can be 3D printed using the low permittivity (2.2) Zetamix filament. Using mm wave frequencies allows the use of relatively small size lens. For the presented case the radius of the hemispherical lens is 33 mm, and the lens' flat surface is suspended 26 mm over the patch antennas' layer. The combination of the lens with the 2×2 patch antennas array results in total realized gain of 23.2 dBi.

articleTitle: Characteristic Modes Obtained Using Conventional Characteristic Mode Analysis and Singularity Expansion Method : A Comparison
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Both the conventional characteristic mode analysis (CMA) involving impedance matrix diagonalization and singularity expansion method of scattering decomposition essentially depend on the object dimension. In this paper, we have presented a comparative study of the modes extracted for canonical metal objects using both techniques. The matrix pencil method (MPM) of singularity expansion was used to extract natural resonance frequencies from the scattered field of various metal objects and is being compared with the resonance frequency of different modes obtained using CMA. Findings reveal that for highly resonant objects, the resonance frequency obtained using CMA approaches the natural resonance frequency obtained using SEM. However, for lower aspect ratio objects, the resonance frequency obtained using CMA is not equal to the natural resonance frequency attained using SEM.

articleTitle: Vector Vortex Wave Generation for Tunnel Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present a method to generate vector vortex wave that can carry Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) and Spin Angular Momentum (SAM), for wireless communication in tunnels or similar structures. Inside a closed environment, vortex waves are free from beam divergence issue and show a central null in the field magnitude distribution. Additionally, these waves possess the ability to carry multiple modes at the same frequency due to the unique phase distribution on the phase front and greatly enhance the channel capacity. These distinctive characteristics make vortex waves favorable for wireless communication in tunnel like structures. In this work, we present a method to generate the vortex waves using a radial array of monopoles inside a metallic waveguide. Different shapes of metallic guided structures resembling typical tunnel forms used in transportation or mining are studied. Simulation results show that the proposed method can generate vortex waves inside such closed environments.

articleTitle: New Linear Sparse Array for Holographic Millimeter Wave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The holographic millimeter wave imaging technology for linear sparse array considering phase center error compensation has been verified efficient recently. In this paper, a new linear sparse array layout is proposed, which solves the problem of missing the equivalent samples and has lower phase center error, resulting in higher imaging accuracy. Synthetic imaging results restored by holographic inversion demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed linear sparse array.

articleTitle: Microstrip CRLH-TL Leaky Wave Filtenna for Multiplexed Antenna Feed Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A leaky wave filtenna (LWF) with a frequency scanned radiated beam in the forward and backward direction is designed in this paper. The LWF is composed of a composite right/left handed transmission line (CRLH-TL) leaky wave antenna (LWA) that is realized with vialess unit cells and the addition of a band stop filter (BSF) element to achieve additional frequency selectivity. The beam scanning capability of the leaky wave structure will be maintained. The LWF prototype is centered for broadside radiation at 4.2 GHz with forward and backward beam scanning and an increased out-of-band suppression compared to a similar LWA. The measured results show good agreement with the simulation.

articleTitle: A New Class of 2D Scanning Planar TTD Multibeam Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, a new class of beamforming networks is introduced capable of steering beams in both azimuth and elevation planes. Traditional planar Blass matrix topologies, can only steer their beams in one plane. Here, we present a new planar Blass matrix topology (and the associated formulation) that can steer its beams in both principal planes. This matrix is (to our knowledge) the first true-time-delay planar multibeam network that can scan the entire field of view. As a proof of concept, an 8-beam 4×2-antenna multibeam network is designed and simulated, showing its full dimensional squint-free beam steering capability over the 24 GHz to 40 GHz bandwidth.

articleTitle: Full-Wave Hamiltonian Analysis of a Coaxial-Fed 3D Microwave Cavity Resonator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Quantum electromagnetic effects in superconducting circuits are promising phenomena to develop revolutionary quantum information processing technologies. To design complex circuits, there is a need for the development of accurate full-wave numerical models. In this work, we study the simpler classical full-wave Hamiltonian of a coaxial-fed rectangular waveguide cavity to validate field-based parts of the corresponding quantum Hamiltonian. We present the formulation of the system Hamiltonian and derive equations of motion. We compare results from our formulation using numerical eigenmodes to traditional transmission simulations of the system to validate the approach.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Sectoral Horn Array for High Power Deep Space Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A circularly polarized sectoral horn array for high power deep space communication at X-band has been designed, fabricated and tested. The array is designed to be compact, lightweight, and efficient. Two antennas were fabricated from 3D printed metal and two antennas were conventionally machined. All antennas show good correlation to measurements.

articleTitle: A Design Method of Broadband Off-Axis Focusing Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a method, which is based on the generalized Snell's law and the Pancharatnam–Berry (PB) phase theory, for the design of broadband off-axis focusing metasurfaces. Based on this method, a circularly polarized transmission focusing metasurface operating from 12GHz to 18GHz is designed.

articleTitle: Multi-Band Dual-Beams Reflectarray for Mode and Polarization Multiplexing of OAM Beams
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel method to enable mode and polarization OAM multiplexing at four different frequencies (30, 70, 90, and 110 GHz) through a reflectarray (RA) antenna. The suggested RA delivers almost matched electromagnetic (EM) responses for x- and y-polarized incident waves for both reflected OAM modes of <tex>$l=2$</tex>. The designed antenna can considerably improve channel capacity and spectrum efficiency.

articleTitle: Mm-Wave Beam Steering Antennas Using Stacked Parallel Plate Lens Antenna Subarrays
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A millimeter (mm)-wave beam steering antenna consisting of subarrays of parallel plate lenses is presented for the first time. As compared to a previously reported antenna that utilized subarrays of dielectric slab waveguide lenses, the presented antenna allows to design and control the beamwidth of the radiation pattern in the plane orthogonal to the beam steering plane by stacking the parallel plate lens subarrays. Additionally, full wave simulations of the presented antenna show performance improvements in gain, side lobe level, and field of view in comparison to the previously reported dielectric slab waveguide-based realization.

articleTitle: A Polarization-Mixed Antenna Array with Wide Beamwidth and Orthogonal Polarizations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a polarization-mixing strategy to significantly widen the beamwidth of a typical ±45°-polarized base station antenna array. Without changing the array topology, the originally narrow beamwidth of the array is significantly enhanced by mixing the two orthogonally polarized radiations. Compared to the traditional pattern synthesis methods, the proposed method can have much wider beamwidth and does not need amplitude weighting. The polarization-mixing method leads to a spatially-variable-polarization (SVP), i.e., the array has different polarizations at different directions. To guarantee the polarization diversity requested in modern wireless communications, two SVP arrays with orthogonal polarizations are designed.

articleTitle: Surface Acoustic Wave Sensor Interrogation Using Goubau Waves
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Electromagnetic waves on single conductors (Goubau waves) are investigated for the interrogation of wireless sensors. A demonstration of interrogation of a surface acoustic wave (SAW) sensor is presented, followed by the results of simulation of wave launchers on conductors of varying radius.

articleTitle: 5.25 GHz Metamaterial Lens for Beam Focusing Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: PCB antennas are an attractive and low-cost method for wireless transmissions. However, many of these designs produce low gain and low directivity. Introducing an array is a common solution to this but brings the complexity and cost of additional components as well as size constraints. An alternate approach to improving gain and directivity is to introduce a metamaterial lens placed above the antenna. This paper takes a Luneburg Lens design approach by adjusting the index of refraction of each cell in the lens. A realized gain improvement of 62% was achieved by adding 8.1mm of overall thickness to a stripline fed coupled patch antenna.

articleTitle: Axial Ratio (AR) Bandwidth Enhancement of a Circularly Polarized Crossed-Dipole Antenna Using Tapered Vacant-Quarter Ring
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A technique to enhance the axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of a circularly polarized (CP) crossed-dipole antenna is proposed in this paper. The proposed crossed-dipole antenna structure has two sets of bowtie-shaped dipole elements oriented in an orthogonal configuration, four parasitic metallic elements, a metallic cavity, and a coaxial feeding. Each crossed-dipole pair is connected by a tapered vacant-quarter ring to generate wideband axial ratio (AR) performance. To further extend the AR bandwidth, four rectangular-shaped parasitic elements are included diagonally. Simulation results show that the proposed tapered vacant-quarter ring based crossed-dipole antenna structure achieves a wide impedance bandwidth from 10-23GHz (78.78% fractional bandwidth) and the 3dB axial ratio bandwidth is about 74.85% (10.15-22.29GHz). The antenna has a relatively stable CP gain patterns with a broadside gain value of (8.2-10.3dBi) over the operating frequency range.

articleTitle: An Effective Beamforming Method for Microstrip Linear Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Beamforming analysis using an effective MVDR algorithm has been investigated and presented for a microstrip linear array operating at 2.45GHz. MVDR algorithm is successfully developed and used to obtain peaks in the angular spectrum for the linear array antenna system. Prototypes for the antenna array have been built and tested with 16Tx/16Rx phased array platform. It is confirmed that the proposed MVDR algorithm provides the peaks accurately to form and steer the beam for the microstrip antenna array that is designed. All the simulation results are compared with measurement results and found to be in agreement.

articleTitle: Required Orders of Interaction for Accurate Ray Tracing Simulations in mm-Wave Indoor Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper investigates the required amount of orders of interaction to obtain accurate ray tracing (RT) simulations for line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) mmwave indoor scenarios. For this purpose, RT simulations with varying orders of interaction, from one to six, are analyzed and compared with previously conducted channel measurements of a kitchen scenario at 28 GHz. Most importantly, all relevant interaction mechanisms, i.e. reflections, diffractions and scattering, are utilized and varied for the comparison and analysis. It is shown, that three to five orders of interaction, for LOS and NLOS scenarios respectively, are needed for the best possible agreement between measurements and RT simulations. Any further increase of the orders of interaction only increases the computational complexity of the simulations without providing any relevant improvements for the respective scenarios.

articleTitle: Modeling of Electron Device with Lumped Elements Base on Vector Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In allusion to many complex microwave structures with lumped electrical circuit elements, this paper proposes an algorithm to model lumped elements, such as resistance (R), inductance (L) and capacitance(C). It can be used to specify any combination of parallel-connected or serial-connected lumped RLC elements on surfaces in terms of circuit definition. And the lumped port is selected to excite the circuit structure. The numerical results are presented and compared with HFSS to verify the numerical solution and illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A UWB Millimeter-Wave Dual-polarized Large-Scanning Array Antenna for Mobile Handset
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A multilayered PCB dual-polarized phase array antenna covering the frequency range of 24 - 40 GHz is presented in this paper. The antenna is aimed to be used for mobile handsets with large beam scanning capability with simple geometry and low-cost manufacturing in 5G wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Beam-Squint Mitigated Transverse-Slot Leaky-Wave Antenna for Wideband Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Leaky-wave antennas (LWAs) have received increasing attentions in the recent decades. Generally, LWAs exhibit frequency dispersion, which would lead to narrow bandwidth for wireless communications. To mitigate this effect, this paper provides an innovative method of creating a non-positive slope in the dispersion diagram. It is attained by introducing square bracket-shaped metal pieces above a transverse-slot LWA. The finalized antenna achieves wideband fixed beams at <tex>$\theta=37^{\circ}\pm 2^{\circ}$</tex> in the band from 9.5 to 12.2 GHz. A low-cost additive manufacturing technology is used for antenna fabrication. The measured performance of the fabricated prototype agrees with the simulated one.

articleTitle: An Application of Angular Network Equations: Exact Solution of the PEC Wedge in Biaxial Media
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The Generalized Wiener Hopf Equations are deduced for a PEC wedge immersed in an anisotropic medium starting from angular network equations. In the case of biaxial medium the Wiener-Hopf model is reduced to Classical Wiener-Hopf Equations that can be solved resorting to exact factorization. The spectral solution allows asymptotic estimates of far-field components in the case of plane wave illumination.

articleTitle: Optimal features of SVO
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We show that the sampling approach provided by the Singular Value Optimization (SVO) technique is “optimal” in the sense that, when defining an electromagnetic link, it leads to the use of elementary antennas having the same performance of “virtual” receiving antennas provided by the application of the Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) approach to the relevant radiation operator. Without loss of generality, the discussion is led in a 2D, scalar setting.

articleTitle: Single Transceiver 3-D Radar Imaging at 80 GHz Via Affine Phase Center Translations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Synthetic aperture radars generate high resolution images using a single transceiver element by moving the transceiver to different locations in time and recording the back-scattered fields. Their main advantage lies in the simplicity and cost-effectiveness of using a single transceiver. For applications where the target scenes are dynamic, such as detection of concealed weapons and automotive navigation, synthetic aperture radars are not ideal due to the long data acquisition time associated with moving the transceiver to different locations. To drastically reduce image acquisition time, the proposed system utilizes a dynamic dual reflector antenna to translate the phase center of a transceiver to different locations in order to form a synthetic aperture. Using this concept, a high speed imaging radar system operating in the 76.5 GHz to 84.5 GHz range is demonstrated for weapons detection at stand-off distances of 2 m. The resulting images are of sufficient quality for object identification by shape.

articleTitle: 2D Eigenmode Analysis Based on Physics Informed Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, a novel deep learning-based approach for identifying the modal field distributions of closed waveguides is introduced. Specifically, physics informed neural networks are used to solve the Helmholtz partial differential equation (PDE) with the imposition of the appropriate boundary conditions. Based on our results, the proposed approach is capable of identifying all the eigenmode distributions of the studied waveguides with an error of less than −12 dB when compared with both analytical and full-wave simulation results.

articleTitle: Research on Active Cancellation Technology Based on Airborne Conformal Antenna for Low-frequency RCS Reduction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a conformal antenna was designed and used as a source of active cancellation in response to the need for low-frequency stealth in aircraft. The stealth effect of active cancellation under different polarization conditions is analyzed and investigated with simultaneous excitation of planar wave source and antenna port source. The results show that there is a reduction of about 30 dB under different polarization conditions, and this research scheme provides a reference value for the application prospect of active cancellation.

articleTitle: MUSIC and Pattern Synthesis Based Anti-Jamming Software Application for Research & Education
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A simple approach for detecting and suppressing interference in a Global Positioning System (GPS) terminal is shown in this paper. Simulations are performed using the L1 band frequency of 1.575 GHz. An easy-to-use software application with Graphical User Interface (GUI) has been developed for the simulations, which allows the user to easily set up the variables, such as the array size, number of jamming signals, their directions, etc. A MUSIC algorithm has been used to detect the direction of incoming interfering signals. A null-steering technique using pattern synthesis is then applied to achieve the correct antenna pattern nulling to target the calculated direction of arrival. The developed software is an excellent tool to train staff in both civilian and defense companies and for usage in research and educational settings. The software uniquely combines both MUSIC direction of arrival and array pattern synthesis techniques to support demonstration and optimization of anti-jamming arrays.

articleTitle: Toward the Development of A Three-dimensional Stable SBP-SAT FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A three-dimensional summation-by-parts simultaneous approximation term (SBP-SAT) finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method with the provable stability is proposed. The modified grids and several fundamental theoretical aspects of the proposed SBP-SAT FDTD method is investigated. Then, the specific absorption rate (SAR) of a human head is carried out to validate its accuracy and efficiency. Results show that the proposed SBP-SAT FDTD method has the same level of accuracy compared with the FDTD method with only a negligible overhead.

articleTitle: Steerable Dipole Antenna Through Huygens Metasurface Coating
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this contribution, the design of a dipole antenna equipped with a Huygens metasurface coat for beam-forming applications is discussed. The coating metasurface is designed to tailor the phase front of the field radiated by the antenna source, transforming the original omnidirectional radiation pattern into a multi-beam configuration. By equipping the metasurface unit cells with varactor diodes, reconfigurability of the pattern and steerable possibilities are demonstrated with the aid of full-wave numerical simulations.

articleTitle: A 2-Bit Reconfigurable Reflecting Metasurface for Mm-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the 2-bit reconfigurable reflecting metasurface for mm-wave frequency band. A low capacitive varactor diode is installed between the unit cells to achieve four different phase states. Moreover, the row-wise feeding is applied, and different coding sequences are used to distribute the reflection phases on a phase gradient metasurface to direct the beam at desired angles. The capacitance of the varactor diode is varied from 0.04pF to 0.2pF to obtain phases varying from 0° to 360° reflection phases with a phase step of 90°. The distance between two adjacent unit cells is kept nearer to lambda/2 to avoid mutual coupling. The design is low loss and can maintain angle reciprocity at the proposed operating frequency band. These functionalities make this reconfigurable reflecting metasurface a great candidate for antenna arrays for 6G communications.

articleTitle: Multifunctional Intelligent Reflective Surface by Continuously Controlling Amplitude and Phase
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: An Intelligent Reflective Surface (IRS) has the capability to dynamically control and continuously tune its functionality, making it essential for a wide range of applications in wireless communication systems. However, designing a multifunctional IRS that can independently control both amplitude and phase has been a challenge. We propose a novel approach utilizing two independent control varactor diodes and a lumped resistor in each unit cell, allowing for manipulation of local field interactions and achieving these functionalities. We demonstrate various functionalities, including reflection, absorption, and dual- and single-beam steering with amplitude control. This approach could be an improvement over previous IRS designs, which could only control phase and change beam direction. With the ability to control both amplitude and phase, we believe that it could achieve more additional functionality.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact Reconfigurable Antenna with Hybrid Polarization and Frequency Control for Geofencing Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A frequency reconfigurable antenna for location monitoring is proposed. The antenna developed can be reconfigured at two frequencies with suitable polarization and radiation pattern which designed for geofencing application, thus it either can operate at 1.575 GHz band or 2.45 GHz band. The expected outcome of this work is that when the user is within the geo-fence area it will use WIFI, while when the user exits the geo-fence area, GPS application will be selected. With the use of two switches, the antenna can operate either at band from 2.335 GHz to 2.593 GHz for S<inf>11</inf>< -10 dB and from 1.546 GHz to 1.588 GHz at S<inf>11</inf> <-6 dB. The axial ratio results of less than 3 dB is achieved at 1.575 GHz with a bandwidth of 20 MHz.

articleTitle: Aperture Area Reduction in Planar Microstrip Phased Arrays of Small Wideband Patch Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper we present a systematic characterization of planar microstrip phased arrays, in various lattice arrangements, with the objective of aperture area reduction. The antenna element design avoids sophisticated prototyping and can be used to design small antennas (<tex>$0.6\leq ka\leq 1.4$</tex>) with <tex>$\geq 30\%$</tex> impedance bandwidth. Investigation of phased arrays, composed of the designed antenna elements, show that a transformation from a square-grid-rectangular-aperture to triangular-grid-hexagonal-aperture leads to <tex>$28.68\%$</tex> aperture area reduction without proportionate reduction in gain (<tex>$6.1\%$</tex>). The planar arrays of all configurations are shown to be free of scan blindness over the angular range of ±45° from boresight, in the principal E- and H-planes.

articleTitle: A Broadband Discrete Exterior Calculus A-Φ Formulation Solver with Sparsified Nested Dissection Ordering Preconditioner
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A modified version of the sparsified nested dissection ordering technique is proposed as a broadband preconditioner for general comlex-valued, non-Hermitian indefinite matrix systems generated by the discrete exterior calculus <tex>$\mathbf{A}-\Phi$</tex> solver. Numerical examples indicate that the proposed preconditoner works for arbitrary frequencies with <tex>$O(N\log N)$</tex> complexity and the iterative solver takes almost a constant number of steps to converge regardless of <tex>$N$</tex> and the condition number. The proposed preconditioner is ideal for broadband and multi-scale analysis.

articleTitle: Mechanically Reconfigurable Multi-Band Antenna on a 3D-Printed Substrate for C/X Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a multi-band Vivaldi antenna design on a 3D-printed substrate is presented. The frequency reconfiguration is achieved using different small dielectric bars. The proposed antenna was built using a low-cost PLA printed substrate and two layers of copper adhesive tape. The simulated and measured results confirm the good performance of this design operating as a frequency reconfigurable antenna covering the band from 3.5 GHz to 13.6 GHz. The design is suitable for applications in the C and X bands, including the 5.8 GHz ISM band, for uses in radar, medical devices, and IoT devices.

articleTitle: Embedding General Antenna Patterns in Machine Learning Based Propagation Models
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Designing an efficient wireless communication system requires careful planning for access point placement and antenna pattern selection. Extensive measurement campaigns can be performed to assess the signal levels for a specific antenna configuration. However, that process is time-consuming and expensive. Simulation methods such as ray-tracing can be used instead. Even though these methods are more cost-effective than measurement campaigns, changing the position of a transmitter or its pattern still necessitates new runs of the solver. This can quickly present a considerable computational load, especially in large venues such as stadiums, where large numbers of transmitting antennas are used. In this paper, we present a solution to this problem based on machine learning. Off-line synthetic (simulation) data are used to train an artificial neural network model. The model learns the relation between a set of features, including the antenna location and its pattern, with the received signal strength across a communication channel within a frequency bandwidth of interest. We show that the trained model is very accurate at predicting the signal levels for arbitrary transmitter locations and antenna patterns. That enables rapid and efficient selection of the optimal locations, number or patterns of the transmitting antennas, to meet any design objectives.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of DGS-Based WPT System Using Double Negative Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the development of the defected ground structure (DGS)-based wireless power transfer (WPT) system and its performance enhancement by incorporating the double negative metamaterial. Initially, the WPT system realization is achieved by coupling two identical DGS-based resonators operating at the medical band of 405 MHz. Afterward, the metamaterial possessing negative permittivity and permeability is designed. The obtained results demonstrate increased power transfer efficiency (PTE) up to 38.5% at the 50 mm distance with metamaterial placed in between resonators.

articleTitle: A Gap Coupled Patch Array Based on the Multilobate Design
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A gap coupled Antenna array for operation in C-band is presented. The array is based on the gap-coupling of two similar patches, shaped with a multilobate contour. The multilobate patch design is suitable for generating Circularly Polarized far-fields, exploiting the mechanism of modal degeneration. At the same time, the multilobate design is suitable for the gap-coupling of complementary shaped patches. The combination of these two feature permits to design affective antennas characterized by circular polarization and broadband of operation. The design with best gain it exhibits a maximum left hand gain of 7.0 dB, a cross polarization discrimination exceeding 25 dB at the frequency of 5.8 GHz. The design with best dual band of operation exhibits 6.2 dB and 3.8 dB at 5.8 GHz and 6.4 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: A Compact Dual-Polarized Antenna with Indoor/ Outdoor Localization for WPAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel wideband dual-polarized antenna with indoor/outdoor localization abilities. This antenna operates in the WMTS band (1.395 GHz∼1.4 GHz) for medical services, the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) L1/E1 band (1.57 GHz) and Global Positioning System (GPS) L5 band (1.17 GHz) for outdoor localization, and an ISM band (2.45 GHz) for indoor localization. The antenna is designed with an operational bandwidth from 1.15 GHz to 2.62 GHz to avoid system failure due to frequency detuning of the antenna. Simulation results show the proposed antenna can operate with Linear-polarization at 1.4 GHz for wireless medical telemetry, and circular-polarization over 1.17, 1.57, and 2.4 GHz for localization.

articleTitle: Four Port CP-MIMO Antenna of Triangle Slots
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A 2 x 2 multiple input multiple outputs (MIMO) circularly polarized CP-MIMO antenna is designed. An artificial magnetic conductor backs the slots to eliminate back radiation. Each slot is coupled to two orthogonal printed microstrip lines from a power divider that equally divides the power with a 90° phase difference for CP radiation. The proposed antenna provides 7.5 dBi peak gain and 12.7% axial ratio (AR) bandwidth with isolation better than -20 dB.

articleTitle: Asymmetric Electromagnetic Absorption and Reflection Based on Transmissive Metagratings
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We propose an asymmetric electromagnetic absorber and reflector design based on a transmissive printed circuit board (PCB) metagrating. By selecting the length of the supercell, the metagrating presents only the 0<sup>th</sup>reflection diffraction mode and 0<sup>th</sup>transmission diffraction mode. Then, by designing the meta-atoms composed of a microstrip capacitor and a lumped resistor on both sides of the dielectric substrate, the destructive interference between the 0<sup>th</sup>reflection diffraction and specular reflection and between the 0<sup>th</sup>transmission diffraction and direct ray transmission are achieved to realize the wave absorption effect under forward illumination. In addition, when the incident wave is incident from backward, a phenomenon of reflection is presented. The proposed structure does not contain any ground plane, which makes the design suitable for applications where the absorber should not block transmission outside the absorption band.

articleTitle: Upper Bound on Transducer and Radiation Efficiencies of a Multiport Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The optimal performance of MIMO antennas is studied via the tools of convex optimization, utilizing two different concepts of power entering radiating systems: available and incident power. Two figures of merit – radiation and transducer figures – are defined as Rayleigh quotients over network system matrices and used to study several cases involving dipole antennas of various arrangements and balun transformers. It is concluded that the design strategy significantly differs depending on the amount of information known about the MIMO system and its excitation.

articleTitle: A Compact Dual-Polarized Millimeter-Wave Array with Wide Beam Scanning for Mobile Terminals
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper describes a compact four-element dual-polarized millimeter-wave array with wide beam scanning for mobile terminals. A modified dual-polarized shorted patch antenna is designed to cover N257 band (26.5–29.5 GHz). The coupled shorted structure is applied to suppress the cross-polarization level in H-plane. The array is constructed with a small element spacing of <tex>$0.4 \lambda_{0}$</tex>. Three decoupling slots are used to improve isolation for both polarizations. An overlapped −7.5 dB impedance bandwidth of 27–29 GHz is achieved in the array. The proposed array occupies the smallest size of <tex>$1.39 \lambda_{0}\times 0.28 \lambda_{0}$</tex> for the four-element dual-polarized array in the open literature. A wide beam scanning range of ±60° with low scanning loss is achieved for both polarizations. The proposed array with superior performance of a small size and a wide beam scanning is promising for mobile terminals.

articleTitle: Far-Field Pattern Tolerance Analysis of Petal Antenna Structure Errors Based on Interval Arithmetic
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Little attention has been paid to the relationship between the electrical performance and the structural error of the petal antenna. In this paper, the power pattern of the petal antenna under the system error has been calculated by using the traditional interval arithmetic and relevant derivation, and has been verified by Monte Carlo results.

articleTitle: Influence of the Impedance Profile on the Performance of the Tapered-Impedance Half-Impulse Radiating Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work we consider several alternative geometries for the feeders of the Tapered-Impedance Half-Impulse Radiating Antenna (TI-HIRA). The aim of the paper is to study the impact of the impedance on the electric field radiated by each antenna.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized SIW Leaky-Wave Antenna with Continuous Dual-Beam Scanning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study presents an X-band leaky-wave antenna (LWA) using the slotted substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology. It exhibits the unique characteristic of dual beams scanning with circular polarization (CP). This proposed LWA is experimentally verified, and a wide 10-dB return loss bandwidth of 27.9<sup>%</sup> is observed. With the increase of source frequency, one beam scans from -12° to 14° in the upper half-space and the other beam steers from 190° to 166° in the lower half-space. These two beams achieve the same right-handed CP throughout the scanning bandwidth. The achieved largest in-band peak gain in broadside is 10.8 dBic.

articleTitle: HFSS Auto Solver Combining Direct and Iterative Methods Revolutionizes Full-Wave FEM Electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the auto-solver option in HFSS for efficient and robust solutions to a wide range of full-wave electromagnetic problems. This solver examines the performance of direct and iterative methods and offers a hassle-free optimum solution based on available computing resources and the complexity of the intended project.

articleTitle: Pattern Reconfigurable Capped Patch Antenna for mm-Wave 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A simple design for a pattern reconfigurable antenna is presented in this paper. The proposed antenna is a typical rectangular patch with an inverted U-shaped trace of metal (called a cap) printed around the patch. To achieve pattern reconfiguration, a cut is made on either side of the cap. Different beam tilting was achieved depending on the position of the cut along the cap. When the longitudinal distance between the center of the cut and the center of the patch is small, a maximum scanning angle of 60° is obtained. The pattern tilting was achieved without any active devices. The antenna achieves a gain and directivity of 6 dBi and 7 dBi respectively, and an impedance bandwidth of 1.8 GHz (28–29.8 GHz). Additionally, the cap and the cut did not affect the antenna's performance, although a slight shift in resonance is observed. The antenna can be employed for mm-wave 5G/6G antenna array applications.

articleTitle: Dielectrics of Glucose Solutions by Broadband Transmission Line Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A Transmission line-based microwave method is utilized to characterize the dielectrics of glucose aqueous solutions in this work. An N-type adapter pair is accurately modelized to determine the complex dielectric of the aqueous solution filled inside the chamber. Dielectric parameters of a modified two-term Debye dispersion model of the aqueous solution are retrieved from the 10MHz-18GHz spectroscopic measurements. It was demonstrated that two-term relaxation model is suitable for the selected frequency range. The dependency of the dielectric properties on various glucose concentrations in the range 50-30,000 mg/dL was evaluated. The comparison between the predicted and the measured reflection and transmission coefficient indicates this model-based transmission line method can accurately characterize the complex dielectric of various glucose aqueous solutions and can be utilized in non-invasive biomedical sensing study.

articleTitle: Object Localization Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study explores the method of using machine learning techniques to localize objects in a three-dimensional space based on signatures of their scattered field. The antenna systems that stimulate and collect the scattered field are kept small to avoid a high cost and deployment difficulties. The cases of localizing a single object and simultaneously localizing two objects are reported, and two types of artificial neural networks are considered. It is found that a multilayer perceptron outperforms a convolutional neural network for the system under test. With a single object to locate, a trained network delivers very good performance. When there are two objects, the achieved performance is much lower, for which the constraints on the antenna systems and the amount of available training data are believed to be major limiting factors.

articleTitle: Magnetic Metamaterial Frequency Tunable Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a frequency-tunable patch antenna printed on a dielectric-magnetic composite substrate is presented. The antenna substrate is constructed using duriod dielectric with ferrite slabs embedded into the substrate. Split-ring resonators (SRR) are integrated into the magnetized ferrite slabs to achieve frequency-reconfigurable properties. The constructive coupling between the resonances of the magnetized ferrites and SRR is optimized to achieve a better tuning range by minimizing the required external magnetic field needed to magnetize the ferrite. The frequency tuning range of the proposed frequency reconfigurable antenna is improved, and a 670 MHz range has been achieved. The antenna exhibits a very good gain of 7.1 dB and an efficiency of 77%, and the experimental results corroborate the simulation results.

articleTitle: Recovery of Missing Radar Returns with Compressive Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Missing backscatter returns when using stepped-frequency radar are recovered using compressive sensing techniques. The recovered return is then used for target recognition. Compressive sensing-based signal reconstruction methods permit the recovery of the target's high range resolution profile, and consequently identifying the identity of unknow non-cooperative targets. The approach is first tested on synthetic targets, then on real commercial aircraft models with returns that could be contaminated with additive noise.

articleTitle: Design of a Ceramic-Based Stepped-Index Rectangular Dielectric Rod Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a Stepped-Index Rectangular Dielectric Rod Antenna (SIRDRA) with relatively high gain and wide bandwidth. The proposed device comprises of four sections with tapered permittivity, which are implemented using a single ceramic material (alumina) through unit cells. The first section consists of a solid block structure of permittivity 7.1, with the remaining three sections consisting of unit cells with dimensions precisely controlled to taper the permittivity from 7.1 at the beginning of the rod to 2.04 at its end. Simulation results show that the proposed antenna exhibits a wide matching bandwidth with a return loss below −10 dB over the entire frequency range of 15 to 22 GHz, and a peak gain of 13.1 dBi. Comparison of the SIRDRA with the solid uniform rod and the geometrically tapered rod shows that the SIRDRA exhibits better performance.

articleTitle: Linear Frequency Modulation-Based Architecture for SM Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, a new architecture using linear frequency modulation (LFM) as an alternative to the conventional fixed carrier frequency version for spatial modulation (SM) systems is proposed. SM signaling allows a new transmission mechanism in MIMO structures where the data and the activated antenna index are sent in a single block. Herein, we propose to exploit LFM to activate either, solely, the pair- or the odd-indexed antennas among the total available number and restrain the antenna index decoding to either pair or odd cases at the LFM chirp detector in the same way, depending on the recognized LFM signal. The objective of the proposed solution, in addition to reduce the research space range of antenna indices, is to lower the indices ambiguity between adjacent antennas, thereby enhancing their estimation. Furthermore, the impacts of channel estimation errors and receive antennas correlation on the performance are investigated for the iterative maximum ratio combiner (i-MRC).

articleTitle: Development of High Gain Reflectarray Over Wide Bandwidth Using Fitting Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an effective method for enhancing and maintaining the gain of the reflectarray antenna over the given millimeter-wave bandwidth. In particular, the proposed technique revolves around the “ideal graph” fitting method. Initially, the obtained phase responses of designed unit cells (UCs) were compared to the provided ideal theoretical phase values. Then, two reflectarray antennas were developed employing the evaluated polynomial- and ring-shaped UCs. As a consequence, it was explored that the former possesses greater bandwidth with the maximum gain.

articleTitle: Beam Scanning Antenna of Transmitting Metasurface and Radial Line Slot Antenna with Beam-Tilted
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a continuous beam scanning flat antenna with high gain, low cost is proposed. A beam-tilted RLSA is used as the base antenna, and a single transmitting metasurface (TM) and RLSA rotate together to control the deflection of electromagnetic waves. The simulation results show that the antenna can achieve beam deflection of <tex>$\pm 31^{\circ}$</tex>, axial ratio of less than 3dB, the gain of the antenna is <tex>$25.9\text{dB}\sim 26.4\text{dB}$</tex> and then gain loss of less than 0.5dB in the scanning process, and the antenna aperture efficiency is 31.42%~35.36%. The antenna has potential application value in satellite system and high gain beam scanning system.

articleTitle: Radiated Spectrum of Focal Plane Array Antennas with LINCA Array Feeds
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this contribution, radiation pattern measure-ments of a focal plane array antenna are combined with simulated outphasing waveforms to investigate the radiated spectrum. The recombination of the outphasing signals takes place in free-space (LINCA). The dynamic range is calculated and it is discussed whether the spectral masks would be violated with this system. A dynamic range of 24.1dB can be achieved, but the radiated out-of-band spectral components are not mitigated by the directive nature of the reflector.

articleTitle: On the Influence of the Antenna Group Delay on the Quality of Signals Obtained with GPR Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper studies the influence of the group delay of UWB Vivaldi antennas on the radiated pulse and on the quality of the B-scan acquired by a GPR. The study is developed in the context of landmine detection.

articleTitle: A Terahertz Photoconductive Antenna Design for Gain Enhancement Based on the Chinese Totem Tai-Chi
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: As a promising terahertz (THz) radiation source, the photoconductive antenna (PCA) is often used in investigating and analyzing THz applications. In this paper, a novel geometric structure of THz PCA is proposed. The design is composed of a gallium arsenide (GaAs) substrate and a silicon (Si) hyper hemispherical lens. Several existing PCA designs are compared and analyzed, showing that the directivity and gain of the proposed work are significantly improved in <tex>$1.5\sim 3.5 \ \text{THz}$</tex>, up to 15.45 dBi and 15.06 dBi. The design of electrodes and silicon hyper hemispherical lens are demonstrated in this paper. The proposed PCA is ideal for future THz wireless communication due to its great performance and simple structure.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Flat-Top Beampattern with Minimax Sidelobes and Constrained Dynamic Range Ratio
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper considers optimization-based design of symmetric arrays with arbitrary degree of flatness at beam's top and minimax sidelobes. Basic design is formulated as a convex optimization problem. The problem is then equipped with constraints which bound dynamic range ratio (DRR) of excitation coefficients. Since the coefficients in such a design can take positive and negative values, the DRR constraints are nonconvex. To deal with them, recently developed branch and bound method is utilized which solves the problem globally and allows certain coefficients to take zero values.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Branch Line Coupler-Based Circularly Polarized Antenna for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A dual-band circularly polarized antenna radiating at 28/38 GHz is proposed. The circular polarization is achieved by exciting the inputs of the two orthogonally placed antennas through a 90° phase shift using a dual-band branch-line coupler (BLC). The proposed antenna shows an overall system bandwidth of 13.23% (26.1-29.8 GHz) and 5.68% (37.6-39.8 GHz) in terms of <3dB Axial ratio (AR) and <-10dB S11. Such wide system bandwidth at dual frequencies makes the proposed antenna a good candidate for millimeter-wave (mm-wave) applications.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Radio Frequency Interference Suppression Method for Multi-Functional Cognitive Radar System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an adaptive radio frequency inter-ference (RFI) suppression method based on software defined radio technology is proposed for multi-functional cognitive step-frequency radar system. The radar system is capable to perceive the surrounding spectrum environment and optimize the detection strategy to suppress RFI adaptively. Meanwhile, to reduce the influence of direct current noise and interferences, the superheterodyne receiver is adopted in the radar system and redundancy transceiver is introduced for signal coherent purpose. The results of field experiments validate the excellent performance of the multi-functional cognitive radar system in RFI suppression.

articleTitle: A Single-Layer Metasurface Structure for Forward-to-Backward Scanning Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A single-layer penetrable modulated reactance surface over an impenetrable reactance boundary for tunable leaky-wave radiation is presented. A TM-polarized slow wave feeds a radiating aperture in a waveguide comprising a perfect electric conductor cover and an impenetrable reactance surface. Introducing a set of surface waves, complete tangential fields on the aperture are synthesized under the power balance condition, resulting in a reactive impedance surface. Three 10-wavelength-long apertures are designed and numerically validated for broad-side and ±60° scans.

articleTitle: Grid-Based Dielectric Mapping of Heterogeneous Tissues Using an Open-Ended Coaxial Probe
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work investigates the potential of grid-based dielectric mapping of inhomogeneous tissues using an open-ended coaxial probe by means of simulation and measurement. Microwave-range coaxial probe measurements provide fast and broadband results and can be used in-vivo or ex-vivo, and detailed tissue maps would be highly useful in both diagnostic and therapeutic applications. The results indicate that accurate mapping of the dielectric properties of biological tissues is achievable.

articleTitle: An Explicit Discontinuous Galerkin Time-Domain Scheme to Simulate Kerr Nonlinearity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A discontinuous Galerkin time-domain (DGTD) method is formulated and implemented to analyze transient electromagnetic field interactions in a medium with Kerr nonlinearity. The (nonlinear) Maxwell equations in conservative form are discretized using a DG scheme that employs the Harten-Lax-van Leer numerical flux to facilitate the information exchange between discretization elements. A slope limiter is introduced into the DGTD method to prevent generation of non-physical oscillations in the solution and maintain the stability of the explicit time marching. Numerical examples, which demonstrate the applicability and the accuracy of the proposed method, are presented.

articleTitle: Intelligent Design of Antenna for CubeSat Application Using Machine Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an intelligent design approach of a corner truncated microstrip patch antenna (CTMPA) operating at 32 GHz using different well-known machine learning (ML) algorithms. Our goals are to achieve 1) a gain of >6 dBi, 2) an axial ratio (AR) of <3 dB, and 3) a return loss of < -10 across a 10% bandwidth. To do so, we start with a data-set of 715 full-wave simulated samples with 4 different antenna parameters (<tex>$vi{z}$</tex>. features) along with the corresponding computed <tex>$S_{11}$</tex>, gain, and AR. Various ML regression models were analyzed to compare the training data with new predicted values using mean square error (MSE), root mean square error (RMSE), and <tex>$\mathrm{R}^{2}$</tex> score. Then, the best model that meets our goals was chosen. In our work, ten different regression models were analyzed. Among them, the K-nearest neighbor (KNN) regression produced the lowest error. Using the outcome of this model, we predicted the design parameters that achieve our desired goals. The predicted design was verified using full-wave simulation, showing a great agreement.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Sensorized Nozzle for Material Properties Monitoring through Electromagnetic Field
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes the use of a circular waveguide operating around the fundamental mode cut-off frequency to be employed as a sensorized nozzle in the food industry or in 3D printers. Specifically, this paper aims to demonstrate the use of a metallic nozzle as a circular waveguide to detect foreign bodies or air bubbles during material sliding in order to guarantee an automatic product quality assessment. As a matter of fact, the presence of undesired inclusions changes the mixture dielectric permittivity, resulting in the waveguide cut-off frequency shift. To validate this theoretical approach, a circular waveguide operating around 2.5 GHz has been numerically designed and a set of materials, different in terms of dielectric properties, are used as waveguide fillers. A correlation between the real part of the material permittivity and the cut-off frequency shift has been observed, hence proving the possibility to detect foreign bodies or air by using the metallic nozzle as a circular waveguide. Therefore, the proposed system can be potentially used for innovative industrial applications, encouraging further analysis.

articleTitle: Memory-Enhanced Evolutionary Strategy for QoS-Driven RIS Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Operating Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) requires a control strategy capable of coping with a constantly changing propagation environment. The use of a memory-enhanced evolutionary strategy is proposed here to exploit good solutions found at previous times and boost the exploration of the highly-dimensional solution space. The proposed approach does not require channel sensing at the RIS and its potentiality is demonstrated in a small-scale numerical analysis.

articleTitle: Dependable Wireless Powering for the Wireless Sensor Station by Using Combination of Solar Cell and Rectenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes an experimental evaluation result of the combination of solar cell and rectenna for wireless sensor network to realize the dependable wireless powering. 100 W class microwave power transmission (MPT) and 3000 Ix illuminance photovoltaic power generation are combined to the system. The measurement results of the output DC power were 325 mW and 160 mW for the configuration of combination of MPT and 3000 Ix photovoltaic power generation and the configuration of MPT only, respectively. The combination of the MPT and photovoltaic power generation is effective to get large DC power.

articleTitle: Numerical Eigenfunction Expansions for Optimizing Arbitrarily-Shaped Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, a new approach for generating lowfidelity models for multi-fidelity surrogate optimization methods is examined. Specifically, numerical eigenfunction expansions are used to characterize the solution domain of arbitrarily shaped patch antennas. These numerical eigenfunction expansions are based on analytical eigenfunction expansions. Our results show that the proposed expansions exhibits rapid convergence to errors on the order of 10<sup>–2</sup>when compared with full-wave simulation results.

articleTitle: Design Printed-Circuit-Board Antennas Using Image Classifier and Fixed Dimension Components
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: To extend antenna designs on printed circuit boards for more engineers of interest, we propose a new simple method that models PCB antennas by a few basic components. By taking two separate steps to decide their geometrical properties, antenna prototypes can be facilitated with no experience required. Random sampling techniques are used in selecting high quality candidates. A novel image-based classifier is introduced to convolutional neural networks to further filtering out the premium topological structures. Examples from wearable products have been chosen to examine the entire workflow. Their final designs are realistic and their performance metrics are not inferior to the ones designed by experienced engineers.

articleTitle: Integration of Active Circulators in STAR Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A simultaneous transmit-receive (STAR) operation of a 4-element phased array with an integrated active circulator is analyzed through harmonic balance simulations using an equivalent circuit model for the over-the-air link. Array selfinterference levels and effects of active circulator saturation are calculated for an example narrowband array at 9.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Circular Polarized 3D-Printed Enclosed Twist Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article presents a circular polarized enclosed twist dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) manufactured using 3D-printing, operating at 5.8 GHz. The circular polarization is obtained by twisting the top a rectangular DRA 60 degrees with respect to its base, while the sense of the polarization is given by the turning sense of the twist. The DRA includes a cubic dielectric enclosure to give mechanical stability to the structure. Simulations results shows that the antenna have a gain of around 6.7 dB, and an axial ratio below 3 dB at the operational frequency.

articleTitle: Novel Radio Frequency (RF) Based Wireless Gas Sensing Using Polypyrrole (PPy) Smart Films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design and analysis of a novel hexagonal resonator for radio frequency (RF) based wireless gas sensing. The proposed resonator is designed and simulated using CST Microwave Studio and operates in the Ultra-Wide Band (UWB) frequency range. A thin film of Polypyrrole (PPy) is incorporated on the resonator surface which acts as a smart sensing material to detect the presence of nitogen dioxide (NO<inf>2</inf>). The response of the proposed resonator with and without the smart material is analyzed. This work reports the novel use of PPy thin films for NO<inf>2</inf> detection in RF domain.

articleTitle: Characterization of Low-Dispersive Materials based on Transmitted Power
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a complex permittivity measurement method for low-dispersive materials as a function of frequency. The introduced method relies only on transmitted power signals collected using a spectrum analyzer/power meter, removing the need for phase measurements and a vector network analyzer. This method provides competitive accuracy along with easy and inexpensive permittivity measurements.

articleTitle: Rotman Lens Based Wireless Power Beamforming System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A Rotman lens with 9 beam ports, 8 antenna ports and 4 dummy ports is designed at 2.45 GHz. A series fed patch array with five elements is connected to each antenna ports. The simulated and measured S parameter responses are provided. A wireless power transfer system is implemented using this Rotman lens. A received power of approximately −0.3 dBm is received at 30mm from the Rotman lens with the antenna array.

articleTitle: Sub-6 Ghz Rotman Lens for Underground Mines Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The paper introduces a new approach of using machine learning in the design of a sub-6 Ghz Rotman lens for underground mine applications. The lens, optimized through machine learning technique, showed good results in terms of insertion losses. The design is optimized to operate in the sub-6 GHz frequency range, especially at the 3.5 GHz band. In order to be employed in underground mining. The final lens structure and port placement were both generated using machine learning.

articleTitle: H-Plane Sliced Stepped Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: An H-plane sliced rectangular patch antenna with two steps is proposed for wearable antenna. It comes from the conventional patch antenna fed by a coaxial line but the patch is sliced into 3 pieces along the H-plane direction and two steps with the same spacing are formed. The piece far away from the feed receives power by coupling from the middle piece of the top layer, which is connected to the feeding cable. The overlap area is large enough for the effective coupling, while the other piece receives power by the conduction current without overlap area where 11 posts are used to connect to the middle piece. The stepped antenna maintains almost the same characteristics with those of the conventional.

articleTitle: Electro-Mechanically Tunable Low-Loss mm-Wave LP to LHCP or RHCP Conversion Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The design of a novel electro-mechanically tunable reflection polarization conversion metasurface at millimetre-wave frequencies is presented. Tunability is achieved via a variable air cavity between an anisotropic impedance surface and a ground plane. The air cavity height variation provides a polarization conversion from linear polarization to right-handed circular polarization or left-handed circular polarization. Simulations have been carried out using CST Microwave Studio to evaluate the proposed metasurface's reflection characteristics and tunability. Simulations demonstrate a controllable transition between the two circular polarization states at 76 GHz with extremely low reflection losses.

articleTitle: A New Method for Improving Return Loss in Additively Integrated Bare Die Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work presents a novel technique for reducing reflections arising from impedance mismatch in additively integrated bare die amplifiers. Although printed interconnects show advantages over traditional wire bonds at higher frequencies, mismatch has remained an issue due to bond pad capacitance as well as discontinuities over transitions between different z-heights. Matching techniques reported to date require time-consuming optimization for different designs. Here, a simple drop-in solution is proposed wherein a technique used in traditionally fabricated systems is presented for the first time with additively integrated Low Noise Amplifiers (LNA's).
