Two LNA's are arranged in a balanced/parallel-series topology with quadrature hybrid couplers, nullifying reflections due to impedance mismatch at the LNA. This concept is demonstrated in simulation with good results, and a design is proposed in order to validate the approach experimentally.

articleTitle: Simplifying Building Structures for Efficient Radio Propagation Modeling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Accurate three-dimensional models for building structures play a key role in radio propagation modeling using ray tracing method in city environments. As the frequency of wireless systems increases to centimeter/millimeter bands and the application of narrow beam signals, more accurate models containing higher level-of-detail structural information are needed. Currently, digital databases represent such building structures in a manner that may be not suitable for efficient propagation modeling. One issue is the fragmentation of structures that unnecessarily increases the size of the model and reduces the computational efficiency. It also results in ray double counting problems that reduces the simulation accuracy. We propose practical methods to tackle the fragmentation to create models with much smaller sizes. We also propose strategies to treat small structures to further reduce the sizes of environmental models without affect the simulation accuracy significantly.

articleTitle: A Scalable 16-Element 76-to-81 GHz Phased Array Antenna-in-Package for Automotive Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A compact 12.4 <tex>$4\text{mm} \times 10.2$</tex> mm <tex>$\times 0.7\ \text{mm}$</tex> flip-chip chip-scale package (FCCSP) with integrated antennas is presented for automotive radar applications. 16 <tex>$(4\times 4)$</tex> wideband (76–81 GHz) slot-coupled patch antennas are embedded with uniform spacings in this 10-layer antenna-in-package (AiP), which can be further tiled to create a larger array aperture. Antenna feeds and transitions are optimized for bonding a 16-channel phased array front-end transmit (TX) or receive (RX) beamforming IC. Antenna bandwidth and radiation patterns are verified by full-wave package-level electromagnetic simulation. Measurement results of near-ideal in-air power combining of the AiP module are also demonstrated.

articleTitle: A Wideband and High Gain Dual-Polarized Base Station Antenna with Parasitic Patch
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A wideband and high-gain dual-polarized base station antenna based on a triangular parasitic patch is proposed in this paper. The radiator consists of two dipoles and triangular parasitic patches which are loaded under the end of the dipole arms. Also, two baluns are loaded to feed the radiator. The proposed antenna was designed, fabricated and tested. The measured results show that a −10 dB impedance bandwidth of 74.42% (1.35-2.95 GHz) with a port-to-port isolation of more than 21 dB across the bandwidth, and a stable gain of <tex>$8.3\pm 0.8\text{dBi}$</tex> are realized. The proposed antenna shows the useful characteristics of wideband and high gain which exhibits great potential in broadband base station applications.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Liquid Crystal Based Reflectarray Antenna for Indoor Wireless Localization Applications Operating in the Ka-Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This contribution proposes the use of reconfigurable reflectarray antennas, based in liquid crystal technology, as the radiating core of the next generation of wireless localization systems, at Ka-band. This kind of antenna is cost effective and is a potential candidate to improve the accuracy and dependability of localization systems in indoor scenarios. The design of a 28 GHz antenna is presented with a 46% efficiency, and the capability of steering a narrow beam in a continuos way.

articleTitle: The Impact of Vibration on TNR for a GPR System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we analyze the effect of vibration on B-scan image quality for ultra-wideband (UWB) ground penetrating radar (GPR) systems. Specifically, we consider the target to noise ratio (TNR) specification for each B-scan taken, comparing it with a control setting with no vibration. The vibration frequencies are 10 Hz, 27 Hz, and 37 Hz. Compared to the non-vibrating condition, TNR is reduced by at least 3.75 dB in each vibrating scenario. Among all different vibration settings, the TNR values stay within 0.71 dB of each other.

articleTitle: Multi-Mode Heterogenous Dielectric Resonator Antennas with Very Wide Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a new approach for designing wideband dielectric resonator antennas (DRAs) operating across multiple modes by exploiting the spatial variation of their dielectric constant with heterogenous materials. We show that in comparison with ring-loaded configurations that use a few different materials with different dielectric constants, the heterogeneous approach allows for a smother impedance variation and results in an improved bandwidth. A Wi-Fi band aperture coupled cylindrical DRA with a 57% impedance bandwidth using a heterogeneous dielectric is demonstrated. While a linear dielectric taper is implemented in the reported studies, the proposed approach opens the doors to exploit the capabilities of designing tailored dielectric profiles for different DRA applications.

articleTitle: The Direct Spectral Projection Model for Electromagnetic Scattering
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The spectral projection model (SPM) was presented in two previous papers as a fast and accurate method for analyzing electromagnetic scattering from two-dimensional surfaces [1], [2]. SPM is derived by applying the addition theorem for Bessel and Hankel functions to the specific integral equation, which describes the boundary conditions associated with the scattering problem. In this paper, SPM is manipulated further to derive a set of eigen functions, which describe the solutions to the specific scattering problem. Each eigen function, represented by a particular source and corresponding induced current, may be viewed as a stand-alone solution to the problem at hand, i.e. satisfy the boundary conditions. In the Direct Spectral Projection Model (DSPM), the solution to the scattering problem is derived by decomposing the incident fields in terms of these eigen functions. This decomposition is achieved by equating the spectral signatures of the incident sources to the weighted sum of the spectral signatures of eigen function sources. Simulations are conducted using DSPM for a variety of conducting cylinders with different cross-sectional shapes, for both TM and TE polarizations. The results are compared with those from SPM and the Method of Moments (MoM). The simulations compare well with the results generated by SPM and MoM and provide validation of DSPM.

articleTitle: A Compact SIW Feeding Network with Arbitrary Distribution for Non-Uniformly Antenna Array Excitation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a simple and efficient feeding network for an antenna array with a small number of elements operating in the millimeter-wave (mm-wave) bands. The novel feeding method is based on a substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity feed by a unique line, resulting in a non-uniform power distribution without the use of a power divider. The proposed power splitter offers great flexibility in terms of elements and amplitude distribution. This feeding is associated with high-gain broadband vertical integrated Yagi-Uda antenna. The simulation with the incorporation of the vertical Yagi as an antenna element shows that the proposed antenna array has a reflection coefficient better than −10 dB with a fractional bandwidth of 32.4% over a frequency range of 24.15–33.5 GHz. Additionally, the designed antenna has a realized peak gain of 15.5 dBi at 30 GHz and an SLL reduction of 34 dB.

articleTitle: Advancements in Additively Manufactured Radio Frequency Connectors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Due to recent growth in additive manufacturing (AM) technology, engineers can fabricate affordable and versatile antennas; however, poorly matched antenna connections and terminations continue to limit the capabilities of AM antennas. There have been several advances in the design and testing of AM radio frequency (RF) connectors to replace the standard components of the shelf (COTS) connectors. In this paper, an overview of the methods and types of connections for integrated AM antennas using AM technology is provided. The ability to seamlessly integrate the RF connector with the AM antennas or microwave circuits offers tremendous advantages including reduced cost, complexity, and flexibility.

articleTitle: Dual Band, Dual Sense Circular Polarized Antenna for Sub-6G Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A dual-band, dual-sense circularly polarized (CP) crossed dipole antenna is proposed. The proposed antenna consists of two dipole antennas, with 180-degree passive phase shifter and phase compensation line incorporated into it. Conventional dipole antenna radiates circular polarization when the amplitude of the orthogonal waves is equal with a quadrature phase difference. In this work, narrowband 180-degree phase shifters are introduced to offset phase difference and change polarization sense in specified operating band of the antenna. Measured axial ratio bandwidth are 7.1% over 3.09-3.32 GHz for left-handed CP and 10.1% over 4.94-5.47 GHz for right-handed CP. Measured gain above 2 dBic in both operating bands validates dual-band, dual sense characteristic of the proposed CP antenna.

articleTitle: Anechoic Chamber Clean Zone Analysis with Angle Dependent Reflection Coefficients
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: An important part of a radio frequency (RF) anechoic chamber design process is the selection and placement of absorbers to make the quiet zone devoid of unwanted electromagnetic (EM) waves. Due to their nature, absorbers have different reflection coefficient values depending on the incidence angle and frequency of operation, albeit the reflection coefficient values depending on the angles are seldom shown on the specification sheets of commercially available absorbers. In this study, a chamber illuminated with a semi-isotropic antenna is simulated to calculate the incidence angles of the EM waves on the absorbers. The obtained results are presented as a percentage distribution of incidence angles. It is seen that, most of the reflections occur at angles far from normal incidence. Quiet zone analyses with and without angle dependent reflection coefficient values are carried out to quantify the error made by assuming a constant reflection coefficient. It has been quantitatively shown by three examples that a better isolation level estimation can be made if the angle dependent reflection coefficient values are taken into account.

articleTitle: Compact Circularly Polarized High Gain Yagi-Uda Antenna at UHF-Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work proposes a circularly polarized compact and directive Yagi-Uda antenna operating at the UHF band. The proposed antenna utilizes broadband novel coupled turnstile antenna feed that incorporates perpendicularly downward bent radiating elements with different longitudinal lengths. The proposed antenna achieves 11.08 dBi circular polarization gain (dBic) while having less than 0.65λ height. Compared to the typical Yagi-Uda antennas, the proposed structure has broader impedance bandwidth. The acquired return loss bandwidth of the proposed antenna is 12.5%. Typically axial ratio bandwidths of the circularly polarized antennas in the literature are comparatively less than the return bandwidth of the antennas. The proposed antenna achieves 11.5% 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth, nearly as much as its return loss bandwidth. Moreover, the proposed antenna has excellent cross-polarization rejection properties and achieves a maximum 27 dB cross-polarization level.

articleTitle: Effect of Feeding Network Configuration on Power-Weighted Linear Array Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The method of power weighting is very common and usually applied in the design of antenna array to satisfy the pattern requirements. Basically, power weighting is implemented by arranging the distribution of weighted power on the feeding network of antenna array. As a consequent, this affect the current flowing on each part of the feeding transmission line. This paper investigates the effect of feeding network configuration on the characteristics of power-weighted linear array. The types of feeding network used in the investigation include serial, corporate, and parallel types which are implemented on the modified proximity coupled technique. Characteristics comparison of these three configurations show resemblance results, especially in terms of reflection coefficient (<tex>$S_{11}$</tex>) and sidelobe level (SLL). In other perspective, each type of feeding network has its own advantages and drawbacks. From the results of three types of feeding network configuration on a power-weighted linear array, the value of <tex>$S_{11}$</tex> is between −17 dB to −12.5 dB, while the suppression of SLL is from 18 dB to 31 dB. In addition, the serial type is more promising for the development of planar array, albeit the scheme of weighting implementation tends to be more complicated.

articleTitle: 3D-Printed Conformal Metamaterial Lens with Multiple Beam Steering Functionalities
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a 3D transmitting cylindrical conformal meta-lens is proposed, as a height-to-phase controlled system for electromagnetic beam manipulation, namely beam-steering. The full structure is composed of 79 independently tunable metaatoms columns, using 3D printing, providing full 360° phase compensation. CST Microwave Studio is used for both the unit cell and full structure analysis, where a standard horn antenna is used to illuminate the 3D meta-lens. The far-field beam-steering mechanism of the proposed antenna is achieved by calculating the required phase compensations for each column of meta-atoms, to redirect the beam to a predefined angle. Simulation results show two unique beam scanning techniques, one for a single beam and the other one for a dual-beam steering, at different angles of 0°, 15°, 30°, and 45°, and this capability can be further extended to enable wider 2D beam scanning, with independent beam deflection for the dual-beam functionality, making the proposed meta-lens a potential low-cost candidate for high-gain beam steering mm-wave wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Novel mmWave Wireless Power Transfer Systems Using Broadband Circularly Polarized Rectennas and Leaky Wave Transmitters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Millimeter wave wireless power transfer (WPT) has attracted an upsurge of interest recently. Here we present the design of a novel WPT system consisting of a wideband circularly polarized leaky wave antenna transmitter and wideband circularly polarized rectenna receiver, over the frequency band of 24–35 GHz (fractional bandwidth: 37.3%). Due to the simultaneous dual-CP radiation of the leaky-wave antenna, the proposed system overcomes the polarization misalignment issue of the antennas in the far field, thereby enabling a robust WPT. Our rectenna also realizes state-of-the-art performance in terms of bandwidth, RF-DC efficiency, and CP radiation. This is the first mmWave CP WPT system and will be experimentally verified.

articleTitle: UAV Classification Utilizing Radar Digital Twins
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The potential dangers of the unauthorized use of Unmanned Air Vehicles (UAVs) have made remote detection and classification crucial. Radar detection systems are preferred as they operate in all weather situations and during any time. Identification of UAVs threats is aided by knowledge of the number of detected UAVs and their directions. In this paper, a digital twin of a Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) radar is used to detect a number of CAD replicas of various UAVs, and enable their simultaneous classification. Rather than resorting to complex measurement campaigns, a full-wave electromagnetic CAD tool was used to generate the digital twins, and the radar datasets which are then fed into machine learning classifiers. The proposed approach will enable antenna and radar system researchers to investigate an unprecedented plurality of possible scenarios when it comes to the use of radars for UAV detection and classification.

articleTitle: A Via-Less Fully Screen-Printed Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface for 5G Millimeter Wave Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a via-less fully screen-printed reconfigurable intelligent surface which can establish a second line-of-sight communication from 23.5GHz to 29.5GHz. By serially connecting the H shaped resonator along the H field of the incident wave, we minimize the effect of the biasing lines and make a via-less design, which reduces the fabrication difficulty and cost. The unit-cell simulation of the array with screen-printed VO<inf>2</inf> switches shows a 215° to 160° phase shift difference between the ON and OFF states within bandwidth. During the field testing of the ideal arrays, we verify that the array can redirect the 45° incident wave to 0° reflection with a signal enhancement of at least 10 dB as compared to the array which has all unit cells in the OFF condition.

articleTitle: Design Considerations for Focal-Plane Array Antennas for 6G Millimeter-Wave Backhaul Links
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present three designs of W-band Focal-Plane Array (FPA) antennas as possible candidates for the next-generation millimeter-wave (mmWave) backhaul links. The considered FPAs comprise different types of waveguide antenna elements and are optimized to feed a prime-focus reflector with 400 mm aperture diameter. The main design goal is to realize a high directivity (50 dBi) with minimum beam scan loss, while complying with the strick side-lobe level requirements (ETSI class 3).

articleTitle: Broadband Dielectric Characterization of Glasses and Other Silicates up to the THz Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The dielectric characterization of silicate materials up to 2.5 THz is presented in this paper, to try to fill up the THz gap between electrical and optical measurements. Several measurement techniques have been employed to provide a broadband response. Materials in the silicate family can be classified as amorphous or crystalline. The internal structure, as well as the composition of the material, influences the dielectric properties. The loss of a material depends on its crystallinity, with higher crystallinity exhibiting lower loss.

articleTitle: Calibration of Active Electronically Scanned Arrays on Aerial Vehicles Through SAR Image Formation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In-situ calibration of Active Electronically Scanned Arrays (AESA) is a challenging problem that is still considered open. In this paper we propose a novel method for calibration of such arrays on aerial vehicles using the backscatter from the terrain below. To limit the extent of the terrestrial targets, the relative motion of the vehicle with respect to the ground can be used to form a pixelated synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image of the scene. The individual pixels of this image are used as calibration targets for a pair of transmitter and receiver modules. This way for an array with N transceiver modules, <tex>$\boldsymbol{NXN}$</tex> SAR images can be formed, co-registered, and used to determine the phase variations across the array elements. It is interesting to note that the measured phase difference between the backscatter from two co-registered SAR images can be averaged over all pixels to provide a much better estimate of the array phase error. Array channels can be aligned within the measurement phase errors, allowing for calibration without the needs for signals-of-opportunity or strategically placed calibration targets. Monte Carlo simulation of array beamforming with random phase difference errors on each element can then be used to determine degradation of array performance metrics.

articleTitle: Performance Metrics for Biomimetic Antenna Array (BMAA) Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Biomimetic antenna array (BMAA) systems consist of antennas spaced by much less than one-half wavelength and an external coupling network (ECN) that matches the impedance of the antenna array with the measurement device. BMAAs with two antennas have been designed and fabricated during the past 12 years. The primary performance metric considered in past studies is the phase difference in the measurements, which is comparable to antennas with much larger spacing. In this paper we characterize BMAA systems with respect to three other performance metrics: power gain, differential geometry properties of the array manifold, and the Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) on the angle of arrival parameter (which characterizes direction finding accuracy). This provides a more comprehensive view of BMAA system performance and design insights. Numerical results are presented for dipole antennas.

articleTitle: Indoor Field Trials for RIS-Aided Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Recently, both academics and industry have paid close attention to the potential of adopting the prototyping of a Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS)-aided wireless communication. In this paper, we present a novel RIS prototype operating in the 3.75 GHz range with 4096 configurable elements. We propose a realistic receiver-RIS Wi-Fi feedback link and an effective method for configuring the RIS over the air by taking advantage of the geometrical array features. Our 1-blt RIS prototype offers an 18 dB power gain over the case when it is replaced with a metal plate. The indoor measurements have been carried out where the transmitter and receiver are separated by a concrete wall.

articleTitle: Phased Array Antennas with Wide-Angle Scanning: Design of Decoupling Feeding Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a new approach to address the challenge of achieving wide-angle impedance matching across the entire angle sweep in phased array antennas. This approach involves the design of a novel decoupling feed network structure that compensates for the changes in the active impedance of each antenna element during angle scanning. The proposed structure includes a loop with two different paths between the antenna feed, with one path taking a sample coupling from one antenna element and canceling out the over-the-air coupling effect on the other antenna. By properly designing the length of the path to be 180 degrees out of phase, the proposed approach achieves about 20 dB mutual coupling reduction at the center frequency. The decoupling network is applied to a 4 by 4 array antenna, and full-wave simulation results demonstrate its effectiveness. Compared to conventional wide-angle matching impedances, the proposed approach is adaptable to any linear array and does not require a real state on the aperture to operate.

articleTitle: Antenna in Package with Double-Layer Parasitic Elements for 28/39 GHz Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In order to satisfy the requirement of applications at 5G or next-generation communication, the mmWave antenna becomes an important part of systems. In this work, the stacked patch antenna is adopted in the 8-layer packaging with a thickness of 0.92 mm. The double-layer parasitic elements are proposed on the antenna in package (AiP) to achieve a broad band. This AiP operates in dual polarization and dual band which includes the low band from 24.2 GHz to 29.6 GHz and the high band from 36.6 GHz to 40.5 GHz.

articleTitle: A miniaturized Wearable Finger-Ring Antenna For Medical Sensing at 2.45 GHz ISM Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A low-profile wearable finger-ring antenna, operating at the 2.45 GHz industrial scientific medical (ISM) band, is presented. The antenna was miniaturized to match the standard ring size (0.46λ ×0.04λ ×0.004λ) available in the market, making it suitable for daily activities and wearer's lifestyle integration. The antenna was attached to an average hand size phantom in the simulation. The obtained results illustrate that the proposed design provides good performance in terms of bandwidth, radiation characteristics, low specific absorption rate (SAR), and compact size, which makes it a strong candidate as a finger-ring antenna for medical sensing applications.

articleTitle: A Compact and Geometrically Simple CPW Fed Antenna for 2.4/5.4 GHz ISM and WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a compact and geometrically simple Co-Planar Waveguide (CPW) fed antenna proposed for ISM and WLAN applications. The antenna operates on ISM band at 2.45 GHz (IEEE 802.11b/g), 5G and WLAN band at 5.4 GHz (IEEE 802.11a). The proposed antenna is embedded on FR4 substrate material with thickness of 1.6 mm. Moreover, the antenna consists of CPW feed, slotted rectangular patch and rectangular stub placed at the top of radiator to improve performance of antenna. The design evolution is discussed in detail and various performance parameters have been analyzed. Furthermore, the proposed antenna is compared with state-of-the-art works to demonstrate the potential of proposed design for the applications in the targeted frequency bands.

articleTitle: A Signal Processing Framework for Rapid Detection of Tree Defects via a Standoff Tree Radar System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a framework for processing the B-scans of tree trunks and revealing the presence of trees' internal defects (i.e., cavities and decays) from the signatures of their reflections. The framework uses the B-scans obtained by a standoff step frequency continuous wave radar system, moved in straight trajectories at a standoff distance facing the tree trunks' surfaces. In particular, the proposed framework first applies an antenna calibration to the raw B-scans to suppress the antenna's internal reflections. Then, it leverages a column-connection clustering (C3) algorithm to remove the signatures of the reflections from the trunk surface. Finally, it applies a Kaiser window to the Fourier-transformed A-scans of the processed B-scan to further increase the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). The application of the proposed framework to measured (raw) B-scans shows that the proposed framework improves the SNR by more than 30 dB and reveals the signatures of the defects in the B-scans. The proposed framework can be used for many other standoff radar applications, such as through-the-wall imaging, defect/anomaly detection in concrete walls, in which the magnitude of the reflection from the main target is two/three orders smaller than the magnitude of the unwanted reflections from the surfaces or other objects.

articleTitle: Performance of a Class of Stacked-Disk Dielectric Lenses for Lightweight Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The electromagnetic performance of a class of lightweight stacked disk dielectric lenses, useful for reducing the cost and construction complexity of a radiating system, are compared with the massive counterpart in order to highlight their strengths and weaknesses. A full-wave numerical technique to include field propagation and diffraction effects taking place between the different disks forming the considered lenses, was employed. Information useful to exploit the electromagnetic characteristics of the analyzed lenses are suggested.

articleTitle: Measurement of 300 GHz Band Radio Propagation Characteristics in the Vicinity of Human Body using Terahertz Hemispheric Scanner
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the measurement of the direction of arrival (DOA) of 300-GHz-band radio propagation in the vicinity of a human body. We have developed a high-speed terahertz hemispheric scanner that can measure the DOA of 300-GHz-band radio signals with an angular resolution of 0.5°, and a human body phantom whose complex permittivity is close to the human body at 300 GHz band. Furthermore, DOA measurement results indicate that clothing significantly affects diffraction and reflection characteristics near a human body at 300 GHz.

articleTitle: Impact of Bodies on Harmonic Transponder Conversion Loss and Radiation Patterns
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, we demonstrate the impact of body proximity on the conversion loss and radiation patterns of harmonic transponders. Two different devices are characterized using a biological phantom of an upper arm, which is shown to degrade the transponder's performance by more than 3 dB.

articleTitle: An Equation-based Method for the Design of End Couplings in Combline Microwave Cavity Filters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The manuscript presents an equation-based method for achieving the desired end coupling in combline microwave cavity filters. The equations are based on the formula for the resonant frequency of a lumped <tex>$LC$</tex> circuit and a simple relationship between the external quality factor and the height of the pin feeding the end resonator. The algorithm is tested on a combline microwave cavity filter for the E1 Galileo band.

articleTitle: Experimental Characterization of Ferrite Material Embedded Microstrip Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The experimental characterization of a square-shaped bulk ferrite material embedded microstrip antenna is presented. The ferrite material exploited for the characterization is Yttrium Iron Garnet (YIG) which has the geometric dimension of <tex>$5\ \text{mm}\times 5\ \text{mm}\times 1\ \text{mm}$</tex>. This proposed configuration is intended to maintain a low profile structure of the microstrip antenna while incorporating additional material in the host substrate to affect its performance. The fabricated ferrite material embedded microstrip antenna has the final dimensions of <tex>$38\ \text{mm}\times 38\ \text{mm}\times 3.2\ \text{mm}$</tex>. In comparison with the conventional microstrip antenna, the characterization result shows that the resonant frequency of ferrite material embedded microstrip antenna could be shifted while maintaining its radiation characteristics in elevation plane at the desired working frequency.

articleTitle: Numerical Modeling and Experimental Validation of Path Loss in Realistic RIS-Enabled Links
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The accuracy of a recently proposed hybrid full-wave/ray-tracing method to model wave propagation in realistic reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-enabled communication channels, is examined via a measurement campaign in an indoor environment. The geometry under study is a hallway junction that includes a metasurface, to enable coverage within the shadow region of a hallway corner. The comparison between measurement and simulation results for the received signal strength in this geometry confirms the validity of the model and its value for the planning of RIS-based wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Multibeam Coverage Optimization for Broadband Satellites with Hybrid Beamforming Direct Radiating Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article presents a beam distribution methodology adapted to direct radiating arrays with hybrid beamforming techniques conceived to maximize the throughput of telecommunication systems. The optimal multiple beam coverage is achieved when the beam centers are superimposed with null positions of the other beams. An optimal spectral efficiency is achieved on links established at the vicinity of the beam centers, and is similar to that achieved when precoding is implemented in order to mitigate co-channel interferences.

articleTitle: Measurement and Analysis on Time Correlation of Wireless Channel in Tunnel Entrance Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Railway passengers have experienced call dropping or Internet disconnect when the train goes through tunnels, which significantly affects train-ground communication quality of railway mobile communications. In this paper, the channel characteristics of the time correlation function are analyzed based on measurements in tunnel entrance scenarios. The analysis results of this paper show that the channel characteristics of tunnel entrance scenarios and single scenarios are different. Therefore, the channel model of tunnel entrance scenarios can not be replaced by which of tunnels. Also, the conclusion that the channel characteristics are influenced by the location of the antenna can be used in future system design.

articleTitle: Suppression of EM Coupling between Microstrip Patch Antennas Using a Simple Meander Line Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A meander line is one of the potential decoupling structures suitable for reducing electromagnetic (EM) coupling that appears between two or more planar antennas. This paper presents an implementation of meander line structure to suppress EM coupling between microstrip patch antennas. To exhibit decoupling effects, a model of simple meander line structure is inserted between the antennas. A circuit prototype has been realized and examined for verifying those effects. The measured result shows a coupling suppression of about 6 dB to 10 dB within operational bandwidth can be achieved with a small resonant frequency shift of 60 MHz, or 2.5%, compared to the simulated one. The result proves that the proposed model is a promising decoupling structure to minimize EM coupling which is also further implementable on a planar antenna array.

articleTitle: Phase Gradient Metasurface Rasorber for Combined Beam Steering and Absorption Capability
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel radome design is presented which acts as a phase gradient metasurface (PGMS) and a radar absorber to provide both beam steering and absorbing functionality. By replacing the traditional frequency selective surface or lossless layer, in a radar absorber (i.e. a rasorber) with a PGMS, a new multi-layer structure is proposed which provides dual functionality. The design consists of a PGMS composed of several differently sized circular plate unit cells with two resistive layers placed a quarter wavelength above it. By this configuration, the radome structure supports steering whilst providing absorption bands from about 1.2 GHz to 5.5 GHz and 6.1 GHz to beyond 10 GHz. To best knowledge of the authors, this design is the first of its kind and it has many interesting applications for future phased arrays and related radar scenarios whilst reducing requirements for antenna beamformers and array phase shifting networks.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Dielectric Resonator OAM Antenna with Augmented Modes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Possibility of increasing the excitation of Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) modes are explored in this brief. As a matter of the fact, the utilization of single-antenna elements generating reconfigurable OAM modes in a uniform circular array (UCA) paves the way for producing different number of OAM modes. Analytical explanation of the mentioned technique is expressed as well. As a practical instance, a single antenna element designed based on a cylindrical dielectric resonator (CDR) provides the generation of tunable OAM modes +1 and −1. Arranging the antenna units in a 2 by 2 UCA brings about the condition for creating four OAM modes, which is unique in such a UCA.

articleTitle: Electrically Small Antennas in High-Density, Broadband Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A design concept for transmitting and receiving antenna arrays that allow for less mutual coupling and close proximity of components is described. The suggested approach employs the Bode matching theory to connect electrically small antennas with high reactance and low radiation resistance to front ends with high/low impedance. This method permits the concurrent achievement of miniaturization, proximity, and broadband properties. Finally, the suggested method is implemented by an array of four-element electrically small antennas in a 25mm-by-25mm ground plane over a frequency range of 1 GHz to 7 GHz. The proposed array can be used over a broad frequency band while the mutual coupling is below -20 dB. This approach applies to MIMO/SIMO and sensor system applications.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Split Beam Antenna for 28GHz Multi-Sector Indoor Base Station
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A dual polarized two-branch MIMO is used for multi-sector antenna under indoor environments, and a base station antenna should provide identical radiation pattern for both polarizations. To increase the channel capacity, a split beam antenna is proposed for multisector antenna for 28GHz indoor base station of 5G system, instead of overlapped dual-polarized antenna. Radiation pattern is defined to keep the same EIRP and the channel capacity distribution is estimated. Under the indoor environment, the split beam provides the channel capacity higher than the overlapped beam.

articleTitle: Numerical Modelling of the Grimeton VLF Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Numerical modelling of the historical Grimeton VLF antenna is presented. Simulations using NEC-5 show the operation of this multiple-tuned, electrically short antenna at resonance. Simulation results agree with theoretical expectations and documented performance for this antenna. This modelling also provides a validation of NEC-5 on a complex antenna design having substantially different wire diameters at acute angles.

articleTitle: A Circularly Periodic Multi-band High-Impedance Surface Integrated with a Spiral Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A circularly periodic multi-band High Impedance Surface (HIS) is integrated with a spiral antenna and performance is demonstrated in three bands (centered at 1.375 GHz, 2.4 GHz, and 5.8 GHz) with simulation. The design procedure for the multi-band HIS is presented, for each sub-band frequency. Zero phase response for each sub-band design frequency is obtained by stimulating the HIS with a concentric circular waveguide port. Then, a spiral antenna is placed at a height of <tex>$\mathbf{0}.\mathbf{02}\boldsymbol{\lambda}$</tex> above the HIS. The full antenna structure achieved good multiband performance in terms of return loss, bandwidth, radiation patterns and gain.

articleTitle: Towards a 5G n260 Band Phased Array Based on Vanadium Dioxide Switches
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A four element phased array design on silicon operating in the 5G n260 band is presented. The design incorporates a true time delay (TTD) phase shifter based on vanadium dioxide switches to select variable lengths of coplanar waveguide (CPW) transmission lines. A cavity backed slot antenna is implemented on a silicon substrate so that the array may be fully integrated. The phase shifter demonstrates a maximum insertion loss of 7.4 dB over the range of 37–40 GHz, with 11.25° of phase delay resolution and a 47°/dB figure of merit. The four element array demonstrates beam steering from −35° to +35° in the H plane.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Self-Duplexing Antenna for Millimeter-Wave and Microwave Frequency Bands
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a compact self-duplexing antenna working at mm-wave and microwave frequency bands. The configuration is based on Half-mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide (HMSIW) and operates at 5.8 GHz and 38 GHz. In the design of the antenna, initially, a square cavity is cut into two triangles. Then, one of the triangles is considered. After that, the chosen triangle is bisected into two portions. The bigger one is taken for the microwave frequency band, and the other one is taken for the mm-wave frequency band. Finally, by introducing four capacitive slots, the desired frequency bands are achieved. The isolation between the two ports is 22 dB. In addition, the gains of the proposed antenna at two frequencies are 3.35 dBi (5.8 GHz) and 5.48 dBi (38 GHz). Furthermore, the size of the proposed antenna is only <tex>$0.002 \lambda_{g}^{3}$</tex> which is the most compact self-duplexing antenna in literature that operates at both microwave and mm-wave frequency bands. The aforementioned results show that the proposed antenna is a good candidate to use in dual-band application systems.

articleTitle: Wideband of Microstrip Patch Antenna for 28 GHz 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this article, the design of an annular ring patch antenna in the millimeter-wave range is presented. The antenna is placed on a 1.524 mm Rogers RO4003C substrate with a dielectric constant of 3.55. The antenna is designed to resonate at 28 GHz. The presented structure shows that the annular ring antenna in an uncomplicated structure can offer wider impedance bandwidth than the rectangular shape. The proposed antenna provides a wide impedance bandwidth of 71.4% and a realized gain of 5 dBi. The antenna results of this work provide to be suitable for automotive applications at the mm-wave band.

articleTitle: Experimental Observation of Lateral Waves Propagation Along Seabed
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Effective use of radio frequency (RF) waves propagation in sea environment and development of high-efficiency antennas are crucial to utilize RF waves in seawater which has high attenuation coefficient. Lateral waves are theoretically well known as surface electromagnetic waves propagating along the boundary of lossy and relatively low loss media, which can expand the horizontal propagation distance than direct waves through homogeneous lossy medium. However, lateral waves propagating along seabed has been less experimentally studied than those along sea surface and far from practical realization. Our experimental results at real sea environment show that lateral waves along seabed expand horizontal propagation distance as expected by numerical calculation results. We believe this achievement is a significant step to realize underwater wireless sensor networks on seabed.

articleTitle: Bespoke Luneburg Lens for Two-Dimensional Beam-Steering Antennas for SatComms on the Move
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The paper presents a 3D bespoke Luneburg lens with a planar focal surface designed using quasi-optical transformation for applications in satellite communications on the move. The bespoke lens produces a continuous two-dimensional beam-steer of ± 50° in both azimuth and elevation plane as the feed point is varied. The lens design is used with a circularly polarized horn antenna, operating in the Ku Band of 10 to 15 GHz with a total efficiency greater than 80% and presents a gain of 20.6 dBi.

articleTitle: Dual Sided Data Dense 25-bit Chipless RFID Tag
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article presents a 25-bit dual sided, passive chipless RFID tag. The novelty of research relies on the concept of utilizing ground area of tag to incorporate alternating metals and slits in reference to the structure on top of the substrate, hence yielding high code density. Compared to previous latest research, the structure and data capacity are significantly improved. The tag has been designed and analyzed on low-cost FR-4 substrate along with copper as radiator to label up to <tex>$2^{25}$</tex> number of unique objects in frequency band of 4.5-12.5 GHz while staying in 27 <tex>$\mathrm{x}12.5\text{mm}^{2}$</tex> dimensions. This paper yields pathways towards wireless tracking of things via battery-less passive miniaturized transponder.

articleTitle: Reflectarray Concept for Interference Mitigation in Radio Astronomy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a composite reflectarray system for realizing a reflector antenna for radio astronomy applications. The system is equipped with a tunable reflectarray rim that enables nulls to be formed within the field of view and reduce the impact of interferers on the observations. Full-wave simulation results of a physical reflectarray system are presented to validate the concept.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarized Vivaldi Antenna for Tree Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A dual-polarized Vivaldi antenna with a compact size and high gain performance is designed for tree radar applications. The antenna consists of four Vivaldi elements, two of which are orthogonal to the remaining two. Each pair of two elements works together in an array configuration to form a single polarization, while two pairs form a dual polarization with a shared aperture. To increase the radiation performance, planar directors and edge slots are introduced in the design of a single Vivaldi element, and a reflector is placed behind the Vivaldi elements. The simulation results show that the designed antenna achieves a high gain ranging from 5.5 to 15.6 dBi, while its cross-polarization discrimination is larger than 30 dB, demonstrating its high purity for each polarization.

articleTitle: Highly Efficient Linear Array Antenna Implementation for 5G Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A highly efficient broadband passive antenna array with a dielectric resonator is presented in this paper for integration into a single-layer MHMIC module for high data rate 5G IoT applications. The antenna uses a microstrip transmission line to feed a broadband rectangular dielectric resonator. The feed network of the proposed array antenna is designed using a wideband Wilkinson power divider. The experimental results show excellent agreement with their corresponding simulation parameters. The designed DRA array achieves as much as 25% fractional bandwidth with 90% efficiency. The antenna also boasts impressive gains of 13.5 dBi total and 12.7 dBi realized gain across the band, making it suitable for a range of 5G IoT applications.

articleTitle: A Novel Design Method of RIS Element with A Wideband Varactor-Tuned Example
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) are developing rapidly nowadays and considered as a key technology for next-generation communications. However, when designing RISs with wideband feature, the traditional design method is complex and time-costly because the trial-and-error simulations lack clear design guidance. Here, we propose a radiation method to model, design and evaluate a RIS element, where the design goal is to match the element impedance to a pre-calculated impedance determined by the diode parameters. Using the novel method, a varactor-tuned RIS element is designed with a wide bandwidth of 20%, and the average loss is about 1.1 dB at 5.4 GHz, which significantly improves the performance of RIS elements.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Folded Monopole Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Three fully 3D printed wideband monopole antennas are presented. The antennas are elliptical monopole. The first antenna is a traditional flat monopole antenna on a dielectric substrate. The second and third antennas feature unique single and double folded dielectric substrate, which enables increase in the bandwidth. The silver conductive traces were aerosol jet printed on the conformal substrate using reactive silver ink. This ink has conductivity close to bulk silver and requires low sintering temperature of 80 °C. The antennas show wideband performance and omnidirectional radiation patterns in the azimuth plane.

articleTitle: Characterization of $\text{VO}_{2}\text{-Based}$ Reconfigurable Linear-to-Circular Polarization Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present the quasi-optical free space measurement of a reconfigurable linear-to-circular polarization (LCP) converter. Reconfigurability is achieved using vanadium dioxide (VO<inf>2</inf>), a phase-change material (PCM) that experiences a reversible metal-insulator transition (MIT) at 68°C. Preliminary measurement results for a static, non-reconfigurable device correlate well with simulations, validating the accuracy of the measurement setup. The static device achieved phase error below 20°, axial ratio below 3 dB, and insertion loss below 1 dB across the Ka uplink band (27.5–31 GHz). Measurement results for the full device with VO<inf>2</inf> switches will be presented at the conference.

articleTitle: A Dual-Sense Circularly Polarized Flexible Asymmetric CPW-Based Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A conformable, Circularly Polarized (CP), with dual-senses of rotation, antenna is introduced. The antenna has an area of <tex>$25\ \text{mm}\times 26.5\ \text{mm}$</tex>, where Co-Planar Waveguide (CPW) excitation technique is the means for feeding. Rogers Ultralam 3850 substrate material is used to ensure that the antenna is flexible. By designing an asymmetric CPW ground in the essence of elongating the length of one ground plane, with respect to the second one, and engraving a T-shaped slot on the left side CPW ground, Left Hand Circular Polarization (LHCP) and Right-Hand Circular Polarization (RHCP) are accomplished. The antenna resonates at 5.8 GHz of the Industrial, Scientific, and Medical (ISM)-band, with 1.75 GHz–10 dB bandwidth, realized gain of 2.4 dBic. It possesses CP features with Axial Ratio (AR) of 0.27 dB at the boresight direction, and 225 MHz worth of 3 dB-AR bandwidth. Thanks to the achieved specifications, it is a good candidate for flexible CP-related wearable applications.

articleTitle: Ku-Band Metal-Only Flat Metasurface Radar Antenna for Small Platforms
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Metal-only metasurface antennas for small platforms are under development at the NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory to provide high gain, low-profile, low-cost and harsh environment survivable solutions for small airborne and spaceborne platforms. A metal-only Ku-band co-located metasurface antenna pair has been developed for a UA V snow radar with approximately 30 dBi gain, -14 dB reflection coefficient and 60 dB port-to-port isolation over 15–16 GHz band. The antenna has been manufactured and tested, and is currently being used for the field measurements.

articleTitle: Spectral Element Method for Modeling Anisotropic Circular Waveguides Loaded with Eccentric Rods via Conformal Transformation Optics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A spectral element method (SEM) is developed for the analysis of anisotropic circular waveguides partially filled with eccentric dielectric rods. The proposed formulation employs conformal transformation optics to map the original problem into an equivalent concentric circular waveguide. The mapped problem is solved using the SEM in cylindrical coordinates. The approach is validated against the finite-element method (FEM). Preliminary results show that the proposed SEM requires far fewer degrees of freedom (DoF) than FEM.

articleTitle: A Wideband Rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antenna with Varying Material Distributions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a new wideband DRA design implemented with unit cells which facilitates prototyping using 3D printing. In this design, a rectangular DRA was divided into multiple small blocks. Each block was assigned with a different permittivity based on the material profile optimized through a genetic algorithm. As a result, the proposed compact DRA design gives 68.8 % (4.04 - 8.28GHZ) of impedance bandwidth at <tex>$S_{11}=- 10 \ dB$</tex>, which is significantly higher than the bandwidth of the original bulk DRA.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Magneto-Electric Dipole Isolation Enhancement using Superstrate-Based Decoupler
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work presents a superstrate-based decoupler to increase the isolation between two closely spaced Magneto-Electric (ME) dipoles in the 52–64 GHz millimeter wave (MMW) frequency band. The decoupler consists of a single row of 15 vias, and a copper plate carefully inserted into a high-permittivity superstrate between the two-element MIMO antenna. The vias help to mitigate the surface coupled waves in the antenna substrate, while the copper plate and the high-permittivity superstrate help to alter the space permittivity, disturb the space coupling, and increase the isolation. This combination improved the proposed antenna's isolation by a maximum of 31 dB over the 52–64 GHz bandwidth (14.3%) in the H-Plane, with a very close edge-to-edge spacing of 0.62 mm (0.12λ), where λ is the free-space wavelength at the center frequency of 60 GHz. Additionally, the superstrate-based decoupler structure improved the antenna's bandwidth (52–70 GHz), without distorting the radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Towards Chipless RFID Based Temperature Sensing for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel technique to measure temperature by using a chipless RFID tag and smart material in view of loT application. The proposed technique incorporates a unique design of a chipless RFID resonator and a novel chipless technique for sensing temperature by combining ETFE fluroploymer with the resonator. The simulated material is placed on the top of the tag and dielectric parameters are varied. Initially, the original RCS response of the resonator is simulated which is then observed while varying the values of permittivity to obtain a correlation between different frequencies and dielectric constants. This correlation is further compared with the dielectric parameters of the material and the corresponding temperatures found from the literature. Finally, a calibration curve obtained where any temperature within the range can be measured by simply mapping the frequency of operation of the chipless resonator.

articleTitle: High Efficiency and Dual-Band RF Rectifier Circuit for Energy Harvesting Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work presents a dual band, high efficiency RF rectifier circuit using dual section microstrip lines as the matching circuit. This dual band rectifier operates at two different frequencies, 0.915GHz and 2.45GHz. Several input powers are applied to the input of this rectifier to confirm that it is suitable for energy harvesting systems. The results indicate that at 0.915 GHz and 2.45 GHz, the power conversion efficiency is 77.3% and 80.2%, respectively, with 15 dBm input power. According to the simulation results, the dual-band RF rectifier circuit has the advantages of being dual-band and highly efficient.

articleTitle: A Planar Dual-Polarized Wideband Antenna Feed Element Design for Gradient-Index Luneburg Lens Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A planar wideband and dual-polarized antenna feed element for gradient-index (GRIN) Luneburg lens antenna is proposed. The designed dual-polarized antenna feed element is a standalone antenna element and has wide impedance bandwidth with high port-to-port isolation and low cross-polarization level. An example antenna feed element was designed and manufactured using standard printed circuit board (PCB) technology to operate at Ku-band (10.5-14.8GHz) and was used as a feed source for a 12-inch diameter Luneburg lens structure. Measured and simulated results show that the proposed dual-polarized antenna feed element has good impedance bandwidth with low cross-polarization level (<16dB) and high port-to-port isolation (>20dB) making it suitable for practical applications such as satellite communications.

articleTitle: Blockwise vs. and General MNA for MOR
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes two distinct approaches for construction of the Modified Nodal Analysis (MNA) matrices in Model Order Reduction (MOR) techniques, namely the Blockwise MNA and the General MNA. In this work, we apply the proposed approaches to construct MNA matrices of a multi-port network, then reduce their order using the MNA matrices through each approach. As a numerical example, the Y-parameters of full- order and reduced-order networks for a 4-port optical network, operating in the frequency range 175–215 THz, are obtained and are compared in terms of execution time, memory usage, Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), reduction controllability, efficiency, and passivity point of view.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Subwavelength Reflectarray Unit Based on Minkowski Fractal Geometry
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, we propose a dual-band subwavelength reflectarray unit based on Minkowski fractal geometry. To take the advantage of the miniaturization capability of fractal geometry and achieve a dual-band performance at the same time, the unit consisting of 5 first-order Minkowski fractals with optimized patch sizes and scaling factors is designed. The well-known full wave simulation software HFSS is used to analyze the proposed unit cell, and simulation results show that the proposed reflective unit can achieve a dual-band performance in frequency bands centered at 15 GHz and 17 GHz, and the total area of each unit is less than <tex>$1\lambda\times 1\lambda$</tex> where <tex>$\lambda$</tex> is the wavelength of the operating band. Therefore, the proposed unit is very suitable for the design of millimeter-wave reflectarray antennas focused on beam-forming and beam-steering applications.

articleTitle: A High Gain SIW Elliptically Polarized Antenna for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A high-gain SIW elliptically polarized antenna combination of a dipole and loop antenna based on substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) is proposed for millimeter-wave (mm-wave) applications. The dipole and loop antenna are differentially excited by a longitudinal slot etched on the top layer of SIW. The proposed combination of dipole and loop antenna forms a parallel electric dipole and magnetic dipole, which radiates two orthogonal electric field components and <tex>$90^{\circ}$</tex> phase difference in the far-field radiation when they are excited with the same phased signal. The proposed antenna achieves a realized gain of 8.346 dBi, with a radiation efficiency of 89.40% at 60 GHz.

articleTitle: Time Division Duplex Beam Switching System Using a Common Multi-Port Junction Transceiver
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The paper proposes a compact multi-port transceiver for time division duplex systems. Both uplink and downlink transmissions of the transceiver are combined in one six-port junction. To validate the performance of the modulator and demodulator, prototype circuits are simulated with different PSK/QAM signals at the carrier frequency of 61 GHz. The obtained results indicate an excellent performance of the system, as well as implemented TDD beam switching antenna networks.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of a Wide-Band Quad-Ridged Polarizer for Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents design and optimization of a wide-band quad-ridged waveguide polarizer using irises for satellite communications. The design steps of the polarizer and the parameters used for optimization are explained. The designed polarizer overcomes the conventional bandwidth limit and covers about 30% bandwidth from 21.4 to 29.3 GHz. The electrical performance of the polarizer is analyzed using the commercial electromagnetic simulation software, CST Studio Suite. The performance of the final design shows that insertion loss is <0.2 dB, return loss is >23 dB, and the phase difference is smaller than 10° as a reference point by 90° in the overall band.

articleTitle: High-Speed Train Channels with Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface: Modeling and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a geometry-based millimeter-wave channel model is proposed for on-board reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted high-speed train communications, where three propagation cases are considered to describe real channels. In addition, RIS phase optimization method is presented to enhance received power and mitigate channel fading. Based on the proposed model, impacts of RIS phase optimization and channel parameters on channel impulse responses are analyzed. Numerical results indicate that received power at a specific area can be enhanced by adjusting the phase of RIS elements, and a larger number of RIS elements can effectively improve performance of high-speed train systems. These observations and conclusions are insightful for designing and realizing RIS-assisted high-speed train communications.

articleTitle: Wideband Feed and Reflector Ground Shield for the Deep Synoptic Array (DSA-2000)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present the low-cost, dual-polarized, wideband quad-ridge choke horn (QRCH) feed with a low-loss dielectric lid optimized for the Deep Synoptic Array (DSA-2000) in radio astronomy. The ridges and dielectric lid allows for a compact feed diameter with small blockage of the 5-meter-diameter axially-symmetric prime-focus reflector. A wide feed pattern suitable for applications with f/D below 0.35 is achieved over the frequency range 0.7-2 GHz. The band-average aperture efficiency in simulation is 66 % in the unshaped reflector including blockage. An extension of the reflector rim reduces the spillover noise contribution to less than 1 K at zenith pointing. Together with an excellent ambient temperature low-noise amplifier developed for DSA-2000 the predicted system noise temperature is 25 K.

articleTitle: Kriging Methodology for Predicting Material Uncertainty Impact on FEM Scattering Computations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a Kriging interpolation surrogate function for use in reconstruction of probability density function in scattering uncertainty quantification problems, focusing on predicting material uncertainty impact on finite-element scattering computations. The results show extremely high reconstruction accuracy while reducing computation time by approximately two orders of magnitude relative to the conventional Monte Carlo approach. This tool offers a robust option for future uncertainty quantification problems in the field of computational electro magnetics.

articleTitle: Effect of Antenna Pattern on Time-Domain Canceling of Interference from Satellites
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Signals from satellites are a source of interference to radio telescopes. One possible scheme for mitigation of this interference is coherent time-domain canceling. Using a simple but broadly-applicable model for the antenna pattern, we show how the antenna pattern combined with the motion of the satellite limits the time available to compute an accurate estimate of the interference waveform, which subsequently limits the extent to which interference can be canceled in the output. We suggest a simple remedy to the problem.

articleTitle: Band Gap Based Power Dividers in Parallel Plate Waveguide Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper is described a novel and low-cost method for the realization of electromagnetic band gap (EBG) based power dividers in Parallel Plate Waveguide Technology (PPW). The proposed configuration can be employed as a basic element of the highly efficient Continuous Stub (CTS) array antenna feeding network. The resulting band-gap feeding network overcomes the problem of good electrical contact between the metallic layers thanks to the use of printed mushroom-type EBG embedded inside the PPW. The EBG is designed to provide a forbidden band that covers the operating frequency range of the waveguide, in this manner electromagnetic leakage from the air gap between layers is avoided simplifying the mechanical assembly of the antenna with a significant reduction of manufacturing costs and complexity. The metallic units of the CTS antenna can be easily fixed by screws, and no additional welding assembly is required. A design example operating in the 27.5-31 GHz band (Tx Satcom band) is presented and compared with a classical configuration. The proposed solution provides a good matching on the whole bandwidth, while the insertion loss remains unchanged.

articleTitle: Modeling of Miniaturized 4×4 and 8×8 Butler Matrix Based on Complementary Rose Curves Resonators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work focused on the design of miniaturized 4×4 and 8×8 Butler matrices (BMs) using a metamaterial approach. The proposed structure is based on complementary Rose curve resonators (CRCRs). The frequency of the design was 2 to 4 GHz. Because of the negative permittivity structure of the metamaterial and the coupling of this resonator with the stripline, the RF component can be reduced in size. Using this reduction strategy to replace crossover places, the suggested Butler matrix produces results that are favorable with respect to those found in the literature.

articleTitle: Propagation Measurement and Analysis of a Large Cubicle Office Environment at 159 GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper reports on 159-GHz propagation measurements collected in a large cubicle office environment and provides an analysis of path loss and delay spread characteristics. The directional propagation characteristics (by selecting the best-beam directional combination), denoted by Max-Dir, and the synthesized omnidirectional characteristics, denoted by Syn-Omni, are investigated. The measurement results show that the Syn-Omni path losses are smaller than the Max-Dir losses, but the Syn-Omni delay spreads are greater. The NLoS losses do not seem to be considerably different from the LoS losses, especially for the Syn-Omni case. Additionally, the empirical CDFs of the delay spread appear to follow a lognormal distribution.

articleTitle: Development and Characterization of A Sticker-Typed Flexible Dipole RFID Tag Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The paper deals with the development of a flexible dipole antenna which is printed on a thin plastic mica sheet for Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) application. The characterization is applied experimentally for the proposed antenna in some bending conditions to demonstrate its feasibility as a front-end flexible device at Ultra High Frequency (UHF) band. The proposed dipole RFID tag antenna which takes a sticker-typed form is made by an aluminium foil as the radiator with the total size of 72.27 mm by 18.83 mm. The result shows that the realized antenna resonates at the frequency of 975 MHz and has the bandwidth response covering the desired application.

articleTitle: Preliminary Data from Phase Coherent Vertical Array During the Coastal Land-Air-Sea Interactions Mission, Florida, 2023
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Propagating electromagnetic wave trapping in the marine boundary layer induced by unique weather conditions influences electromagnetic system performance in this domain. Characterization of the trapping effect utilizing signal phase in addition to signal magnitude is of great interest. The Winter of 2023 campaign of the Coastal Land-Air-Sea Interactions mission includes a phase coherent vertical array which measures electromagnetic power and phase having propagated through the marine boundary layer. Preliminary results from the deployed system during this campaign are shown.

articleTitle: A Wideband Dual-Band and Dual-Circularly-Polarized Wide-Angle Scanning Phased Array Antenna with Single-Port Feed at K-/Ka-Bands
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A dual-band and dual-circularly-polarized phased array antenna is presented with the single-port feed for K-/Ka-bands satellite communication applications. To achieve the left-hand circular polarization (LHCP) in K-band and the right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) in Ka-band, the wideband and dual-polarized magnetoelectric-dipole (MED) is connected in series with the dual-band coupler. The dual-band coupler is carefully designed to achieve the amplitude and phase requirement for generating the circular polarization (CP) at K-/Ka-bands. Then, an <tex>$\mathbf{8}\times \mathbf{8}$</tex> phased array antenna consisting of the MED unit cells is designed and simulated. It shows an axial ratio (AR) lower than 4 dB within the scanning range of <tex>$\pm \mathbf{55}^{\circ}$</tex>, over these frequency bands from 17.7 GHz to 19.7 GHz and from 28 GHz to 30 GHz.

articleTitle: A Diamond Ring Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A wearable antenna with diamond-ring shape is proposed in this paper. It employs differential feeding method to achieve a compact structure, whereas realizing dual-mode dual-band and high-gain performance at the same time. By exciting two different modes of the DR, dual millimeter-wave (mmW) operating bands located at 27.0 GHz and 32.5 GHz are realized. A unique higher-order mode is excited inside the diamond-shaped dielectric resonator (DR) which produces a peak realized gain of 8.4 dBi. The proposed antenna enjoys the benefits of compact structure, simple design and dual-band high-gain performances, which make it suitable for mmW Internet of Things (IoT) applications.

articleTitle: An Antenna with Quasi-Isotropic Radiation Pattern Designed with Bent Dipoles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) devices, typically, need electrically small antennas that can maintain orientation insensitive communication. This is feasible with quasi-isotropic radiation patterns. This paper presents a theoretical model, based on annular currents, for the design of antennas with quasi isotropic radiation patterns. The theoretical model is then used to design an antenna that comprises two orthogonal bent dipoles. The effect of the bending radius on the radiation isotropy performance has been studied. The theoretical results obtained using the annular current model have been verified by simulations and a fabricated antenna prototype. Measured results are in decent agreement with the simulated results and a quasi-isotropic radiation pattern of the antenna with a gain variation of 5.7 dB has been achieved.

articleTitle: Miniaturization of Yagi-Uda Rectenna by Impedance Loading
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: By applying the principle of the Yagi-Uda antenna, it is possible to extend the wireless power feeding distance. However, the Yagi-Uda antenna has restrictions on the shape and arrangement of the elements. To overcome this problem, this paper proposes a novel rectenna array that downsizes the elements by loading impedance. Electromagnetic analysis shows the results of that the downsized rectenna array with load impedance is achieved higher the wireless power transmission efficiency than that without impedance. The prototypes of the loaded rectenna could light up an LED using leaky waves from a microwave oven nevertheless the without a load rectenna could not light the LED.

articleTitle: Cloaking of Rectangular Patch Antenna Arrays with Coated Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The concept of electromagnetic cloaking is applied to eliminate the adverse effects of mutual coupling between the tightly spaced, interleaved rectangular patch arrays operating at C-band frequencies. We demonstrate that by coating the top surfaces of each patch antenna element with a suitably patterned metasurface, the elements appear to become electromagnetically invisible to each other.
