Particularly, the cloaking and decoupling effect is evaluated to enhance the functionality of the coupled arrays in terms of their realized gain and total efficiencies. Subsequently, the interleaved patch antenna arrays, even though placed in close proximity, can radiate independently as if they were isolated. The fact that these specifically designed metasurfaces achieve cloaking of an electrically large surface, makes our design unique in itself. The decoupling and cloaking action of the metasurfaces are demonstrated by various full-wave numerical simulation results.

articleTitle: A Phase Delay Line Sensor for Water Quality Monitoring Based on Spherical Conformal Reflectarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a phase delay line sensor for water quality monitoring based on spherical conformal reflec-tarray antenna (RA) operating at a central frequency of 5.8 GHz. The sensor is used in radio frequency identification (RFID) systems and is composed of a spherical rectangular patch antenna array and a reconfigurable phase delay transmission line. To ensure the omnidirectionality, four array units are placed in the spatial location around the upper hemisphere. To achieve the largest phase shift in a limited space, a bent microstrip line is used as the phase-signal transmission line for the water channel. Simulation results show that as the relative permittivity of water decreases, the phase shift of the backward scattered wave increases rapidly. If the phase shift of pure water is used as a reference, the phase shifts caused by the air and oil in the channel are 358.11° and 248.41°, respectively. The big difference of phase shifts between oil and water allows a sensitive monitoring for water quality by the RFID systems.

articleTitle: Using Camera Boxes to Build Reproducible CEM Benchmarks with Complex Ducts
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A cylindrical hub is inserted into a pipe inside a scaled camera box—a recently introduced structure intended to host differently-shaped ducts behind an aperture. The resulting metallic structure simplifies a commonly used model of jet-engine inlets and is designed to serve as a precisely-defined, easy-to-reproduce simulation and measurement benchmark. Results show that the fields scattered by the structure, while highly sensitive to small changes, can be both measured and simulated accurately even at frequencies with many interior propagating modes.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Holographic Metasurface Leaky-Wave Multi-Beam Antennas with Gain and Polarization Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a holographic multiple-beam leaky-wave antenna (LWA) synthesized by metasurfaces with controllable polarization and amplitude of the radiated beams. The interference pattern is first obtained by the inner product of the reference and object wave vector field functions, the former being that of a cylindrical source surface wave, the latter comprising the vector sum of the phase projections onto the hologram of the various incident plane waves, the directions, amplitudes and polarizations of which are to be reproduced as LWA beams upon illumination of the synthesized hologram by the same source. By DC-biasing and amplitude modulating the sinusoidal interference pattern to fit the surface reactance range of the metasurface patch arrays for the synthesis, the spatial distribution of the required surface impedance over the holographic surface is then devised. Simulations of designs by this approach check well with expected results in terms of the beam direction, amplitude, and polarizations.

articleTitle: Ball Grid Array Integration of Wideband Planar Printed Array Apertures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents experimental results for a Planar Ultra-wideband Modular Antenna (PUMA) array integrated with a coaxial feed network using Ball Grid Array (BGA) technology. A PUMA aperture is designed and manufactured with a BGA interface in place of typical feed structures. The BGA-backed PUMA aperture is then connected to a matching BGA interface on a coaxial through test circuit, allowing typical embedded element RF characterization performance and functionality evaluation of the PUMA aperture as a BGA package.

articleTitle: Compact Broadband Rate-Race Coupler for Millimiter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel mm-wave rat-race coupler with broadband operating bandwidth based on parallel microstrip lines is presented in this paper. The useful practical bandwidth for this hybrid covers a frequency range 20–42 GHz for both sum and difference situations. The proposed design could be easily fabricated by printed circuit board (PCB) technology.

articleTitle: On the Spectral Efficiency of UAVs-assisted D2D Cooperative Communications Using NOMA
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The tomorrow's 6G wireless networks require high spectral efficiency to accommodate a massive number of devices over the limited available frequency spectrum. This paper aims to investigate a Device-to-Device (D2D) cooperative system for maximizing the spectrum efficiency in disaster management scenario, wherein multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) act as relays to facilitate seamless communication between D2D transceivers. In this perspective, we integrate non-orthogonal-multiple-access (NOMA) technology to further enhance the transmission efficiency of the system. Simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the UAVs-assisted D2D cooperative solution when using NOMA in terms of spectral efficiency.

articleTitle: APS 2033: A Future for Women in Electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The vison of APS 2033 as a strong, inclusive professional society that serves all of our engineers is a valuable and achievable goal. We need to think of our networks and IEEE activities as inclusive not exclusive by making changes to processes within our society that reflect that expectation. We need to invite, nominate, and support engineers outside of our immediate network for all IEEE APS activities and have a society-wide call for volunteers for all activities. We need to make a systemic effort to nominate a diverse pool of Fellow candidates every year, and seek Award nominees broadly. We need to individually support all of our colleagues, in order to reach a APS 2033 that is stronger, larger, and more supportive for all of its members. We will be rewarded with a larger, broader, creative professional society that supports Antenna and Propagation engineering for all

articleTitle: Angularly Stable Metasurface Filter Using a Cloverleaf Element
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a method to design a single-layer angular stable metasurface (ASM) filter unit cell for a nearly full range of angles of incidence for both TE and TM polarization. We formulate the optimization criterion using the energy balance condition derived from Poynting's Theorem. The proposed unit cell has a “cloverleaf” geometry, and we show that by adjusting the properties of the cloverleaf we obtain the desired angular stability. After optimization we revisit the energy and show how optimization at three points is enough to obtain such balance for the entire angular spectrum.

articleTitle: Modeling of Electromagnetic Wave Phase Front Aberration in Rain
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a physics-based model for estimation of phase and amplitude variation in the phase front of high frequency electromagnetic waves propagating in rain. The model accurately predicts the statistical behavior of the phase and amplitude variation of the fluctuating part of the waves due to scattering by rain particles. The model is useful in performance analysis of MIMO systems for communication and radars. The modeling approach is discussed and the statistical parameters of the model are provided for rain rate of 10 mm/hr at 77 GHz.

articleTitle: 2×2 Planar Array of X-Shaped Slot Antennas for Millimeter Wave Frequency Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a 2×2 planar array of slot antennas for use in local 5G of 28 GHz frequency band is presented. The X-shaped slot antennas are used as radiating elements in the planar array. The feeding circuits of the planar array are conventional microstrip line and slot line. In this paper, antenna characteristics are evaluated by using the Finite Element Method in the commercial simulation software EMPro (Keysight). From the simulation results, -10 dB impedance bandwidth is obtained within the frequency range of 27.4 GHz to 30.5 GHz which is about 3.1 GHz bandwidth. The realized gain has the peak value of 14.6 dBi within 28.3 GHz to 28.5 GHz.

articleTitle: High-Frequency Limits for 3D-Printed Gradient-Index (GRIN) Lens Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Artificial dielectrics are widely used for Gradient-Index (GRIN) lens antennas. The unit-cell size of an artificial dielectric determines the maximum operating frequency and also drives cost and yield. To explore the frequency limitations we printed four identical Luneburg lens antennas using gyroid unit-cells of 12.5, 10, 7.5, and 5 mm and measured their gain over the K- and Ka-band. We find maximum frequencies of 20, 25, 33, and >40 GHz for each unit-cell, respectively. These measurements suggest a print resolution limit of <tex>$0.7\lambda_{g}$</tex>, where <tex>$\lambda_{g}$</tex> is the wavelength in the host dielectric.

articleTitle: A 3D-Printed Wide-Band Wrist-Worn Wearable Antenna For 4G/5G Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A wideband, conformal, and wearable antenna designed for 4G/5G wireless communication is proposed. The 3D-printed antenna, which uses coplanar waveguide (CPW) feeding, is printed on the front side of a 1.75mm thick flexible Polyflex dielectric material. The proposed antenna resonates at 2.65 and 3.70 GHz, resulting in a wideband impedance bandwidth of 65.23% (2.19 - 4.31 GHz) due to the merging of these two resonances. The antenna was fabricated using a LulzBot 3-D printer and tested for −10 dB impedance bandwidth in free space and on a human body. Its robustness was also evaluated by analyzing its performance under bending, to ensure its functionality in the desired band of operation when used on the human body.

articleTitle: Single-Fed Electrically Small Antenna with Circular Polarization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A single-fed electrically small antenna with circular polarization is presented. The antenna is composed of two crossed electrically small half loops. The loops are reactively loaded in which the loads provide the current phasing on each loop element. The antenna is matched to the reference impedance due to the excitation technique as well as the loops reactive loads.

articleTitle: Compact Slot-Patch Antenna with Dual Circular Polarization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a compact Circularly Polarized (CP) slot-patch antenna operating in dual polarization is presented. The proposed solution, designed to operate at 412 MHz, consists of a circular patch on top of a layer of dielectric substrate, backed by a circular cavity to increase radiation efficiency. The radiating patch has two slots sector notches on opposite sides and is coaxially fed in two different points to achieve both right-hand and left-hand circular polarization. The proposed design shows a minimum Axial Ratio (AR) of 1.16 dB and a gain of 5 dBi near the resonance frequency. The obtained results make the structure suitable to be integrated into array systems for satellite applications.

articleTitle: Fundamental Study on Electrically Controllable Broadband and Thin Non-Reciprocal Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we report fundamental simulation results on a novel structure combining magnetic materials and metal patches towards the realization of non-reciprocal metasurfaces that can be controlled by electrical signals to achieve stealth properties. The proposed structure realizes non-reciprocity with a cylindrical magnetic body and a metal patch placed next to it. Unidirectional microwave propagation is achieved by combining the circular propagation characteristics of magnetic materials and the transmission/reflection control of metal patches. As a result of simulation, it is possible to achieve isolation of 10 dB or more and a thickness of 1/3 wavelength or less with a bandwidth of 3GHz or more in the X band.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of 3-D Printed Wideband Cavity Antenna for WLAN
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a 3-D printed wideband cavity antenna with enhanced gain operating at the 5.8 GHz Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) frequency. The bandwidth of the cavity antenna is 1 GHz resulting from the slots created at the upper side of the antenna structure. The bandwidth of the cavity antenna with metasurface is 5.07 GHz - 6.08 GHz indicating that there is no change in the total antenna bandwidth post the metasurface placement inside the cavity. The metasurface enhances the antenna gain by 2.4 dB at 5.8 GHz. Through the flexibility provided by 3-D printing, the metasurface layer can be attached to the cavity structure giving the design much-needed robustness and strength. It proves the feasibility of using 3D printing technology in antenna design.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Antenna-in-Package (AiP) Front-End Module for 5G mmWave Mobile Device Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band antenna-in-package front-end module for 5G mmWave mobile device applications is presented. A stacked dual-band dual-polarized broadband patch antenna loaded with parasitic patches were designed as a unit cell for antenna array. A proposed antenna module is composed of 1×5 patch antenna array and RFICs. The designed RFIC-integrated AiP module has measured EIRP value of 29.9 dBm at 28 GHz and 30.1 dBm at 29 GHz. It also has <tex>$+/-45^{\circ}$</tex> beam-steering angle in both V- and H-pols. The designed mmWave module for 5G mmWave band has compact size of 26×5.2×2.1 mm<sup>3</sup> which is small enough to mount sides of most of commercial mobile devices.

articleTitle: A Broadband Low Profile SIW H-Plane Horn Antenna with Improved Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper is presenting a broadband, low-profile (<tex>$0.008 \lambda_{0}$</tex>) substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) H-plane horn antenna with the reduced side lobes and improved front-to-back ratio (FTBR). This is achieved implementing three rectangular slots near the coaxial feed. The hexagonal slots in front of the horn aperture are used to improve impedance matching. The measured fractional impedance bandwidth of 29.5% (3.25 GHz), the maximum gain of 5.52 dBi (minimum: 2.85 dBi), the maximum radiation efficiency of 95.99 %, the FTBR of 15.83 dB, and the low cross-polarization level have been achieved at the frequency of 9.85 GHz.

articleTitle: Designing the Reconfigurable Over-The-Air Chamber
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work proposes a computational tool appropriate for designing a reconfigurable over-the-air chamber (ROTAC), which is an advanced reverberation chamber for testing mobile wireless devices. The tool uses the electric field integral equation to determine the fields within a chamber test zone based on currents on the ROTAC antennas and then optimizes the antenna placements to maximize the chamber's ability to synthesize desired fields. The work also provides a way to compare the sensitivity of different design configurations to operational errors. Application of the tool to the design of a representative ROTAC shows that while optimization can improve the chamber's ability to synthesize fields, such optimization results in a notable increase in the sensitivity of the synthesized fields to errors in the chamber excitations.

articleTitle: The Effect of Range on Close-Range Millimeter-Wave Imaging Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The effect of range distance in millimeter-wave imaging is explored in this paper. The established physical model treats the incident and scattered signals as plane waves, and this has been applied successfully for some years. However, this model does not fully account for propagation loss, and it is shown in this paper that this can lead to a degradation in the results for multiple objects when they are at different ranges from the source. It is shown that, when using the established algorithm for image reconstruction in a monostatic system, it is more difficult to correctly image multiple objects when they are at different ranges.

articleTitle: A Planar Conformal Microwave Resonator for Subcutaneous Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A planar conformal microwave resonator is developed to detect malignant tumors inside tissues. The tuned sensor with localized field distributions can noninvasively distinguish permittivity variations within tissues. The principle is based on electromagnetic-wave interaction in materials where permittivity variations due to malignant tumors among normal tissues affect the field distributions. The imaging process is conducted with a two-dimensional raster scan to record reflection coefficients in pixels. The normalized resonant frequencies and magnitudes of reflection coefficients are fused to generate localization maps. The concept is validated by promising results with tumor phantoms at different depths and of various sizes. The fused maps indicate a great potential for subcutaneous imaging on the skin in a more efficient and safer way with lower costs than the traditional nondestructive evaluation methods such as X-ray.

articleTitle: Design of a Flexible Antenna Using Weaving Technique for C-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A flexible C-band antenna design using conductive wire weaving technique is introduced. An antenna consists of three layers: a groundplane, a radiator, and a parasitic element on top. The square radiator element is made of woven ladder yarn. At the same time, both the grounding element and the parasitic element are made of flexible copper sheets. On the other hand, the antenna substrate is made of denim material with a dielectric constant of 1.7 and a loss tangent of 0.024. The antenna design is optimized using finite element method (FEM). The antenna is designed for use in the C-band with a center frequency of 5.3 GHz. Simulation results show that the antenna design has a gain of 4.8 dB, a reflection coefficient bandwidth (S11) of 7.02%, and the highest efficiency of 62.7% at the center of the operating frequency. Based on the simulation results, the weaving technique produces good antenna performance and can be used in various C-band applications.

articleTitle: EBG-Backed Head Wearable Antenna Array for Transcranial Radio-Frequency Stimulation Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A head wearable antenna array embedded on a multilayer substrate to enable unidirectional radiation pattern, broad bandwidth and compact size for trans cranial radiofrequency stimulation is proposed. The top layer consists of <tex>$4\mathrm{x}4$</tex> radiating patches, an EBG array and feeding network while the bottom layer consists of <tex>$4\mathrm{x}4$</tex> MTM reflectors. The EBG array consists of 9-unit cells arranged near the feeding network to reduce the surface waves while the MTM reflectors compel the antenna to radiate towards the broadside thus achieving a unidirectional radiation pattern for the complete structure. A broad impedance bandwidth and compact size are achieved by using the DNG properties of the meta material. The unidirectional pattern along with compact size and broad bandwidth enable the proposed design to be used for transcranial radiof-requency stimulation and other biomedical applications.

articleTitle: Impact of Ground Plane Scattering on Performance of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) are being considered for 6G as they can facilitate favourable radio channels. To rigorously model the characteristics of an array antenna-based RIS, this paper proposes an approach to separately evaluate scatterings from the antenna elements and ground plane of RIS. Simulation results show that, depending on the absolute phases of variable loads in the RIS, the scattering from the ground plane can have a non-negligible effect on the performance of the RIS.

articleTitle: A Compact Millimeter Wave Polarization Reconfigurable Double Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A polarization-reconfigurable single-fed patch antenna loaded with a smaller parasitic stacked bandwidth-enhancing patch are reported in this letter. The antenna system is optimized to operate at 29 GHz with three polarization modes that can be reconfigured electronically. The structure consists of two Rogers 3003 substrates of thicknesses of 0.25 and 0.50 mm for the driven antenna and the parasitic one, respectively. The main antenna's ground layer has four square loops etched out to excite the current paths on the driven patch needed for circular polarizations. These four slot loops are placed in the driven patch's four corners and are controlled with four P-I-N didoes. By shorting two diagonally placed slot loops, a circular polarization (CP) mode is created while shorting all of them will result in linearly polarized (LP) radiation. The measured gain and relative impedance bandwidth (BW) of the left-hand circular polarization (LHCP) are 3.1 dB and 5.4%, respectively. Similar results are obtained for the RHCP due to symmetry in structure and biasing conditions. The LP case reached a gain of 4.0 dB and a relative impedance BW of 5.45%. The overall size of the antenna system is 10.2×14.1×0.784 mm<sup>3</sup> with a radiation efficiency above 90%. Measurement results are compared and validated with simulations.

articleTitle: Terahertz Antenna Design Using Machine Learning Assisted Global Optimization Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In the terahertz (THz) frequency band, high path loss necessitates designing the antenna with high-gain characteristics, making it challenging to obtain an optimal design solution. This paper investigates the feasibility of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven antenna design techniques to address the challenges, specifically the Surrogate Model- assisted Differential Evolution for Antenna Synthesis (SADEA-I) algorithm. SADEA-I has been employed for the first time (to the best of our knowledge) to optimize THz antennas. The simulation results show that SADEA-I is more effective than conventional design methodologies. Additionally, it takes only 30 hours to perform the global optimization, and it is a fully automated process and does not require any initial design.

articleTitle: Effects of Mismatch on IC-Equipped Programmable Metasurfaces with Multibeam Functionality
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Integrated circuit (IC) technology can be incorporated in programmable metasurfaces (PMSFs) and reduce their cost and power consumption while increasing their electromagnetic manipulation capabilities. Such improvements can succour the incorporation of PMSFs as a common telecommunication technology. In order for this to be realised, the reproducibility and reliability of IC-equipped PMSFs need to be addressed. A study is presented on effects of IC mismatch on the performance of a PMSF with multibeam functionality. A mismatch of 10% to 40% of the nominal IC response is used and the effects on the far field are presented.

articleTitle: Estimating Antenna Measurements Uncertainty from Quiet Zone Variation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Antenna far-field performance is conveniently measured in plane wave-based systems such as Compact Antenna Test Range (CATR) and Plane Wave Generators (PWG). The quality of the realized plane waves in such system is commonly expressed as amplitude and phase variation from the ideal plane wave. This QZ metrics does not translate to a direct contribution of an antenna measurement uncertainty analysis, which instead significantly depends on the Antenna Under Test (AUT). In this paper we introduce a new tool to evaluate the measurement accuracy for a given antenna with a specific QZ generated by such systems. The model consists of an “ideal” plane wave generator in which the QZ amplitude and phase variation can be controlled by the amplitude and phase of additional sources away from the origin. The coupling between the model of the measurement system (e.g. the CATR or PWG) and a general AUT can be evaluated accurately by the Spherical Wave Expansion (SWE)-based transmission formula given their respective spherical wave coefficients.

articleTitle: A Parallel Implementation of Solving Radiative Transfer Equation using Discontinuous Galerkin Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The discontinuous Galerkin (DG) finite element method (FEM) is used to solve the radiative transfer equation (RTE) for two-dimensional problems involving absorption, emission, and scattering with the semitransparent medium. The DG approach discretizes both spatial and angular directions. A series of sub-domains implemented by angular decomposition and domain decomposition algorithms are solved by the RTE in parallel. A semitransparent medium with a two-dimensional problem is conducted to study the performance of the method.

articleTitle: Improvement of Beam-Scanning Gain of Multi-Beam Lens Antenna Fed by Circularly Arranged Horns with Separated Phase Centers in E/H-Planes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes wide-angle beam-scanning technique of a multi-beam dielectric lens antenna fed by horns with separated phase centers in E/H-planes by different wall heights. The phase centers of the horn antenna in E/H-planes were designed independently by the wall heights to be coincident with two lens focuses caused by astigmatism in the beam-scanning plane and in its orthogonal plane, respectively. Wide-angle beam-scanning and broadband reflection characteristics were confirmed by electromagnetic simulation in this work.

articleTitle: Near-Field Focusing Conformal Magnetic Metasurface for Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a conformal magnetic metasurface whose response can be opportunely controlled to obtain an efficient near-field focusing for resonant inductive Wireless Power Transfer applications. In particular, an analytical model is employed, allowing a proper control of the metasurface response so that a the magnetic near-field focusing can be achieved. A numerical Wireless Power Transfer set-up, working at 13.56 MHz, is designed to demonstrate the validity of the proposed approach. The results obtained through full-wave simulations prove that the magnetic field can be focused in the desired spatial spot, although the low frequency herein employed and overcoming the effects of metasurface conformal shape. In addition, the power transfer efficiency has been tested by positioning the receiver in two distinct spatial regions, respectively coaxial to and far from the focalized location. The results demonstrate that the WPT efficiency is effectively enhanced only when the receiver is positioned above the magnetic field focalized spot. Several WPT technologies, including charging pads, biomedical implants, and automotive applications, may advantageously exploit these features to precisely power multiple receivers, to achieve reconfigurability, and to realize conformal devices.

articleTitle: Study on Co-and Cross-Polarization Radiation Patterns of Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, radiation patterns of a dipole antenna are analyzed for different orientations with the help of horn antenna. The horn antenna is considered as a receiver, and the dipole antenna is considered as a transmitter. Co-and cross- component of the radiation pattern of a dipole antenna, in terms of <tex>$E_{\theta}$</tex> and <tex>$E_{\phi}$</tex> can be easily visualized by rotating the dipole along the particular axis. This method can be applied to any antenna to get 2D radiation pattern in terms of <tex>$E_{\theta}$</tex> and <tex>$E_{\phi}$</tex> in any plane.

articleTitle: Locating EMI Sources in Shielding Enclosures Using a Two-Step Source Reconstruction Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Locating the sources of electromagnetic interference (EMI) in shielding enclosures is a complex task due to the intricate electromagnetic environment. In this study, we propose a two-step source reconstruction method (SRM) as a solution to this issue. The EMI sources are initially modeled as equally distributed equivalent electric dipoles inside the enclosure, taking into account the effects of the surrounding environment through the use of numerical Green's functions. These initial equivalent sources are subsequently downsized by evaluating the contribution of each dipole, leading to the update of the parameters of the remaining dipoles through a further source reconstruction process that includes the incorporation of additional equivalent magnetic dipoles for enhanced precision. Our method allows for the clear identification of the locations and geometries of EMI sources in the enclosure and accurate estimation of their radiated emissions. The effectiveness of the SRM is demonstrated through representative numerical examples.

articleTitle: Microwave Nondestructive Testing Using an Array of Near-Field Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Microwave imaging has been a popular high resolution, non-invasive, and non-contact nondestructive testing (NDT) method for detecting defects and objects in non-metallic media with applications toward testing dielectric slabs, printed circuit board testing, biomedical diagnosis, etc. In this paper, we employ an array of microwave sensors designed based on the complementary split ring resonators (CSRR) along with nearfield holographic microwave imaging (NH-MWI) to assess the hidden features in the dielectric media. In this array, each element resonates at a different frequency in the range of 1 GHz to 10 GHz. Performance of the proposed method is demonstrated via simulation and experimental results.

articleTitle: Recent Progress in Fault Diagnosis of Phased Antenna Arrays Using Excitation Engineering
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We review recent results in the area of fault diagnosis of phased antenna arrays. These results have distinguishing features that set them apart from related work, namely the use of a single, fixed measurement location, and the optimization of the excitations of the antenna elements of the array. We start with the relatively simple scenario of ignoring inter-element mutual coupling, and show how the element excitations can be optimized to reduce the mutual coherence of the sensing matrix. This leads to successful fault diagnosis with a reduced number of measurements. We then generalize this idea in two directions. In the first, we explore applications in the frequency domain by demonstrating online fault diagnosis in multi-carrier precoding systems. Here, a portion of the spectrum is used for fault diagnosis while the remaining continues to be used for wireless communication. In the second, we upgrade our technique for the case when inter-element mutual coupling is significant. By using two popular models that incorporate mutual coupling effects, we demonstrate efficient fault diagnosis also in this scenario. We expect these techniques to greatly simplify the task of fault diagnosis in modern wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Direction of Arrival (DoA) Estimation Using Irregular Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a new method for DoA estimation using irregular synthetic array will be presented. Power spectral density (PSD) which helps to estimate DoA of multiple sources is computed over signals received by irregular arrays/trajectories. The technique exhibits decent accuracy for DoA estimation of multiple non-coherent sources without ambiguity and is robust to imperfect synchronization of receivers.

articleTitle: Improved Reflectarray Feeds Using Gradient Index Lenses
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Reflectarray antenna (RA) systems are being increasingly used in many applications due to the advantages of their simple design and spatial feeding along with their capabilities for beam shaping and beam forming. However, like all aperture antennas, RAs are limited in the maximum gain they can achieve and power handling they can attain as a result of the feed illumination. By augmenting an RA horn feed with a GRadient INdex (GRIN) lens it is shown that it is possible to better distribute the feed's incident illumination across the surface while still maintaining the gain of the nominal system. Specifically, this work demonstrates that a GRIN lens designed for an offset fed RA at S Band operation can reduce the peak field strength by 17.6<sup>%</sup> and correspondingly improve the power handling capability by 47% relative to the nominal, no-lens system.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Assisted Optimization Method with Self-adaptive Hyperparameter Optimization Strategy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel machine learning-assisted method with self-adaptive hyperparameter optimization strategy (SAHO) for antenna optimization is proposed. The computational cost in the ML training processes is largely reduced by introducing SAHO strategy. In an omnidirectional antenna design case, the SAHO is able to save 79% training cost, and provides good convergence speed and robust algorithm performance.

articleTitle: Equatorial Ionospheric D-Region Characterization using Tweeks observed in Sri Lanka
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work shows the initial equatorial D-region density profile generated from the mode cutoff frequencies observed at the extremely low frequency and very low frequency receiver in Sri Lanka. The tweeks show higher order transverse magnetic modes up to the 7th mode. The electron density and the reflection heights calculated based on the mode cutoff frequencies lie within a similar range with the mid-latitude observations previously observed.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Polarisation Insensitive Wideband Metasurfaces for Dynamic Polarization Conversion and Beam Shaping
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Broadband polarization insensitive transmissive metasurfaces were proposed for anomalous refraction with 45° polarisation conversion and vortex beams with 90° polarisation conversion. By using four-way phase delay lines and a transmitting-receiving (Tx-Rx) antenna, the meta-atom can realise both a full-cycle (2π) transmission phase and polarisation conversion. The polarisation conversion and tilted beam angle are fixed with different incident polarisations of electromagnetic (EM) waves. The additive manufacturing technique is used to fabricate two prototypes.

articleTitle: A Wideband Fabry-Perot Antenna with a Bianisotropic FSS Layer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a Fabry-Pérot cavity antenna with a wide bandwidth and high gain working in k-band. The structure includes two layers, a patch as a feeding source and a bianisotropic omega frequency selective surface (FSS) layer to increase the bandwidth, the gain, and reduce the RCS. The proposed antenna has a maximum peak gain of 14.1 dBi, with an impedance bandwidth of 22.7 % (25.76 GHz–32.13 GHz) and a 3 dB gain bandwidth of 14.1 % (26 GHz–30.61 GHz) at the center frequency of 28 GHz.

articleTitle: An Integral-Equation Kernel for Glide Symmetric Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Glide-symmetric structures can improve properties of periodic structures for a wide variety of applications, such as lenses, filters and gap waveguides. Therefore, fast and accurate tools are needed to facilitate their use. In this work, we present a modelling approach based on a method of moments with a novel Green's function. The solutions are found as singularities of the impedance matrix. The results are shown to be in good agreement with a well-established method.

articleTitle: Double-Ridge Horn with Sinusoidally-Modulated Profile Enabled by 3D-Printing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The performance impacts of sinusoidally-modulating the profile of a millimeter-wave ridged horn antenna operating from 36–90 GHz are studied herein. Specific parameters of the geometric modification and their effects on the far-field and impedance performance of the antenna are shown. Simulated results indicate that the proposed modulation can improve the beam efficiency and radiation patterns of the horn above 85 GHz while also extending the maximum usable frequency up to 95 GHz.

articleTitle: A Simple and High-Efficiency Dual-Band Element for Active Reflectarray Designs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A highly efficient dual-band radiating element design is presented for reconfigurable reflectarray (RRA) applications. Namely, a properly designed planar inverted F antenna (PIFA) is thoroughly designed for operation at the 20/30 GHz band communications satellite links. Notably, our linearly polarized element exhibits high polarization purity that is in the order of -20 dB, and very low transmission losses in the order of 0.15 dB. This element is the first step towards realizing dual-band RRAs that are simple, low-cost, and efficient. Such RRAs are urgently needed in MIMO, 5G/6G, wireless links, and satellite communications systems.

articleTitle: Analysis of Microstrip Antennas Considering Conductivity of Lossy Metal with IBC-MoM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: To analyze a microstrip antenna consisting of a dielectric substrate and lossy metal, we propose a method of moments to consider the zero-thickness impedance boundary condition. The proposed scheme simulates a case where the metal of the microstrip antenna is a perfect electric or imperfect conductor like AgHT-8 metal. The accuracy of the proposed method is verified by comparing simulation results such as directivity, gain, efficiency, and s-parameter with those of the commercial software FEKO and HFSS.

articleTitle: A MIMO Monopole Antenna for Harsh Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a Multi-Input Multi-Output (MIMO) antenna of 4 monopole elements is presented on Zirconia Ribbon Ceramic (ZRC) substrate. Utilization of this substrate material allows an implementation of an antenna system that is able to withstand harsh environments and high temperatures due to inherent substrate characteristics. The proposed MIMO design supports an operational antenna bandwidth from 2.44 GHz to 2.55 GHz with a center frequency around 2.5 GHz covered by all 4 antenna elements. High antenna isolation below -15 dB is obtained among the ports. The antenna also provides a peak gain over 3 dB through the entire band of interest (3.34 dB at 2.5 GHz) and low cross-polarization.

articleTitle: A Broadband Co-Linearly Polarized Full-Duplex Antenna-in-Package (AiP) for Integrated Sensing and Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel 24 GHz ISM-band broadband co-linearly polarized full-duplex microstrip antenna-in-package (AiP) with high isolation and wide isolation bandwidth is proposed for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) in this paper. Two <tex>$\mathbf{1}\times \mathbf{2}$</tex> microstrip patch antenna arrays are used as Tx and Rx antennas, respectively. The direction of the feeding ports is orthogonal to that of the elements to improve the Tx/Rx isolation. In addition, parasitic patches are introduced to enlarge the impedance bandwidth of the proposed AiP. To further suppress surface waves and space waves between array elements, two decoupling loops with different optimized lengths are employed to enhance Tx/Rx isolation and widen isolation bandwidth. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed AiP possesses the merits of wide impedance bandwidth (up to 10% from 22.5 to 24.9 GHz), high Tx/Rx isolation (up to 52 dB), and wide isolation bandwidth (greater than 40 dB across 22.9-24.87 GHz). The measured data show good agreement with simulated results, further proving the feasibility of this design methodology.

articleTitle: Calculating Power Wave S-Parameters Using Only Port Voltages or Currents
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A method is presented for calculating the power wave S-parameters of a multiport network using only the voltages or currents evaluated at the port terminals with one port driven by a Thévenin or Norton equivalent circuit with its impedance matched to its respective reference impedance and the other port(s) loaded with their respective reference impedances. The calculations can be performed using general mathematical analysis software; specialized RF software is not required.

articleTitle: Modeling and Design of a Folded Transmitarray Antenna on Quartz for Radiometric Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an effective modeling strategy applied to the design of a folded transmitarray (TA) antenna at 183 GHz. The structure at hand is amenable for fabrication by photolithography on low-loss quartz substrates. The proposed method, based on ray-tracing, provides a good agreement with full-wave simulations for the folded TA. A peak gain of 28.2 dBi and 52% aperture efficiency is achieved for a folded F/D of 0.33, which translates into a total TA thickness of 6 mm.

articleTitle: Portable Electromagnetic Multi-Band Resonator for Instantaneous SARS-CoV-2 Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a highly sensitive portable multiband resonator is employed as a sensor to instantaneously detect the presence of the SARS-CoV-2 virus. At its core, the sensor leverages the interaction between the resonating electromagnetic waves and the sample under test and extract the resulting changes in the corresponding scattering parameters. Once these changes are recorded, machine learning data analytics algorithms are applied to correlate these changes with the presence or absence of the virus in the sample. The proposed sensor is fabricated and validated in pre-clinical and clinical settings. Pre-clinical measurements on SARS-CoV-2 heat-inactivated viral phosphate-buffered saline (PBS)-based samples with distinct viral concentrations demonstrated an enhanced sensitivity towards change in the SARS-CoV-2 viral concentration with a 1.92% mean absolute relative error of prediction. Clinical measurements on nasopharyngeal (NP) swabs diluted in PBS samples reported a high accuracy of 94%, a sensitivity of 95%, and a specificity of 97.5%. These results are highly promising and they manifest the potential of the proposed sensor to substitute current test kits and fit point-of-care settings for instantaneous SARS-CoV-2 viral detection.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Analysis Using the Temporal and Spatial Interpolated Subgridding Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) analysis of electromagnetic (EM) scattering and radiation problems included locally fine structures or electrically small objects requires more finer cell sizes. This will increase the total number of cells and therefore the resulting computational time and memory. Therefore, a subgridding algorithm provides accurate solutions without the need for large amounts of computation resources. Numerical results show that the subgridding algorithm provides accurate solutions for the 3D EM problems having locally fine structures and significantly reduces the computation resources.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Atmospheric Gradient Derived from GNSS and NWM for Tropical Stations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Over the years, GNSS has been an emerging technology in the field of meteorology as it provides better spatio temporal resolution over other conventional methods. At present, the numerical weather models (NWMs) are excessively used for weather prediction as it provides estimates of atmospheric parameters at regular interval along latitude and longitude across the globe. Numerical models become highly beneficial for the requirement of dense network for weather analysis specially over sea surfaces where the GNSS station is not always available. This paper provides a comparative analysis between the atmospheric gradient derived from two methods in order to describe the uniformity in the estimates so that both techniques can alternatively implemented in meteorological application without significant reduction in accuracy. Despite an overestimation of GPS derived atmospheric gradient in comparison to NWM estimation, both the gradient vectors predominantly remain oriented in the same direction which increases the reliability of both the methods for weather applications.

articleTitle: Materials Design for Charge-Programmed Additive Manufacturing of Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Antennas fabricated with traditional manufacturing methods typically carry redundant weight and are limited in 3D architecture complexity. Current additive manufacturing (AM) methods also lacks the capability to construct antennas with multiple materials. The charge-programmed multi-material AM process demonstrated in this work allows the design and manufacturing of antennas with previously unattainable mechanical properties. In this paper, we discuss the principles behind the multi-material printing and the versatility of the selective metal deposition process. We also introduce the material designs that enables the variation of material property, which makes it possible to print both stiff and flexible antennas.

articleTitle: LTCC On-Ground Chip Antenna for 3.6 GHz IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an electrically small low-profile chip antenna. The size of the antenna is 0.12 <tex>$\times 0.06\times 0.03\lambda_{0}^{3}$</tex>, and the antenna can be installed on a ground plane without a dedicated clearance area. The antenna operates at 3.6 GHz for IoT applications and is designed to be installed in size-limited devices. The antenna has been fabricated with LTCC technology and experimental results are also presented in good agreement with the simulated ones. Results show 1% impedance bandwidth and a total efficiency of −5.1 dB when the antenna is installed in an infinite ground plane.

articleTitle: Gain Optimization of Sparse Antenna Array Configurations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present an optimization technique for a 25-element array <tex>$(5\ \times 5)$</tex> of microstrip patch antennas using the concept of the sparse antenna array. This method reduces the size, cost, and power requirements of planar arrays by thinning elements that have minimal impacts on the effective area. Throughout the optimization process, we removed 16 elements randomly and kept 9 elements active (64% removed). Different configurations were analyzed in full-wave simulation to find the optimal gain. The best thinning configuration shows losses of only 1.66 dB at the broadside compared to a fully populated 5 <tex>$\times 5$</tex> array. This technique will significantly reduce the amount of space, weight, power, and cost needed for current telecommunications, radar, and satellite systems (5G).

articleTitle: A 33–101 GHz Ultra-Wideband Tightly Coupled Monopole Array (TCMA)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A new ultra-wideband tightly coupled monopole array (TCMA) is introduced. Namely, the unit-cell of our TCMA consists of a modified monopole element, which is capacitively coupled to two grounded vias. Notably, both the common-mode and loop-mode resonances are pushed out of the operating frequency band of our array, while the well-known broadside null found in the radiation pattern of traditional monopole antennas is entirely eliminated. In addition, to improve the scanning bandwidth of our array, a dielectric superstrate is accordingly utilized. The proposed antenna array is extremely low profile with a maximum thickness of <tex>$0.4\lambda_{H}$</tex>. Infinite array simulations of our antenna array demonstrate a bandwidth of 3:1 (33 GHz to 101 GHz) with VSWR<3 for a maximum scan-angle of ± 45° for all principal E-, H- and D-planes.

articleTitle: 60 GHz Perforated Dielectric Resonator Antenna Fed By Substrate Integrated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design and study of a high gain and wideband perforated dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) fed by a low loss substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) feeding technology at the frequency range of 54–65 GHz. The applied perforated technique improves the bandwidth and the excitation of a higher order mode enhances the antenna gain. The designed antenna shows a peak gain of 8.6 dBi and 18.5% impedance bandwidth. Therefore, it is capable of covering multiple standards as well as have a single element high gain. The proposed DRA can be a good candidate for short-range wireless communications at millimeter wave bands.

articleTitle: Bowtie Antenna with Integrated Matching Network for Wideband and Circular Polarization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: An improved bowtie antenna is designed by integrating a wideband matching network into the antenna. Simulated and measured results are presented. An important observation on polarization measurements is made that will lead to more accurate measurements in future work.

articleTitle: Design, Optimization and Fabrication of a X-Band Septum Polarizer for Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design steps, numerical optimization and fabricated of a 4-stepped septum polarizer. The structure of the septum polarizer consists of a square waveguide, a segment of several steps called the septum, and two rectangular waveguides. The simulated result shows that the proposed structure accomplished return losses of lower than -18 dB, forward transmission characteristics between -3 dB and -3.2 dB, isolation characteristics between -25 dB and -37 dB and the phase difference between two modes is between 89°-90.5° at the target frequency ranging from 7.25 to 8.4 GHz. Based on the obtained results, X-band prototype was manufactured, and its performances were measured. The measurements of the prototype are in good agreement with simulations. The designed and manufactured septum polarizer was used in the feed of the satellite antenna.

articleTitle: EBG Cell Size Reduction by Elongating Surface Current Path
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Electromagnetic band gap (EBG) cells are integrated among several applications due to their ability to suppress waves at a certain bandwidth. Moreover, some waveguides incorporate them in their structure, such as gap waveguide, which is suitable for millimeter-wave frequency applications due to its relatively low-loss, compactness, and simple fabrication. Here, a new EBG cell is presented to miniaturize the size to make it suitable for low-frequency applications. A spiral strip unit cell is introduced to shift the stop-band center frequency to half that of a conventional patch cell of the same cell size and parameters. Scaling the spiral to shift the stop-band lower frequency to that of the square patch offers 30% size reduction. However, the stop bandwidth is reduced.

articleTitle: Investigating Adverse Low-frequency Effects of Log-periodic Dipole Antenna Resonant Radiation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Log-periodic dipole antennas provide a series of regular resonances logarithmically spaced over the operating frequency band, but these are disturbed by mutual coupling in closely spaced arrays. We examine how such resonant features on the low-frequency range of a certain log-periodic design, the SKALA4.1, depend on the antenna reflection coefficient. We also propose a way of shifting the electric field peak frequency of these resonances and reversing the reflection coefficient by loading some of the antenna dipoles. The analysis is focused on one antenna, while mutual coupling of two antennas could potentially benefit from controlling such characteristics.

articleTitle: Mutual Coupling Reduction via Concentric SRR Wall for MIMO Antenna Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, a multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna array with a mutual coupling reduction is suggested using meta-surface (concentric SRR wall). The proposed MIMO array is consisting of 2*2 conventional 2.4 GHz rectangular patches. The concentric SRR wall structure is utilized and integrated into the middle of the spaces between every two patches. The proposed arrays are simulated utilizing the CST studio simulator. The output performance parameters show the impact of using one, and two concentric SRR lines wall. Using the proposed design minimizes the mutual coupling.

articleTitle: A Provably Stable SBP-SAT FDTD Subgridding Method without Modifying Yee's Grids
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A stable finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) sub-grid ding method using the summation-by-parts simultaneous approximation term (SBP-SAT) technique is proposed. To meet the SBP properties and keep Yee's grids unchanged, the projection operators are carefully designed to extrapolate fields on the boundaries. Then, the SATs are used to weakly enforce the boundary conditions between multiple mesh blocks with different mesh sizes. Therefore, its long-term stability is theoretically guaranteed. An iris filter is simulated to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Results show that the proposed SBP-SAT FDTD subgridding method is stable, accurate and efficient.

articleTitle: High Gain Antenna for SatCom Applications in Hybrid CNC-PCB Technologies at K/Ka Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This communication presents a high gain antenna covering the full frequency band from 17 to 31 GHz, suitable for satellite communications (SatCom) at K/Ka band. The radiating aperture is designed as a continuous transverse stub (CTS) array fed by a tapered corporate feed network (CFN) to reduce the sidelobe level (SLL) in the radiating plane orthogonal to the stubs/long slots. This part is done in printed circuit board technology (PCB) to ensure a very low profile (namely 11.5 mm, or equivalently <tex>$\mathbf{1.2}\ \boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\mathbf{0}}$</tex>, where <tex>$\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\mathbf{0}}$</tex> is the free space wavelength at 31 GHz). Moreover, a pillbox coupler is used as a line source to illuminate the CFN. It consists of an integrated parabolic reflector illuminated by a displaceable H-plane horn in its focal plane. The pillbox coupler is realized in aluminum to reduce losses and fabricated by using computer numerically controlled (CNC) fabrication techniques. The total size of the antenna is <tex>$\mathbf{44.5}\times \mathbf{33.1}\times \mathbf{3.3}\ \boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\mathbf{0}}^{\mathbf{3}}$</tex>. The latter exhibits a minimum measured directivity of 34.6 dBi at 17 GHz. The antenna is able to steer its main beam along the slot plane to cover a field of view exceeding 45° in elevation by displacing the H-plane horn in the focal plane.

articleTitle: Creeping Wave on Body for VR Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Creeping wave on the body surface is critical to the cross-body communication when the Line-of-sight (LoS) path of the two antennas are blocked by the human body. This work focuses on the creeping wave in virtual reality (VR) on-body link. Link loss between head-mount display (HMD) and controller is tested for four antenna locations on head at 8 GHz with full body phantom. Moreover, four simplified phantom block shapes with two PIFA antenna are simulated at 2.4GHz to understand the impact from different bends.

articleTitle: Application of Autofocus Algorithm in Millimeter-Wave Narrowband Holographic 3D Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A single-frequency millimeter-wave imaging system can only acquire two-dimensional information of the target. Moreover, during the imaging process, the position of the reference plane needs to be adjusted in real time according to the distance from the target to the scanning array to maintain high-quality focusing effect. Therefore, in this paper, a single-frequency millimeter wave imaging autofocus algorithm is proposed by using the amplitude value of the inversion image as the basis for evaluating the image focus. The method can realize automatic focusing of narrow-band holographic imaging, and at the same time, for distributed targets in practical application scenarios, the method of multi-focus image fusion of slices is used to realize all-focus inversion imaging of multiple targets. Finally, simulation experiments verify the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Radio Frequency Directed Energy Weapon Mitigation via Passive Beamforming Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) are an emerging transmission technology to aid wireless communication. However, the potential of using RIS to mitigate directed energy weapons (DEW) is not widely recognized. In this paper, we propose to leverage RIS (based on spiral antenna elements) to aid the mitigation of high-energy radio-frequency (RF) sources applied to a DEW. For example, integrating a broadband circularly-polarized antenna system with RIS technology can successfully mitigate DEW attacks across a wide range of frequencies regardless of how the radio waves are polarized. We simulated a spiral antenna that operates within a frequency band of 1.3 GHz to 7 GHz with a 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) covering from 2 GHz to 7 GHz. Full-wave simulation results show the potential promising application of RIS for the mitigation of DEW attacks.

articleTitle: Intelligent Phase Mapping Approach via Neural Networks on Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: An Intelligent Phase Mapping Approach via Neural Networks (PM-NN) on metasurfaces is proposed in this paper, which is characterized by the performances of stable feasibility in different sizes and broadband. The technology of multi-layer perceptron (MLP) is introduced to address the limitation of traditional empirical formulas in nonlinearity representation. Experiments verify the validity of PM-NN. For future works, more discussions of the proposed PM0NN will be applied to further complex metasurfaces.

articleTitle: Transparent Uniplanar Circular Polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes the design of a compact circular polarized (CP) antenna constructed from transparent metal mesh. A good impedance matching and CP radiation bandwidth is achieved at Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) L1 band (1575.42MHz~1609.31MHz) without the need of matching circuit. The simplicity of its uniplanar structure and easy to feed makes it a good candidate for the future head-worn devices for outdoor navigation.

articleTitle: Vanadium Dioxide Aperture-Coupled mmWave 1–bit Reconfigurable Dual Polarization Reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A vanadium dioxide aperture-coupled patch 1-bit reconfigurable reflectarray was designed for operation in the n260 5G Band (37–40 GHz). The reflectarray can be used with a dual linearly polarized feed. The unit cell was simulated with a periodic boundary condition. The maximum reflection loss in the unit cell is less than 2 dB for both polarizations. The phase difference is 180° between the bits at the center frequency. Fabrication progress and finite array simulations will be presented at the conference.

articleTitle: Examination of Reduced Complexity of Multi-level Fast Iterative Physical Optics for Simple Target
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The iterative physical optics can be accelerated using the fast far field approximation for the analysis of the scattering by a perfectly electrical conducting and impedance objects. The computational complexity of multiplications of fast IPO is compared with conventional IPO according to the number of meshes.

articleTitle: Dual-Band 3D Multiferroic Antenna Stack for Passive Telemetry Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Multiferroic antennas can operate at lower frequencies with smaller dimensions as they scale with the acoustic resonance wavelength of the transducer. This has specific advantages such as antenna miniaturization and operation at lower frequencies. In this paper, we investigate multiferroic antennas for dual-band operation to enable passive backscattering telemetry-based antennas and sensors. Fabrication and testing results demonstrate the dual-band operation. A 3D antenna stack concept is described to combine the antenna pair into as integrated multiband antenna.

articleTitle: Design of Pixelated Metasurface Using Genetic Algorithm with HFSS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A pixelated metasurface was designed to match the response of an already simulated metasurface unit cell. The reflection coefficient response was matched over a broad bandwidth from 10 GHz to 20 GHz. Using a binary GA, an RMSE of 0.12 was achieved which was greatly reduced from the initial RMSE of 0.444 of a random seeding point. Matlab was used to interface with HFSS and automate the iterative design process. This allowed for hundreds of simulations to be run so that the GA could explore a wide solution space.

articleTitle: Exploring Generalized PT-Symmetry for Efficient Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A wireless power transfer (WPT) system of dynamically high and stable power transfer efficiency is proposed based on generalized parity-time (GPT) symmetry. By introducing a saturable gain, <tex>$\mathrm{g}_{\text{sat}}$</tex>, GPT-symmetry can be reconstructed in non-Hermitian systems dominated by intrinsically unbalanced coupling. The parity of the system can be analyzed by a topology decomposition approach. In the coupling parametric space, a global GPT-symmetric eigenstate is observed, and the spontaneous phase transition of the local GPT-symmetric eigenstates is identified on the exceptional contour. A band theory interpretation is proposed to analyze the efficiency-compromised states. Our study shows that the global GPT symmetric state corresponds to an efficient and stable power transfer across the distinct coupling regions, which provides insight into practical WPT systems involving asymmetric coupling.

articleTitle: Theoretical Model of Dielectric Materials for Forensic Science in terms of Frequency
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The dielectric properties of materials provide important information on electromagnetic propagation and dispersion. This led to substantial research on the parametric modelling of dielectric properties of materials. In this paper, such modelling of materials is studied for frequencies up to 100GHz. The new model describes the variation of dielectric properties of material as a function of time, frequency, moisture, and age. Forensic science plays a crucial role in the judicial system, as it helps to make right decisions based on the scientific examination of evidence. Each piece of evidence is properly packed and analyzed using specific methods depending on the type of evidence. Some methods of analysis are destructive, while others are not. The examination and analysis of samples such as saliva, blood, ink, alcohol, water, using the correct technique is so important in forensic science. This study aims to compare theoretical and experimental analyses of indicated samples and the results are compared with the existing literature.

articleTitle: An Ultracompact Omnidirectional Circularly Polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: An ultracompact omnidirectional circularly polarized (OCP) antenna is presented in this paper. An innovative antenna configuration has been adopted that consists of a full-wavelength folded helical dipole radiator and a closely placed half-wavelength parasitic helical arm. Compared with the conventional single-arm half-wavelength helical OCP antenna, the current density has been significantly enhanced and thus the radiation resistance of this design has been improved substantially from 10 to 43 Ohms. As a result, a good impedance matching is realized. Moreover, very compact physical size has been maintained, i. e., only being <tex>$\pi(0.044 \lambda_{0})^{2}\times 0.088 \lambda_{0}= 0.0005 \lambda_{0}^{3} (\lambda_{0}$</tex> is the free-space wavelength at the center frequency). A prototype operating at 915 MHz ISM band has been designed. Simulated results demonstrate that the antenna has a good impedance matching around the targeted 915 MHz and achieves an excellent OCP radiation performance, e. g., the out-of-roundness value of the co-pol radiation pattern is less than 0.2 dB. It is an ideal candidate for IoT applications that requires very compact OCP antenna system.

articleTitle: Antenna for Millimeter Wave High Gain Arrays using LTCC Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work presents a low-profile antenna element for millimeter wave high gain arrays. The proposed structure utilizes Low Temperature Cofired Ceramic (LTCC) technology to create a vertical stack of open-ended radiating stubs for gain enhancement. The proposed antenna element operates at 30 GHz with 15% impedance matching bandwidth and peak gain of 7 dB. In addition, a high gain hexagonal array of volume 4.5 ×4.5 ×0. 126 <tex>$\lambda_{0}^{3}$</tex> was developed; it exhibits a peak gain of 20 dB and 3dB beam steering range of ±55°.

articleTitle: Wideband THz Yagi-Uda Bond Wire Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We model, design and compare the characteristics of Yagi-Uda quasi-half loop bond wire antennas (QHL-BWAs) on low-loss and lossy substrates at THz frequencies. Our results reveal that lossy substrates can be used for the development of these antennas, even in the 0.3 THz band, without severe degradation of the antenna performance. A Yagi-Uda QHL-BWA is fabricated and measured in the 0.3 THz band. Good correction is obtained between measurement and simulation results.

articleTitle: Higher-Order Array Decomposition Method for Array Antennas with Connected Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The Higher-Order Array Decomposition Method (HO-ADM) is extended to handle regular array antennas with interconnected elements. The Discontinuous Galerkin Method (DGM) is used to retain the multi-level block-Toeplitz Method of Moments (MoM) matrix structure, even for connected elements. The presented method yields more than an order of magnitude reduced solution time for a <tex>$8\times 8$</tex> real-world antenna array and similar memory consumption compared to existing fast methods.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Wire-Mesh Antenna Arrays for 3D-Printed Flexible Radars
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a 3D-printed millimeter-wave microstrip patch antenna array with wire-mesh structures is reported. The antenna array is realized by silver nanoparticle inks on a 3-mil LCP substrate. The performances of the antenna array are verified by both simulations and experimental characterizations. The proposed wire-mesh structure can increase the array radiation efficiency by at least 31% and enhance the realized gain by at least 1dBi. Measured reflection coefficients and radiation patterns on both E- and H-planes match with the simulations. The proposed antenna array shows great potential for applications such as 3D-printed flexible radar systems and flexible wireless mmWave communication systems.

articleTitle: An Improved Physical Optics Technique for Multiple Shielding Electromagnetic Scattering Problems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The traditional physical optics (PO) method is faced with the difficulty of dividing light regions and dark regions for the electrically large scattering problem. To compensate for these shortcomings, an improved PO method is presented in this paper, including multiple shielding or oblique incidence at different angles. Compared with the traditional PO method, this paper provides an important technology on multiple shielding or oblique incidence by three-layer nesting steps. Combining with coarse mesh, refined mesh, and some key projection techniques, this method can effectively deal with the object occlusion. Especially for the complex physical model, the radar cross section can be quickly and accurately solved. As a result, it's helpful to simulate and design different electromagnetic problems.

articleTitle: Non-Invasive Target Detection Enhanced Through a Low-Frequency Passive Metasurface for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an innovative biomedical system for magnetically-contrasted malignant inclusions detection, exploiting a low-frequency and passive metasurface, is presented. In particular, the proposed system, operating around 3 MHz, is composed by a passive metasurface inductively coupled to an external probe loop. The 5×5 metasurface, whose unit-cells consist in a 10-turn planar resonant spiral coil, globally covers a 21 cm × 21 cm area. The inclusion detection and localization are achieved by observing an external probe loop input impedance variations, enhanced by the interposed passive metasurface. By scanning through the probe loop the passive metasurface, placed 2 mm below the investigated tissue, a detection over the entire Field of View can be carried out. To validate the theorical approach, we performed preliminary full-wave simulations, obtaining promising results and demonstrating the possibility to detect and localize a 5 mm radius magnetic inclusion inside the investigated tissue, although the extremely low frequency adopted. Beside the good sensitivity, one of the most important advantages of the system is also the use of non-ionizing radiation, allowing to reduce the invasiveness for the patients. For this reason, the proposed solution can be considered as a non-invasive, low-frequency and contactless near-field biomedical system, encouraging future works.

articleTitle: Experimental Monitoring of Microwave-Induced Thermoacoustic Signals Generated During Pulsed Microwave Ablation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We experimentally investigate the evolution of microwave-induced thermoacoustic signals generated during pulsed microwave ablation in bovine liver tissue. Using an X-band interstitial ablation antenna and a microsecond pulsed microwave source operating at ~9.4 GHz with an average power of 5 - 10 W, we simultaneously heat tissue and generate thermoacoustic signals. We conduct ablation experiments in both fresh liver tissue as well as boiled liver tissue to decouple the impact of temperature and tissue coagulation on thermoacoustic signal characteristics. We find that the time of arrival of the thermoacoustic signals decreases over the course of microwave ablation due to the change in the temperature-dependent speed of sound as well as tissue shrinkage. Thus, the thermoacoustic time of arrival may be used to monitor microwave ablation in real-time.
