articleTitle: Design of a 3D Printed 4-Arm Conical Spiral Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A four-arm conical spiral antenna is designed to operate in Mode 1 over a 2 to 8 GHz instantaneous bandwidth. The antenna has stable unidirectional radiation with high front-to-back ratio, axial ratio <tex>$< 2\mathbf{dB}$</tex> within <tex>$\pm 30^{\circ}$</tex> from the main beam, and radiation efficiency greater than 80%. Modifications to the metal-to-slot ratio are found to provide a simple means to control the impedance match. The final design includes a hollow conical shaped ground plane where receiver electronics can be integrated for a highly compact system.

articleTitle: Worst-Case Electromagnetic Coupling to an Accelerometer using an Equivalent Circuit and Experimental Co-Characterization Methodology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Worst-case coupling estimation to a complex Printed Circuit Board (PCB) system typically requires an expensive computational and/or experimental approach. Therefore, there is a strong need for a deterministic approach that can accurately predict the worst-case coupling with the least computational and experimental cost. This work uses a hybrid equivalent circuit approach coupled with experimental measurements to simplify predicting the worst-case coupling to an accelerometer board. The predictions of the proposed methodology are validated using experimental measurements with excellent agreement.

articleTitle: Efficient Automotive Radar Simulations Using Spherical Modes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We demonstrate faster and efficient simulations of behind-the-bumper installed millimeter wave automotive radars using spherical modes. The spherical mode coefficients are extracted from the standalone radar radiation pattern, and these coefficients are used as equivalent sources as excitation for the bumper. In this way, the simulations can be completed with significantly less computation time (from 8 to 2 hours) and memory (8 GB per processor to 240 MB per processor) compared to the full-wave simulations. In addition, the effects of secondary surface (e.g. bumper) on the performance of installed radar are also characterized by analyzing the spherical mode coefficients.

articleTitle: Benchmarking Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Time-Domain Electromagnetic Simulations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We benchmark physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for time-domain electromagnetic simulations, systematically addressing fundamental questions on their accuracy, stability and computational efficiency. A U-Net is trained to solve the wave equation for the electric field in the time domain, in an unsupervised manner. The performance of the physics-informed U-Net is evaluated by varying its architecture, while monitoring its accuracy and stability. Thus, we propose a counterpart of the familiar and insightful dispersion and stability analysis of conventional numerical techniques (such as FDTD) for PINNs. We demonstrate the significance of this approach for building effective and accurate PINNs for time-domain electromagnetic simulations.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of a GaAs Millimeter-Wave On-Chip Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design of an ultra-thin, inset-feed rectangular patch on-chip antenna in a pHEMT 0.1µm GaAs process. The antenna covers the 60 GHz ISM band, achieving a maximum simulated realized gain and efficiency of 2.29 dBi and 69.68%, respectively, and a -10 dB return loss bandwidth from 59.7 to 61.8 GHz. The antenna has a small and thin footprint of 1.5×1.5×0.07 mm<sup>3</sup>, which makes it suitable for 5G, Internet-of-Things, and millimeter-wave communication systems.

articleTitle: ADS-B Performance Parameter Variation Along Trajectory
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This manuscript presents an evaluation of performance of Automatic Dependent Surveillance - Broadcast (ADS-B), which transmits an aircraft position from transponders installed on the aircraft. The position datum is basically calculated by the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receiver. We investigated the performance parameters of ADS-B with respect to the aircraft's position to assess whether they are acceptable for safe operation. In this manuscript, we focus on the variation in values and present the trajectories with the performance parameters of the aircraft's position.

articleTitle: Adaptive Quadrature for the Chebyshev-Based Boundary Integral Equation Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The recently presented Chebyshev-based Nyström method enables efficient, high-order discretization and solution of boundary integral equation problems. The approach handles far-interactions using the Nyström method by leveraging a high-order quadrature rule and treats the self-singular and near-singular interactions by expanding the unknown densities in terms of Chebyshev polynomials and precomputing the interactions of the integral operators against the Chebyshev-basis to high accuracy. This work presents an adaptive quadrature scheme which enables evaluating these precomputation integrals to a prescribed accuracy threshold. The approach is able to achieve the same accuracy as the prior static refined-integration-grid based method while being up to a factor of 6.6X faster for certain challenging geometries. An example is presented which highlights the advantages of the adaptive approach using the Magnetic Field Integral Equation (MFIE) to model a NURBS-based hummingbird CAD model.

articleTitle: A Flexible Chipless RFID Sensor for Humidity Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel flexible chipless radio-frequency-identification (RFID) sensor is proposed to monitor the change of relative humidity (RH) in environments. The monitoring is realized by coating a humidity-sensitive polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) film on the surface of the resonant structure of the RFID tag and measuring the change on the relative permittivity of the material caused by the change of RH. The change of relative permittivity can produce the shift of resonant frequency of the tag, which can be recorded by the RFID reader. Simulation results show that the maximum humidity sensitivity of the tag with a coating of film is about 2.03 MHz/RH. Also, the tag has been extensively tested for bending and it performs very well, showing its good flexibility.

articleTitle: An Ultra Low Cost Orthogonal Pattern Diversity Antenna Module for Compact mmWave 5G Mobile Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A wideband microstrip-fed end-fire antenna is proposed in this paper. The antenna is designed on the low-cost commercially viable FR4 substrate. The proposed antenna is electrically compact with dimensions, 2.1λ × 0.466 λ × 0.14 λ, the free space wavelength is calculated at 28GHz. The input impedance bandwidth is 46% with reasonably high pattern integrity across the operational bandwidth. A panel mountable two port pattern diversity system with low mutual coupling is also presented.

articleTitle: A Single Receiver Direction of Arrival Estimation using Optimized Meta-surface Reflector
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Direction of arrival (DoA) estimation using a meta-surface (MS) reflector with an optimized arrangement of MS elements is proposed and its performance is theoretically proved. The system is capable of estimating DoA by a single receiving antenna which is a half-wavelength dipole antenna. By optimizing the arrangement of MS elements, the estimation accuracy of DoA is improved compared to a non-optimized MS reflector antenna. In addition, the system has almost the same estimation accuracy as the DoA estimation system using a 3-element linear array antenna.

articleTitle: Ray Tracing Prediction for 5G Propagation Characteristics in a Modern Office Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper reports broadband simulations and measurements results to gain a thorough insight into mm-waves link budget within a typical modern office channel. The analysis is based on comparing the Directional-Omnidirectional (Direct-Omni) antenna with the Omnidirectional-Omnidirectional (Omni-Omni) antenna and finds that the Direct-Omni has a reliable link budget because it can reduce the path loss by more than 20dB and compress the rms delay to 7.6 nanoseconds. The experimental data offer an efficient means to identify physical features related to propagation phenomena within indoor building offices.

articleTitle: Emerging Interface Effects in Flat Optics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we discuss how the manipulation and control of surface-wave propagation can be achieved in natural low-dimensional materials or metasurfaces through the engineering of planar discontinuities in the surface impedance. We present two specific examples, “ghost line waves” and “flat leaky waves”, that offer new possibilities for controlling light at the nanoscale and may have potential applications in areas such as integrated waveguides, nonlinear optics, optical sensing, and sub-diffraction imaging.

articleTitle: Compact High-Index Resonator Supercavity System with a Complementary Backplane Feed Element
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We study the excitation of extended supercavity (SC) modes in a microwave microstrip-high-index resonator (m-HIR) system. The extended set of SC points in the spectral response of the m-HIR system is achieved after adding a complementary feed element to the backplane that generates a scaled negative image of the original feed current. The optimal design of the complementary feed element for operation at the extended SC regimes enables a desired high-Q resonance while cutting the required volume of the high-index resonator in half.

articleTitle: Measurement of the Complex Permittivity of Dry, Humidified and CO2 -Loaded Zeolite 13X at RF Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper describes a procedure to measure the permittivity of Zeolite 13X at RF frequencies under fresh, humidified and CO2 loadings. We present results of measurements performed at room temperature and describe our technique to interpolate and extrapolate the measurement to other frequencies.

articleTitle: A D-band Low-cost High-gain Phased Antenna Array for 6G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Severe path-loss and small wavelength makes the D-band (110–170 GHz) antenna design, fabrication, integration and measurement challenging. This paper presents a novel antenna design using a single-layer printed circuit board (PCB) process. By optimizing unequal antenna row spacing, row-to-row shift and different unit-cell parameters, the proposed patch antenna array is capable of 45-degree slant polarization. The designed impedance/length matching components can support both wire-bonding and flip-chip antenna integration techniques, which are compatible with different chip pitch dimensions. The boresight realized gain of a 32-channel array is 26.7 dBi at 140 GHz with a 3-dB realized gain bandwidth from 136.5 to 146.4 GHz. The simulated scanning range is <tex>$\pm 45^{\circ}$</tex>. Therefore, the proposed antenna array maintains high gain, wide gain bandwidth and moderate beam steering angle with low-cost, low-complexity and easy fabrication.

articleTitle: The Design of Realizable Cylindrical Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Cylindrical metasurfaces are often represented by idealized and homogenized impedance/admittance boundary conditions. However, realizing them with practical metallic patterns has posed challenges. In this paper, we propose a rigorous approach for designing cylindrical metasurfaces that are realizable. A multimodal wave matrix formulation, which accurately describes intercell coupling and accounts for spatial dispersion, is reported. Additionally, a cylindrical extraction technique is adopted to account for the curvature of metasurfaces. As a proof of concept, a practical, coaxially-fed azimuthal mode converter is presented and verified using a commercial full-wave electromagnetic solver.

articleTitle: A Diplexer-Based Dual-Slot LTE Antenna Design for Laptops with Metal Housing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Due to the compact form factor and widely used metal enclosures in state-of-the-art laptops, the design of LTE antennas, which require several broad operation bands, is rather challenging. In this paper, a dual-slot antenna, which is aimed to be placed on the corner of the laptop base, is proposed. In order to cover low and high LTE bands with a common feed, a diplexer integrated with matching networks is employed. The slots are placed at the joints between the metal base and the rim. The T-shaped slot comprises two shorted ends and an opening on the rim to provide two resonant modes. To meet the LTE operation needs, the two modes can be joined to form a broader matching band. Simulations and measurements are executed to demonstrate that the proposed design can suffice the WWAN antenna need on laptop platforms.

articleTitle: On Vehicular Model Reduction for Antenna Simulation Using Spherical Wave Expansion
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The performance of a vehicular antenna is greatly affected by the vehicle body. Thus, it is imperative to simulate the automotive antenna in its installed state. The large electrical size of the vehicle often necessitates a high requirement on computer resources and a long simulation time. In this regard, a mathematically robust method for vehicular simulation model reduction using the Spherical Wave Expansion (SWE) theory is proposed in this paper. The applicability of the method has been demonstrated with an example consisting of a Hertzian dipole antenna integrated to the side mirror of a car.

articleTitle: Shaping the Scattering Pattern of a Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface Through the Manipulation of Composite Vortices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this contribution, we provide new insights into the possibility offered by the composite vortex theory to manipulate the scattering pattern of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RISs). In particular, by dividing the RIS into two concentric circular regions imparting a different helical profile to the incident field, the ability to control the number and position of the phase singularity points of the overall composite vortex is exploited to customize the response of the RIS and achieve peculiar shapes of the scattering pattern (e.g. a saddle- or a sectorshaped pattern).

articleTitle: Power Distributed Network for THz Image System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents three power distributed networks (PDNs) for a terahertz (THz) imaging system. In this work, an advanced 10-layer printed circuit board technology is used to design equal amplitude and in-phase 1-to-4, 1-to-16, 1-to-64 power distributed network at D band. The simulated results of the 1-to-64 PDN achieved a −10-dB fractional bandwidth (FBW) >20% from 130–170 GHz, an insertion loss of 5.32 dB (150 GHz), an amplitude imbalance of 0.68 dB (150 GHz), and a phase imbalance of 7.73° (150 GHz). Some preliminary experimental results on the 1-to-4 PDN are presented for validation purpose.

articleTitle: Recent Advancements on System-by-Design Strategies for the Synthesis of Complex Radiating Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Due to the growing need for advanced electromagnetic (EM) devices in numerous modern applications such as automotive radar systems, the complexity of the radiating systems has risen in recent years. In this context, the System-by- Design (SbD) paradigm has proven to be a reliable framework to efficiently deal with the arising computational complexity to synthesize high-performance EM devices. The SbD approach relies on the smart interconnection of multiple functional blocks, each one aimed at solving a single subtask. Through the proper selection of a single-objective (SO) or multi-objective (MO) optimization the SbD allows to obtain different trade-off solutions among the optimization targets. The effectiveness of the SbD paradigm is shown with an illustrative example concerning the design of perturbed traveling-wave open stub (PTOS) antenna for mm-wave automotive radars.

articleTitle: Uncertainty Analysis on Wall and Radar's Characteristics in Through-the-Wall Context
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Through-the-wall radar imaging (TTWRI) detects concealed objects behind barriers using radar. It is a promising research area for civilian and military applications, including rescuing, surveillance, and target identification. This study evaluates the impact of miss-evaluating wall and radar characteristics on TTWRI results.

articleTitle: Phased Array Scan-Widening Meta-Radome with Low Polarization Sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A meta material radome for planar phased arrays is introduced with the capability of widening the corresponding scan range. The planar phased array with this meta-radome becomes well-matched while scanning in the H-plane up to 65 degrees and a wide range of diagonal planes up to 80 degrees. This is because of the proposed meta-radome structure which shows less sensitivity to the polarization of antenna-radiated fields. This meta-radome can widely decrease scan mismatch loss over most of the scanning planes of the phased array.

articleTitle: All-Metal, High-Efficiency and Wide-Scanning Phased Array Antenna with Sparse Architecture for 6G High-Integration RF Front-End
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes an all-metal and periodically-sparse phased array antenna, which operates from 66 GHz to 76 GHz with high-efficiency and wide-scanning performance. The rectangular waveguide is modified with the double-ridge to extend the single <tex>$\mathbf{TE}_{10}$</tex> mode bandwidth at first. The tapered slot antenna acts as the unit cell and is fed by the ridge waveguide. The adjacent unit cells are connected to enhance the electromagnetic-field continuity of the antenna aperture, so that the bandwidth of the antenna element is wider. The 4-element subarray is excited by the low-loss power divider and the Teflon phase shifters. After the design procedure by the invasive weed optimization and the iterative convex optimization algorithms, the optimal array achieves the 75% channel reduction and the wide-scanning range over <tex>$\pm \mathbf{60}^{\circ}$</tex> without the grating lobes. Moreover, compared with the antenna based on the organic materials, the proposed all-metal antenna achieves the remarkable thermal dissipation performance.

articleTitle: Recent Progress in Reduced Order Models for Electromagnetic Particle-in-Cell Kinetic Plasma Simulations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We discuss recent progress on several model order reduction techniques for electromagnetic particle-in-cell (EM- PIC) simulations of kinetic plasmas: Proper Orthogonal De-composition (POD), Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD), and Koopman autoencoder (KAE). In the past, these techniques have been employed as powerful tools for data-driven modeling of nonlinear complex systems in general. For EMPIC kinetic plasma simulations, we show that they can reduce the number of degrees of freedom by projecting the solution space into a smaller space constituted of representative spatiotemporal modes. The trade- off between accuracy and cost can be controlled, in a tunable fashion, by adjusting the number of retained modes in the reduced model. POD, DMD, and KAE reduced order models are highly desirable to enable kinetic plasma simulations at a much reduced cost and hence more efficient parameter space sweeps during optimization loops for device design. These reduced order models are also useful as diagnosis tools for better understanding of the underlying plasma dynamics through the extraction of dominant features of the solution in a hierarchical fashion.

articleTitle: AMC-Backed Wearable Monopole Antenna for Sub-6 GHz 5G and WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel Artificial Magnetic Conductor (AMC) backed, wearable, wide-band monopole antenna has been designed for the sub-6GHz 5G and Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) bands. To meet the requirements of flexibility and user comfort, the monopole and the AMC structure are printed on textile denim substrate and have a dimension of 0.66λ×0.66λ×0.10λ mm<sup>3</sup> (λ calculated at the resonant frequency of 5.2 GHz). Simulation results have shown that the antenna has a −10dB impedance bandwidth of 31 % (4.40 – 6.02 GHz), directional radiation patterns, gain above 5dBi, and efficiency greater than 80% across the entire operating band. Additionally, the performance of the antenna persists throughout the entire operating band despite structural deformation and the lossy effects of being worn on the human body.

articleTitle: Diversifying the Engineering Faculty Hiring Pool
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper discusses the recent results in recruiting a large cohort of new faculty for new positions within the College of Engineering at the University of Arizona. The results obtained are part of a multi-year plan to grow the overall size of the faculty by 25% of its current size. Aligned with the college and university's commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI), faculty search committees were expected to recruit a diverse pool. This paper discusses the process and the outcomes from implementing an active recruiting plan during three hiring cycles between 2019-2022. Of the 32 faculty hired during this period, over 40% represent one or more underrepresented groups in engineering as identified by the US National Science Foundation.

articleTitle: Detecting Solid Sulfur Deposition Using Dual-Band Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work presents a simple microwave-based detection sensor to monitor the deposition of elemental sulfur in natural gas pipelines. Dual-band microstrip antennas are installed within the inner wall of the pipeline to monitor the deposition of the sulfur superstrate. The onset and the depth of the deposition are determined by studying the different resonant behavior of the antenna. The designed sensor is optimized using commercial EM software.

articleTitle: A Switched-Beam Yagi-Uda Antenna Array for Dual Channel mm-Wave Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A Yagi-Uda array is proposed for dual channel mm-Wave communications. The array is comprised of four Yagi-Uda antennas, each with a driven element and a ground plane reflector. The array is reconfigurable and employs a switched-beam architecture to allow two signals to be transmitted and/or received at once. This preliminary design establishes 360° coverage in simulation. When used in conjunction with a software-defined radio (SDR) system it has the potential to double the processing throughput by using two antennas at once.

articleTitle: Compact Adaptive Metamaterial-Loaded Pattern Reconfigurable Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a compact metamaterial-loaded pattern reconfigurable dielectric resonator (DR) antenna for intelligent communication. By loading the meta-surface layer, the DR radiator can reduce the size (lower the profile). To obtain switchable beams, a novel multi-port DR radiator with high-port isolation is explored. Owing to the superposition of the incident field and the scattered field, both the asymmetric field distribution and electric field (E-field) null regions are achieved. When these feeding ports are arranged at the E-field nulls, this multi-port DR radiator not only realizes directional radiation but also exhibits high port isolation. More importantly, by exciting these ports independently or in combination, this antenna can realize flexible multi-beam steering. Here, a three-port metamaterial-loaded DR antenna is developed. The measured −10 dB impedance bandwidth is 3.24-3.82 GHz (16.4 %), and the port isolation is greater than 15 dB. Besides, the proposed design realizes six-beam scanning in the horizontal plane with a 60°-step by switching those three ports.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual-Band, Quad-Element Dipole
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A dual-resonance, quad-dipole antenna design is presented combining two dual-element dipoles, one of which is oriented in the YZ plane, and the other of which is in the XY plane. The antenna demonstrates a −10-dB IBW of 16.4% in the lower band, and 9.9% for the upper band. It demonstrates a peak realized gain in the lower band of 5.8 dBi in the <tex>$+z$</tex> direction, and the upper band of 5.4 dBi in the <tex>$+x$</tex> direction.

articleTitle: Shared Aperture Triangular Antenna Array for Ka-band LEO Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a triangular antenna array design that allows an interlaced receive and transmit antenna array to be placed in the same array aperture on a single plane. This system is designed for Ku and Ka band LEO communication targeting the bandwidth of 18.8 - 20.2 GHz and transmit antennas at 27.5 - 30 GHz. This system is capable of reconfigurable circular polarisation for both RHCP and LHCP at both Rx and Tx bands. The array design can provide beam steering to <tex>$\theta=\pm 40^{\circ}$</tex> with only phase shifting applied. This system provides a very compact design that is easy to integrate with RFIC based feeding networks.

articleTitle: Full Wave Analysis of the Exposure of Implantable Medical Devices to Electromagnetic Fields
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present numerical results on the exposure of Implantable Medical Devices to electromagnetic fields produced by radio communication systems in common usage scenarios. Initially, a theoretical model based on simple formulas provides an order-of-magnitude assessment to identify critical cases that require further analysis. Subsequently, full wave analysis is carried out considering the detailed composition of the body of the patient bearing the Implantable Medical Device (IMD), the source of electromagnetic field, and the characteristics of the IMD.

articleTitle: A Dual-Resonance Frequency Selective Surface Genetically Optimized for Dielectric Characterization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The use of frequency-selective surfaces for the characterization of dielectric materials has been demonstrated. In this simulation study, a surface with dual resonances is optimized for this purpose using a genetic algorithm and a finite-difference time-domain model. The dependence of transmission spectra on various dielectric test materials is also presented.

articleTitle: Peculiar Multipath Channels From THz Horn Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the peculiar multipath channels witnessed upon introducing two perforated metal plates each within the beam spot size of employed horns in a bistatic simulation setup at 300 GHz carrier frequency. The diameters of the circular perforations are 0.1, 0.5, and 5 mm whereas the square perforations are 0.1 mm × 0.1 mm, 0.5 mm × 0.5 mm, and 1 cm × 1 cm in size. The THz simulations are performed in four chosen scenarios, thus exploring this distinctive multipath behavior which can provide valuable information and insights for reliable system design for a wide range of THz applications. Moreover, these ray-tracing simulations help to understand the interactions of THz waves with micrometer-sized tiny objects for THz sensing.

articleTitle: A Comparison of Machine Learning Algorithms for Micro-Doppler Based Drone Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We characterize the performance of a set of machine learning algorithms for classifying simulated micro-Doppler responses of a set of rotorcrafts. Scattered radar signals are generated using a kinematic model of aircraft rotors as a function of signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). The training and test datasets are transformed using the principal components analysis method to extract the most salient features. The classification accuracy is investigated by varying the SNR of the signals to determine the minimum SNR needed to obtain a classification performance. Our results demonstrate that an SNR of at least - 5 dB is sufficient to achieve high classification accuracy based on simulated micro-Doppler signatures.

articleTitle: Attenuation Statistics For Millimetre-Wave Links in Tropical Regions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In tropical countries with high rainfall rates, rainfall and attenuation vary with location. Therefore, accurate estimation of rain fade margin in each location is crucial to predict rain attenuation in designing Millimeter Wave (mmWave) links to achieve an availability of 99.99%. The rainfall prediction method recommended by ITU-R might show inaccuracy in the tropical area, as has been reported by many. In this work, local rainfall statistical data were obtained from the TRMM 3A25 and 3B43 recorded data. The results show that different cities show different rainfall statistics. This leads to differences in the suggested rain fade margin or maximum link lengths for different cities. Results also indicate a potential difficulty of having a mm Wave cell radius of more than 200 meters with 99.99% availability in the tropics.

articleTitle: Novel Wideband Beamformers for AESAs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work describes a RF beamforming phased array architecture enabled by a novel wideband polyphase combiner/divider that generates 36 differential I/Q pairs (144 outputs) over 10-20GHz (66% fractional bandwidth). The polyphase combiner is designed in LTCC technology and fuses together two stacked parallel-plate waveguide (PPWG) radial power combiners with a 5-stage PPWG branch-line hybrid coupler. Through rigorous full-wave simulations, it is shown that multiple wideband 0°, 90°, 180°, and 270° phases are produced with <7° phase imbalance, ±1dB amplitude error, and better than 0.5dB excess insertion loss over most of the design bandwidth.

articleTitle: A Novel Dual-band Metasurface Antenna Unit Cell with Varactor Diodes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel reflectarray metasurface unit cell controlled by varactor diodes. The dual broadband metasurface unit operates under 14 ~ 19 GHz and 25 ~ 30 GHz. Under 14 ~ 19 GHz, the sub-wavelength unit cell can achieve a 300° phase shift, facilitating miniaturization and high gain. Under 25 ~ 30 GHz, the unit realizes an 800° ultra-wide phase shift when the varactor diodes' capacitance is 0 ~ 1 pF. The analysis and optimization of unit structures are performed by the HFSS software. This metasurface unit cell can be used in reconfigurable reflectarray antenna for its outstanding reflection performance and programmable diode circuit.

articleTitle: Dielectric Loaded Reconfigurable SIW Slot Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel passive/mechanical technique is proposed in this paper, to tune the operating frequency of substrate integrated waveguide slot antenna array, by loading dielectric rods at the center of the slots as well as outside of the slots. The antenna array is designed using 3D electromagnetic simulation. Then it is fabricated and verified with measured results. The operating frequency is reconfigured with a simultaneous change in the relative permittivity of all the dielectric rods, which are fabricated in-house from the widely used substrates. For all the tuning cases, the array is maintaining good similarity in radiation patterns and with a gain of 9.3 dBi. This simple cost-effective mechanical tuning technique eliminates the use of any external DC bias circuitry, hence reducing parasitic effects and loss involved in the widely used active reconfigurable circuits. This initial investigation demonstrates a frequency tunability of 11.3 % (at X-band), which is the highest ever reported, even using active tuning techniques. This reconfigurable antenna array is developed for wideband and high-speed point-to-multipoint communication, especially in remote areas where power is very limited. Further, the proposed technique is suitable to overcome fabrication uncertainties and temperature variation in on-field post-installation tuning.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of Terahertz Elliptical Slot Antenna Based on Photonic Crystal Substrate
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper aims to develop a photonic band gap substrate-based slot microstrip patch antenna for terahertz applications. The proposed antenna is based on an elliptical slotted patch placed on the top of a photonic crystal structure to improve the conventional microstrip patch antenna in terms of the undesirable surface waves and its electrical properties. As a result, good radiation characteristics are achieved. Besides, an enhancement of more than 35% and 91% are observed for a total bandwidth of 203.5 GHz and a realized gain of 9.1 dBi, respectively.

articleTitle: 2*2 Millimeter Wave Antenna with Simultaneous Decoupling of E-plane and H-plane
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A 2*2 millimeter wave antenna with simultaneous decoupling of E-plane and H-plane is proposed in this paper. The decoupling of E-plane and H-plane is realized by loading metal branches Bar-I and Bar-II respectively. The measured results show that the antenna achieves <tex>$\vert \mathrm{S}_{11}\vert < -10\text{dB}$</tex> in band of 25.7-26.3 GHz, the <tex>$\vert \mathrm{S}_{21}\vert, \vert \mathrm{S}_{31}\vert$</tex> and <tex>$\vert \mathrm{S}_{41}\vert$</tex> are less than <tex>$25 \text{dB}$</tex> in this frequency band. The antenna has good radiation performance and good decoupling characteristics in both E-plane and H-plane., which can be applied to millimeter wave MIMO communication systems requiring high isolation.

articleTitle: Digital Array Calibration Utilizing A Reduced Scale Planar Near-Field Measurement Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The cost and time required to calibrate phased arrays increases with the number of antenna elements. In this work we determine amplitude and phase calibration coefficients for an element-level digital linear receive array antenna by applying a reduced scale planar near-field measurement method. As the linear array is steered in one dimension, the measurement plane is reduced to a single dimension. Due to the element-level digital architecture, calibration time is further reduced as all elements are calibrated in a single scan. The extracted calibration coefficients are applied to the array element patterns and produce a steerable beam pattern.

articleTitle: High-Gain, Conical-Beam Arrays with Elevation Beam-Steering
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper demonstrates array pattern synthesis for high-gain (> 20 dBi), conical patterns with elevation scanning from boresight to the element 3-dB beamwidth. We realize acceptable patterns with unit element excitation, enabling efficient power amplifier operation for transmit applications.

articleTitle: Transient Response of Circuit Shape Right- and Left-Handed Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The circuit-shaped waveguides have been reported as a method for melting snow over a large area by using one power source. However there exist a problem in the previous study that the electromagnetic waves from the feeding point radiate symmetrically yields cancelation of the radiation or collide at half the circumference, resulting in a decrease in efficiency. To overcome the issue, this paper proposes to incorporate a left-handed waveguide to align the propagation direction of electromagnetic waves. The left-hand and right-hand waveguides are in the straight sections of the circuit, respectively. The transient response of the proposed right- and left-handed waveguide is shown by the electromagnetic field animation using the FDTD method. The analysis results show that the proposed left-hand and right-hand waveguides successfully achieve to make the electromagnetic waves within the waveguide travel in a circle in almost the same direction.

articleTitle: Characterization of SPS Multiple-Beam-Scan Antenna for Wireless Platforms Emulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Rapid advancement in material science and digital revolution pushing in the deployment of Synthetic-Phasor-Sensor (SPS) antenna for modern telecom and wireless applications. This design significantly enhances the RF performance for various synchronized platforms. It is built on the idea of systematically integrating Phased-Array sensors measurable Input-Output matrix for optimized performance. It is a form of correlated wireless sensors, designed to provide extended coverage i.e., wide field-of-view to compensate for the signal scan-loss attributed to the single-unit phasor sensor. This design is so flexible that they can be reconfigured easily and readily for various modern wireless applications. These systems are especially adaptable to mobile structures such as auto-pilot unmanned vehicles and Drones.

articleTitle: Tri-Axial Magnetic Field Sensor up to VHF with Frequency Weighing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This contribution presents an isotropic magnetic field probe with shaped frequency response in the band 100 kHz - 400 MHz to ponder the aggregate response according to the ICNIRP 2020 guidelines. The basic sensor is a printed loop which is modelled as a Thévenin source obtained through full-wave simulation. A canonical filter is optimized considering the frequency response of the equivalent source, the detector and the desired transfer function. Finally, a cubic arrangement of three elementary sensors is used to assess the isotropy and isolation of the probe.

articleTitle: A Learning-Based Inversion Method for Phaseless Profiling of Circular Buried Objects
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A deep learning algorithm for phaseless microwave imaging of circular buried targets, is proposed in this paper. To that end, a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is implemented, in which the amplitude of the measured scattered electric field is directly fed to the network as the input. By using phaseless data, the measurement setup cost and complexity can be reduced at the expense of bolding the ill-posedness challenge. To reduce the output unknown parameters, the commonly used assumption of circular cross-section is considered for defining the scatterers. For tackling the required large data set, the fast CG-FFT method is used for generating synthetic data. The obtained results reveal that the proposed simple CNN-based technique can accurately predict in real-time the location, radius, and the dielectric permittivity value of the subsurface objects of circular shapes.

articleTitle: Time-Domain Boundary Element Method Incorporating Strongly Nonlinear Conductivity for Application in the Modeling of 2D Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, a time-domain surface integral equation with a strongly nonlinear Resistive Boundary Condition is formulated and approximately solved using the march on in time scheme. The discretization of the nonlinear relation between the surface current density and the electric field is approximated such that the final system of equations to be solved are linear. It is applied to solve scattering of a Gaussian plane wave by a sphere possessing a strongly nonlinear conductivity relation. This solver is developed to specifically model the effects due to the region of negative differential conductivity in the conductivity relation, which is expected in graphene superlattice structures. Numerical results demonstrate the stability and convergence of the method and the ability to enforce the constitutive relation within controllable error bounds.

articleTitle: Fully Analytical Formula for Input Impedance of Center-Fed Hemispherical Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: An explicit analytical solution is derived for the input impedance of a center-fed hemispherical dielectric resonator antenna. The reflection coefficient at the resonator boundary is presented in a computationally simplified form, with real and imaginary parts separated. The new expressions enable a straightforward study of an interplay between the probe and resonator parameters.

articleTitle: Using MGAWE Method for Waveguide Structure Analysis Based on Finite Element DDM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The broadband electromagnetic response of complex waveguide structure using domain decomposition method (DDM) still remains a formidable challenge. To address the efficient computation of the electromagnetic responses over a wide frequency band, multipoint Galerkin asymptotic waveform evaluation (MGAWE) based on DDM has been adopted in this paper. The resulting solution procedure of using MGAWE to solve complex waveguide allows for wideband frequency simulations with a reduction in total computation time. Numerical simulations using these methods are shown along with discrete sweep frequency calculated by HFSS software at each frequency point of interest.

articleTitle: Modified H-Plane Sectoral Horn for FSS Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The use of frequency selective surfaces (FSSs) as sensors has found recent success in the structural health monitoring realm. FSS theory assumes infinite FSS dimensions and planewave illumination. However, in practice, an FSS sensor is finite, and the illuminating field varies across the plane of the sensor. As such, it is of interest to reduce the nonuniformity of the incident electromagnetic energy incident on the sensor. To this end, this work explores the modification of a standard H-plane sectoral horn through the addition of a ridge to generate a uniform electric field over a specified region of interest. In addition to this modified antenna, standard gain (pyramidal) and H-plane sectoral horns were also considered for comparison. The results show that variation in the electric field pattern is reduced for the modified sectoral horn but at the cost of matching properties.

articleTitle: Antennas and Propagation Research Fueling the Mobile Wireless Revolution
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In just a few decades, mobile wireless connectivity has dramatically changed the way people approach almost all aspects of their lives. This wireless communication revolution has been fueled by advancements in many technologies including antennas and propagation. This paper briefly summarizes two key areas of focus in antennas and propagation - specifically the development of electromagnetic modeling tools that allowed characterization and design of advanced antenna topologies and the exploration of multi-antenna techniques to improve communication in mobile channels - that have been driven forward by the vision and research activities of Prof. Yahya Rahmat-Samii.

articleTitle: Engineering Thermal Radiation Using Bound States in the Continuum
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work presents a novel method to achieve mid-infrared coherent thermal emitters using bound states in the continuum. We show that narrowband emission peaks are realized by adding a dielectric layer to a phononic substrate and forming Friedrich-Wintgen interfering resonances. The phononic metasurface demonstrated here can be employed to design and fabricate the next generation of narrowband coherent light emitters in the mid-infrared wavelengths, opening up new opportunities in the area of on-chip optical communications, sensing, infrared spectroscopy, and photodetection.

articleTitle: Energy-Efficient Wireless Channel Deployment Using Self-Sustainable Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface with Cognitive Radio Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper describes a self-sustainable reconfigurable intelligent surface with embedded sensing circuits for optimal propagation links under random channel conditions. Adaptive beam scanning from 20° to 57° is achieved by a liquid crystal (LC)-driven reconfigurable unit cells, while the channel estimation information (CSI) is estimated by Rotman lens with reduced signal processing complexity. The feasibility of this work is experimentally verified in non-line-of-sight environments, achieving high data throughput of 2.8 Gbps for 64 quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM). This paradigm-shifting wireless channel deployment strategy is expected to provide optimal propagation paths with self-sustainable feedback system.

articleTitle: Dispersion Engineered Nonlocal Metasurfaces with Customizable Wavefront-Selectivity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We propose and demonstrate nonlocal metasurfaces with wavefront-selective customizable features. In particular, we engineer in extreme ways the modal dispersion of metasurfaces, to go from positive to negative curvature across a flat dispersion regime. This result opens a new degree of freedom to selectively control metasurface responses, added to the already rich opportunities of nonlocal metasurfaces, such as frequency and polarization selectivity, as well as unitary-efficiency wavefront manipulation. We achieve customizable wavefront-selectivity by adding metallic via walls into bilayer nonlocal metasurfaces, which control the lateral energy transfer inside the metasurface while preserving the desired nonlocal properties imprinted in the bilayer. Based on these principles, we demonstrate highly-efficient wavefront-selective and wavefront-independent anomalous reflection and focusing, combined with frequency and polarization selectivity.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Nonradiating Surface Sources
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We develop a general construction procedure for electromagnetic nonradiating surface sources, whose generated fields vanish entirely in a given region. Two different kinds are considered. The first kind is based on the solution of an exterior radiation or boundary value problem, while the second kind is based on the solution of an interior problem. The formulation pertinent to the first kind renders nonradiating sources whose fields vanish in an interior region, while the second approach provides nonradiating sources whose fields are zero in an exterior, unbounded region. These surface sources include, in general, both electric and magnetic components, and can be realized not only in time-harmonic steady state but also under transient conditions. We show that purely electric and purely magnetic nonradiating surface sources also exist, which arise under resonance conditions and exhibit interesting properties.

articleTitle: A Shifted-Beam Method for Near-Field Wireless Power Transfer using Parasitic Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Optimizing near field (NF) wireless power transfer (WPT) to ensure maximum power transfer efficiency (PTE) is essential for a number of applications such as radio-frequency identification (RFID) and device charging. A new WPT method using a parasitic array is proposed, inspired by a shifted-beam (SB) wave interference technique for field focusing. The SB method is implemented for target distances between <tex>$\mathbf{1}\lambda$</tex> and <tex>$\mathbf{2}\lambda$</tex> at 2.4 GHz <tex>$(\lambda=12.5\ \text{cm})$</tex>, which lie roughly in the radiative NF. PTE from the SB method is compared with results from a uniformly excited array of similar length, as well as a phase optimization (PO) method based on conjugate-phase (CP) focusing. The transmit <tex>$(\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{x}})$</tex> system is implemented as an array of center-fed dipoles, with a <tex>$\mathbf{0.48}\lambda$</tex> non-excited dipole used as the receive <tex>$(\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{x}})$</tex> element. The results show an enhancement of PTE compared to the baseline uniform array, and in some cases the PO array. The simplicity of the SB method makes it an advantageous design choice.

articleTitle: A Dual-Linear Polarized Beam-Scanning Holographic Antenna Using Compact Pillbox Feeding System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a dual-linear polarized holographic antenna with a compact-sized pillbox feeding system that generates surface waves for orthogonal directions. The proposed antenna consists of a three-layered pillbox feeding system for dual orthogonal surface waves and a dual-linear polarized hologram pattern for radiating the field toward the desired directions. The proposed antenna steers the beam direction from −10°to +5°in 23 to 25 GHz, radiating the beam at 24 GHz with a realized gain of 19.5 dBi in each polarization.

articleTitle: The Wavelia#2 Microwave Breast Imaging scanner: experimental performance analysis towards clinical investigation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the methodology for experimental testing and validation of the 2<sup>nd</sup>prototype of the Wavelia Microwave Breast Imaging (MBI) scanner, towards acceptance at clinical investigation site, is presented. The notion of measurement repeatability assessment in MBI imaging is critically introduced for the first time, as part of this analysis. Indicative imaging results are presented and briefly discussed.

articleTitle: Wave-Controlled RIS: A Novel Method for Reconfigurable Elements Biasing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel method for biasing the varactors of a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) by using resonant standing waves on the biasing transmission line (TL) at a layer below the RF reflective surface to eliminate the need to bring external bias for each element of the RIS is described. We use an analytical model of the RIS to compare the field pattern of the reflected wave by (i) considering the ideal case, (ii) the case where reflection accounts for the varactor's model, and (iii) the case as in (ii) but where the biasing voltage distribution is constructed by using the wave control (i.e., standing waves).

articleTitle: Radiation Pattern Reconfigurable MIMO Antenna with EBG for Improved Steering Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a radiation pattern reconfigurable (RPR) multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna with an electromagnetic band gap (EBG) for improved steering performance. The designed RPR-MIMO operates at 3.5 GHz with S<inf>11</inf> < −10 dB, S<inf>21</inf> < −15 dB, steered angle of more than 19° and a minimum average gain of 5 dBi at all steered directions. The proposed EBG structure improved the steering angle that is affected when the RPR is deployed as the MIMO.

articleTitle: Tunable Notch UWB Antenna Based on Variable Liquid Metal Coupling Length
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this article, we present a novel tunable UWB reconfigurable notch band antenna based on variable liquid metal (LM) coupling length. The band rejection reconfiguration is achieved by adjusting the length of LM. The mechanism of switching is based on controlling the LM in 3D print microfluidic channels by applying variable voltage. The proposed antenna has a simple configuration and compact size covering UWB (4.1-12.5GHz) and generates the band rejection in working frequency bands such as WiMAX, WiFi, Wlan, etc that is suitable for cognitive radio applications.

articleTitle: Impacts of Paint Color on a Honeycomb Composite Ka-Band Antenna Gain
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Paint and primer properties can negatively affect numerous antenna parameters, such as noise temperature, gain, and polarization isolation. Of these effects, thermal strain induced by solar radiation has been shown to significantly impact gain. Changes in paint color can drastically change solar thermal strain, and therefore potentially affect gain. This study builds on previous mechanical analysis techniques and applies them to a 3.9-meter honeycomb composite sandwich style reflector across several different color conditions. Results show minimal impact of paint color in RF gain, however non-uniform distortion of solar loading can affect anticipated gain.

articleTitle: On the Accuracy of Dielectric Characterization of Solid Materials by Open-Ended Coaxial Cable
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In the field of electromagnetic characterization of solid materials, waveguides have long been regarded as the gold standard. However, when dealing with high-technology epoxy resins, this method can be inefficient as it may require a large amount of material resulting in a huge expense in manufacturing the prototype under test and associated additional costs. Alternatively, a method employing an in-house open-ended coaxial probe technology is presented in this work. Specifically, the proposed technique can be applied to broadband assess the dielectric properties of resins in a more cost-effective and non-destructive manner, utilizing a small amount of material. In the literature, it is well stated that the main drawback in the dielectric characterization of solid material by using open coaxial probe is the formation of air gaps at the probe tip-to-material interface. To overcome these limitations, we have designed an appropriate mechanical support. To evaluate the reliability of the method, experimental measurements were performed in the 6.4 GHz–8.2 GHz frequency range and then compared with standard waveguide measurements. This study demonstrates that the proposed system is a valid alternative for preliminary dielectric characterization of hard materials such as epoxy resins.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Classification of Snowflakes to Enhance Microphysical and Scattering Characterization of Snow
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: No two snowflakes are alike. However, they can be classified into over a hundred different categories based on their geometry. Recent developments in machine learning algorithms have led to the possibility of automatically classifying more classes of snowflakes more accurately and efficiently. We present supervised and unsupervised learning approaches to snowflake classification coupled with dimensional reduction techniques. Proper automatic and detailed classification of ice and snow hydrometeors enables advanced characterization of geometrical, microphysical, and scattering properties of particles, which, in turn, is essential for development of radar-based quantitative precipitation estimation of snow.

articleTitle: Sub-Millimeter Ranging Accuracy for Distributed Antenna Arrays Using Two-Way Time Transfer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Distributed antenna arrays can provide unique capabilities in applications such as distributed communication and sensing. However, in order to coordinate distributed arrays, accurate positioning information of all nodes in the array is required to ensure coherent operations at the target location. Other works have shown that two-way time transfer using spectrally sparse two-tone ranging waveforms provides high accuracy timing synchronization. In addition to time correction, these waveforms may provide inter-node ranging with high accuracy. In this paper the accuracy of ranging via two-way time transfer for a two-node time synchronization system using a two-tone waveform is evaluated. Results are compared to ranging performance using a standard linear frequency modulated waveform (LFM). Experimental results show an accuracy of 0.5 mm using a 40 MHz bandwidth two-tone waveform with a 36 dB signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), supporting a beamforming frequency of up to 40 GHz.

articleTitle: Active Windshield Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Active millimeter-wave (MMW) vehicular antenna with simultaneous multi-beam, for 5G V2X application, is presented. The antenna achieves both high gain and wide angular coverage through multi-array design. Each array has a fixed beam direction and a separate feeding network. The beams have sufficient beamwidths such that the total pattern ensures simultaneous elevation plane coverage. The design consists of four dual-polarized patch arrays. Each array radiates in a different range of elevation angles with beams maxima at 40°, 20°, 0° and −20° with respect to the normal of the windshield. The antenna is matched across the entire 28 GHz 5G band that ranges from 24 GHz to 30 GHz. Miniaturized Wilkinson power dividers are incorporated for feeding each array which ensures minimum beam scanning with frequency. A single active beamformer chip is integrated in the design to feed the two polarizations of each array with an adjustable phase and gain and a maximum active gain of 20 dB for each port.

articleTitle: High-Performance Numerical Modeling for Detection of Rotator Cuff Tear
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, microwave tomographic imaging for rotator cuff tear by numerical modeling and parallel computing is presented. It requires solving an inverse problem by making use of an iterative method based on a minimization algorithm. To this end, efficient parallel algorithms and high-performance computing is utilized that result in an accurate reconstruction of the electrical properties of the propagation medium as well as fast computations. Results demonstrate the possibility to detect different types of tendon tears in a shoulder model.

articleTitle: Design of Cost-Effective and Performant Electromagnetic Skins via Non-Radiating Sources
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work considers the design of Electromagnetic Skins (EMS) that demonstrate remarkable field manipulation capabilities and employ cost-effective materials. Towards this end, a synthesis strategy based on Non-Radiating (NR) sources is devised, exploiting the null-space of the radiation operator. Preliminary results indicate that significant performance improvements are achieved compared to standard approaches.

articleTitle: Single and Multiple Actions of Short-Pulsed Temporal Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Temporal metamaterials that rely on impulsive modulations of the constitutive parameters can perform elementary analog computing on impinging wavepackets. We summarize some recent results on simple and multiple short-pulsed metamaterials and demonstrate their computational capabilities. Our results suggest that the temporal dimension can offer new opportunities for designing metamaterials with computational capabilities.

articleTitle: A Robust Minimum Mainlobe Low Sidelobe Beamforming Method Based on Convex Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: To suppress the beam distortion and sidelobe rise caused by array element position offset, a robust minimum mainlobe low sidelobe beamforming method based on convex optimization is proposed. The constraint of element position offset is introduced into the optimization object on the basis of the element weight vector optimization, in which the improved dichotomy and second-order cone programming method is used for high calculation efficiency. The results of Mente Carlo experiments show the synthesized beam of proposed method outperforms the conventional method in beamforming with array element position offset, its characteristics of narrow mainlobe, accurate direction and low sidelobe enable the proposed method suitable for large beamforming applications.

articleTitle: On the Prospects of Stereolithography Method for 3D Printing of Future Microwave Devices with Low-Dk
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The stereolithography (SLA) method is known for its high-quality surface finish and details, hence, gaining its popularity with the realization of 3D-printed parts and structures for microwave applications. On the other hand, low-dielectric <tex>$(\boldsymbol{Dk})$</tex> materials have an utmost importance in high-frequency PCB design and microwave applications. Here, the authors present the prospects of the SLA method in 3D-printing of <tex>$\mathbf{Low}-\boldsymbol{Dk}$</tex> materials for future microwave devices. The SLA method is a relatively new manufacturing process, so it is critical to explore a range of dielectric constants of a few prospective commercially available materials. Here, eleven different resin-based materials were 3D-printed as cubes using the SLA method and characterized in terms of dielectric constant <tex>$(\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}_{\boldsymbol{r}})$</tex> and loss tangent <tex>$(\mathbf{tan}\boldsymbol{\delta})$</tex> using broadband coaxial probe method. The measured dielectric constant values were within the range of 2 - 4 for all the tested materials which thus proved to be among promising candidates for realizing microwave devices in the frequency bandwidth of 1 to 20 GHz. A few observed failures while manufacturing certain other shapes were also reported as a limitation of the SLA method.

articleTitle: Compact E-plane Patch Antennas Using Decoupling Meander Slot Between Radiating Edges
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A resonant compact meander line slot is etched on the ground plane of two E-plane closely-spaced patch antennas, which is a challenging task with the spacing of λ0/20 between the radiating edges. A fivefold meander line slot is used as a decoupling structure on the ground plane between the radiating edges so that the dimension does not exceed the patch width for the compact purpose. Such a simple decoupling structure improves the matching and isolation to be better than 19 dB in the 5.8 GHz band.

articleTitle: Fast Volume Integral Equation Based Modeling of Quantum Gate Circuitry: Capturing Local vs. Nonlocal Effects on Spin Qubits
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We develop a fast volume integral equation solver in frequency domain to model and simulate nonlocal optical responses in quantum nano-electromagnetic gate circuitry. The convolution involved in the nonlocal constitutive relation is handled efficiently by transforming it to the spectral Fourier domain using fast Fourier transform (FFT), in conjunction with the convolution of Green's function with equivalent volumetric currents. Numerical simulations of 3-D quantum gate devices demonstrate the capability of the proposed solver as well as the importance of nonlocal effects.

articleTitle: Planar mmWave Traveling Wave Amplifier on GaN/AlGaN Heterostructure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a novel on-chip implementation of a traveling wave tube amplifier on GaN/AlGaN heterostructure. The device utilizes the coupling between drifting electrons in a two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) substrate layer and that of an electromagnetic (EM) slow-wave circuit placed on top of the 2DEG to achieve amplification. Measurements are presented for validation. The applied voltage was 8 V and the gain was 2.3 dB at 80 GHz.

articleTitle: An UWB Measurement Error Model for Accurate Positioning Investigation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-wide band (UWB) positioning model is proposed and the influence of nonideal measurement conditions on UWB positioning accuracy is evaluated and analyzed. By extracting the difference features between phase results of typical positioning field test and ideal simulation, the influence of nearfield radiation, receiver eccentric rotation, orthogonal dimension coupling and positioning device tilt are investigated with the UWB positioning model, which provides fundamental error analysis basis for UWB position applications.

articleTitle: Hybrid Genetic Programming-Based Comparative Design of Broadband Metamaterial Absorbers Using Graphene, Resistive Sheets, and Carbon Fiber
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Hybrid genetic programming (HGP) is proposed to create new design topologies in the lower gigahertz frequency with new materials such as graphene, resistive sheet, and carbon fiber. HGP can create new topologies optimized per input parameters, such as low frequency and high broadband absorptivity. These designs are built and simulated in Ansys High-Frequency Simulation Software (HFSS) and evaluated by HGP. Graphene, resistive sheet, and carbon fiber patterning are explored and implemented with HGP to create low-gigahertz frequency and high-absorptivity MMAs. The graphene, resistive sheet, and carbon fiber-based patterned designs achieved 80% bandwidth above 80% absorptivity from 4.6 to 11 GHz, up to 15 GHz, from 3.83 to 9.13 GHz, and from 3.77 to 10.28 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Cavity Backed Metasurface Antenna for High Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Metasurface antennas provide high performance in terms of gain and bandwidth. However, it suffers from back lobe radiation and low power handling capability. This paper proposes a cavity-backed metasurfaces design that can handle high input power. The proposed model operates from 2.1 GHz to 3.6 GHz with a 53 % bandwidth and 6 dB gain. Furthermore, perfect matching between experimental measurements and simulated results is achieved.

articleTitle: Multipurpose Reconfigurable Reflectarray Antennas for Dual-Polarization Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a multipurpose reconfigurable reflectarray antenna (MRRA) is presented. The proposed MRRA features low-profile and it independently controls orthogonal polarization of incident waves. The unit cell of MRRA consists of two parts: an antenna and a phase shifter. The antnenna has two slot-coupled feeding networks to excite orthogonally polarized waves and parasitic patches to improve impedance bandwidth. The proposed phase shifter is a reflection-type phase shifter using a single hybrid coupler and two varactors. The measured the relative phase shift range was 0 ~ 360° with a DC bias voltage range of 0 ~ 7 V. The proposed unit cell strucutre for MRRA was fabricated and verified by a customized waveguide structure. An 8×8 array composed of the proposed unit cell structure is also proposed and its performance is studied.

articleTitle: Augmentation of Volume-Surface Integral Equations for Low-Frequency Modeling of Interconnect Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Interconnect structures include both conducting and penetrable media and electromagnetic (EM) modeling and analysis for them require the use of volume-surface integral equations (VSIEs) in the integral equation approach. The VSIEs include the <tex>$\mathcal{L}$</tex> operator in both surface integral equations (SIEs) and volume integral equations (VIEs), and it will produce a low-frequency-breakdown (LFB) problem for low-frequency modeling. Although the augmentations of SIEs for both conducting and dielectric media have been proposed for remedying the LFB problem, the augmentation for the VSIEs has not been addressed yet. This paper aims to this problem and proposes an augmented VSIEs (AVSIEs) by introducing the magnetic charge density and continuity equation of magnetic current density. A numerical example is provided to demonstrate the approach and its effectiveness has been validated.

articleTitle: Fully 3D Printed Antenna for C-V2X Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A helical antenna for cellular vehicle to everything (C-V2X) communications is developed using additive manufacturing techniques on temperature sensitive and curved 3D printed substrate. The antenna has an omni-directional radiation pattern and vertical polarization. The measured maximum realized gain of the implemented antenna is -1.78 dBi at 5.65 GHz. The overall antenna size with the ground is 50mm x 50mm x 4.6mm.

articleTitle: Metamorphosis of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) into Scientific TCM (STCM)-New Visions and Principles for Human Physiology and Medicine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) practiced in China since 2700 BC was metamorphosed to Scientific TCM (STCM) in year 2022. The approach was to latch TCM onto the newly discovered human organ called Interstitium and then distil and synthesize TCM procedures, one bye one, to conform to modern sciences. The theory of Chee, which had been the foundation of TCM, had to be formulated mathematically to qualify for a scientific theory. The present paper presents the finalized scientific theory of Chee, which adds new visions and principles to modern human physiology and medicine. This new frontier of research is expected to lead to fundamental discoveries. It should also lead to new diagnostic and therapeutic instrumentation and treatments on major illnesses, such as the chronic pain-which sickens 1/5 America adults and costs $635 billion annually. We have conceived a treatment approach for achieving long-term whole-body health.

articleTitle: HFSS Hybrid Electromagnetic Simulation Accelerates Radome Design
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive solution for the electromagnetic characterization of radomes. The efficient simulations for a large radome structure can be performed by utilizing the hybrid approach, which is otherwise almost difficult to achieve. The accuracy of the hybrid solution is comparable to the full wave model with significantly reduced solve time. The HFSS simulation technology, therefore, accelerates the radome design. A comprehensive picture of robust design and various case studies will be presented at the conference.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of the Common Mode Noise Filter for Battery Charging System in a Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A common-mode noise filter is studied for the battery charging system in a vehicle. The filter is designed by using an ideal low pass filter topology and practically evaluated by considering the inductor's saturation characteristic affected by a noise frequency. Finally, the filter's performance is estimated by virtually implementing the CISPR 25 test setup for conducted and radiated emission simulations.

articleTitle: A New Element Pattern Model Enabling Agile Optimization of Modern Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Phased array technology has of late enjoyed a dramatic increase in utility in such varied applications as millimeter-wave communications and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces [1]. The increased use of this important enabling technology warrants strong design capabilities, to include rapid and accurate modeling of expected array behavior. To that end, we present in this report a new element pattern model which faithfully reproduces practical real-world, arbitrary array elements. Also, spherical integration of the proposed model results in a completely analytical solution, allowing for greatly reduced computational complexity in the optimization of arbitrary array topologies.

articleTitle: A Channel Decoupling Method for Digital Phased Array Beamforming Based on Chaotic Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a channel decoupling method based on chaotic genetic algorithm is proposed for accurate digital phased array beamforming.
