With the increase of working frequency and decrease in element spacing, the channel coupling in phased array has more severe influence on array radiation pattern. Making use of a-prior measured radiation patterns, the optimal channel coupling compensation matrix is estimated with the genetic algorithm, which greatly reduces the error between decoupled radiation pattern and ideal radiation pattern. The simulation results show that the maximum beam pointing deviation is reduced from 1.8° to 0.5° and the sidelobe level is reduced by 8 dB when the channel decoupling method is applied.

articleTitle: Design of Efficient and Wideband 60 GHz Series-Fed Millimeter-Wave Antenna Array for Next-Generation Multi-Gigabit Industrial Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A compact, highly efficient, and wideband 8-element series-fed array with parasitic patches is designed at 60 GHz millimeter-wave ISM band. The proposed array covers the license-free band from 57–66 GHz with −10 dB impedance bandwidth of 25.94% (53-68.8 GHz) and peak realized gain of 14.60 dBi at 65 GHz. The gain fluctuation is less than 0.75 dB in the entire band of interest, and the radiation efficiency is above 91.8% The array prototype was fabricated and tested. The measured reflection coefficient closely matches with the simulated one. The proposed antenna array is suitable for unlicensed 60 GHz mmWave industrial applications to support multi-gigahertz bandwidth and multi-gigabits-per-second data rate. It can operate with various 60 GHz protocols such as IEEE 802.11ay, IEEE 802.11ad, IEE 802.15.3c, Wireless HD and ECMA-387.

articleTitle: Wide-Area Spectrum Cartography
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper describes U.S. spectrum management measurement challenges and a potential scalable solution using satellite-based observations. Specifically, we investigate the radio frequency passive imaging technique of synthetic aperture source localization (SASL), which combines elements of aperture synthesis (cf. synthetic aperture radar) and time and frequency difference of arrival. We simulate the use of low-cost software-defined radio receivers and low-gain antennas at a common small-satellite altitude of 550 km to implement a SASL approach. Preliminary results demonstrate resolution of emitters with sufficient spatial and spectral detail to provide useful statistical spectrum quantification information to U.S. policymakers and technology developers.

articleTitle: Bunching Effects at Emitted Radiation from GeV Electrons in a Strong Laser at Future TW Experiments
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Future experiments that consider the collision of GeV electrons and TW laser have as central objective to probe non-perturbative QED at the strong field where processes derived from Schwinger critic field can be observed. Nevertheless, the huge photon density will allow to electron to absorb and emit various photons as creating a bunching of them, fact that might be an obstacle to observe a clean signal. In this paper, with basic principles of classical electrodynamics, the radiated intensity is numerically estimated. Unclear nonlinear final states emerge as potential background to reduce signal efficiency drastically.

articleTitle: Development of Monopulse Antenna Feeding System with Microstrip-Line-to-Waveguide-Transition Using SIW Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper discusses the development of microstrip line to substrate-integrated-waveguide (SIW) transition for monopulse antenna feeding system using SIW technology. A simple tapered microstrip line is applied in the implementation of transition between microstrip line and SIW to improve impedance matching, as well as to easier incorporate with other planar structures. The realization of the proposed monopulse antenna feeding network which operates at S-band frequency of 2.4 GHz uses a 1.524 mm thick Rogers RO4003C dielectric substrate. The measurement characteristics demonstrate that the realized monopulse antenna feeding network based on SIW technology can provide the isolation of around 15 dB, with the insertion loss of approximately 3 dB, the return loss of more than 15 dB, and the phase difference of around 180°.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of a 24 GHz Series-Fed $1 \times 5$ Antenna Array with Material Deformation for D2D Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design and simulation of a 24 GHz <tex>$1\times 5$</tex> series-fed microstrip patch antenna array and its performance analysis with structural deformation. The optimized design comprises of 5 antenna elements arranged in series, where the entire design is symmetric about the center antenna element. The parameters such as <tex>$S_{11}$</tex>, gain vs. theta plots are analyzed with and without the material deformation. The shape deformation analysis is indeed needed to determine the performance efficiency of the designed antenna when deployed on drones, where the antenna needs to be flexible enough to be aligned with the curvature of drone's body. The simulation results are analyzed to see how best can the proposed antenna array can perform with the structural deformation.

articleTitle: Passive Reconfigurable Dual Linear and Dual Circular Polarization with CLRH-TL for Triangular Microstrip Patch Array
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Passively controlled antenna arrays for a variety of applications can require a myriad of design criteria such as beam steering, wideband operation, and reconfigurable dual linear and dual circular polarizations. This paper presents a unique design of quadrature hybrid that is configured with composite left/right-hand transmission lines (CLRH-TL) consisting of series capacitors and shunt inductors to create the required phase difference for dual linear and dual circular polarizations at four different frequencies. The modified quadrature hybrid is integrated in the feed system of an aperture coupled square microstrip patch antenna that is set in a stacked arrangement to increase the bandwidth to 17% (10.7-12.7GHz). Simulations with HFSS are shown to verify the design for the different polarizations. Next, a planar array of the patches is arranged in a triangular configuration with beam steering of ±60° demonstrated by path length changes in the feed system. The prototyping to validate the design will be done in the X-band.

articleTitle: Wideband Circularly Polarized Slotted Multi-Port Patch Antenna for High-Precision GNSS Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A modified patch antenna based on the four-port feeds connected with 0°, 90°, 180°, and 270° phase shifters is presented to achieve a broadband circular polarization performance. The impedance bandwidth at or above 10dB return loss is about 620MHz, from 1.07GHz to 1.69GHz. The 3dB-axial-ratio bandwidth is about 610MHz, from 1.12GHz to 1.73GHz. The proposed patch antenna is suitable for high-precision GNSS applications.

articleTitle: Antenna Circuit Model Synthesis for Circuit-Based Transient Radiation Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Optimization methods are used to synthesize a highpass circuit approximation of two parameterized electrically small dipole antennas. We conduct parametric sweeps to assess the variation in antenna characteristics and model accuracy with changes in critical dimensions. We demonstrate the accuracy and utility of these circuit approximations in circuit-based transient simulations, such as those encountered in the analysis of non-LTI systems.

articleTitle: Dual Band Dual Polarized Electrically Small Antenna Employing a Magnetic Material
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Here, we present a novel dual-polarized electrically small antenna that covers two cellular frequency bands. The design employs a magnetic material that aids in reducing the overall size of the antenna. We find that the bandwidth is improved relative to materials where μ<inf>r</inf> = 1. However, we also see that having a low magnetic loss tangent is critical to preserving radiation efficiency.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Rapid Indoor Mapping Using a Very High Resolution Radar at J-Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A fast J-band FMCW radar system is modified with a fast scanning elliptic toroidal reflector for high resolution mapping and navigation. The system operates in the 222–228 GHz frequency band and is capable of generating FMCW chirps with a rate of 28 <tex>$\text{MHz}/\mu \mathrm{s}$</tex>. The block diagram and component description of IF and RF modules is presented. The radar uses a 3D printed reflector antenna to mechanically scan the surrounding with a <tex>$0.3^{\circ}$</tex> azimuthal resolution. Combined with 15 cm range resolution, the system is used to generate a 2D images with 15 cm pixel size at 30 m distance. The radar is then used to investigate indoor imaging and mapping capabilities. The approach used in the experiment produced images that identify main building features such as doors, windows and wall corners. For target detection, the CFAR algorithm is applied and the multipath backscatterr is eliminated by considering only the first detection at each angle, removing most of the ghost targets in the radar image.

articleTitle: Low-Loss Multi-Beam Large Phased Array Architecture
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel architecture to achieve multi-beam scanning for large arrays. The proposed phased array architecture benefits from low-RF complexity and low-loss feeding network. This phased array architecture works based on one 90-degree hybrid coupler behind each two antenna elements to excite them orthogonally and make two independent radiation beams. The phase shifting mechanism is applied by the phase shifters, placed on the 90-degree hybrid's input ports. To validate the performance of the proposed architecture, a <tex>$4^{\ast} 2$</tex> patch antenna array excited by liquid crystal phase shifters is manufactured and measured. The measurement result shows two independent beams are scanning up to ±20° over the elevation angle.

articleTitle: Spectral-Domain Method of Moments for the Study of Line Waves
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The dispersion properties of edge modes supported by linear discontinuities of surface impedance planes, i.e., the so-called line waves, are studied here by means of a full-wave numerical approach based on the method of moments in the spectral domain. The proposed formulation, based on entire-domain basis functions defined on a half line, is both versatile and computationally efficient; its accuracy is validated through a comparison against analytical results obtained with the Sommerfeld-Maliuzhinets method.

articleTitle: Characteristic Mode Decomposition of Polarizability Tensors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This abstract presents a method for evaluating four polarizability tensors using characteristic mode decomposition and scattering description based on the method of moments formulation of field integral equations. The method's precision is confirmed by comparison with polarizabilities obtained from the six-waves method.

articleTitle: A Novel Antenna Peaking Technique Using Machine Learning in Noisy Satellite Communication Channels
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to antenna tracking and pattern reconstruction using machine learning as demonstrated here using a single class support vector machine. It assumes a global estimation technique peaks a noisy main beam with finite pointing error but then the proposed method finetunes the peaking to produce the true beam maximum. The finetuning processes uses a u-v coordinate raster input to a single class support vector machine to classify an n-dB main beam contour and provide a true peak likelihood score therein (essentially filtering out the outlier noise). The results show a 97% improvement over picking the global maximum. The intention of the work is to provide a theoretical foundation from which an actual tracking algorithm could be based.

articleTitle: A Single Layer Frequency Selective Surface for Dual Communication and Localization Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design, analysis and fabrication of a single layer frequency selective surface (FSS) operating in both sub-7 GHz and 77 GHz bands. The application of this FSS is two-fold. The first is to act as a radome in the lower band by shielding an antenna and the second is as a 77 GHz radar reflector operating over a range of angles of incidence from 0° to 20°. In the lower band, the goal is maintaining high transmission to allow for the pass-through of communication signals. A band-stop filter response is designed with a square loop unit cell at 77 GHz to ensure high reflection. Simulation results using Ansys HFSS are shown for both bands. Experimental results validating the transmission and illustrating the use case are carried out by placing the FSS in front of a dual-polarized antenna and measuring its characteristics at 5.4 GHz.

articleTitle: An SIE-GSTC Solver for Simulation of Monoanisotropic Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A surface integral equation (SIE) solver is proposed to simulate electromagnetic field interactions on three-dimensional arbitrarily-shaped monoanisotropic metasurfaces. The metasurface is modeled as an infinitely thin sheet on which generalized sheet transition conditions (GSTCs) are enforced. These conditions “connect” the equivalent electric and magnetic surface currents on two sides of the metasurface using susceptibility tensors that characterize the electromagnetic response of the metasurface. A coupled system of equations in unknown surface current densities is obtained by linearly combining electric and magnetic field integral equations on two sides of the metasurface and GSTCs.

articleTitle: Finite Ground Plane Effects and Sensitivity Analysis of Microstrip Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The finite ground plane effects on specific performance parameters for a microstrip patch antenna are analyzed. Several microstrip patch antennas with varying ground plane dimensions are fabricated and measured. Results reveal significant influence of ground plane dimensions on all pertinent parameters addressed in this paper.

articleTitle: Ultrawideband Gain Enhancement Using 3D Printed Dielectric Gradient Refractive Index Lens
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present a lightweight 3D printed gradient refractive index (GRIN) lens that enhances a dual-ridge horn antenna gain in the 1 to 7 GHz frequency spectrum. The lens design process utilized optical path length transformation techniques and optimization of ideal focal length and thickness. The GRIN lens was fabricated using variable infill fused de-position modeling. The measured result shows an average gain enhancement of 2.82 dBi across the entire frequency spectrum. Overall, the measured and simulated data demonstrated good agreement. The developed prototype is an example of low-cost, ultrawideband, and directive gain enhancement for amateur radio purposes (emergency communications), directed energy, and high-power microwave systems.

articleTitle: Examinations and Modeling of Metal Mesh Surfaces for Antenna-on-Display (AoD) Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The metal mesh structures for Antenna-on-Display (AoD) are investigated in this paper. Their equivalent electromagnetic properties are extracted from the simulated results by applying the Floquet theorem. The equivalent homogeneous model is studied, provided and validated with measurements in this paper which can be employed to simplify AoD structures for the ease of simulation and antenna design.

articleTitle: Design of a Broadband MIMO Antenna with High Isolation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Antenna is a device used to transmit and receive electromagnetic signals in wireless communication equipment, and its quality will determine the performance of the whole communication equipment. Traditional wireless communication, the data transmission speed slows down and the error rate increases because of multipath effect and wall effect. Nowadays, a large number of researchers at home and abroad combine UWB(Ultra-Wideband) and MIMO(multiple input multiple output) technology and apply them to the antenna field. In this paper, a two-element MIMO antenna with a size of <tex>$\mathbf{35}\ \mathbf{mm} \times \mathbf{25} \mathbf{mm} \times \mathbf{1}\ \mathbf{mm}$</tex> is designed, by using the DGS(defective ground structure) and isolating parasitic branches, the isolation is improved, Achieving <tex>$\vert\mathbf{S}_{\mathbf{11}}\vert < -\mathbf{12}\ \mathbf{dB}, \vert \mathbf{S}_{\mathbf{21}}\vert < -\mathbf{20}\ \mathbf{dB}$</tex> in the ultra-wideband range from 3.8 GHz - 13.3 GHz.

articleTitle: Path Loss Analysis for Array Antenna systems in Underground Mine at 3.5GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, path loss characteristics of the underground mine channel for a 64-element uniform rectangular array (URA) antenna system at 3.5GHz are presented and analyzed. Measurements were conducted in an underground mine environment, including both line-of-sight (LoS) and best-line-of-sight (Best-LOS) scenarios, with the transmitter-receiver (Tx-Rx) separation distance ranging from 5m to 70m. The log-distance path loss model was used to evaluate the path loss performance from the measurement data. The obtained path loss exponents were found to be 1.56 and 1.76, with shadow fading standard deviation of 1.34dB and 2.32dB for LoS and Best-LOS, respectively. These results indicate that the propagation characteristics in an underground mine have a waveguide effect on the propagated signal. As a result, the 3.5 GHz frequency band could be a suitable candidate for 5G communications in underground mine environments.

articleTitle: Breaking the Degree-of-Freedom Limit of Aperture-Constrained MIMO Communication Systems by 3-D Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The performance of aperture-constrained multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) communication systems, which use two-dimensional (2-D) planar antenna arrays, is limited by the degree-of-freedom (DOF) constraint that arises from the physical property of electromagnetic waves. This constraint is approached when the element spacing is nearly half a wavelength, which limits the system's overall performance. To overcome this fundamental limitation, we propose a new concept of using three-dimensional (3-D) antenna arrays, which can take advantage of the additional volume available in the vertical dimension. Particularly, we analyze the MIMO performance of 3-D arrays under different scenarios using Clarke's correlation model, and demonstrate their potential to break the DOF limit of aperture-constrained MIMO systems.

articleTitle: TM Polarized Plane Wave Scattering by a Conducting Plate with Multiple Holes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The Kirchhoff approximation (KA) is utilized to analyze electromagnetic scattering of an electromagnetic plane wave by a plate with multiple holes. Scattering far-fields are obtained by the summation of the radiation integrals due to the equivalent magnetic currents on the virtually closed surface on holes and the exterior of the plate. The accuracy of our formulations has been compared with the numerical solution, and good agreement has been confirmed to validate our formulation.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Scanning System for Pneumothorax Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the use of an electromagnetic scanning system for pneumothorax detection and classification. An 1 x 8 antenna array is distributed around the thorax, operating within the 0.49 - 1.63 GHz frequency range. Four different cases of thorax models are generated. Machine learning techniques are considered for the final classification of healthy and unhealthy cases. Simulations reveal promising results, achieving an accuracy of 75%.

articleTitle: Dual-Band, Dual-Pol Array for Ocean Salinity Measurements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper discusses the effect of the patch metal thickness on the performance of a dual-band (L/Ka), dual-pol microstip patch array to measure sea-surface salinity. The array has a 13.3 dB gain at 1.41 GHz and 12.7 dB at 31.5 GHz. It was found that the metallization thickness has a significant effect on the cross-polarization levels for the individual element and the array.

articleTitle: Adaptive Mesh Refinement Strategy for Solving Electromagnetic Radiation and Scattering
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In radiation and scattering problem, when perfectly matched layer (PML) is adopted as the truncating boundary for the infinite region exterior, the global adaptive mesh refinement (GAMR) will deteriorate the properties of the finite element (FE) matrix and increase the difficulty of solving. This paper presents a local adaptive mesh refinement (LAMR) method, which only refine the tetrahedral mesh in the non-PML computing domain and guarantees the properties of the matrix. Based on the least square method, a single tetrahedron is regarded as the minimum implementation unit for constructing posteriori error (PE) estimation, which avoids data interaction with other tetrahedrons. Since the required information is relatively concentrated, the problem of special handling at the boundary is avoided. Numerical results are presented and compared with GAMR method to illustrate the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Cell Rover: An Intracellular Antenna for Radio Communication in 3D Biological Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: An intracellular antenna can enable wireless sensing, modulation, and power transfer for electronic computation within living cells. They could also work in optically opaque environments and in vivo since they communicate using radio frequency waves. However, due to fundamental limitations in the miniaturization of conventional antennas developing an antenna which can fit inside a cell and can be possibly extended for use in vivo remains an unmet challenge. Here, we present the Cell Rover [1], a sub-mm magnetostrictive antenna which can operate wirelessly inside a living cell. Cell Rovers are acoustically actuated by an AC magnetic field and resonantly operated at low MHz frequencies, which is ideal for living systems. Cell Rovers are first characterized in air and water following which intracellular operation is demonstrated in fully opaque, Stage VI, Xenopus Laevis oocytes for which real time sensing with conventional technologies is difficult. Intracellular injection of Cell Rovers is achieved by applying a gradient magnetic field to ensure cell viability following which wireless detection is shown using a gradiometer coil assembly. We also demonstrate the possibility of using Cell Rovers for multiplexing applications to communicate with multiple antennas within the same cell or different cells.

articleTitle: A Compact Filtering Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a 4 × 4 microstrip filtering antenna array with compact size is presented. The proposed antenna array consists of three metal layers which are bonded by two substrates. The radiation patches are placed on the top layer which are fed by the feeding network on the bottom layer through the slot on the middle layer. There are no extra filtering elements in the antenna array therefore miniaturization is achieved. The return loss of the proposed antenna array is better than 10dB, and the radiation suppression is higher than 20 dB at the stopband, and the maximum gain in the passband is 14 dB.

articleTitle: A Novel Cross-Interspersed Design of Multiband Antennas for Base Station Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a dual-band dual-polarized antenna for 5G base station application. The proposed antenna avoids using the conventional interspersed technique, which causes cross-band scattering. It consists of a novel cross-interspersed configuration, and the working frequency covers low-band (LB) 690-990MHz and high-band (HB) 1810–2690 MHz bands. For demonstration, the proposed design is fabricated and measured. The dual-band prototype features stable radiation patterns with HPBW <tex>$65\pm 5^\circ$</tex> and wideband matching >10dB in the entire frequency bands of interest. Moreover, the experimental results verified that the port-to-port isolation is better than 36 dB in the operating band.

articleTitle: Tightly Coupled Vivaldi Arrays with Increased Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A tightly coupled Vivaldi array (TCVA) with increased bandwidth is introduced. Notably, this is acomplished by applying the frequency pulling technique (FPT). FPT, a new method that uses the insertion loss design methodology of bandpass filters to increase the bandwidth of antennas. Here, FPT is used to more than double the bandwidth of an infinite TCVA compared to the one of a traditional TCVA with the same profile. Infinite array simulations are performed for the proposed and traditional TCVAs, their bandwidth is calculated as <tex>$16.32:1$</tex> and <tex>$7.84:1$</tex>, respectively (for a <tex>$VSWR < 2.3$</tex>).

articleTitle: Millimeter Wave Channel Measurements and Analysis for Integrated Sensing and Communication Scenario
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: As the potential techniques to deal with increasing demands of native perception ability in the sixth generation network, integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has recently attracted a lot of attention. ISAC channel measurements and analysis have been essential and urgent. In this paper, a <tex>$4\times 8$</tex> array antenna is used to conduct channel measurement campaigns at millimeter wave frequency band in outdoor ISAC scenario. The corresponding communication channel and sensing channel of ISAC are analyzed and compared based on measurements.

articleTitle: An UWB Hyperbolic Lens-Integrated Dual-Polarized Quad-Ridged Horn Antenna for UAV-Based In-Situ Characterization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-wideband (UWB) dielectric lens-integrated quad-ridged horn antenna (QRHA) is proposed to achieve narrow beamwidth in both E and H planes throughout the frequency of operation. For instance, at 3 GHz, the beamwidth is reduced by around 50% by integrating the proposed dielectric lens. The proposed QRHA has a compact size of <tex>$190\times 160$</tex> mm<sup>2</sup>compared to other QRHA's presented in the literature. It has 2-decades of operational bandwidth from 1–20 GHz and has a unique feeding design that helps in eliminating unwanted pattern-degradation at higher frequencies. For ease of integration and stability concerns, the aperture opening of the QRHA has been calculated such that the lens can be integrated exactly on the aperture of the QRHA with a focal point that coincides with the phase center of the QRHA.

articleTitle: Advancing Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion in the IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society: An Early-Career Researcher's Perspective
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society is actively promoting diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) through the establishment of a DEI committee and initiation of several actions towards gender equity. This paper provides an early-career researcher's perspective on the current and future opportunities for advancing DEI in the field of antennas and propagation. Based on personal experience, I would like to highlight the importance of mentorship and research visibility in promoting DEI for early-career researchers, particularly those from underrepresented groups.

articleTitle: A Compact High Gain WideBand MIMO Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a new design of four-port multi-input multi-output (MIMO) antenna operating at 60 GHz is proposed for 5th generation wireless communications. The total size of MIMO antenna is only <tex>$20\times 20\times 0.508\text{mm}^{3}$</tex>. The proposed antenna exhibits an impedance bandwidth of 55.3-65.3 GHz. A maximum isolation enhancement of 16 dB is achieved in the most covered band without using any isolation coupling methods. As a result, a good average gain of 12 dBi is achieved over the operating band, with a maximum Envelope Correlation coefficient (ECC) of 0.003. The proposed antenna is a good candidate for 5G smart devices at 60 GHz.

articleTitle: Gain of LL Metaloop-n Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A metaloop antenna whose circumference, <tex>$C$</tex>, is larger than two free-space wavelengths <tex>$(C=m\lambda_{0}$</tex> with <tex>$m > 2$</tex> is designated as an LL metaloop antenna. This paper focuses on the gain of the LL metaloop antenna. Firstly, the gain is investigated under the condition that <tex>$C$</tex> is one guided wavelength: <tex>$C=m\lambda_{0}=1\lambda_{\mathrm{g}}$</tex> with <tex>$m > 2$</tex>. This gain is referred to as the reference gain. Secondly, a different situation is simulated, where an electronic component, ELC, is inserted into the large space within the loop of the LL metaloop antenna. It is found that the gain at certain sizes of the ELC is either larger or smaller than the reference gain.

articleTitle: A Fully Integrated Planar Dielectric Rod Antenna Based on SIIG Technology for mm-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article presents a mechanically stronger version of a Substrate Integrated Dielectric Rod Antenna (SIDRA) for millimeter wave (mm-wave) applications. In the proposed design, the feeding part and the radiating element are embedded in a single-layer planar substrate, thus reduces the integration complexity and production cost. Unlike the traditional SIDRA, the proposed antenna incorporates air holes on both sides of the tapered end of the dielectric rod. The effects of the rod length on the performance of the proposed antenna are also studied. The proposed SIDRA achieves a wider bandwidth, compared to conventional SIDRAs reported in the literature. Results show a -10 dB bandwidth of more than 80 GHz and a stable gain of 12 dBi in the frequency range of 130–180 GHz.

articleTitle: Prediction Method for Incident Angle Characteristics of Bistatic RCS of Reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the prediction method of bistatic radar cross section (RCS) of reflectarray. The reflectarrays have been gained attention to reduce the coverage holes for 5G. To evaluate received power from the reflectarray, bistatic RCS of incident angle is required. The Bistatic RCS of incident angle characteristics can be measured by changing the transmitter position, however, it is time consuming. This paper proposes to prediction method to reduce measurement time by the calculation process of near field and far field transformation.

articleTitle: An Integrated 5.8-GHz FMCW Phased Array Doppler Radar Utilizing Wideband Miniaturized TX/RX Patch Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A 5.8-GHz integrated FMCW phased array Doppler radar utilizing wideband miniaturized patch transmit and receive (TX/RX) antenna arrays is presented for object localization and range detection applications. The system consists of a core 5.8-GHz sensor chip including a homodyne 8-element array receiver with maximum gain of 47 dB, a 4-element transmitter array with maximum EIRP of 26 dBm and a signal generation unit with a maximum FMCW bandwidth of 275 MHz. Two 2×4 (RX) and 1×4 (TX) antenna arrays are fabricated to cover the required FMCW bandwidth and maintain 70 dB of TX-to-RX antenna isolation for proper target detection up to 6m away from the radar. A maximum <tex>$+/-50^{\circ}$</tex> of field-of-view is achieved by beam steering capability of the phased array transceiver radar. The number of RX antenna elements are considered twice the TX array to enhance the receiver gain and sensitivity.

articleTitle: MoM Modeling of Thin Wires with Finite Conductivity for Radio Astronomy Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: An overview of published surface impedance approximations for round conductors is presented. Including finite conductivity in a Galerkin Method of Moments Mixed Potential Integral equation formulation is discussed, and verification results shown. A apparently non-physical effect is noted for wire dipoles beyond the first anti-resonance.

articleTitle: A Modulated Reactance Spherical Surface Cloak for 3-D Invisibility
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Toward practical 3-D invisibility, passive spherical surface cloaking applicable to large, freestanding scatterers is presented. Characterized by a spatially modulated impenetrable tensor surface reactance, a spherical surface cloak converts the incident plane wave on the lit side into surface waves that carry power to the shadow side. Leaky waves of planar wavefronts are continuously shed in the forward direction to remove the shadow behind the sphere. Numerical design and simulation of a 4-wavelength-radius spherical cloak confirm the effectiveness in minimizing scattering in all directions.

articleTitle: PCB Based Modulated Scatter with Enhanced Modulation Depth
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The modulated scatterer technique (MST) has shown promise for applications in microwave imaging, electric field mapping, and materials characterization. Traditionally, MST scatterers are dipoles centrally loaded with an element capable of modulation (e.g., a PIN diode). By modulating the load element state, the scattered fields are also modulated. However, due to the small size of such scatterers, it can be difficult to reliably detect the response. Increasing the modulation depth (MD) of the scattered signal may improve detectability. This paper presents simulations and measurements of PCB-based MST elements that, through reactive loading, are designed to be electrically invisible during the reverse bias state of the modulated element (a PIN diode in this case) while producing detectable scattering during the forward bias state. The results show a significant (<tex>$>$</tex> 90%) improvement in the MD of the scattered signal when compared to a traditional MST scatterer.

articleTitle: An SIE Formulation With Loop Analysis for Large-Scale Arbitrarily Shaped Interconnects
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A magneto-quasi-static (MQS) surface integral equation (SIE) formulation with loop analysis is proposed to extract the impedance of interconnects in packages. The loop analysis is developed with an independent and complete set of unknowns according to the graph theory, which can significantly reduce the dimension of the final matrix. With the pre-corrected fast Fourier Transform (pFFT), large-scale interconnects can be efficiently modelled. A practical example in packages is carried out to validate the effectiveness and scalability of the proposed formulation. Results show that the proposed formulation is accurate and flexible to model complex interconnects in packages compared with the industrial solver.

articleTitle: Wireless Sensing with Software Defined Radio
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the application of using software defined radio (SDR) and surface acoustic wave (SAW) devices for wireless measurement of the response of in-situ sensors. In the proposed system, SDR collects magnitude and phase of the reflected waves from a SAW device connected to a sensor. The spectral-domain data is then converted to time-domain to extract the sensor responses. By comparing the results obtained from SDR with those obtained from a commercial vector network analyzer (VNA), we show the accuracy of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: An EFIE-TD Solver for Thin-wire Structures with Time-varying Loads
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Time-varying discrete loads in antennas/scatterers are used to introduce remarkable electromagnetic properties in comparison to their unloaded counterparts. To further explore these capabilities, an efficient numerical procedure to include time-varying passive loads for thin-wire structures modeled by means of an electric-field time-domain integral-equation (EFIE-TD) is presented in this work. The passive loads in this framework are solved by using a transient modified nodal analysis (MNA) technique. Numerical results illustrates remarkable effects of these structures, such as a non-linear frequency redistribution of source energy which effectively integrates mixer and antenna properties in a single device.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Two Bluetooth Antennas for Biomedical Device Using Ansys
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Two novel Bluetooth antenna designs are presented and compared in the paper. Both patterns can be laser-direct-structuring (LDS) printed on the inner surface of a specific industry-oriented structure. As the designs are potentially applied for a biomedical device which has very compact volume and light weight, a precisely defined simulation model of human body is required for accurate simulation results through the design procedures. Two designs have different relative orientations to the human body, from which the influence of the human body on antenna performance can be compared in two scenarios. Return losses, total efficiencies, and radiation patterns are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Wideband Multi-Port Network Based on Printed-RGW for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel multi-port interferometer circuit using four rounded 90° couplers based on Printed Ridge Gap Waveguide (PRGW) technology is presented in this paper. The work is focused on designing the low-loss and wideband multi-port network to easily integrate with millimeter-wave (mm-wave) receiver antennas for 5G applications. The simulated results assessed with full-wave computer simulation technology (CST) show the presented multi-port design covers a wide frequency bandwidth of around 8 GHz at the center frequency of 28 GHz with excellent phase resolution at four output ports, which completely meets the needed features for future high-data-rate wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Transparent MIMO Antenna for Closely Spaced Antenna Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The development of a metal mesh transparent MIMO antenna with closely spaced transparent square patch elements has been presented. A square lattice structure is used to design the conductive metal used in metal mesh antennas and has been fabricated with conductive metal wired metal to achieve 83% transparency. The closely spaced transparent antenna elements are isolated by a novel transparent thin decoupling structure. The transparent metal mesh conductors are printed on a 1mm thick transparent Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) substrate, which consists of a stack of 10 layers and each layer has a thickness of 0.1 mm. CST Microwave Studio is used to design, analyze and optimize the proposed antenna.

articleTitle: An Accurate Method for Modeling High-Order Mandelbrot Fractal Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a method for two-dimensional Mandelbrot fractal programmatic modeling is proposed. Compared with the existing similar method, this method has a faster speed, higher accuracy, and full removal of manual operation. It not only solves the problem that it is usually difficult to accurately model and simulate the Mandelbrot fractal structures, but also further solves the problem of modeling more complicated Mandelbrot fractals with larger iteration numbers. The method can lay a foundation for the automatic optimization simulation of two-dimensional Mandelbrot fractal antenna. The method is based on MATLAB programming and can be easily applied to the well-known ANSYS HFSS and AutoCAD.

articleTitle: Design of Huygens' Cells for Transmit-Reflect-Arrays at 30 GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, it is demonstrated that Huygens' metasurfaces can achieve equi-amplitude reflected and trans-mitted waves and a <tex>$360^{\circ}$</tex> phase coverage in transmission and reflection, when illuminated by a normal plane wave. To exploit this property, a procedure for designing unit-cells of transmit-reflect-arrays is presented. First, the optimal surface parameters are analytically determined. N ext, the design at 30 G Hz of four cells with three patterned layers, compatible with printed circuit board technology, is presented. These cells operate with a maximum phase error of a <tex>$10^{\circ}$</tex> over a 5 % relative bandwidth at the operating frequency, thus realizing a uniform 2-bit phase quantization in transmission and reflection.

articleTitle: 300 GHz On-Chip Horn Antenna with WR-03 to SIW Transition Using Integrated Passive Device
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an on-chip H-plane horn antenna operating at 300 GHz is proposed and simulated. The antenna is realized on the integrated passive device (IPD) process, fed from a WR03-to-substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) transition. The transition comprises a stepped waveguide section, a coupling aperture, and a substrate integrated waveguide section. The integrated passive device (IPD) process selects the intrinsic Gallium arsenide (GaAs) as the carrier substrate. The chip is integrated with an aluminum split-block for measurement purpose using a standard WR-03 waveguide. The simulated Sparameter reveals a reflection coefficient of -12.4 dB at 300 GHz. The antenna achieves a realized gain of 6.4 dBi and a radiation efficiency of 62%. The aluminum housing significantly suppresses the broadside/back radiation and fulfills the desired end-fire pattern with front to back ratio of 11.5 dB.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Metasurface Synthesis from Far-Field Masks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A neural network is developed to infer the required tangential fields on the output face of the metasurface so as to meet mask-based far-field (FF) design constraints. Full-wave simulation is performed to evaluate the performance of omega-bianisotropic metasurfaces designed based on this approach.

articleTitle: A S/Ka Dual-Band Shared-Aperture Circularly Polarized Antenna Combining Spiral Antenna and Substrate Integrated Waveguide Slot Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper represents a dual-band shared-aperture circularly polarized antenna with a large frequency ratio. Based on the concept of structure reuse, the spiral antenna combined with the slot array antenna achieves the high aperture reuse efficiency. The spiral antenna operated at 2.75 GHz has the advantages of circular polarization and wide bandwidth. To realize the circular polarization of the slot array antenna, a pair of <tex>$+45^{\circ}/-45^{\circ}$</tex> linearly polarized slot arrays operated at 27 GHz is employed based on the substrate integrated waveguide (SIW). In order to widen the bandwidth of the slot array antenna, two slots are regarded as one unit to generate multiple resonance points. The upper-frequency radiators will affect the radiation of the lower-frequency radiator. Therefore, the inner diameter of the spiral antenna and the position of the slot array antenna should be designed together to avoid the main radiation area of the spiral antenna being blocked. The results show that the antenna proposed obtains impedance bandwidths of 33 % and 12.2 % with the peak gains of 4.6 dBi and 12.8 dBi at the corresponding bands.

articleTitle: Spectral Projection Model Applied to Electromagnetic Scattering from Dielectric Cylinders with Arbitrary Cross-Sections
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In 2019, a new technique named the Spectral Projection Model (SPM) was formulated by the Remote Sensing Group at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, as an alternate approach to Method of Moments to estimate the fields due to the scattering of electromagnetic waves from arbitrary cylindrical conducting surfaces [1]. SPM evolved from the decomposition of the Green's function in the electric field integral equation (EFIE) for describing the boundary conditions. The decomposition of the Green's function is implemented using the addition theorem for Hankel and Bessel functions. In this paper, the technique is extended to scattering from dielectric cylinders with arbitrary cross-sections. The far field patterns are calculated and compared with results using the modal expansion technique. Simulations are performed for cylinders of arbitrary radii with both TM and TE polarization and compared with the results from the modal expansion technique to study the method's accuracy.

articleTitle: 360° Single/Dual-Beam Steering of an EBG Encircled Monopole Antenna by Controlling Ground Surface Currents
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A monopole antenna encircled by an EBG ring is proposed for 360° beam steering with single-and dual-beam modes by controlling the currents on a ground. The monopole is located at the center of the square ground. The EBG ring is formed with 15 identical mushroom-like unit cells. The radiation beams are formed, and their directions are changed as the direction of the traveling surface current on the ground plane is controlled by combining the on/off states of the EBG unit cells. Simulated and measured results show the proposed antenna operating at 2.45-GHz band achieves single-beam scanning with 24° resolution and dual opposite beam scanning.

articleTitle: Compact Flexible Heart Rate Monitor Simulations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Cardiovascular disease is a global health concern; heart rate monitors can help assess cardiac health. Sensors must be effective and non-invasive. This project develops and characterizes flexible substrate antennas for heart beat detection through reflection coefficient measurements. Antenna substrate printing and sensor applications are through external collaborations. The project includes curved ground plane and substrate HFSS models to determine reflection coefficient responses to chest expansions.

articleTitle: Towards Accelerating the Feed Design of a Series of Different Reflector Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We introduce a surrogate-based model to reduce the simulation and design time of the full system radiation pattern of a reflector antenna. The technique is applied in the context where feeds are to be designed for a series of similar, but different, reflector antenna systems. One reflector system is selected as the reference antenna, and its pattern is completely simulated over the required design space. The resulting information is used to inform the design of other reflectors, which are simulated only sparsely in their design space. In this paper, we show that the reference antenna could have a different focal distance compared to the original antenna and that a single reflector antenna could be used as a reference for a dual reflector system.

articleTitle: Recent Developments in mm-Wave Tomographic and Radar Imaging for Breast Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this contribution, some of the main results of millimeter-wave imaging for breast cancer diagnosis using both radar and tomographic approaches are presented. In addition, the idea of using a dual-step approach for reconstructing the dielectric profile of the anomaly using the morphological information provided by the faster and computationally less expensive radar approach is presented.

articleTitle: Isogeometric Analysis for the Scattering of NURBS Surfaces with Coinciding Knots
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper first introduces and addresses the discontinuity problem in isogeometric analysis (IGA) for nonuniform rational B-spline (NURBS) surfaces. Herein, we focus on solving the scattering problem of the perfect electric conductor (PEC) based on the electric field integral equation (EFIE). This discontinuity problem arises from the coinciding knots in the knot vectors of NURBS surfaces, where the NURBS basis functions have a reduced differentiable continuity. The basis functions with reduced continuity may dissatisfy the div-conforming requirements in the EFIE and finally lead to the wrong simulation. To address this problem, this work split the surfaces at the coinciding knots by inserting the knots repeatedly and making the one-to-one correspondence for the two sets of basis functions at the splitting interface. Numerical results demonstrate the validity and accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Coupling-Robust Sensing System Based on Nonlinear Parity-Time-Symmetry Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We propose a system based on a nonlinear Parity-time-symmetry circuit. By adjusting the loss of the passive oscillator, the system can still work near the exceptional point even when the coupling changes. The experiment proves that the signal-to-noise ratio of the output signal of this system is robust to the change of wireless coupling coefficient while maintaining extremely high sensitivity. Compared with the commercial envelope detector sensing method, the signal-to-noise ratio of the output signal is improved by up to 14 dB under minimal coupling conditions.

articleTitle: Ultra High Sensitive Neural Recorder with Additive Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Neuronal activity recordings are essential for evaluating and understanding the brain's function and possible neurological disorders. In this paper, we present a first of a kind 3D additive manufactured sensor for recording biopotentials in a battery-less and wireless manner. This was done by establishing an RF link between the implanted device and an exterior interrogator. The associated antennas are designed and optimized to achieve the best performance in communicating through the skin. In addition, the antennas and matching circuit are integrated in a multilayer design to decrease the footprint by 52%. The first fabricated prototype shows good agreement with simulations with less than 3dB of discrepancy in manufactured phantom to emulate the skull's skin properties. The proposed implant design offers a 10-fold increase as compared to previous wireless and battery-less brain implant recorders.

articleTitle: Conformal Slot Antenna Array Fed by Metal Gap Waveguide/Cavity for Multi-Beam Radiation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A two-dimensional circularly cylindrical phased array of waveguide slot antennas is presented for beam steering applications. Each column waveguide (WG) slot array is equally spaced to radiate linearly polarized electromagnetic fields, which are horizontally conformal to a circular boundary for circular beam steering. The beamforming network (BFN) is designed interior to the circular boundary, which is formed by metal gap WGs and cavities for high-efficiency array excitations. Due to the noncontact nature of the gap WG BFN to the WG slot antennas, the WG BFN can be rotated by a motor to switch the beam directions, extending the coverage range. This antenna array is realized at Ku-band for microwave links with low radiation losses. Full-wave simulation results are shown to demonstrate the radiation characteristics and validate the feasibility.

articleTitle: A Circular Millimeter-Wave Printed Ridge-gap-Waveguide Crossover
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A circular millimeter-wave crossover based on printed-ridge-gap waveguide structure is proposed and designed. It is constructed by an easy-built structure consisting of a circular junction etched by four fan-shaped EBG units. A crossover working at 28GHz is designed to provide a 14.6% of the bandwidth regarding 0.5 dB insertion loss, which could be a good candidate component for the 5G Millimeter-wave beamforming network applications.

articleTitle: A High Gain Wide Beam U-Slot Elliptical Microstrip Patch Antenna for Phased Array Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A high gain and a wide beam U-Slot Elliptical Microstrip Patch Antenna(USEMPA) for phased array antenna (PAA) as required for radar applications is presented. This paper presents the design procedure of the USEMPA operating in the X-band. The antenna element proposed has a low profile and is easy to fabricate. The element shape is chosen and optimized to achieve a compact form factor much lesser than a half wavelength to minimize the mutual coupling effects. This also helps in blind mating the transceivers directly to the elements in an active PAA. The −10dB impedance bandwidth of the USEMPA is approximately 1GHz. The gain of the single element is 6.3dBi. This element is extended to a 4 × 4 array and is fabricated on RT Duroid 5880 substrate. The fabricated USEMPA 16-element array shows a scan volume of ±60° over a bandwidth of 1GHz. The gain of the 16-element array is 18.56dBi. The mutual coupling between any two elements of the fabricated USEMPA 16-element array is < −18 dB. Simulated and measured results are in close agreement.

articleTitle: Optimized UHF Patch Antenna for Cryospheric Communications on Europa
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: To search for extraterrestrial life, a semi-autonomous, thermo-nuclear powered cryobot has been designed to penetrate the 20–50 km of cryogenic ice surrounding the inner ocean of the Jovian moon, Europa. Several cryospheric (in ice) communication schemes have been devised to relay critical science data from the cyrobot to a surface station. One such system is a relay system of transceiver “pucks” that are released from the cyrobot as it burrows through the ice. These relays form a wireless network connecting the cyrobot and surface station. In this paper a circularly polarized, circular patch antenna with a matching layer is designed and optimized for cyrospheric communications as the physical layer of the puck relay network. A hybrid theoretical and simulation based design technique is presented, and predicted parameters achieve good agreement with compared measurements.

articleTitle: Full-Wave Simulation of a 10,000-Element Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface with a Single Workstation Computer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Nowadays, extensive research conducted on electromagnetic materials has led to many innovative devices and systems. While the potentials of advanced materials and their applications are appealing, it is often difficult to model them accurately by computational methods due to the inherently multiscale, complex structures involved. We propose a metamaterial Green's function with the geometry-aware domain decomposition method for modeling complex, heterogeneous materials. The outcome results in quasi-sublinear algorithms, in which the computational complexity does not depend on the microscopic size of metamaterial structures. The results have the potential to make the high-fidelity analysis of metamaterials and metasurfaces orders of magnitude faster.

articleTitle: Design and Modeling of the SuperDARN HF Log Periodic Array at the South Pole
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: SuperDARN is a network of some 35 high-frequency (HF) Doppler radars located in the high-latitude and midlatitude regions of the northern and southern hemispheres. The radars detect backscatter from ionospheric electron density irregularities and deduce various parameters. This paper will discuss replacement of the present array consisting of 20 HF horizontal log periodic antennas at the South Pole. These current log periodic antennas cover a frequency range of 8 to 20 MHz and maximize radiation in takeoff angles from 5 to 35 degrees. The present antennas have backlobes in the same takeoff angular sector only down 10 to 15 dB from the front main beam. It is desirable to have a much higher rejection of the backlobes (more than 25 dB) that will be shown is possible with new design methods. Furthermore, the new design will incorporate crossed-diagonal dipole elements to provide polarization measurements that are not found in any of the other SuperDARN systems around the world. The log periodic dipole elements will be formed from wires supported by insulated catenary cables and a system of support towers. Extensive modeling results are shown using FEKO antenna software for antenna performance characteristics of VSWR, gain, radiation patterns, polarization, etc.

articleTitle: Broadband Green's Function-Multiple Scattering Theory for Fast Band Solutions of Vector Electromagnetic Waves in 3D Perioidc Strutures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We extend the Broadband Green's function-Multiple Scattering Theory (BBGF-MST) approach to 3D problems of vector electromagnetic waves in periodic structures. A feature of BBGF is that the lattice Green's functions are broadband so that the coefficients of the vector spherical wave expansions are calculated rapidly for many frequencies. These are then used for speedy broadband calculations of the matrix elements of the KKR (Korringa-Kohn-Rostoker) eigenvalue equation. For the first two bands, the dimension of the KKR matrix equation is only 6 by 6. BBGF facilitates the calculations of the matrix elements for 5000 frequencies in 2.89 seconds. With this method, the band eigenvalues in vector 3D problems are computed in 2.89 second on a standard laptop for the first 2 bands. Results are illustrated and the lowest band solution has good agreement with that of the Maxwell-Garnett mixing formula at low frequency.

articleTitle: Metasurfaces for Broadband Analog Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Analog computing using metasurfaces offers significant potential for processing information at ultrahigh speeds and low power consumption. Among several operations, implementing spatial differentiation and edge detection with metasurfaces is an active area of research for its potential impact in the automotive industry and for image recognition. However, current designs have been suffering from limitations due to trade-offs between bandwidth, spatial resolution and efficiency. In this work, dispersion engineering of a nonlocal metasurface is leveraged to obtain analog edge detection over a moderately large operational bandwidth, without sacrificing numerical aperture and efficiency. We demonstrate the implementation of this concept by using a single-layered silicon metasurface with triangular lattice of holes, which exhibits dual-polarization and azimuthally isotropic response up to large numerical apertures (NAs ∼0.35), and with an operational bandwidth of 5 THz around a central wavelength of about 1500 nm. The proposed design approach can also be extended to other platforms, operational frequencies and materials.

articleTitle: A Low Profile Improved Gain SIW-Based H-Plane Horn Antenna for X-Band Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW)-based H-plane horn antenna with enhanced gain made on a very thin substrate (0.009λ0) is proposed for X-band application. Improved impedance matching is obtained by implementing three stepped quarter-wave transformers in the feed section and four circular slots at the front of the horn. Two rows of teflon vias are used to enhance the gain, and the corrugated wall technique is also implemented to improve other antenna radiation characteristics. The measured fractional impedance bandwidth of 5.22%, the gain of 10.82 dBi, the radiation efficiency of 88.56%, the front-to-back ratio of ≈15 dB, and the low cross-polarization level have been achieved at 10.71 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact 2-by-2 Horn Slot Antenna Array Fed by Printed Ridge Gap Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a 2-by-2 horn slot antenna array at X-band. Metamaterial concepts are applied to the antenna design using printed ridge gap waveguide (PRGW) technology as a magnetic ground for the antenna array, which is excited by a 1-to-4 power divider. Each of the array power-divider branches excites a slot, while maintaining the impedance bandwidth of the original unloaded power divider. Directive horn antennas are used to control sidelobe levels and increase the gain. Simulation results demonstrate an impedance bandwidth of 23% and a gain of 12.7 dBi at 10 GHz, which is a significant improvement compared to an impedance bandwidth of less than 14% and a gain of 9.7 dBi for the antenna array without the horns.

articleTitle: Temperature-Based Performance of Millimeter-Wave Antenna-In-Package
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Advances in millimeter-wave (mm-wave) electronic circuits enable the integration of entire transmitter/receiver radio modules in a single chip or system on chip (SoC). SoC and the introduction of antenna-in-package (AiP) technology facilitate the integration of transmit and receive modules in a single packaged solution. With new developments in materials and processes in <tex>$\text{AiP}$</tex> technology, the operating frequency range can shift to values greater than 100 GHz. One important aspect to consider in the design of mm-wave <tex>$\mathbf{AiP}$</tex> is the temperature effects on the dielectric substrates of the antenna. In this paper, we introduce a broadband E-Shaped patch (ESP) antenna integrated in a flip-chip enhanced quad flat no leads (FCeQFN) package with silicon die, working in the WR8 band (90–140 GHz) with simulations results comparing the <tex>$\text{AiP}$</tex> performance when substrates are exposed to <tex>$23^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> and <tex>$150^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Analysis of Transmit Piano Board Based Metasurface Illuminated by a Dual Polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a transmit electromagnetic surface based on piano board configuration, which can realize two different multi-beam radiation patterns with orthogonal polarizations independently. A Dual Linearly Polarized (DLP) microstrip antenna is designed to excite the metasurface with a 27 GHz to 29 GHz operating frequency band. The structure made by combining the DLP antenna and the transmit metasurface can produce the specified radiations.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Angular Stability of an FSS Based on the Geometry of Open Asymmetrical Trapezoidal Rings
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper investigates the angular stability of a FSS based on the geometry of open asymmetrical trapezoidal rings. The initial equations for the first and second resonant frequencies were presented. An FSS prototype was fabricated and characterized, verifying a good agreement between the numerical and measured results. The FSS showed angular stability for incidence angles of up to 30°. In addition, a comparison was made between the initial equations and the numerical and measured results, showing a maximum percentage difference of 6.25%, which is a good result.

articleTitle: Design of a Monolithic Monocone and Radome with a Conical Skirt Ground
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A wideband monocone antenna is designed for monolithic fabrication in additive manufacturing with an elliptical radome. To enhance gain pattern stability, the ground plane is modified with a conical skirt shape. The final design demonstrates a bandwidth of 7–40 GHz with a -3 dBi field of view from 62° to 102°. Two types of manufacturing resins are used in the development of this antenna and their impact on impedance and radiation characteristics examined.

articleTitle: Anomalous Reflection or Refraction Based on Transmissive Metagratings with Few Meta-Atoms
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We propose the design of transmissive printed circuit board (PCB) metagratings with few number of meta-atoms to achieve extreme-angle anomalous reflection or refraction under normal incidence. Based on this, two metagrating prototypes with 70° anomalous reflection and 80° anomalous refraction under normal incidence are designed. The simulation results show a highly efficient extreme beam deflection, which can be a good alternative for future beamforming applications.

articleTitle: Dual Band Independent Phase-Shift Control Reconfigurable Transmitarray Unit Cell
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band independent phase-shift electronically reconfigurable miniature wide band unit cell has been demonstrated for Ku-band. The transmitter layer (M1) exploits two metal patches containing two pin diodes for each lower and higher frequency patch. The receiver layer (M4) includes a pair of passive metal patches at the receiver end that resonates independent frequency bands for lower and higher frequency bands. Four magnetic dipoles are engrave on a single unit cell for low and high frequency bands. Four metal layers reduce the complexity and manufacturing cost of the unit cell. A novel technique with magnetic dipoles helps to miniaturize the unit-cell and diminish the mutual coupling between lower and higher frequency patches. Moreover, four parasitic patches with magnetic dipoles enhance the unit cell's overall bandwidth. Four states of transmission coefficient (S21) are obtainable for independent phase shift for each lower and higher frequency band. The higher band realized a minimum transmission coefficient up to 0.59 dB more than 1.09 GHz bandwidth. In contrast, the lower band exhibits minimum transmission coefficient up to 0.68 dB and 1.27 GHz bandwidth, approximately due to low inter mutual coupling between patches. Thus, 1-Bit independent phase-shift attained for both higher and lower frequency bands.

articleTitle: Mechanically Reconfigurable Helix in a Feedback Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We report a feedback oscillator tuned by a helical structure whose compression or extension is actuated mechanically: a spring-tuned oscillator. The oscillator consists of a reconfigurable helix antenna as a feedback element, a power amplifier, and a directional coupler. The fundamental and higher harmonics tune monotonically in two length regimes (compression and extension) demarcated by one in which its output is unstable. The circuit has potential applications both directly and as a scale model of a sub-millimeter-wave active sensor that can wirelessly report local mechanical strain and vibration: Wireless reporting is demonstrated using the helix itself as the circuit's antenna.

articleTitle: An Overview of Novel Antennas Manufactured via Charge-Programmed Multi-Material 3D Printing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Charge-programmed multi-material (CPMM) 3D printing is a unique additive manufacturing technology that emerged recently and has shown promise in manufacturing innovative antennas. With CPMM printing, conductive materials such as copper can be selectively deposited on specified areas of the supporting structure, thus making it possible to develop antennas with intricate 3D structures and (or) interpenetrated metal and dielectric. In this invited paper, we provide an overview of the recent novel antenna developments at the University of California Los Angeles (UCLA) enabled by the CPMM printing method. This includes lightweight multi-layer transmitarrays for beam collimation and beam steering applications in K-band, as well as a monolithic K-band septum horn antenna.

articleTitle: Dielectric Resonance Modes Effect on Enhancing the Rx-Sensitivity in Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) RF Coil
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Dielectric resonators with Ultra-High Dielectric Constant (uHDC) materials possess intrinsic resonance modes which can be employed in the design of transceiver coils for magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) applications. The resonance modes and conditions of the uHDC discs were studied through computer simulations. We compared the magnetic field and Rx-sensitivity when employing cylindrical uHDC discs at both resonant and non-resonant conditions. We showed in this work, to achieve the maximum focusing of the magnetic field into the phantom, the design with uHDC material should operate around the first TE01δ mode and lower than the second mode with the highest permittivity.

articleTitle: A Passive Phased Array Antenna for SatCom in K- and Ka-Band with Low-Loss Power Distribution Circuit in Hollow Waveguide Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A new design of a phased array antenna module in hollow waveguide technology is presented for SatCom in K- and Ka-band. It includes a new transition from a coplanar waveguide structure on a PCB to the supplying ridged waveguides of the antenna module. The transition reveals a high return- and low insertion loss and enables both feeding and terminating, thereby measuring its radiation patterns. The measured realized patterns show values of up to 25 dBi for the complete phased array which is in good agreement with simulations.

articleTitle: Radar Change Detection in the Time Domain
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We develop novel wave scattering principles and illustrate their application to the important problem of detecting changes or scatterers in a general background medium. The derived theory and algorithms are developed directly in the time domain, and are applicable to the analysis and processing of pulsed radar data. Envisioned applications include the detection and localization of silent threats, e.g., intrusion detection, in indoor facilities, tunnels, and caves. Of particular interest is the detection of changes in areas where radar surveillance is necessary due to practical inaccessibility via other sensing modalities such as video cameras.

articleTitle: Wallops Flight Facility 2021‐2022 Winter Snow Events: A Case Study Using Surface Instrumentation and Radars
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a case study that showcases the analysis of four snowstorms that occurred during the winter season of 2021‐2022 at Wallops Flight Facility. The study includes data collection and analysis from various instruments ranging from delicate optical, electronic, and mechanical surface instrumentation to state-of-the-art radars. Surface observations of geometrical and microphysical properties of winter precipitation coupled with radar scattering measurements and computations are crucial for the advancement of our understanding of snow events, numerical weather prediction models, and correct interpretation of data from the national network of weather radars.

articleTitle: A Millimeter-Wave Wideband Dielectric Resonator Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, we proposed a novel aperture-fed dielectric resonator (DR) antenna (DRA) to achieve wideband performance in the millimeter wave (mmW) band. Different from the traditional aperture feeding mechanism, the coupling aperture under the DR is comparable to it. This arrangement helps produce a wideband antenna element. At the same time, a parasitic metallic patch is placed on the top of the DR to further expand the bandwidth and reduce the overall profile. To facilitate the gain enhancement, a <tex>$4\times 4$</tex> antenna array is implemented. The simulated results show that it can achieve a wide impedance bandwidth of 37% from 25.1 to 36.5 GHz.
