Throughout the whole operating bandwidth, stable radiation patterns with low levels of cross-polarization can be observed.

articleTitle: A Full-Duplex MIMO Antenna for Integrated Sensing and Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposed a full-duplex antenna for multi-input multi-output (MIMO) communication that applies circularly-polarization for transmitting and linearly-polarization for receiving, respectively. With this non-orthogonal Tx and Rx polarization, it is useful for applications of integrated sensing and communication, as well as producing simplified residual coupling signals. By incorporating resonance structures and decoupling networks, residual coupling signals could be easily eliminated. The proposed antenna comprises two channels constructed on a 2-by-3 patch array within an aperture of <tex>$2.03\lambda 0^{*}0.91\lambda_{0}$</tex>. Simulation results show that it achieved both MIMO and duplex isolation more than 59 dB, as well as realized gain of 5.92 dBi for Tx and 10.43 dBi for Rx over a 130 MHz band centered at 5.8 GHz.

articleTitle: Calculating Wideband Far Fields at Wide Angles via Planar Near Fields from Time Domain Simulations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Planar near field measurement techniques provide numerous advantages for the characterization high-gain antennas and phased arrays including reduced test volume, high signal-to-noise, stationary test antennas, and efficient far field transforms. However, modern communication systems require the adaptation of these techniques to determine the radiated far fields of the test antenna over multi-GHz frequency ranges and wide fields of view. A single time domain simulation yielding broadband planar near fields from a Ka-band conical horn antenna is presented. Control scripts were developed to generate over four thousand broadband ideal PNF probes and to export the complex simulated near field data from each one in CST Microwave Studio. The radiated far fields at one thousand frequency points spanning 34–44 GHz were calculated from the 2D Fourier transform and compared with far fields sampled from the same simulation to validate this method.

articleTitle: A Thin Transparent Phase Correction Surface for Patch Antenna Gain Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Antenna gain can be increased significantly by achieving a uniform phase distribution in its electric near-field. Phase correction must be implemented to the non-uniform field radiated by the antenna to compensate for the phase variations and create a uniform radiated field phase front. This paper demonstrates the gain enhancement of a simple circularly polarized patch antenna by using a thin, low-cost, passive phase-correcting surface (PCS). The PCS consists of only three metal-dielectric layers and uses thin substrates separated by air gaps of only <tex>$0.16\lambda_{0}$</tex>. The gain enhancement of 11 dB has been demonstrated for a simple patch antenna with a maximum gain of 18.4 dBi at 20GHz. The designed antenna is planar with a bandwidth of 600MHz.

articleTitle: An HF Magnetoelectric Dipole Element
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel antenna element is introduced that is suitable for high frequency (HF) applications. Namely, we propose a high frequency magnetoelectric dipole (HFMD) antenna with superior electromagnetic characteristics compared to state-of-the-art HF antennas. Notably, the proposed design is inspired by the traditional magnetoelectric dipole (MED) antenna and is properly modified to satisfy all the stringent HF electromagnetic and mechanical requirements of wide bandwidth, high efficiency, and low design complexity. Full-wave simulations are conducted demonstrating a bandwidth of 45%, which is almost two times greater than the BW of traditional HF monopole antennas.

articleTitle: A Ferromagnetic-Resonance Based Electrically Small Antenna with Circular Polarization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A circularly polarized electrically small antenna (ka=O.176) based on ferromagnetic resonance is presented at 3.352 GHz, with a radiation efficiency of 12.36%, realized gain of -7.13 dB, and a cross-polarization ratio of 35.91 dB. Because the resonant frequency of the antenna can be rapidly changed with the biased magnetic field, the design has the potential to be integrated with direct antenna modulation for realizing a large efficiency-bandwidth product on electrically small antenna.

articleTitle: Equivalent Circuit Analysis of an Open-Ended Slot Type RFID Tag Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we discuss UHF (RAIN) RFID tags with open-ended slot type antennas. We show that such tags can be analyzed using the same equivalent circuit that represents T-matched dipole tags. We explore the correspondence between slot type tag antenna geometry and its equivalent circuit parameters. We also present a practical <tex>$80\ \text{mm}\times 25\ \text{mm}$</tex> RFID tag example with good agreement between model and measurements.

articleTitle: Low Rank Direct Finite Element Solvers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A low-rank direct domain decomposition method (LR-D<sup>3</sup>M) is proposed. The proposed method couples the memory efficient direct domain decomposition method with single-level rank-revealing numerical linear algebra algorithms to produce a scalable direct solver suitable for the finite element (FEM) analysis of Maxwell's equations in the frequency domain. Through numerical experiments, the method was found to be error controllable with low memory footprint and approximate <tex>$O(N^{1.5})$</tex> factorization complexity in both memory and time for 3D problems of increasing electrical size up to 6.2 million unknowns.

articleTitle: Optimization of Non-Linear Feeds to Broadband Radiating Systems Using Transient Port-Extraction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The ability to optimize transient systems comprising broadband electromagnetic (EM) devices fed by strongly non-linear circuits is of great interest in a number of design applications. However, existing techniques to optimize these systems are computationally infeasible for large-scale problems due primarily to the cost associated with solving the EM system. In this work, we propose a model order reduction technique based around transient port extraction to efficiently optimize a non-linear EM-circuit system. We show through numerical results that our method agrees with a traditional self-consistent solve, while being less computationally expensive.

articleTitle: ML-enabled Resonance Prediction for SGP-Based WPT
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the effective use of a machine learning-based approach in predicting the resonance of slotted ground plane (SGP) resonators. The resonance prediction model was developed employing a convolution neural network (CNN) and images. In particular, a synthetic dataset based on the surface current distribution plots of designed SGP resonators. As a result, the trained CNN-based model demonstrated the 94% accuracy in the resonant frequency prediction. Finally, it is imperative to note that the resonance values for simulation, experimental, and prediction are in good consonance.

articleTitle: Fully Metallic 3D-Printed Omnidirectional High-Gain Array Antenna for 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel omnidirectional high-gain array antenna operating at 5G-NR band based on fully metallic 3D printing technology. Radiation units consist of V-shaped slots. And open-ended sleeves are applied to the air-filled coaxial line. Omnidirectional radiation pattern is achieved by the modes of open-ended sleeves, and this array antenna presents a high-directivity beam at boresight direction. To verify the performance of proposed design, a prototype is fabricated. The measured results demonstrate wide impendence bandwidth of 19.5% (3.20 GHz to 3.89 GHz) and peak gain of 8.13 dBi with radiation efficiency of 99.2%, which are well matched with the simulated results.

articleTitle: A Compact Self-Duplex Antenna For Wireless Capsule Endoscopic Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a compact out-of-band duplex antenna for the simultaneous data transmission and reception of capsule endoscopic devices. The proposed antenna involves two slotted semi-circular patches with a 0.4 mm gap. It operates at 1.85 GHz and 2.4 GHz with an isolation level of better than 26 dB. This antenna is designed and optimized in the center of a homogeneous muscle box with an implantation depth of 62 mm. This antenna has compact geometry of 3.67 mm<sup>3</sup>. The miniaturization techniques involve shorting pins and capacitive slots. Good isolation between the transmitting and receiving ports is obtained by keeping a gap of 0.6 mm between them. The main features of this antenna include compact dimensions, high isolation between the ports, and its ability to transmit and receive data simultaneously. Due to these features, the proposed antenna is suitable for implantable devices if two-way communication is required.

articleTitle: Hybrid Fourier Neural Network in Solving 2D Electrodynamic Equations in Multilayer Media
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Numerical simulation of electromagnetic (EM) wave propagation in multilayer media is essential for many EM applications. This paper explores a data-driven machine learning neural network, Unet-Fourier neural network (U-FNO), as an alternative to traditional simulations in solving TMz field in a two-dimensional multilayer medium. U-FNO learns the mapping between multilayer dielectric distribution and output <tex>$E_{z}$</tex> field distribution from randomly-sampled multilayer dielectric-solution pairs. After the U-FNO model is trained, given a multilayer dielectric medium, the U-FNO model computes the <tex>$E_{z}$</tex> field distribution in the frequency domain with good accuracy and a speedup factor of 13 compared to traditional finite difference solvers. The U-FNO also outperforms its counterpart data-driven machine learning models in terms of accuracy.

articleTitle: Amplitude and Phase Decoupled Metasurface for Low Side-Lobe Circularly Polarized Transmitarray Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a transmissive metasurface with decoupled amplitude and phase for circularly polarized (CP) incident waves. The cross-polarized transmission amplitude and phase are independently controlled by different structural parameters. Then, a transmitarray antenna with a low side-lobe level (SLL) based on the proposed metasurface is demonstrated. Compared to transmitarray antenna with phase-only modulation, the SLL of the proposed transmitarray antenna with simultaneous amplitude and phase modulation is reduced by 5.1 dB, which validates the proposed design methodology.

articleTitle: Modified 2D Backprojection Decomposition for 3D Imaging in Through-the-Wall Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Through-the-wall (TTW) radar imaging techniques are a promising research area for the radar community. These techniques are useful for detecting and identifying objects that are hidden behind walls making them a valuable tool for a variety of applications. The present study aims to develop a method for achieving 3D imaging using TTW radar by rotating 2D Backprojection (BP) planes. This approach is expected to provide an efficient and effective means of obtaining 3D images of hidden targets.

articleTitle: Fast Inference Beamforming Prediction using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work introduces an efficient, novel framework using a machine learning (ML) model to estimate beamforming weights on a Raspberry pi microcontroller. Tracking fast-moving targets and dynamically adjusting the weights of each antenna element in a phased array to transfer maximum energy to the target is desired in many beamforming applications. This work exploits ML models' fast output predicting nature to calculate optimum weights. A KNeighborsRegressor (KNR) is embedded into the proposed beamforming framework, which can predict the appropriate beam pattern of a 3×1 fractal array antenna. The process carried out on Raspberry pi has successfully calculated beamforming weights for 100 random targets within 62.8 seconds.

articleTitle: Multifunctional Electronically Reconfigurable Electromagnetic Surfaces for Ka-Band Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design and performance of two novel Ka-band reconfigurable unit-cells, using p-i-n diodes, for electronically controlled intelligent surfaces. The first cell operates in reflection or in transmission mode, by properly biasing its 4 diodes, and achieves a 1-bit and 2-bit phase quantization, respectively. The second cell comprises the first one, in transmitting mode, and a reconfigurable linear-to-circular polarization converter with 2 diodes, spaced by an air gap. It radiates a circularly-polarized wave with switchable handedness. The possibility of realizing wide-angle scanning and polarizationagile transmitarray antennas attaining limited phase quantization losses and enhanced aperture efficiency with respect to the state of the art is experimentally and numerically demonstrated.

articleTitle: New Strategies for CEM Simulation of Microstrip Circuits and Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper describes several novel strategies which help reduce the runtimes and memory requirements when simulating antennas and associated RF circuits in the millimeter-wave region, where the physical size of the radiating module is often large w.r.t. the wavelength. These strategies include the use of a hybrid domain-decomposition solver which combines the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method and the method of moments (MoM). The MoM domains are discretized by using a uniform Cartesian mesh to simplify the meshing problem, and this type of mesh provides the basis for defining the piecewise sinusoidal (PWS) basis functions. Likewise, the moment-matrix generation process is greatly simplified and enhanced in numerical efficiency by using the Equivalent Medium Approach (EMA) to circumvent the problem of generating the layered medium Green's function for the layered problem at hand, in addition to deploying the available GPU resources to reduce the matrix fill-in time even further. Moreover, the size of the generated MoM matrix can be reduced significantly by generating the reduced set of high-level basis functions on the selected domains, the underlying concept behind for instance the Characteristic Basis Function Method (CBFM).

articleTitle: Compact Wideband and High Gain Microstrip Patch Antenna for Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel wideband and high gain microstrip patch antenna for 5G millimeter wave applications is presented. The proposed antenna is designed on a 2-layers RO4350B substrate with a relative permittivity of 3.48 and loss tangent of 0.0031. The proposed design has an impedance bandwidth of 41% at 28 GHz resonant frequency and a maximum gain of 12.5 dB. As shown in Table 1, this design is the simplest 2-layer design that provides the widest bandwidth and has the highest aperture efficiency.

articleTitle: Multiple Folding Array Antenna Packed in a CubeSat and its Radiation Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A multiple folding array antenna is composed of plural flat panels, and deployed leaving steps between panels. The steps are compensated by adjusting the element excitation phase. Accordingly, it has a large deployed / folded area ratio, and enables two-dimensional deployment. In this paper, the configuration of a multiple folding array antenna that can be packed in a CubeSat of 3U is investigated. The antenna deployment operation is presented. The radiation patterns are discussed including beam shift capability.

articleTitle: A Compact Narrow-Band Harmonic Tag for Harmonic Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, we present a compact, narrow-band harmonic tag based on a circular patch antenna embedded within a micro-strip ring resonator antenna. The 2.8 GHz ring resonator filters incident harmonic radar signals over a narrow fractional bandwidth, passing the received signal to a diode that generates a frequency at the second harmonic of the incident signal, which is retransmitted by the 5.6 GHz circular patch antenna. The ring antenna is capacitively coupled to the diode to further reduce the bandwidth. The tag obtains a fractional bandwidth of 0.43% at 2.6 GHz (0.22% at 5.8 GHz) with antenna gains of 3.6 dBi and 3.0 dBi at 2.6 GHz and 5.8 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Electrically Small Loop Antenna with Horizontally Omnidirectional Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an electrically small loop antenna (ESLA). Using regularly placed capacitors between segments of the loop and proper feeding structure provides a uniform current distribution along the ESLA resulting in a horizontally omnidirectional radiation pattern. The antenna is simulated at 100 MHz producing a high radiation efficiency of over 90% and desired omnidirectional radiation pattern, showing potential for use in a direct antenna-modulated system.

articleTitle: Wideband Circular Polarization Reconfigurable Phased Array using Rotating 45-Degree Linearly Polarized Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband circular polarization reconfigurable phased array antenna (CPRPAA) is presented. The CPRPAA is designed with wideband 45-degree linearly polarized elements (45LPE). Sequential rotation technique (SRT) is applied to achieve circular polarization (CP). Results show the proposed CPRPAA not only exhibits high gain in whole operating band, but also has low axial ratio (AR) with wide-angle scanning.

articleTitle: Efficient Electromagnetic Simulation of Large Quasi-Periodic Arrays Based on FEM-BEM-DDM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this article, a modified characteristic subdomain method is presented for analyzing large quasi-periodic arrays based on the hybrid finite element-boundary element-domain decomposition method (FEM-BEM-DDM). This technique considers the large-scale quasi-periodic array as an expansion of several characteristic units, and utilizes the identity of characteristic subdomain system matrices to save the memory consumed in the process of constructing and analyzing these matrices, which significantly improves the performance of the algorithm. By comparing with commercial software FEKO and existing FEM-BEM-DDM method, the accuracy and the efficiency of the proposed technique is validated.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Segmented 3D Printed Luneburg Lenses
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: 3D Printed Luneburg lenses are manufactured - one as a spherical lens, and one as a joining of two hemispheres. The lenses are fed with an open-ended Ku-Band coaxial-to-waveguide adapter and measured over 10- 15 GHz to study the impact of the planar seam between the two hemispherical lenses. Conclusions drawn from the seam investigation provide insight for making larger Luneburg lenses from smaller subsections.

articleTitle: Slotted Stepped Impedance Ring Resonator Embedded Multi-Resonant Filtering DRA for 5G Sub-6 GHz Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, a filtering dielectric resonator antenna (FDRA) is proposed with compact size and frequency selectivity for 5G sub-6 GHz applications. The FDRA contains a slotted stepped impedance ring resonator (SIRR) with a circular dielectric resonator (DR) as the radiator and excited by an aperture coupled microstrip line loaded with a transverse arm. The proposed prototype of FDRA offers an operating bandwidth from 3.35-3.52 GHz with a peak realized gain of approximately 7.4 dBi. Further, the filtenna features sharp roll-off with two radiation nulls (3.19 GHz and 3.72 GHz) near the band edges allowing the proposed DRA to obtain high frequency selectivity.

articleTitle: RCS Uncertainty Predictions for Scatterers with Uncertain Material Parameters Using FEM, Adjoints, and HOPS Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present radar cross-section uncertainty predictions for dielectric scatterers with uncertain material parameters using higher order finite element method, adjoint solution, and higher order parameter sampling (HOPS) methodology. The HOPS method utilizes the adjoint problem to solve for gradient information, which is used to create a surrogate function that can replace traditional Monte Carlo methods. This reconstruction can be done using several different methods, each with their own strengths and weakness, but all greatly contributing to uncertainty quantification within computational electromagnetics.

articleTitle: High Gain Microstrip Patch Antenna as Illuminating Source for Near Field Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The design of a high gain circular patch antenna with the superstrate technique is presented. The antenna was used as an illuminating source for near field imaging. The antenna was designed, constructed and its radiation pattern measured in an open range measurement setup. Measured results showed a maximum antenna gain of 12.0 dBi at 3.0 GHz, and an operating bandwidth of 7.7% (2.86-3.09 GHz). Measured 3-dB beamwidths in the E- and H-planes are 30° and 40° respectively. Maximum side-lobe level is −12 dB at +/− 100° angle in the H-plane, and the front-to-back ratio is 15 dB.

articleTitle: An Ultrawideband Microwave Absorber Based on Graphene Frequency-Selective Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A absorber with graphene-based frequency-selective surfaces with ultrawide absorption bandwidth is presented. The absorber can achieve measured absorption over 90% from 1.85 to 18.2 GHz with factional bandwidth of 163%, which fully cover S-band, C-band, X-band and Ku-band. The proposed absorber also shows an insensitive performance against the polarization and incident angle. The measurement results that proposed absorber achieves a well trade-off between ultrawide effective bandwidth and thickness.

articleTitle: X-Band Superstrate Antenna for High Data Rate CubeSat Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work presents the concept of a high gain X-band superstrate antenna suitable for high data-rate CubeSat communication links. This antenna provides a common bandwidth of 530 MHz, a maximum gain of 15.1 dBi, and Left Hand Circularly Polarized (LHCP) waves. Two layer patches are utilized in the superstrate layer to get both good axial ratio bandwidth and gain. In the operating band, gain variation is less than 0.5 dBi. This article also demonstrates a deployment mechanism where by stowage, a volume of 80 mm × 80 mm × 18 mm can be saved.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Compact Bi-static Measurement Platform for Ka/Ku Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work presents design and fabrication of a compact 3D-printed bi-static measurement setup for mmWave applications. Two critical factors contributing to the bi-static measurement error were discussed: (1) mutual coupling and (2) scattering effect. A conventional horn antenna with a customized 3D-printed GRIN lens was proposed to address those critical issues. The horn antenna with 3D-printed GRIN lens features narrow 3-dB beam width to minimize the scattering effect. The proposed compact 3D-printed bi-static measurement setup shows robust measurement data with low noise.

articleTitle: A Compact 3-Way Power Divider Based on Bagley Polygon
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: 3-way Bagley power dividers are an interesting alternative to Wilkinson ones, due to the lack of lumped components - if perfect matching at output ports, as well as isolation - is not required; yet they occupy a large area, that of a triangle half wavelength in side, on the board. In this contribution a 3-way power divider based on Bagley polygon is reduced in dimension shortening the half wavelength delay lines by resorting to a midpoint reactive loading via open ended stubs.

articleTitle: Experimental Set Up to Test the Exposition of Implantable Medical Devices to Electromagnetic Fields
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Two real implantable medical devices were analyzed when they are subjected to electromagnetic radiation from radio communication systems to assess conformance to the IE 60601-1-2 Ed.2 2014, ISO14708-2:2019 and ISO14708-7:2019 standards in exposition scenarios commonly found in Colombia.

articleTitle: A Novel Reflectarray Unit Based on Mandelbrot Fractal Geometry with Different Degrees and Iteration Numbers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel reflectarray unit based on the Mandelbrot-set geometries with a degree from 2 to 6 and an iteration number from 3 to 6. Extensive simulations and analyses with different sizes, degrees, and iteration numbers are conducted for the unit. The results show that the proposed reflectarray unit can achieve a phase shift of more than 360 degree in multiple operation bands from 15-25 GHz while the dimensions of the unit are all within the operating wavelength, indicating that the proposed unit is very suitable for the design of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antennas in the millimeter-wave communications.

articleTitle: In-Line Microwave Nondestructive Evaluation of Packaged Food Products via the Support Vector Machine Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach based on electromagnetic waves (EM) to classify food packages that hold water as one of the main ingredients from the inside into contaminated or uncontaminated products. A non-destructive technique that can handle a real-time food production line is proposed to achieve this goal. This technique combines the operation of a microwave sensing system (MW) with a machine learning (ML) classifier. An accuracy of 100% has been obtained from training the aforementioned ML tool on a dataset constructed from the retrieved scattering parameters of about 500 measuring samples.

articleTitle: Dual Antenna Support and Isolation Enhancer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This document details the implementation and efficacy of a dual antenna support and isolation enhancer (DSIE). The DSIE is primarily used to isolate a printed Kandoian loop antenna and a dual-band TM20 mode patch antenna, while also acting as the mount for the loop antenna. These cross-polarized elements achieve 35 dB of isolation over the 5 GHz band at 60 mm spacing and greater than 50 dB of isolation with the DSIE.

articleTitle: Compact Omnidirectional Circularly-Polarized Implantable Antenna for Medical Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a compact, circularly-polarized implantable antenna for use in the Industrial, Scientific, and Medical (ISM) band. The antenna is designed for use in medical telemetry and is intended to improve and monitor patients' everyday lives. The antenna is made using a 50-ohm coaxial probe and a slotted patch design, and it is printed on a Duroid RT5880 substrate with a thickness of 0.254mm. The antenna has a small electrical size of 5mm x 5mm x 0.254mm and has an omnidirectional radiation pattern in both the E- and H-planes. The antenna operates within skin tissues from 1.1GHz to 5.4GHz (4.3GHz) making it a good candidate for medical applications.

articleTitle: Design and Development of 3D-Printed Meta-Mirror Antenna for Satellite Links at FR-2 Band of 5G Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a low-profile 3D-printed dielectric meta-mirror(DMM) antenna is designed and developed for ultra-wideband operation of satellite links at FR-2 band of 5G communication. DMM is designed by placing subwavelength unit cells of size <tex>$0.28\lambda_{0}\times 0.28\lambda_{0}$</tex> (where <tex>$\lambda_{0}$</tex> is free-space wavelength at design frequency i.e. 28 GHz) in an array of 18×18. This results in an overall aperture dimension of <tex>$5.04\lambda_){0}\times 5.04\lambda_{0}$</tex>. The complete DMM antenna comprises of 3D-printed dielectric horn placed 100 mm distance apart from the proposed DMM along +z-direction with a help of 3D-printed support structure. The proposed DMM antenna is printed using additive manufacturing process and further characterized for its performance in anechoic chamber. The measured gain of the proposed DMM antenna ranges from 24.2 dBi to 21.3 dBi from 22.4 GHz to 34.8 GHz with 3-dB gain bandwidth of 43 %. Measured maximum gain of 24.2 dBi at 28 GHz is realized resulting in a gain improvement of 10.1 dB. This results in a maximum aperture efficiency of 82.4 % which is in agreement with the theoretical limit calculated taking into account the spillover and edge-taper losses.

articleTitle: A High-Resolution Low-Sidelobe Beamforming Method for Sparse Antenna Arrays Based on CS-GA
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a joint beamforming method based on cuckoo search and genetic algorithm (CS-GA) is proposed for sparse array optimization. The locations and feed signal amplitudes of sparse array elements are optimized using CS-GA, and the radiation pattern of optimized spare arrays have superiorities of low sidelobe and high resolution owning to the global optimization and fast convergence advantages of CS-GA. The comparison result of CS-GA, linear array synthesis, and Chebyshev array synthesis demonstrates the superiority of CS-GA in high resolution and low sidelobe array synthesis applications.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of 3D Cassegrain Antenna Using HFSS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Parabolic antennas offer high gain and narrow beamwidth by employing a reflector to collimate radio waves. Dual reflectors reduce antenna system size over single reflectors and increase design optimization options. This paper introduces a detailed HFSS-based Cassegrain dual reflector design procedure for antenna design engineers. A stripline power splitter excites a 4x4 patch feed array. The parameterized model illustrates performance tradeoffs to meet system operating requirements.

articleTitle: A Novel DoA Algorithm for Coherent Signals with Asymmetric Multipath Phase Delays Based on a Modified Toeplitz Matrix Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a new direction of arrival (DoA) method based on a modified Toeplitz matrix reconstruction (NMTMR) algorithm. The proposed method overcomes one of the primary challenges of the traditional Toeplitz DoA algorithm, the asymmetric multipath phase delay scenarios. Unlike the conventional Toeplitz algorithm, the NMTMR algorithm can maintain the diagonality of the signal covariance matrix (<tex>$R_{ss}$</tex>) and hence can retain the full rank of the array covariance matrix (<tex>$R_{c}$</tex>) under different multipath phase delay scenarios. Specifically, the proposed NMTMR algorithm incorporates some pre- and post-signal processing and reconstruction steps to omit the elements that contributed to the deterioration of the diagonality of the signal covariance matrix (<tex>$R_{ss}$</tex>). A successful demonstration of the proposed algorithm has also been presented using MATLAB simulation to validate the viability of the algorithm, albeit with the cost of increasing the number of the required antennas.

articleTitle: Developing a Hybrid Radome Structure with Stable Suppression of RCS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid radome structure with the stable suppression of RCS. It applies two cross types of frequency selective surface in the same layer and two kinds of dielectric loading. Using phase cancelation and resonance property of periodic structure, the radome provides the transmission band and RCS reduction band. The simulated results also show that the radome stably reduces RCS in the fixed frequency range with different distances to the covered antenna.

articleTitle: Professor Yahya Rahmat-Samii's Exceptional Contributions to Research and Teaching as Seen by a Ph.D. Student: A Great Advisor and a True Friend
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper aims to recognize and honor the exceptional contributions of Professor Yahya Rahmat-Samii to the fields of research and teaching as seen through the eyes of a Ph.D. student. The author, who had the privilege of pursuing a Ph.D. degree under the supervision of Professor Rahmat-Samii from 2017 to 2022, reflects on how the professor's guidance and mentorship played a crucial role in shaping their academic and professional journey. The paper highlights Professor Rahmat-Samii's outstanding skills as a researcher, teacher, and academic advisor and how his approach to education and research inspired the author to pursue their own research endeavors. Additionally, the author shares personal anecdotes that illustrate Professor Rahmat-Samii's qualities as a great advisor and a true friend, who went above and beyond to support and mentor his students. The paper serves as a testament to Professor Rahmat-Samii's 50+ years of dedication to the academic community and his lasting impact on the lives of his students.

articleTitle: Inverse Design of Wire Antennas Using a Hessian-Based Nonlinear Optimizer with Automatic Differentiation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A Hessian-based approach to perform efficient optimization of wire antennas modelled using Pocklington's integral equation is proposed. We demonstrate how the Hessian matrix of a cost function can be utilized to significantly improve the convergence of an optimizer. The gradient of an antenna parameter is obtained by modifying the Numerical Electromagnetic Code (NEC2) software using a technique called automatic differentiation (AD). This enables us to accurately obtain the derivatives without the need for making significant changes to an existing solver. The gradient of a cost function is computed by a single functional call irrespective of the number of design variables, which makes it very attractive when compared to traditional finite difference methods. The validity of the proposed method is demonstrated by an application example and its advantages are compared with a non-gradient optimization method.

articleTitle: Miniaturization of A Single Feed Dielectric Loaded Wideband High-Gain Circularly Polarized Microstrip Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A dielectric superstrate-loaded circularly polarized microstrip patch antenna with a complimentary aerial ring at the center is presented in this article. The loading miniaturizes the antenna reasonably. The patch antenna is designed on a 1.575 mm-thick Rogers RT/Duroid 5880 substrate material with a resonant frequency at 11 GHz. The 25 × 25 mm<sup>2</sup>antenna has a 3 dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of 14.3% (10.4 - 12 GHz) with a peak gain of 13.3 dBi. The 3 dB AR bandwidth of the antenna increases by 700 MHz with the loading of a dielectric superstrate. The small antenna exhibits about 6 dBi more broadside gain than a regular circularly polarized microstrip antenna when the dielectric is used, which makes the antenna suitable for X-band applications.

articleTitle: Free-Space Biological Tissue Measurement at W-band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The dielectric property of biological tissues is essential to calculate specific absorption rate (SAR) for assessing excessive EM energy exposure to the human body. This paper presents the permittivity of the skin of micro-pig measured by a free-space material measurement system at the W-band (75–110 GHz) and shows its validity.

articleTitle: Four-Layer Dual-Band Metasurface Polarizer Device for Linear-to-Circular Polarization Conversion at Ka-Band SatCom Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A method to design a unique dual-band linear to circular transmission polarizer converter is presented in this paper. The polarizer is developed for use in the SatCom Ka-band. It needs to provide two transmission/reception bands with orthogonal polarizations (RHCP/LHCP). It is composed of four identical metasurface sheet separated by quarter-wave thick substrates for easy impedance matching. The susceptances of the metasurface exhibit series resonance for the horizontal linear polarization and parallel resonance for the vertical polarization. The method is based on the dispersion diagrams (phase versus susceptances) and choose the solutions that ensure orthogonally conversion for the two bands. The designed polarizer shows a good frequency behavior with a large bandwidth (up to ~2 GHz for each band), low insertion loss (<0.5 dB), angular stability (up to ± 45°) and axial ratio below 1.5 dB. By twisting the structure by 90°, circular left hand/right hand conversions can be interchanged in the two bands.

articleTitle: Multiband X-Band Frequency for Reflecting Intelligent Surfaces (IRSs)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A multiband reflector is proposed to operate in X-band frequency by employing a multi-ring resonator for an intelligent reflecting surface (IRS). The effect of the incident wave angle is simulated by moving the source signal along the horizontal line to assume the position of the incoming signal relative to the reflector. The simulated results of the proposed reflector show the optimum performance in terms of reflection coefficient and phase at 0 degrees incident wave, which is 0.93 and 32.14° at 8 GHz, 0.78 and -24.14° at 10 GHz, and 0.799 and 5° at 12 GHz. Also, the overall bandwidth for all resonance frequencies is approximately 0.61 GHz at 8 GHz and 0.2 GHz at 10 and 12 GHz respectively.

articleTitle: Design of 4 × 8 Filtering Butler Matrix With Unequal Power Distribution
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper reports a novel 4 × 8 filtering Butler matrix with unequal power distribution. The filtering Butler matrix is composed of 90° couplers as well as 180° couplers with a second-order bandpass filtering characteristic. The detailed design process and synthesis method for the 4 × 8 filtering Butler matrix are reported. To validate the analysis, a 4 × 8 filtering Butler matrix with unequal power division, operating at 2.4 GHz, is devised, manufactured, and measured. The results of the simulation and experimentation are matched very well.

articleTitle: Hyperthermia Brain Cancer Treatment Using a Wideband Antenna with an Elliptic Reflector
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A new wideband antenna configuration has been developed for microwave hyperthermia treatment of brain cancer and other types of cancer. It consists of an elliptic reflector and a small feed antenna centered at its first focal point. The reflected rays from the reflector collimate at its second focal point, which is managed to be at the’ cancer zone. By controlling the design parameters of the developed antenna configuration, these reflected rays of electromagnetic waves can exactly cover any 3D (three-dimensional) zone of cancer cells, without heating any of the surrounding healthy tissues. Different cancer spots can be, simultaneously, covered using different feed antennas with the same reflector.

articleTitle: A Stable and Symmetric FDTD Subgridding Method with Arbitrary Grid Ratio
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A stable and symmetric finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) subgridding method is proposed to effectively and accurately solve the three-dimensional electromagnetic prob-lems. The linear interpolation coefficient (LIC) and the length cutoff coefficient (LCC) are carefully designed to guarantee the stability of the proposed method. In addition, the proposed method is applicable to arbitrary grid ratios and nested meshes. A practical multiscale example is used to validate its accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Brain Stroke Detection Using Electromagnetic Tomography: A New Portable Scanner
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a new system for brain stroke detection using electromagnetic tomography, which has two components. On one hand, a small, lightweight and portable scanner which collects the measurement data from the human brains under study. On the other hand, an image reconstruction cloud platform which processes the data from the scanner in almost real-time and capable of generating DICOM images to help clinicians and radiologists in their decision making to identify brain pathologies such as stroke.

articleTitle: Heterogeneously Integrated 6–12 GHz Butler Matrix
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A 4x4 Butler matrix designed in a Metal Embedded Chip Assembly (MECA) process is presented. The broadband multi-beam feed network covers 6–12 GHz and is designed to be integrated with a double-ridged horn array. Three individual alumina pieces are integrated in a metal-embedded process using the interconnect layer for the final connections. Simulation results show the expected performance with amplitude imbalance less than 1.5 dB and phase imbalance less than 21° across the 6–12 GHz octave. The resulting radiation patterns using the Butler matrix are shown with steering of 14° and 40° at 6 GHz and 7° and 21° at 12 GHz.

articleTitle: Efficient Design of Multilayer Wideband Absorbers Using Analytical Grid Impedance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A numerically efficient design technique for planar microwave absorbers comprising multiple metal-dielectric layers on a ground plane is presented. Each patterned metallic sheet comprises orthogonally placed strips, for which an analytical homogenized surface impedance is available. Using a transmissionline model, complete reflection characteristics are efficiently evaluated for both polarizations and all incidence angles. The analytical formulation allows a large design space to be efficiently explored for wideband, wide-angle absorption responses. An example X-band absorber is designed and validated using full-wave simulation.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarized Beam-Steerable Antenna Utilizing Complementary Reconfigurable Parasitic Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A new dual-port reconfigurable antenna design with both polarization and pattern diversity is described. For each polarization, beam-steerable function can be realized in the same steering range by utilizing two pairs of complementary reconfigurable parasitic elements. Four RF switches are located on these parasitic elements to provide reconfiguration. The bandwidth for each port is 3.4-3.8 GHz with more than 20 dB port isolation for all reconfigurable states. This reconfigurable antenna can be utilized in multiple wireless communication or sensing scenarios to provide performance gains.

articleTitle: A Frequency-Reconfigurable Filtenna for UWB and 5G Sub-6 GHz Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work presents a solution for a reconfigurable filtenna with three operation modes: ultrawideband (from 690 MHz to 6 GHz), 3.5 GHz (from 3.3 to 3.71 GHz), and 700 MHz (from 705 to 773 MHz). These bandwidths have large applications on 5G sub-6 GHz. The structure is built on an FR4 substrate using a bio-inspired antenna and filters based on fractal and defected ground structure (DGS). The proposed model was simulated, and a prototype was manufactured and measured. The simulation results were very congruent with the proposed operation, and the prototype presented relatively good coherence with these simulations.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Complementary Planar Antenna with Conical Radiation for 6G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Along with the gradually shift of wireless communication research interests towards sixth generation (6G), conical-beam (CB) antenna has recently become an attractive candidate for millimeter-wave (mm-wave) 6G satellite/drones applications owing to its valuable radiation features. Nevertheless, to the date, there are only few reported mm-wave CB antennas constructed with completely planar structures and most of them perform limited gain and impedance bandwidth. In this study, we propose a complementary planar antenna exhibiting a high-gain and wideband conical radiation by configuring a circular array of magnetoelectric (ME) antenna elements fed by a multiple-stage substrate-integrated-waveguide (SIW) circular-cavity. By leveraging the multiple-stage structure of the cavity and control TM010/TM020 resonance modes, the proposed antenna can exhibit a high-gain and wideband performance covering entire E-band and upper V-band spectrum while maintaining a compact planar structure. Particularly, proposed structure performs an impedance BW of 59.38–89.95 GHz (40.9%) with highly stable CB radiation across operating frequency and peak gain of 12.05 dBi at 76 GHz.

articleTitle: Improved Wireless Position-Detection of Metallic Plates in Orthopaedic Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We investigate possible techniques for improved detection of position, i.e., distance from the referent location, and angle of deflection of large metallic implants using two wireless sensors (antennas) at microwave frequencies. By means of electromagnetic simulations in free space, we compare the results obtained by the beamforming algorithm, calibrated changes in antenna resonant frequencies, and time-domain reflectometry.

articleTitle: An In-Situ Eddy Current Diagnostic for Temperature Monitoring in Metal Additive Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We propose a novel, non-contact diagnostic for monitoring of sub-surface temperature in metal additive manufacturing (AM) using an eddy current (EC) system. An EC probe produces time-varying magnetic fields, that induce eddy currents in the sub-surface of a metal AM part. Variations in sub-surface temperatures lead to perturbation of the flow of the induced eddy currents and hence appear as localized magnetic anomalies. A controlled heat source is used to heat the metal surface, while the EC probe monitors the temperature from the opposite surface in a non-contact manner. The overall EC physics, a finite-element based numerical model and preliminary temperature monitoring experiments are presented.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable SIW Antenna Array for Sub-6GHz 5G Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an electrically reconfigurable beam-forming antenna is presented. The proposed antenna operates at 5.8GHz and it could be implemented on a single PCB laminate. The simulated gain and radiation efficiency for the proposed array are 13.6 dBi and 53.5%, respectively. In the presented beam-forming antenna, phase shifts are controlled by altering the switch states, then the main beam direction can be electronically steered.

articleTitle: Upper Bound on Instantaneous Power Flux
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This abstract presents a method for maximization of the radiation in a given direction and a given time. The radiation mechanism and the impedance matching are taken into account in a full-wave manner. The approach is based on the method of moments formulation of field integral equations and convex optimization.

articleTitle: Additively Manufactured K-Band Septum Polarizers: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: <tex>$A$</tex> septum waveguide polarizer with integrated circular to square waveguide transition has been manufactured using three different additive manufacturing (AM) processes. Polymer and AlSi10Mg printing processes from a specialized RF manufacturer and a selective laser melting (SLM) process from a university research group are evaluated. Measurements confirm the polarizer design is well suited for AM.

articleTitle: Dynamic Control of Dispersion in a Monopole Antenna Having a Time-Varying Switch
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Time-varying antennas are known to enable broad-band operation by dispersing energy in space (angle) and time (frequency). Dynamic control of the antenna's dispersion across these degrees of freedom could enable new modulations. This work applies a time domain full-wave circuit co-simulation technique to investigate the case of a simple monopole antenna having a single switch near its end. An amplitude modulated waveform is applied to the feed point of an antenna while a square wave is applied to control the switch. Finally, the reflection and transmission properties of the antenna under distinct switch waveform delays are evaluated in the electrically small regime using a full-wave finite difference time domain co-simulation technique.

articleTitle: Broadband Transition from Waveguide to Substrate-Integrated Waveguide with Back-Short Structure in Multilayer Substrate at 300-GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A broadband transition from a hollow rectangular waveguide to a substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) was designed in 300-GHz band. The prepreg layers in a multilayer substrate are unified through rectangular apertures opened in the inner printed patterns. A back-short structure was formed at one end of the thick SIW in the multilayer substrate by a via hole arrangement. The back-short length and the locations of matching via holes were optimized to produce double resonance for broadband characteristic. The simulated bandwidth of the proposed transition for <tex>$S_{11}$</tex> lower than −10 dB was 71.2 GHz, and the fractional bandwidth was 25.9%.

articleTitle: On the Performance of New Spatial Modulation Scheme for Frequency Selective Channels
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: OTFS has been recently proposed to achieve time and frequency diversities, especially in linear time-variant (LTV) channels with large Doppler frequencies. The idea is based on the precoding of the data symbols using symplectic finite Fourier transform (SFFT) then splitting the frequency selective channel into flat components via OFDM waveform. Implementing OTFS technique when the number of transmit/receive antennas increases may become very fast computationally prohibiting, because of the augmented number of RF chains and the one of OFDM subcarrier branches per RF chain. One promising solution to such issue in the context of massive MIMO is the spatial modulation (SM) technique, which only activates a single transmit antenna in any symbol-interval, thereby necessitating a sole RF chain. In this paper, we propose to incorporate OTFS signaling into SM architecture and evaluate the attained data reliability. Simulation results show that OTFS-based solution outperforms the recently presented SM-OFDM alternative.

articleTitle: High Gain 1-D Complementary Paired Combline PLWA with Backward to Forward Scanning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A design of a 1-D PLWA is discussed where a pair of complementary radiating stubs are connected to microstrip fed line. The edges of the stubs are tapered to get good impedance matching and OSB suppression. A slot is further introduced to this design to improve the gain and scanning range. The proposed antenna can achieve 17. 75dbi peak gain and have scanning range from −61° to +19°, bandwidth 6.1GHz – 10.5GHz, its dimensions are <tex>$8.25\lambda_{0}\times 1. 5 \lambda_{0}$</tex> with a small 1.5dbi gain variation at the broadside.

articleTitle: Multihyperuniform Shared Aperture Antenna Arrays for Multiband Unidirectional Emission Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The multihyperuniform disordered distribution is an aperiodic distribution that was firstly identified on avian eye retina and is the reason behind their wideband and highly directive vision attributes. In particular, five different photoreceptor species are arranged in a disordered manner following a hyperuniform distribution which provides low side lobe levels and highly directive radiation patterns, while the overall photoreceptor distribution is hyperuniform as well, hence the term multihyperuniformity. Inspired by this, we are applying the concept in the field of shared-aperture antenna array design and to prove the concept, design a penta-band shared-aperture antenna array of circular patches operating in microwave frequencies. The proposed antenna array has low side levels over the whole frequency bandwidth and provides high peak realized gain values at the patches' resonant frequencies.

articleTitle: A Switchable Transmission/ Absorption/Reflection Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel polarization-insensitive frequency selective surface (FSS) design realizing the switching between the three functions of transmission/absorption/reflection is presented. The proposed structure consists of two active frequency selective surfaces (AFSSs) printed on different dielectric substrates and separated by an air spacer. By controlling the status of the PIN diodes between the upper and lower AFSS structures, three different electromagnetic functions of transmission/absorption/reflection are realized. In addition, the proposed solution achieves a valid oblique incident angle and dual- polarization characteristics.

articleTitle: Wireless Time and Phase Alignment for Wideband Beamforming in Distributed Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a two node wideband wireless distributed antenna array operating from 3.1-3.3 GHz on software-defined radios (SDRs). To synthesize the total bandwidth of 300 MHz, a 100 MHz bandwidth signal was used over multiple frequency steps, with the carrier frequency re-tuned between each pulse. The nodes were wirelessly synchronized using a high-accuracy two-way time transfer technique which was also used to determine the inter-node range for beamforming. A total beamforming bias <tex>$\pm$</tex> standard deviation of <tex>$62.46\pm 45.74$</tex> ps and <tex>$0.27\pm 2.28^{\circ}$</tex> at the target beamforming angle at a range of 35.5 m was achieved.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Bandpass Angle-Selective Surface Based on Three-Layer Frequency Selective Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-polarized bandpass angle-selective surface based on three layers of frequency-selective surfaces. The top and bottom layers are identical, while the middle layer can be different. By properly designing the thickness of the air spacers between three FSS layers, the ASS can achieve a bandpass performance at any incident angle for both TE- and TM-polarizations. A bandpass ASS based on the complementary hexagon resonance is proposed. Simulation results show that the bandpass performance is achieved from 9.8 to 10.2 GHz. Besides, the passband <tex>$(\vert \mathrm{S}_{21}\vert > -1\ \text{dB})$</tex> at 30°, and the stopband <tex>$(\vert \mathrm{S}_{21}\vert < -20$</tex> dB) within the range from 0° to 8° and 38° to 70° are obtained for both TE- and TM-polarizations.

articleTitle: Tri-axial H-Field Sensor with Frequency-shaped Response in the band 400 MHz - 6 GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This contribution presents an isotropic field probe to assess human exposition to broadband magnetic fields in the 400 MHz to 6 GHz band according to the ICNIRP 2020 guidelines. This device complements the current practice in this band, based on the measurement of electric field, which may underestimate the overall exposition in the near field of particular sources or scatterers. The design process accounts for the frequency response of all the system components involved. The performance of the isotropic configuration is assessed.

articleTitle: Simple Strategy for Multi-Objective Management in Antenna Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Presented here is an objective function design consisting of a sum of weighted sigmoid and exponential shaped goal functions for the purpose of multi-objective antenna optimization. Details of how design-trade off and optimizer guidance is achieved is provided. An example metasurface antenna optimization problem is included to demonstrate how a solution is synthesized which balances bandwidth and gain.

articleTitle: A Numerical Method to Analyze Electromagnetic Scattering from Composite Plasmonic Structures Involving a Metal-Metal Interface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A coupled system of volume integral and hydrodynamic equations is formulated to analyze electromagnetic scattering from composite plasmonic structures involving a metal-metal interface. This coupled system in unknowns electric flux and free electron velocity is discretized using Schaubert-Wilton-Glisson basis functions. Inserting these expansions into the coupled system of equations and applying Galerkin testing yield a matrix equation. Two-level iterative scheme is used to solve this matrix equation for the unknown expansion coefficients. To demonstrate the accuracy of the proposed method, numerical results are compared to those obtained using an extended Mie series approach that takes into account the hydrodynamic equation and the boundary conditions it requires.

articleTitle: Alternating-Frequency Microwave Hyperthermia: Preliminary Results
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Microwave hyperthermia therapy for breast cancer supports chemotherapy and radiotherapy. The tumor temperature levels are increased using the heat energy emitted from the microwave sources, while the energy is optimized to minimally affect the non-cancerous regions. Introducing different frequency radiation can increase the energy-focusing sensitivity. However, a simultaneous multi-frequency radiation can be challenging when the power and phase requirements for the electromagnetic wave emitted for each frequency are different. This paper presents a frequency alteration approach. The optimized energy distributions for two frequencies were introduced in turns to the breast phantom after each other. The duration for each turn is optimized to obtain the best temperature focusing over the phantom. The alternating-frequency final temperature distribution has an 11.8% higher target-to-breast temperature ratio, <tex>$0.2{}^{\circ}\ \mathrm{C}$</tex> lower healthy tissue temperature values and 11%-20% lower hotspot-to-target temperature ratio compared to the single-frequency results.

articleTitle: mmWave Wireless Power Transmission to Flexible Rectennas in Absorptive and Reflective Media
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Millimeter-Wave (mmWave) wireless power transmission (WPT) can provide theoretical improvements to the end-to-end link efficiency compared sub-6 GHz bands. However, mmWave propagation in the WPT is yet to be explored. Herein, we present the first evaluation of a broadband mmWave rectenna on a lossy phantom based on radiation absorbing material (RAM). The ground reflection is observed over distance from a 20 dBi horn antenna with a 1 W input around 23 and 28 GHz, where the effect of multi-paths reflections is demonstrated and compared to a varying input from the generator. A DC power output over 10 µis measured at 15 cm from a 51 dBm source, showing the potential for meters-range mmWave wearable WPT with the licensed 5G 75 dBm EIRP levels. It is concluded that the electromagnetic (EM) environment and propagation media can have significant influences on mmWave WPT requiring novel signal and EM co-design.

articleTitle: A Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons Bandpass Filter Based on Coplanar Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) bandpass filter based on a coplanar waveguide. The SSPPs transmission lines based on the coplanar waveguide are constructed and their characteristics are analyzed by simulations. It is found that the SSPPs transmission lines have a high cutoff frequency and the bandpass filter can be realized by constructing a zero-transmission characteristic on the transmission lines. Simulation results show that the filter has a low in-band insertion loss of less than 1.2 dB and a high out-of-band suppression of more than 80 dB, verifying its excellent frequency-selection function.

articleTitle: Reducing the Volume of Reflectarray Antennas Using Near-Field Feeding
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We propose a method to miniaturize a reflectarray antenna (RA) using near-field feeding. In a conventional design way of RAs, a source feeder is in a far-field region to avoid ambiguity in incident polarization. However, the distant source makes the corresponding reflectarray large to prevent the incident energy from spillover. To solve the problem, we have proposed a new near-field feeding method, like the way that we put a normal dipole antenna over a ground plane. The expected polarization ambiguity problem was solved using the reciprocal behavior of passive antennas. Consequently, we were able to reduce the overall volume of RAs remarkably.

articleTitle: 2- Bit Tunable Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface for Multibeam Antenna Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work proposes a design and simulation of a 2-bit tunable Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) with four distinct spatial coding patterns to achieve multibeam modulation operating at 4.2 GHz. The embedded varactors incorporate the tunability function into the unit cell, allowing the phase control response of the reflected electromagnetic wave. As a result, the four-state coding is obtained by varying the light intensity of the photodiode elements. We created a proof-of-concept RIS based on different coding patterns to test its reconfigurability for electromagnetic wave (EM) management. The radiation patterns can be reconfigured by controlling dynamic radian beams. Results show the excellent performance of the proposed RIS in terms of managing EM functions.

articleTitle: Characteristic Basis Function Method Using Single High-Level Basis Function Per Subdomain For Efficient Analysis of Large Periodic Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Recently, a novel characteristic basis function method (CBFM) formulation has been proposed for numerically efficient analysis of large truncated-periodic array antennas operating in the radiating mode. In this formulation, a single (and identical) high-level CBF is employed to represent the current distribution in each element of the antenna array. This CBF is constructed by solving the problem of a unit cell of the infinite doubly-periodic array. In this paper, a modified approach is proposed for generating the CBF associated with each edge or corner element in the presence of array truncation effects. The efficacy of both approaches is demonstrated by simulating the <tex>$9\times 9$</tex> array of bow-tie antenna elements. It is shown that good agreement with the reference solution from a commercial CEM solver is achieved, together with a significant reduction of the overall computational cost.

articleTitle: A Deep-Learning-Based Borehole Radar Sparse Target Imaging Method with High Accuracy in Nonuniform Medium
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an accurate borehole radar imaging method based on deep learning is proposed for sparse target detection in nonuniform subsurface medium. With aid of the a-prior medium layout information, a sparse target extractor is derived, whose output is connected to the designed deep-learning-based autoencoder (AE) for sparse target location correction, which is trained by multiple radar echo datasets in simulation scenes. The results validate its high accuracy and universal effectiveness in diverse target imaging under various medium circumstances.

articleTitle: Coupled and Characteristic Modes of a Double-Tuned Loop Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Coupled Mode Theory (CMT) is a classic model that addresses many diverse problems in physics and electrical engineering. Although CMT is well-established in areas such as filter and directional coupler design, its significance in antenna engineering is less well-recognized. Recently, Characteristic Mode Analysis (CMA) has shown how CMT quantitatively models a wide variety of multi-mode patch structures. In this paper, we apply these ideas to a double-tuned loop antenna. CMA decomposition indicates the antenna consists of two resonators: the larger radiating loop and a smaller feeding loop. The two resonators are electromagnetically coupled, which causes the Smith chart impedance locus to encircle to origin, resulting in broad impedance bandwidth. An equivalent circuit whose values are derived from the CMA analysis is given.

articleTitle: A Method to Estimate Varactor Quality Factor at Microwave Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a method to characterize the quality factor (Q) of varactor diodes for tunable antenna applications at microwave frequencies is presented. The proposed technique is based on extracting the unloaded quality factor of a tunable microwave resonator. A varactor is integrated into a tunable combline resonator, which is excited with weak external coupling to extract the total unloaded quality factor. By loading the same resonator with an equivalent ideal capacitor, the varactor's quality factor is determined. The method's efficacy is validated through simulation results to extract the quality factor as a function of applied bias voltage and operating frequency. The proposed technique is not subject to calibration and de-embedding errors, and can be used to estimate the bias and frequency-dependent varactor quality factor for reconfigurable antennas and other varactor-tuned designs.

articleTitle: Effect of Array and Substrate Configurations on Transparent Mosaic Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study investigated the effect of the array and substrate configurations on the performance of the optically transparent Mosaic Frequency Selective Surface (MFSS). The MFSS structural element integrates the double hexagonal loops and Koch fractal structural elements. The transparent polycarbonate substrate (permittivity of 2.9, loss tangent of 0.02, substrate thickness of 1.5 mm) is used, where the silver conductor layer (thickness of 0.006 mm and conductivity of 4.3 x 10<sup>6</sup>S/m) of the MFSS periodic array is patterned on the substrate surface. In this work, three types of configurations are assessed for the optically transparent MFSSs - single-sided MFSS (MFSS), double-sided MFSS (MFSS2), and multilayered MFSS (MFSS3). The simulation of the MFSSs is conducted using the Computer Simulation Technology (CST) Microwave Studio software. Based on the obtained result, it was concluded that the increase of the array and substrate configurations allowed the enhancement of bandwidth, especially for the first and the second bandstop frequency responses, and contrariwise for the bandpass frequency response. Meanwhile, the obtained cross-polarisation <tex>$(T_{yx})$</tex> value showed that the simulated <tex>$T_{yx}$</tex> degraded consequently as the array and substrate configurations of the MFSSs increased.

articleTitle: A Novel Loop Antenna Easily Matching with Radio Frequency Integrated Circuit Chips
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel loop antenna whose input impedance can match directly with that of a radio frequency integrated circuit (RFIC) chip is presented. Specifically, the antenna can be constituted so that resistance and reactance of its input complex impedance may simultaneously become 100 Ω or more. This feature has been realized by the structure winding a loop doubly. In this presentation, the antenna has been tuned to match with the RFIC chip whose complex impedance is 131-j91 Ω at 920 MHz. The performance of the antenna has been achieved with 16% or more in the −10 dB impedance bandwidth, 2.26 dB in the maximum gain and 99% in the radiation efficiency.

articleTitle: Magnetotelluric Data Inversion Using Subdomain Encoding Scheme with Variational Autoencoder
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A 2D inversion scheme based on variational autoen-coder (VAE) is applied to magnetotelluric (MT) data inversion. Trained with the carefully designed data set, the VAE can reparameterize the subsurface model with latent variables in an adaptive manner. To improve the computational efficiency and the generalization ability of VAE, the subsurface model is divided into subdomains, all encoded with the same VAE. In the inversion, the latent variables of each sub domain are inverted with the Gauss-Newton method. This method can flexibly incorporate prior knowledge into inversion. Numerical experiments show that the reconstructed models are more accurate and better consistent with prior knowledge than traditional inversion in the spatial domain.

articleTitle: A Novel Phase Optimization Method for Sidelobe-Level Suppression of 1-Bit Reconfigurable Reflectarrays
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel phase optimization method for sidelobe-level suppression of 1-blt reconfigurable reflectarrays (RRAs) is proposed. Simply by switching/reversing the binary phase states of unit cells, the sidelobe level suppression can be attained. Furthermore, to enhance the effectiveness without significantly increasing optimization complexity, the hybrid optimization algorithm, incorporating EM simulated and theoretically calculated results, is used to determine optimal phase distribution over reflectarray aperture. To validate the feasibility, a <tex>$15\times 15$</tex> patch reflectarray, which is composed of only two physical lengths to represent two phase states, was experimentally developed and tested, where the sidelobe level is improved from 11.1 dB to 14.3 dB with small peak gain variation from 21.4 dBi to 20.8 dBi.

articleTitle: Design of a High Isolation 60 GHz MIMO Antenna Using a Defected Ground Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a compact high isolation MIMO antenna is presented for 60 GHz applications. The proposed design consists of two inset-fed rectangular patch antennas operating at 60 GHz placed on 0.252 mm thick Rogers 5880 substrate. A defected ground structure (DGS) is employed to achieve a high isolation of more than 52 dB at 60 GHz. The size of the proposed MIMO antenna is only 8 x 12 mm2.A peak realized gain of 7.33 dBi and a radiation efficiency of 86.5 % at 60 GHz are also reported for the proposed MIMO antenna.

articleTitle: Evaluating NGBoost as a Model for Probabilistic Prediction for V-Band Power Attenuation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel application of probabilistic prediction for estimating mm-wave attenuation due to varying weather conditions is developed. Validation of atmospheric propagation models in the W/V-bands has progressed greatly in past years, but the confidence of their predictions has not been validated. The Natural Gradient Boosting (NGBoost) algorithm is tested against a deep neural network to estimate atmospheric attenuation on a 72 GHz terrestrial link and to demonstrate the ability to produce prediction confidence estimates.
