articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Leaky Wave Antenna for W Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposed a W band circularly polarized leaky wave antenna based on a single-layer polarization converter. Linearly polarized waves radiating from longitudinal slots of WR-10 waveguide are converted to circularly polarized waves by an array of metallic patches designed on a thin dielectric slab. The implemented antenna is designed for 92 GHz to 96 GHz frequency band which exhibits a measured gain of 14.5 dBi. The presented robust CP antenna design is a good candidate for various millimeter-wave applications.

articleTitle: A Leaky-Wave Antenna Design for RF Gesture Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a conformable antenna design for radio frequency (RF) based tracking of hand gestures. A substrate-integrated waveguide leaky-wave antenna (SIW-LWA) is employed as the radiating element to couple RF signals into the human hand. The antenna is envisaged to be integrated in a wristband topology and capture the changes in the electric field caused by various movements of the hand. In this numerical study, we treat the LWA as a two-port device and design a simplified model of the wrist based on published measured tissue properties. As such, we investigate how the S-parameters are affected due to changes in the wrist anatomy (e.g., tendon displacement). These variations can be mapped to individual gestures and used to interact with a computer. As small as 0.1 mm tendon displacements have shown very distinct frequency responses which highlights the potential sensitivity of such an RF-based system in hand gesture recognition.

articleTitle: Tri-Band Millimeter-Wave Antenna Unit Cell for a Deployable Scanning Reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The design and analysis of antennas to be used in a Configurable Reflectarray for Electronic Wideband Scanning Radiometry (CREWSR) is presented with simulation results. The target application requires independent beam scanning at 24GHz, 31GHz, and 50-58GHz. The low losses and phase linearity shown in the reflection response indicate good coverage for all three channels.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Direction-of-Arrival Estimation Accuracy with Using Antenna Arrays Composed of Diverse Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: An antenna array composed of diverse elements that can improve direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation accuracy is presented in this paper. As many surveillance and radio-frequency positioning systems relay on measuring DoAs, improving the DoA accuracy is of great importance. However, due to the limited array dimension, the DoA accuracy of the arrays composed of identical elements is fundamentally difficult to improve. Besides, given the limited number of elements, arbitrarily increasing the array dimension can cause ambiguity. To alleviate these issues, we employ antennas with diverse shapes of radiation patterns to improve the DoA estimation accuracy. We compared the DoA estimation accuracy of a uniform linear array of three rectangular patch antennas and that of the same array of two rectangular patch antennas and one low-profile antenna with a monopole-like radiation pattern. Theoretical and Monte Carlo simulation results demonstrate that the DoA estimation error of the array composed of diverse antennas can reduce by up to 30% over a wide field of view.

articleTitle: Imageless Detection of Pipe Defects Using a Millimeter-Wave Dynamic Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We demonstrate a novel nondestructive evaluation technique for detecting defects in metallic pipes based on spatial Fourier-domain responses captured with a dynamic millimeter-wave array. The array consists of a two-element noise transmitter and a two-element correlation receiver, all in a linear array configuration. By cross-correlating the two separate received signals and dynamically rotating the array, Fourier-domain responses corresponding to the geometry of objects in the scene can be used to characterize and classify objects without generating actual images. We implement a 75 GHz rotationally dynamic array and explore its use in detecting defects in circularly cylindrical pipes. We present measurements on two conducting cylinders of identical dimension imitating pipe structures where one cylinder includes a slot mimicking a crack. The results show identifiable changes in the Fourier-domain features due to the defect, suggesting an opportunity of periodic monitoring on pipes where responses can be compared to known signatures from pipes without defects.

articleTitle: Enhancing Near-Field Holographic Imaging with Predicted Object Position
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In current near-field holographic imaging, a circular region is scanned using an array of transmitting and receiving antennas over a narrow frequency band. This makes the data acquisition system slow, complex, bulky, and costly. Reducing the number of receiver antennas and using a narrower frequency band can significantly reduce the cost and complexity of the data acquisition system. To do so, we propose a method that uses prior knowledge about the object position, obtained by applying a neural network algorithm, called convolutional neural network (CNN), to the scattered field responses. This prior knowledge is then used to add a new regularization term to the cost function that is minimized in near-field holography.

articleTitle: A Full-Spectrum Approach to Electromagnetic Coupling into Complex Enclosures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Prediction of the coupling of electromagnetic energy into a complex enclosure through multiple apertures is addressed through a variety of efficient reduced-order computational methods spanning dimensions on the order of a wavelength to hundreds of wavelengths. Specially adapted time domain differential equation methods are used at the lower frequencies, waveguide modal and integral equation methods are applied at middle frequencies, and ray-tracing is used at the highest frequencies. Results are validated with independent numerical solutions and experimental measurements.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Tumor Margin Identification in Electromagnetic Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a deep learning technique which accurately divides the electromagnetic images of cancer-affected tissues into two regions of tumorous and normal sections. This capability will enable the visualization of the border of the cancerous tissue for the surgeon prior to or during the excision surgery. We formulate deep learning from a perspective relevant to electromagnetic image reconstruction. A recurrent auto-encoder network architecture is presented. The effectiveness of the algorithm is demonstrated by segmenting the reconstructed images of an experimental tissue-mimicking phantom. The structure similarity measure (SSIM) and mean-square-error (MSE) of the reconstructed result are approximately 0.94 and 0.04 respectively, while the values obtained from conventional frequency-domain reconstruction methods can hardly overcome 0.35 and 0.41 respectively.

articleTitle: A Differentiable Measure of Matrix Coherence
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A new measure to quantify matrix coherence is introduced that is differentiable with respect to the coherence of left-and right-singular vectors. It is shown to correspond better than standard measures with the performance variance of a random-sampling based algorithm for estimating the spectra of sufficiently rank-deficient and incoherent impedance matrices.

articleTitle: Formula for Generating Gaussian Beams Using Smooth-Walled Conical Horn Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: By studying the design procedures of smooth-walled conical horn antennas and the gaussian beam they create, formulas were derived that relate the antenna's dimensions with the beam parameters. These are presented here, enabling the fast design of horns with specific quasioptical characteristics. Using these formulas, two different sets of horn antennas were designed for wireless power transfer applications which were later built by 3D printing or additively manufactured, at 5.8 GHz and 24 GHz, respectively. These antennas are discussed here, validating the formulas derived previously.

articleTitle: A Career in Progress -- Reflections After 50 Years
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This writing is a glimpse of my career journey throughout the years and the lessons that I learned. I have enjoyed every minute of my professional life and learned so much from my students, collaborators and colleagues. It was once said, “It is not how many papers and books you have written, it is not how many awards you have received and it is not how many of your proposals did not get funded; it is rather your family, your students, your collaborators and your friends that you have touched their lives and in the process, they have touched your life!“

articleTitle: Monolithic Co-Design of a 15 GHz SPDT-Antenna Allowing Polarization Reconfigurability
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a new co-design of a 15 GHz SPDT -antenna for RF seekers. The SPDT -switch permits the commutation between the two possible feeding paths of the antenna and, therefore, a switch able polarization between two linear (horizontal and vertical) ones in order to optimize the detection of targets in future RF seekers. Thanks to the silicon substrate, the active elements, i.e., N+PP+ integrated junctions, and the passive parts, i.e., transmission lines and the antenna, are designed and optimized at the same time, which gives some flexibility and degrees of freedom. The flexibility is given by the possibility to choose the doped-areas size and their position avoiding off-the-shelf components that induce parasitic effects at high frequency. The reconfigurability is achieved using integrated semiconductor distributed doped areas (ScDDAs), forming N+PP+ integrated junctions with a chosen length as long as possible to optimize their performances. Firstly, the concept of the SPDT- antenna is discussed followed by the design, the simulations, the fabrication and ending by the measurement of the demonstrator.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of Filtered Low Noise Amplifier Using Square-Shaped Complimentary Split Ring Resonator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the enhancement of filtered low noise amplifier (FLNA) performance by incorporating square-shaped complimentary split ring resonator (SCSRR). The proposed device which is an integration of bandpass filter (BPF) and low noise amplifier (LNA) is expected able to maximize antenna signal reception for radio frequency (RF) receivers at the frequency of 2.4 GHz. An array of SCSRRs in 2x7 arrangement is loaded into BPF which is developed based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW). While a Darlington connection of RF transistors is use to configure the LNA circuit. The characterization results of realized FLNA yield the gain of 16.278 dB at the frequency of 2.4 GHz with the −3 dB working bandwidth of 1.24 GHz ranging from the frequency of 1.88 GHz to 3.12 GHz. These achievements are comparable to the simulated one, albeit there is some discrepancies occurred.

articleTitle: A J-band Fan-Beam 3-D Printed Reflector Antenna with Optimal Moment of Inertia for High Speed Scanning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A 223 GHz offset reflector antenna for high aspect ratio fan-beam generation is presented. The reflector geometry is made from a section of an elliptic toroidal surface. The reflector is designed to be rotated about an axis at high-speeds for azimuthal scanning. To prevent wobble due to asymmetry, the reflector's center of mass and moment of inertia are optimized by introducing a balancing structure. The reflector along with the balancing structure is fabricated using a low-cost Fused Depo-sition Modelling (FDM) 3-D printing technology. The reflecting surface is smoothed and metallized using a conductive paint. The measured peak gain is 38.7 dBi and the beamwidths are 4.6° and 0.42° in elevation and azimuth respectively.

articleTitle: High-Frequency Asymptotic Solution for Scattered Field Near Transition Region Over Plane Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The scattered magnetic field over a plane meta-material is investigated using a high-frequency asymptotic solution. The role of a transition wave that is a component of a uniform asymptotic solution is clarified. The validity of the transition wave is confirmed by comparing the uniform asymptotic solution with a reference solution. The effects of the distance between a source and observation points on the transition wave are discussed.

articleTitle: Dynamical Modeling for Electromagnetic Problems with Changeable Objects Based on a Truly-Meshless Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Some objects like flame-like plasmas mass could be dynamically changeable in both geometry and materials and the modeling of electromagnetic (EM) interaction with them is challenging. The geometric discretization for the objects is either impossible or very difficult since their boundaries are unclear or time-varying. The traditional numerical methods like the widely-used method of moments seems unable to solve the problem since they strongly rely on the domain discretization. A truly-meshless method is proposed to fully overcome the drawback of traditional methods because it transforms domain integrals into boundary integrals so that the domain discretization can be removed. A numerical example is presented to demonstrate the approach and good performance has been observed.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Endfire Antenna Based on Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons and Substrate Integrated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel design of a circularly polarized (CP) endfire antenna by combining the radiation from spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP) structure and substrate integrated waveguide (SIW). The energy is equally divided into two paths, which propagate along the SIW and SSPP structures and generate the horizontally and vertically polarized waves, respectively. Due to the difference in the propagation constant of two transmission lines, the phase difference of 90° at two orthogonal directions is achieved, and thus a CP endfire radiation is excited by this antenna. By simulation, the 3 dB axial-ratio (AR) bandwidth of the proposed antenna is 9.3% from 26.1 GHz to 28.7 GHz, and the left-hand CP gain is above 8 dBi from 20.5 GHz to 28.2 GHz.

articleTitle: A 3D Planar Partitioning Method for Finite Element Domain Decomposition Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: For large-scale multi-scale targets like target such as Aircrafts, ships and large-scale array antenna, the radar scattering analysis or radiation analysis with traditional numerical methods is very challenging. Domain decomposition method (DDM) reduces the solution scale and improve the solution efficiency by decomposes the original problem into smaller sub-domains. However, the convergence of the DDM is not so ideal for domain meshes of large-scale multiscale problem with the non-planar and irregular interfaces. Therefore, a 3D planar partitioning method for finite element DDM is proposed to overcome this problem. Numerical results verify the accuracy and the improved convergence of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Compact MedRadio Implantable Monopole
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A compact implantable monopole antenna for the MedRadio band is presented. Miniaturization is achieved by partial meandering of the radiating element, and by using a voltage nullifying circuit that substitutes for the ground plane. Simulation and experimental results show that the antenna achieves a realized gain of -19.8 dBi at volume 12.6 mm<sup>3</sup>. Max. SAR and telemetry range are evaluated.

articleTitle: General Analytical EM Model for Active Impedance of 2D PAA with Equivalent Magnetic Currents
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a general analytical model for predicting the active impedance variation with the scan angle of phased array antennas (PAAs) of equivalent magnetic currents is presented. The model is based on Floquet modes expansion of magnetic currents and its application to 2D phased array slot antennas. The simulation results calculated by proposed analytical model are presented and compared to those obtained by the numerical EM solver (HFSS).

articleTitle: Dual Band Dual Polarization Phased Array Employing a Magnetic Material
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper will present the designs and performance of a phased array antenna using magnetic material. Array design and synthesis will be presented, as well as the simulated performance of the phased array.

articleTitle: A V-Band Highly Directive Circularly Polarized Antenna Array for Wireless and Contactless Continuous Glucose Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, we present an aperture-coupled, seriesfed, multilayer structure array antenna for contactless continuous non-invasive glucose monitoring. The proposed miniaturized, highly directive and circularly polarized V-Band antenna array continuously and non-invasively monitors blood glucose variations. Experiments executed on fetal bovine serum (FBS) solutions and in-vivo experiments on animal models demonstrate high accuracy in the ability of the proposed wireless system to continuously track glucose variations across the diabetic range [30mg/dl - 500mg/dl]. Furthermore, clinical studies executed reveal an acceptable clinical ability of the proposed system in continuously detecting glucose variations. The antenna array system integrated into an earring is able to transmit its radiated beam across the veins of the neck to be received by a second antenna array integrated into a second earring on the other side of the neck. To our knowledge, this is the first wearable system that is capable of continuously monitoring glucose variations in a fully contactless manner.

articleTitle: Wireless Microwave Signal Transmission for Cryogenic Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Microwave wireless signal propagation in cryogenic environments has applications in radio astronomy and quantum computing. This paper demonstrates for the first time a cryogenic wireless setup and investigates the antenna-to-antenna signal transmission in Liquid Nitrogen (LN) and inside the dilution refrigerator at room temperature (296 K). The antenna under investigation consists of a wideband antenna operating in from 8–12 GHz. The antenna was modelled and designed in CST MWS and fabricated on the Rogers RT/duroid 5880 substrate. The measured transmission coefficient <tex>$(\mathrm{S}_{21})$</tex> results demonstrate that there was reasonable signal transmission between the antenna pairs when tested in LN (77 K) and inside the dilution refrigerator (tested at 296 K). The results indicate that the proposed Over- The-Air (OTA) system is suitable for cryogenic applications down to 77K.

articleTitle: Development of Highly-Efficient Near-Field WPT and RCN-Based Rectifier for IoT Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a highly-efficient wireless power transfer (WPT) system intended to charge various Internet of things devices. The developed system consists of a compact WPT and resistance compression network (RCN)-based rectifier. Furthermore, both circuits operate at the practical frequency of 433 MHz. It is imperative to mention that realized near-field WPT showed 74% power transfer efficiency for the working distance of 20 mm. In addition, the RCN-based rectifier demonstrated a power conversion efficiency of around 60%.

articleTitle: Direct Antenna Frequency Hopping and Beamsteering with Time-Modulated Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, we present an innovative approach to jointly perform direct antenna frequency hopping (DAFH) and beam steering using time-modulated arrays (TMAs). Considering a time-modulated feeding network (TM-FN) with excellent time- modulation efficiency, DAFH is accomplished by changing the fundamental frequency of the modulating waveforms at each hopping period. At the same time, beamsteering is performed by simultaneously adjusting the time delays of such waveforms.

articleTitle: Intelligent Polarization Reconfigurable Surface for S-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: To realize the concept of reconfigurable (cross/circular) polarization of the reflected wave, a reflective intelligent polarization reconfigurable surface (IPRS), operating in the S-band (3.8 GHz) is presented. IPRS consists of periodic unit cells consisting of square shaped structures with a diagonal element and two PIN diodes as switching elements. The simultaneous biasing of the PIN diodes allows the switching of the polarization state of the reflected wave to either cross or circular polarization. The incident wave is linearly polarized, and with the diodes in OFF state, cross polarization is achieved, while with the diodes in ON state, circular polarization is caused on the reflected wave.

articleTitle: A Predictor-Corrector Based Charge and Energy Conserving EM-FEMPIC Scheme
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The state of the art in electromagnetic finite element PIC (EM-FEMPIC) has advanced significantly in recent years, with the state-of-the-art allowing the use of implicit field solvers while satisfying Gauss' Laws to machine precision. As a result, there is growing interest in exploring more robust particle integration schemes - in particular, methods with superior convergence and stability than the boris integrator that conserve energy on asymptotically large timescales. The objective of this work is to construct such a particle integrator using a predictor-corrector method. We show through our numerical results that the proposed method robustly conserves energy both for single particles and within a complete EM-FEMPIC scheme.

articleTitle: Reflection by Random Rough Surfaces at 300 GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the performance of THz wireless channel operating in the 295.92 GHz to 304.56 GHz frequency region for IEEE 802.15.3d-2017 proposed Channel 54. The ray- tracing simulations are conducted in a simple office scenario for both line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) conditions by applying various modeling approaches to evaluate the influence of Gaussian and non-Gaussian rough surfaces on channel performance.

articleTitle: Modular Phased Array Architecture Optimization for Space Antenna Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The design of modular phased arrays for satellite systems is addressed. The array architecture is simplified through an irregular tiling technique where the number of transmit/receive modules is reduced by using a single output/input for all the radiating elements clustered in a tile. An illustrative example is shown to demonstrate the possibility of using tiled arrays for space applications when considering a domino-like shaped tile.

articleTitle: Array Element Model with Improved Accuracy for LOFAR Radiotelescope
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper discusses the newly araised opportunities for accurate modeling of antenna elements in large antenna arrays. The problem is significant in cases when control of beam pointing side lobes and grating lobe levels is relevant to the correct operation of the antenna array and the analysis of the results.

articleTitle: Large Reflectarray for SAR for Earth Observation: RF Design and Measurement Correlation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper the RF design of a large Ka-band reflectarray for Synthetic Antenna Radar (SAR) application and the correlation with the measured data are introduced. The reflectarray is part of a dual-offset antenna system for a high-resolution and wide-swath SAR instrument. The antenna is optimised to work in the high-resolution mode with a directive beam in one linear polarisation, and in a low-resolution mode with a broad beam in the opposite linear polarisation. A dual linear mode sectoral horn is optimised to enable different beam widths for the two orthogonal polarisation. Measurement of the radiation patterns and correlation with the predicted data are presented to validate the design.

articleTitle: An Invasive Weed Optimized Parasitic-Loaded 6-Elements Symmetric Sequential Array for Automotive Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Sequential arrays are particularly lightweight and easy to manufacture, hence at a premium in vehicular communications, yet their design is more demanding than a conventional corporate feed array. In this contribution a symmetric, center-fed, sequential array of 6 patch radiators, loaded with parasites to enhance gain is optimized via the use of a multi-objective invasive weed optimizer.

articleTitle: 6G Single and 2x2 MIMO Antennas Design using Substrate Integrated Waveguide Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, 6G single and 2x2 MIMO slot antennas are designed in the substrate integrated waveguide technology. The antenna consists of an SIW cavity that is fed by an SIW line and a rectangular slot is carved in the upper metal layer of the cavity. A waveguide-PCB cavity is integrated with the single antenna and prototype of the integrated antenna is measured. The antenna yields -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 15.2% with a peak gain of 8.33 dBi. The radiation patterns are also measured and discussed. The proposed antenna was extended to design two configurations of the 2x2 MIMO antenna and simulated results are presented.

articleTitle: Assessing the Performance of EM-Functionalized PANI-CA Sensors for Varying Geometries
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We have previously demonstrated composites of polyaniline and cellulose acetate (PANI-CA) that bend with response to acetone gas and can be fused with electromagnetic-based resonant loops to quantify their bending. An example application lies in monitoring breath acetone as a biomarker of human metabolism. As would be expected, performance of the resulting sensor depends on the form size of the strip and loops. In this work, we explore such aspects using a numerical parametric study. Our results show that lower power requirements and, in certain cases, detection of bending by more than 160° is made possible simply by increasing the loop size or shortening the strip. However, the sensing dynamic range decreases significantly. These findings can be leveraged in the future to modify the chemo-actuators for better sensing capabilities. Concurrently, these results are generalizable for other applications that rely on thin film deformations.

articleTitle: High-Gain, Broadband Radial Elliptical-Slot Array Antenna with Side-Lobe Mitigation for Low-Cost Satellite Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a high-gain and broadband radial elliptical-slot array (RESA) antenna with side-lobe mitigation technique for low-cost satellite communication systems. The aperture of the proposed slot array antenna comprises a set of orthogonal elliptical slots with monotonic slot length variation alongside the radius of the aperture. The design comprises radiating slotted top plate and bottom ground plate parallel to one another separated by an optimal distance of 5.25 mm which is <tex>$1.05\lambda$</tex>. The design is back-fed using a disk-head radiator probe. The overall dimensions of the proposed slot array antenna with the air-gap taken into account are <tex>$300\times 300\times 5.75mm^{3}$</tex>. Simulation results show that the proposed slot array antenna has a broadband operating frequency range from 45 GHz to 110 GHz and beyond, covering both V and W frequency bands with a fractional bandwidth of 88.8%. The peak gain of the proposed design is 35.6 dBi at 60 GHz. The array exhibits a maximum half-power beam width of 9.5°, a low sidelobe magnitude of - 4.12 dBi and a overall simple design indicates its suitability for low-cost SATCOM (satellite communications) applications.

articleTitle: Performance Estimates of the 18-Meter ngVLA Reflector System with Main Reflector Rim Extension
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The mechanical design of the ngVLA 18-meter offset Gregorian reflector system is nearing completion, and requires a main reflector rim extending beyond the nominal optical path defined by a circular projected rim. The extra reflecting area may thus be used to try to improve the electrical performance of the system with little to no extra manufacturing cost. This paper investigates the effect of including the extra main reflector area on the expected performance of the reflector system, in the presence of the extended sub-reflector used to shield ground noise in the feed-down tipping configuration. It is shown that the extra area indeed improves the aperture efficiency, and receiving sensitivity, substantially – especially when accounting for the shape of the sub-reflector extension. This sensitivity improvement, however, comes at the cost of reduced main beam symmetry, presenting a trade-off in the system design.

articleTitle: Dielectric Resonators-Based Large Frequency Ratio Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a DRA-based large frequency ratio antenna that covers two widely separated frequency bands. The overall antenna consists of an aperture-fed RDRA which radiates at 3.4 GHz, whereas a 1x4 CDRA array radiates at the center frequency of 28 GHz. To reduce the area occupied by the radiators of the different bands, the CDRA array is placed on the RDRA and excited through dielectric-loaded waveguides. Overall, the antenna has the dimensions of 50 mmx50 mmx7.5 mm, and the simulated return loss is better than -10 dB in the regions of 3.28 GHz to 3.47 GHz and 27.52 GHz to 28.42 GHz.

articleTitle: MIMO Antenna Array with Mutual Coupling Enhancement Using Cross-Shaped Meta-Surface Wall
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a multiple input multiple output (MIMO) antenna array with a mutual coupling reduction is investigated using meta-surface (MS) walls. The meta-surface structure is placed normally to the horizontal plane between the array of 2*2 rectangular patches. The suggested array is tested using the CST studio program. The result metrics show the effect of utilizing the meta-surface wall. Utilizing the suggested MS walls reduces the mutual coupling.

articleTitle: Ground Moving Target Detection Using Multi-Features Under Antenna Array Crabbing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a new moving target detection method under crabbing error due to platform motion. Two contour-based attributes known as circularity ratio and bending energy are extracted to a transformed domain of the radar samples. These features are applied to detect the target and non-linear clutter using a machine learning classifier. The effectiveness of the contour-based features is validated with simulation results.

articleTitle: A Modified Mandelbrot Fractal Antenna with Multi-Band Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a modified patch antenna based on a Mandelbrot fractal structure which has multi-band characteristics. The geometry of the patch consists of a Mandelbrot set with different iterations in the degree of 4. Simulation results show that the proposed Mandelbrot fractal antenna has a good performance in gains and radiation patterns. Also, due to the nested structure of the antenna, it has much better multi-band characteristics and an area reduction of 15.0% compared to the Mandelbrot fractal patch antenna with only one single iteration.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Orthogonal-Polarization Transmitarray Consisting of Stub-Loaded Ring Elements and Asterisk Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper describes a dual-band transmitarray with stub-loaded ring elements and asterisk elements as unit cells. By designing each element to be interference-free, a high-gain 8/16-GHz transmitarray is designed.

articleTitle: Electric Field Resonant Coupler for Wireless Power Transmission Using Water as a Transmission Medium
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a method to improve the transmission efficiency of couplers by using fresh water as the transmission medium. The wireless power transmission method in which the transmitter/receiver coupler resonates in the near field has a high transmission efficiency, but has the disadvantage that the transmission distance is shorter than the method in which radio waves are used to transmit power. Measurements and electromagnetic field simulations have confirmed that the use of a dielectric as a transmission medium for electric field waves can extend the transmission distance beyond that of air. In particular, the effectiveness of using fresh water as a transmission medium for electric field waves for the wireless power supply of sensors or equipment floating on the water has been investigated.

articleTitle: Design and Characterization of Line-Waves Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this contribution, we outline a workflow for the design of complementary metasurfaces supporting the propagation of line-waves and check its effectiveness through both numerical and experimental results. Specifically, a semi-analytical procedure for designing the complementary patterned sheets composing line-wave waveguides is discussed and some numerical results are provided for validation purposes. Finally, it is reported the experimental results carried out on a manufactured prototype confirming the expected low-loss behavior at high-frequency.

articleTitle: Novel Dual-Frequency Independent Beam-Scanning Reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel reflectarray with independent beam scanning at dual frequencies. Loaded by a single p-i-n diode, two separate radiating structures in a unit cell are used to flexibly fulfill ideal reflection phases in two arbitrary bands. The fabricated X-band prototype shows that the measured 1-dB gain bandwidths at 9 GHz and 11.5 GHz are 31.1% and 26.1%, respectively, and the achieved scanning ranges are <tex>$\pm \mathbf{40}^{\circ}$</tex> and <tex>$\pm \mathbf{50}^{\circ}$</tex> within 3-dB gain variation.

articleTitle: Progress in Diversifying the Editorial Board of the IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Diversity can be accomplished by making it a priority, but it is not just a numbers game.

articleTitle: Phase-coded Magnetic Metasurfaces for Interference Free Multi-receiver Wireless Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this study, the performance of a resonant inductive wireless power transfer system has been enhanced by introducing a phase-coded low-frequency magnetic metasurface in a multi-receiver arrangement. The magnetic metasurface, composed of an array of spirals cylindrically located in 3D space and loaded with a suitable set of capacitors, is able to both control the amplitude and phase of the magnetic field transferred to the receivers. By carrying out accurate full-wave simulations, we proved that it is possible to obtain two spatial regions characterized by a magnetic field distribution constant in amplitude and 180° out-of-phase even by adopting a single driving coil. Thus, two different receivers can be positioned in the aforementioned regions, obtaining two correspondingly out-of- phase useful currents. In this way, power transfer can be combined with interference-free telemetry for both the receivers, opening the way for a new generation of wireless power transfer systems.

articleTitle: Toward Hyper-Compact Rotman Lenses: Meta-Transmission Line Design and Characterization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present the design and characterization of a linear meta-transmission line (meta-TL) suitable for realizing hyper-compact Rotman lenses. Rotman lenses are true time delay beamforming networks that usually find applications in very-/ultra-high frequency systems such as satellite, radar, and unmanned aerial vehicle systems. The lenses designed using existing techniques tend to be at least <tex>$\mathbf{5}-\mathbf{6}\boldsymbol{\lambda}$</tex> long making them infeasible for practical implementations. In this work, we propose a topology that achieves a very high degree of miniaturization by modifying the lumped element transmission line model. Specifically, by introducing mutual inductance terms between the first nearest neighbors in the lumped element model, we realize the meta-TL. The meta-TL can extend the linearity of the dispersion diagram by slowing down the wave within the line and lead to miniaturization. A 1D meta-TL has been designed, fabricated, and characterized demonstrating good transmission performance up to the cut-off frequency.

articleTitle: A Multitrace Multi - Resolution Preconditioner for Solving Piecewise Homogeneous Dielectric Objects
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The development of a multitrace method including an automatic and multilevel quasi-Helmholtz decomposition, until now only applied to perfect electrical conductors, is here presented for the simulation, via the method of moments, of arbitrary complex geometries composed of piecewise homogeneous composite objects in order to improve the conditioning. A numerical experiment demonstrates the flexibility of the proposed approach for the solution of objects composed of multiple materials.

articleTitle: Array Mutual Impedances Can Be Determined From Antenna Range Pattern Measurements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The relationship between array radiation patterns and mutual coupling can be used to determine mutual impedances from measured embedded element patterns (EEPs). We review the EEP loading condition transformations that form the basis of the method and validate the proposed technique experimentally.

articleTitle: Phased Array-Free Multi-Directional 5.8 GHz Wireless Power Transmission Using A Fresnel Lens
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Steerable arrays are often developed based on complex phased arrays or lossy beamforming networks, making them unsuitable for pervasive wireless power transmission (WPT) applications. Here we propose the first sub-6 GHz quasi-optical beam-steering WPT dielectric lens-based system. The lens has an area of <tex>$16.6\lambda_{0}^{2}$</tex> with a height of <tex>$0.83\lambda_{0}$</tex>, achieving an aperture efficiency of 44.7% and a gain improvement of 10 to 14 dB from 5.2 to 6.5 GHz. <tex>$\mathrm{A}\pm 60^{\circ}$</tex> beam-scanning angle is achieved with linear feed displacements, resulting in a 1 Steradian half-power beamwidth. The proposed design could enable switchable and multi-beam transmitters, with broad-beam high-gain rectennas.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of Wideband Reconfigurable Planar Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Design of a wideband planar reconfigurable antenna operating between 9 GHz and 30 GHz using PIN diodes is presented. The performance of the antenna is further enhanced using defective ground structure (DGS) for bandwidth and cross-polarization. PIN diodes have been implemented for reconfigurability and key antenna parameters such as resonance characteristics, radiation pattern, bandwidth, gain, cross polarization, and co-polarization have been investigated in detail using 3D electromagnetic simulator. It has been shown that the proposed design method provides a better reconfigurability within the wideband frequency range of X and Ka bands by improving several of the key antenna parameters.

articleTitle: Diode-based Switchable Frequency Selective Surface at 3.6 GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The paper presents a switchable FSS using P-I-N diodes at 3.6 GHz. The FSS is designed to be able to switch from the reflecting state to the transparent state at 3.6 GHz by controlling the diodes used to connect adjacent unit cells. When all diodes are unbiased, the FSS blocks waves at 3.6 GHz. In contrast, when all diodes are biased, the FSS allows waves at 3.6 GHz to pass through. Some influence of diodes on FSS properties is discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: An Optimal Design of High-Gain Quasi-Cassegrain Antenna for Ultra-wideband Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this manuscript, the design method for cassegrain antennas using geometrical optics is explained, and performance is analyzed. To reduce the axial dimension of the cassegrain antenna, it is suggested that the sub-reflector be replaced with a disk that is inexpensive and simple to make. The close proximity between the feed and sub-reflector has an impact on impedance matching, gain and bandwidth (BW). Computer simulation technology (CST) software is used to design and analyze the performance of the proposed antenna. The proposed antenna achieves a fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 57.14% from 7.5 - 13.5 GHz with an S<inf>11</inf> < - 16 dB over the band. The antenna has achieved the maximum gains of 43 dBi at 13.5 GHz, while the axial ratio (AR) is less than 1.3 dB over the frequency range. The simulated results demonstrated that the proposed antenna is a strong candidate for C and X-band circular polarization antennas with high aperture efficiency, low side-lobe level, and high gain performance.

articleTitle: A Fast Indoor Coverage Prediction Scheme at 60 GHz Based on Image Processing, Geometrical Optics, and Transport Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: 3D ray tracing is used to accurately predict path loss, phase, and Received Signal Strength for various environments. In this paper, we develop a fast and approximate prediction scheme for indoor path loss using digital image processing, geometrical optics and transport theory. The proposed algorithm is tested in an apartment environment, and its performance is compared against a commercial 3D ray tracing software suite, Wireless InSite®.

articleTitle: Fast Computation for Solving Three-Dimensional Electromagnetic Wave Scattering
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Many applications in electromagnetic engineering require the prediction of the current induced by a large range of incident plane waves. This paper presents an efficient and accurate method for calculating the angular response of electrically large targets. The proposed algorithm consists of three steps: use Fourier harmonics to interpolate the right hand side (RHS) within a given angle range; then reduce the number of independent coefficient vectors in Fourier harmonics by singular value decomposition (SVD); finally, effectively solve the matrix solutions of multiple RHSs with the recently proposed Krylov cycle method GCRO-DR. The numerical results are given and compared with other iterative algorithms to illustrate the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Design of a Reflective Metasurface with Broadband Low Detectability on 3-D Targets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A Reflective Metasurface with Broadband Low Detectability (RM-BLD) is designed in this paper, which is characterized by stable performance in broadband, wide incident angles and 3-D targets. The theory of Generalized Snell Law is introduced in the arrangements of unit cells, which makes contributes to broaden the band and incident angles. Results in different frequencies and incident angles are experimented. The average value of RCS is around -20 dBm<sup>2</sup>, which is greatly reduced. The dihedral corner acting as one of the most typical 3-D targets is introduced as well, which verifies the low detectability of RM-BLD applied in 3-D targets. The design of the RM-BLD provides an innovative metasurface for 3-D targets in the demand of low detectability. For future works, more discussions of the proposed metasurface will be applied to further complex targets.

articleTitle: A Multigrid Algorithm with Scaled Stencils for the Fast Scattering Analysis of Multiscale Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We propose an integral method to accelerate the electromagnetic analysis of multiscale structures, based on a multigrid version of the adaptive integral method (AIM). In the standard AIM, the largest mesh elements constrain the resolution of the FFT grid, increasing the number of expensive Green's function integrations required. To overcome this issue, we introduce the idea of scaled projection stencils that are adapted to the size of each mesh element. The proposed method is shown to be 3.6 times faster than AIM in the analysis of a metagrating, and better suited to handle multiscale meshes where mesh resolution is coarsened on large structures such as ground planes.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Fractal Array Carrying OAM Generated from Characteristic Modes Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper the characteristics modes are used in the analysis of element fractal for projects an antenna array. The fractal element is obtained using Koch transformation implemented in Scilab<sup>™</sup>. From the analysis of the characteristic modes, two orthogonal modes were identified and selected. Besides orthogonal modes are generated for yield circular polarization and fields carrying orbital angular momentum. The results computational were obtained and analyzed in the full wave simulator. The results computational shown a good return loss range and axial ratio of project, therefore, can be applicated to vehicular communication standards, which operate in the 5.9 GHz band.

articleTitle: A Dual Band Printed F-Antenna using a Trap with Small Band Separation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Trap antenna is well known and has many applications. With this method, trap(s) are used on antenna to block currents of some frequencies and so electrically divide the antenna into multiple segments and thus one antenna can work on multiple frequencies. In this paper, trap antenna method is used to design a dual band Sub GHz printed F-antenna. The antenna is printed on FR4 board for low cost. The two bands are 865–870 MHz and 902–928 MHz. The challenge of this design is that the separation of the two bands is small. In this case, the extra section for low band is small. Then, the influence of trap LC component variation due to tolerance to the two resonant frequencies is big, and so it is difficult to achieve good in band return loss within the LC tolerance. This is the main difficulty of this design. The problem is solved by placing the low band section away from the end of the antenna.

articleTitle: Comparison between the Fields Modeled by a Circular Cylinder and a Screen in the Transition Region
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes an additional term between the fields modeled by a dielectric circular cylinder and an absorber screen, based on the uniform theory of diffraction (UTD) in the transition region. In the lit side of the transition region, the additional term is derived from the difference between the reflection from a dielectric circular cylinder and the diffraction from an absorber screen. In the shadowed side of the transition region, the additional term is derived from the difference between the creeping diffraction from a dielectric circular cylinder and the edge diffraction from an absorber screen. The proposed model is validated by numerical simulations at a high frequency. Through the proposal, we clarify the contribution of the Fresnel zone number and boundary conditions (i.e., the surface impedance and the polarization) to the scattered field.

articleTitle: The Bayesian Approach to Derive Wireless Fields in Mobile Stations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The fact that a mobile user moves far away from a fixed antenna base station, can be rise to a stochastic scenarios that are entirely governed by a Bayesian theory. This paper introduces a derivation of the electric field at the mobile station. In addition, the received radiation can be expressed in terms of integer-order Bessel functions. A direct derivation motivates to conclude that wireless channels might be obeying a Bayes statistics in according to the simulations done in this paper.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Enhancement of Circularly Polarized Antenna Based on Dual Layer Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel single-feed circularly polarized (CP) patch antenna loaded with a spiral-rhombus-shaped metasurface layer is proposed for communication application. Based on the dual layer 5 x 5 spiral shape external converter generating linear-to-circularly polarized wave, the antenna's AR bandwidth (ARBW) has significantly enhanced. Based on the mode analysis, the CP antenna's mechanism is theoretically examined. The parameters of single feeding structure are studied to achieve wide impedance bandwidth (BW) and axial ratio (AR) BW. The simulated relative impedance bandwidth and 3 dB ARBW were 21.5 % and 8.5 %, respectively, from 3.87 GHz to 4.21 GHz. The CP antenna has a maximum gain of 6.35 dBic.

articleTitle: Method for Tackling the Variations in the Material Properties of 3D Printed Substrates for Microstrip Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Additive Manufacturing (AM) has been gaining popularity due to its low cost, design flexibility, and mass manufacturing capabilities. Despite the numerous advantages, 3D-printed microwave substrates suffer from a high variation (4%-8%) in the relative permittivity <tex>$(\varepsilon_{r})$</tex>. Consequently, the resonant frequency <tex>$(f_{r})$</tex> of the antennas realized on these substrates can be different from its designed value, which is critical for narrowband antennas, such as microstrip patch antennas (MPAs). In this work, we present a post-fabrication method to compensate for <tex>$\varepsilon_{r}$</tex> variation in 3D printed substrates. In the proposed method, we introduce blind vias in the substrate to tune the frequency to its original value. Unlike other methods, here, we can shift the frequency in both directions, i.e. upwards and downwards. Through simulations and experimentation, we have shown that more than 10% shift in <tex>$f_{r}$</tex> is possible in both directions and this is sufficient to compensate for the typical material variations in the 3D printed substrates.

articleTitle: Professor Yahya Rahmat-Samii: A Remarkable Career in Review
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: It has been 50 years since Professor Yahya Rahmat-Samii received his MS degree from the University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign. The year 2023, marks the anniversary of his 75th year on earth. We highlight the many fields where Professor Rahmat-Samii has made pioneering contributions. He is a true leader in electro magnetics and antennas and has made a tremendous impact in research, on students and colleagues, in service to the greater good, and in leadership.

articleTitle: Tracking Tagged Moving Objects in Cluttered Spaces Using Harmonic Micro-Doppler Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a method of tracking the motion of tagged objects in highly cluttered environments with other moving objects based on the use of harmonic tags and harmonic micro-Doppler radar. The harmonic tag receives an incident signal from the harmonic radar at the fundamental carrier frequency, and generates a signal at the second harmonic of the incident signal that is retransmitted and captured by the radar. Since all of the clutter response exists at the fundamental frequency, the harmonic frequency signal can be more easily detected. Based on this concept, we demonstrate the detection of harmonic micro-Doppler signals from a tagged object in a highly cluttered environment consisting of other moving objects that generate strong micro-Doppler signatures at the fundamental frequency, dominating the fundamental frequency response of the tagged object. Experiments with a 2.8/5.6 GHz harmonic radar and an object tagged with a harmonic tag demonstrate in an environment with a fan in the field of view demonstrate the ability to easily discern the harmonic micro-Doppler response, while the fundamental micro-Doppler response is unrecoverable due to the response of the fan. The tag is narrowband, allowing tracking of multiple tags via frequency selectivity.

articleTitle: Dual-Port Endfire Millimeter Wave Reconfigurable Antenna with Optimized Pixel Surface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A dual-port 1×2 antenna array incorporating a parasitic pixel surface in front of the array is proposed. By optimizing the pixel surface, different radiation patterns can be provided by each port. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach, a dual-port design, with patterns directed to 112° and 66° and gains of 7.87 dBi and 6.95 dBi respectively at 28 GHz, is provided. A feature of the design is that no RF switches are needed in the pixel surface. The proposed antenna array can be suitable for future fifth-generation (5G) wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: A Broadband Dual-Polarized Metasurface Antenna for 5G mmWave Communication Using Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In order to meet the needs of 5G millimeter wave communication, this paper proposes a broadband dual-polarized antenna applied in 5G millimeter wave frequency band. The antenna adopts double-layer patch structure, and the upper patch uses <tex>$2\times 2$</tex> metasurface to realize broadband effect, where CMA theory is used to analysze this double-layer patch structure. Proposed antenna is fed by a slot coupling feed structure. By designing the coupling slot and adopting an air cavity structure, the bandwidth of the antenna is widened. Simulation results show that the -10 dB bandwidth of the antenna at the two ports is 26.25-40.83 GHz and 25.91-41.05 GHz, respectively. Within the working bandwidth, a good port isolation of greater than 21 dB is achieved, and the antenna gain is between 4.9 dBi and 6.7 dBi. The antenna has the advantage of low profile with the size of <tex>$0.56\lambda _{0}\times 0.56\lambda_{0}\times 0.13\lambda_{0}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Manipulation of SPPs Antenna's Radiation Pattern for Satellite and Space Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Sufficient signal coverage in satellite and space communication systems (SSCS) play a vital role in meeting the growing demands for high data rates. One of the fundamental components in a satellite is an antenna that transmits and receives data according to its beam direction and signal coverage level. One satellite orbiting around the Earth is wirelessly connected to either other satellites in the space or receivers on the Earth that are located in fixed and different distances. Therefore, efficient signal coverage according to distance is of great importance. The signal coverage can be controlled by manipulation of the antenna's gain in the satellite. For this purpose, one-layer surface plasmon polaritons (SPP) antennas consisting of two parasitic elements are proposed in order to provide different signal coverage levels for the SSCS. The designed antennas can be used to reduce the system complexity due to their simple and cost-effective configurations. The designed antennas provide a simple solution for controlling radiated beam levels.

articleTitle: 3D-Printed Inhomogeneous Graded-Index Lenses For Antenna Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article presents the realization of a 3D-printed graded-index (GRIN) lens, suitable for antenna applications. By tuning the effective permittivity of the host material using a subwavelength patterning, GRIN lenses can be used for increasing the antenna gain in a range from few gigahertz up to millimeter wave frequencies. This type of 3-D printing procedure is likely to enable many novel antenna and microwave devices based on 3-D metamaterial structures.

articleTitle: A Lightweight X-Ku Band Dual-Polarized Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The Advanced Aperture Solutions team at L3Harris Technologies presents a <tex>$\mathbf{4}\times \mathbf{4}$</tex> lightweight, dual-linear polarized, multi-octave bandwidth Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna (AVA) array suitable for multi-function RF applications. This multi-octave phased array provides an active voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) less than 3.25:1 across X – Ku operating frequency bands. The array is designed with a lattice spacing that achieves grating-lobe free operation covering the field of view of <tex>$\pm \mathbf{45}^{\circ}$</tex> scan angles across the operating bands. This dual-linear polarization AVA array is designed such that it achieves multi-octave bandwidth operation while maintaining low size, weight, power, and cost (SWaP-C) making it an attractive solution for modern airborne multi-function RF missions.

articleTitle: A Circular Polarized Antenna for GPS and Iridium Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A patch antenna for operation with Global Positioning System (GPS) and Iridium applications is presented. The antenna design is based on the modal degeneration principle of disc-based patch, combined with the gap-coupling mechanism to increase the bandwidth of operation. The best design is arranged in a 14x14 cm<sup>2</sup> PCB. The performance expressed in term of maximum gain, cross polarization ratio and return loss are respectively 4.9 dB, 15 dB and 20 dB for GPS operations and 2.35 dB, 15.9 dB and 11 dB for Iridium operations.

articleTitle: Slotted Waveguide for High Dielectric Heating
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A longitudinally slotted waveguide (LSWG) for high dielectric <tex>$(\epsilon_{r}=10)$</tex> heating applications has been designed and investigated. The effect of the key design parameters of this LSWG, specifically the slot length <tex>$S_{L}$</tex> and the offset distance <tex>$S_{c}$</tex> were examined using CST Microwave Studio Suite. When <tex>$S_{L}$</tex> and <tex>$S_{C}$</tex> are varied the waveguide resonates at a different frequency. The <tex>$S_{L}$</tex> has a noticeable effect on the resonance frequency, whereas, the <tex>$S_{C}$</tex> has a limited effect. For the <tex>$S_{L}$</tex> of 20.8 mm and <tex>$S_{C}$</tex> of 4.5 mm the waveguide resonates at 2.45 GHz.

articleTitle: A Study on Determination Method of IRS Reflection Patterns Using Radio Environmental Map
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a determination method of IRS reflection patterns using Radio Environment Map (REM). We predict the locations of users from the time series data of the user's received power and REM of each reflection pattern to increase the coverage probability. Then, numerical simulations show that the proposed method can achieve the higher coverage probability than angular beam scanning when the response time of the IRS is long.

articleTitle: Unified View of Surface Integral Equation Based Sub-Structure Characteristic Mode Analysis Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: As an extension of the full-structure theory of characteristic modes (TCM), a unified sub-structure based TCM has been proposed to provide a unified view of different sub-structure CM analysis methods. The proposed general framework of unified sub-structure based TCM can help us understand different sub-structure CM analysis methods in a unified manner.

articleTitle: A Wideband Reconfigurable and Dual-Polarized Transmitarray Unit Cell
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work presents a wideband, reconfigurable transmitarray antenna (TA) unit cell (UC) design that supports dual-linear polarization. Namely, a novel TA UC is proposed, inspired by the magneto-electric dipole (MED) element, that achieves a 46% fractional bandwidth (BW). This UC utilizes a central via that is appropriately designed to allow the easy integration of the required PIN diodes, and enable 1-bit phase modulation (0° and 180°) between the transmitting and receiving elements. In addition, due to its design simplicity, our element is at least 4 times smaller compared to state-of-the-art MED elements. Notably, the small size and small number of vias of our element enable us to incorporate two orthogonal elements in a single TA UC so that two polarizations can be supported. The wideband performance of our proposed UC in the Ku band is demonstrated using simulation analysis in ANSYS HFSS.

articleTitle: Delay Spread Model for Inter-Rack Environments with Small Mesh Panel at 285GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we derive a delay spread model for inter-rack communication in a wireless data center environment in the 275 GHz to 295 GHz band and present statistical characteristics. Vector network analyzer and frequency extender are used to measure and analyze terahertz frequency band signals in inter-rack communication, and antennas with different beamwidths are used for measurement. The distribution and model of delay spread are derived based on the measured data in our measurement scenario.

articleTitle: A Plasma-Based Technique for Wideband Matching of Electrically Small Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A plasma-based approach for wideband matching of electrically small antennas is introduced and validated in this work. The proposed technique relies on the negative permittivity of plasmas, which can be utilized to realize a negative capacitor within a capacitively coupled structure. The negative capacitance of plasma can compensate for the reactance of small antennas over a wide bandwidth while not introducing a significant loss. So, this technique can be a viable solution for efficient radiation over low frequency ranges, especially for high-power scenarios.

articleTitle: Reduced-Order Mode Discovery in Arbitrary Cavities via Proper Orthogonal Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) is a technique that extracts a set of mutually orthogonal spatiotemporal modes from a dataset of interest; these modes can then be used for analysis of the underlying dynamics of the problem or to construct reduced-order models for fast simulation of new results. Here, we apply the POD to electromagnetic cavities; for canonical cases the technique is able to recover the cavity modes exactly, while for cavities of arbitrary shape or arbitrary filling we are able to extract the dominant (most energetic) modes in a simple and fast way with no modification to the algorithm.

articleTitle: Antenna Fabrication Techniques Using Multilayer Insulation Materials for Spaceborne Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Spaceborne assets are subject to the harsh environments of outer space requiring the use of Multilayer Insulation (MLI) to provide the electronics inside the asset with a stable environment to operate. These assets are vulnerable in contested space and require some means of monitoring their surroundings. Most electronic payloads exploit the environmental stability underneath the MLI. These internal components would not be able to monitor the space outside of the asset. Sensing capabilities that can survive the harsh environments must be integrated to the asset's exterior. In this work, a Leaky-Wave Antenna (LWA) radar is designed and fabricated using bonded MLI materials. The fabrication techniques utilized involve both technical embroidery and laser ablation to create the antenna structure out of and directly on the skin of the spaceborne platform itself. This allows the radar to be integrated conformally onto the MLI surface, using materials which have already undergone space qualification. While this effort focusses specifically on a particular implementation of a conformal radar antenna, the processes developed here uncover a much broader and generalized potential of applications including communication, sensing, and imaging use cases.

articleTitle: Digital Beamforming with Unsynchronized Arrays with Unknown Element Location Errors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In dynamic high-interference environments, classical approaches to digital beamforming typically can't distinguish between the intended signal and interferences, which disrupts the intended operation. We consider a dynamic scenario where carrier frequency offset, in addition to element location errors, severely corrupts the received signal. We show that while traditional methods fail, our solution is effective. We present a mathematical model for the signal under these conditions, and then implement an evolutionary search approach that minimizes the peak interference amplitude using this received signal model. Our numerical studies show that the proposed approach removes the issues with both phase drifts and element location errors in dynamic digital beamforming scenarios.

articleTitle: From Time-Modulated Arrays to Time-Modulated Metasurfaces - Advanced Implementations and Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The exploitation of time-modulated metasurfaces (TMSs) as suitable solutions to be employed in a smart electromagnetic environment (SEME) for wireless communications is preliminarily investigated in this paper. More specifically, a TMS is used to reflect the user's signal towards the direction of the base station by means of optimized switching sequences controlling in time-domain the reflection coefficients of the elementary cells, jointly generating a difference beam at the first sideband harmonic exploited for tracking purposes.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave Defected Ground Structure-based MIMO Antenna for 6G Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a <tex>$\mathbf{2}\times \mathbf{2}$</tex> multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) assembly of an elliptical-shaped millimeter-wave (mm-wave) antenna with defected-ground structures (DGS) is presented. The antenna is integrated with ring slot-shaped cut-outs as DGS on the bottom ground to generate multiple resonances combined in a wide bandwidth of 25.0-29.7 GHz. The simulated results show an efficiency above 75% and realized gain above 4.5 dBi in the entire range with a peak gain of 7.64 dBi at 27 GHz. The proposed MIMO antenna is well-suited for the 6<sup>th</sup> Generation (6G) wireless applications.

articleTitle: Analytical Eigenstate Equivalent Circuit for Narrow-Slot Bi-Periodic Scatterers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The analytical values of the parameters of an eigenstate-based equivalent circuit are obtained for the analysis and modeling of a simple bi-periodic scatterer. The scatterer geometry consists of a rotated, very narrow slot. Analytical values of this kind of equivalent circuit are obtained for the first time by comparison with a fully-analytical multi-mode equivalent circuit. Analytical results are contrasted with simulated ones, and a very good agreement is found.

articleTitle: Channel Capacity of Resonant Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Active/nonlinear antennas do not always have a well-defined impedance or bandwidth, which makes it challenging to provide apples-to-apples comparisons between different antenna technologies. Here, we derive a simple expression for the maximum data rate that can be reliably communicated (i.e., capacity) through a narrowband, passive, resonant antenna. The achievable data rate of every active/nonlinear antenna can be compared to our derived limit for passive antennas. Thus, we introduce a new, well-defined metric for characterizing arbitrary antenna technologies.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Beam-Reconfigurable Antenna Using Multiple Parasitic Elements For UAV Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a low-profile beam-reconfigurable antenna using multiple parasitic elements for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) applications at 5.09 GHz is presented. Multiple parasitic elements consisting of four horizontal parasitic elements (HPEs) and four vertical parasitic elements (VPEs) are arranged around a monopole antenna. Eight bow-tie-shaped HPEs and monopole-shaped VPEs have several advantages, including broadband properties, a reconfigurable beam control, and a small size occupancy for compact low-profile antenna applications. The proposed antenna can control the main beam by electrically switching the PIN diodes in the multiple parasitic elements. It formed an omni-directional reconfigurable beam patterns. The proposed antenna achieves approximately 4.8 dBi of peak gain and a low-profile structure of <tex>$\mathbf{1}.\mathbf{00}\lambda_{0}\times \mathbf{1}.\mathbf{00}\lambda_{0}\times \mathbf{0}.\mathbf{22}\lambda_{0}$</tex> operates at 5.09 GHz.

articleTitle: Theorical Analysis of All-Pass Filter Based Negative Group Delay Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The development of NGD circuits brings new possibilities to microwave technologies. However, due to their construction based on filters cause the signal's amplitude reduction. To overcome this technical limitation, this work analyzes the possibility of NGD circuits based on all-pass filter theory. It is shown mathematically that with non-foster elements, all-pass filter based NGD circuits with almost amplitude flat response and good NGD near the resonant angular frequency can be obtained.

articleTitle: An Improved Deconvolution Algorithm for Sidelobe Suppression in Sparse Array SAR and MIMO Imaging Radars
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A deconvolution algorithm to suppress the sidelobe and grating lobe effects in sparse array Synthetic Aperture Radars (SAR) and Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) radars is proposed. To reduce the cost and complexity associated with large uniform arrays, sparsely populated arrays can be used. This introduces sidelobe and grating lobes effects that degrade the image quality. Knowing the point spread function, these undesirable effects can be suppressed using the proposed deconvolution algorithm. The algorithm comprises of 4 main steps: 1) Peak search, 2) Sweep and Extinguish, 3) Recursive Nulling and 4) Reconstruction. The basic idea is to find peaks and decorrelate them by recursively approximating their location and magnitude. The image quality after applying the algorithm is greatly improved at the cost of longer computation time. The algorithm is experimentally verified using a 31-element X-band circular array with a diameter of 30 <tex>$A$</tex> in scenarios with canonical targets and real-world targets. It is shown to improve the dynamic range by 20–30 dB and the resulting array complexity is shown to be reduced by a factor of 200.

articleTitle: An Unsupervised Learning Approach for Human Activity Recognition Based on Wave Propagation in Wireless Body Area Networks
