publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: On-body propagation in wireless body area network (WBAN) provides a low-cost and energy-efficient method to monitor and recognize human activities. In this paper, the transmission coefficients in WBAN are measured when the body performing some activities, and an unsupervised learning approach is proposed to cluster the unlabeled data so that the human activities are recognized. In the proposed approach, transfer learning is employed to extract features from the unlabeled data. Then the K-Means algorithm is used for clustering and pseudo labels are generated. To evaluate the accuracy of feature extraction and clustering, a CNN model is constructed to train the clustered data with pseudo labels, and the training error is used as an accuracy indicator to guide and optimize the feature extraction and clustering process. Experimental results demonstrate the feasibility and accuracy of the approach.

articleTitle: Microwave Imaging Based Lesion Monitoring During Infarct Ablation: Feasibility Study
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Sudden cardiac death rate post-myocardial infarction due to arrhythmia is increasing. Cardiac ablation of infarcts is shown to reduce arrhythmogenic events. Current methods are inadequate to monitor the lesions during infarct ablation. Therefore novel noninvasive tools are necessary to provide real-time monitoring of ablation and to titrate the ablative power to reduce arrhythmogenicity. The purpose of this simulation study was to demonstrate the feasibility of microwave imaging (MWI) to monitor the temperature profile of the lesions during infarct ablation. A 2D model of the left ventricle was used with an infarct region of interest for microwave imaging electromagnetic simulation at 915 MHz using known myocardial dielectric properties and its temperature dependence. Distorted Born Iterative Method (DBIM) was used to reconstruct the relative permittivity that is mapped to the temperature field and compared within the infarct region. Good agreement was observed between the reconstructed and assigned temperature field within the infarct region. The study demonstrates the feasibility of using MWI for the non-invasive assessment of infarct tissue temperatures during ablation.

articleTitle: Bianisotropic Susceptibility Theory of Artificial Magnetic Conductors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Over the past 30 years, Artificial Magnetic Conductors (AMCs) have generated immense interest in the microwave community. However, their description has been restricted to crude RLC design or subsidiary transmission-line network modelling. This paper introduces an electromagnetic theory of AMCs in terms of bianisotropic susceptibilities. This theory will be completed by precise explanations of the corresponding dipolar responses in generic AMC structures that will be presented at the conference.

articleTitle: High-Efficient Double Negative Metamaterial-based Absorber
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a multi-layered, high-efficient metamaterial-based absorber operating at 3.7 GHz. The metamaterial is constructed on the basis of a single unit cell (UC) and possesses a compact board size of 25-by-25 sq. mm. It is imperative to mention that the UC parameters were optimized in order to obtain maximum efficiency. Besides, a feed line was added to the bottom layer that enables connecting the metamaterial to any given load with a 50-Ω impedance. Finally, the designed metamaterial demonstrated the double negative material properties and the absorbance efficiency of 85%.

articleTitle: Material Selection and Process Optimizations of Additive Interconnects in Printed Circuit Boards
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Additive Manufacturing (AM) is a rapidly growing technology which many industries have employed in design and manufacturing processes. Use of AM in Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs) is of particular interest since AM allows for more compact design. Using AM processes to create conductive conformal interconnects has the potential to reduce the mechanical stress when compared to traditional wire bonding. In addition, the conformal traces require less physical space in the design. In this work, an AM interposer is mounted into the cavity of a traditionally manufactured PCB, with a gasket securing the interposer. Conductive traces are printed from the PCB to the interposer across the gasket material. Careful selection of material based on adhesion and electrical properties, and optimization of print parameters were crucial to ensure the highest performance and reliability of the interconnects.

articleTitle: An Accurate Retrieval Method for Complex Electrical Parameters of Materials Based on Partially Filled Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Determination of the permittivity and permeability for penetrable materials is very important in many applications. There exist several common techniques such as resonant cavity method, free space method, and waveguide method presently. Partially filled waveguide method is another one which enjoys the feature of reduced fabrication precision requirement for the dielectric sample under test. In the original paper proposing the partially filled waveguide method, only TM modes are considered. Through mode matching analysis, we show in this paper that both TM and TE modes shall be considered so as to give correct results.

articleTitle: Cavity-Excited Metagrating Antennas with Controlled Frequency Diverse Patterns
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a semianalytical approach to design frequency diverse cavity-excited antennas, using metagratings (MGs, sparse arrays of subwavelength scatterers). Harnessing the reliable frequency response prediction of the underlying analytical model, tying the MG parameters to the waveguide eigenmode composition at the aperture, a single MG design that radiates prescribed (significantly different) patterns at different frequencies is obtained. This systematic method and resultant devices, validated via full-wave simulations, could find use in mm-wave imaging systems and emerging security schemes.

articleTitle: An Electronically Reconfigurable Dual-Mode Dual-Band Ring Antenna Based on CMA
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, an electronically reconfigurable dual-band dual-mode microstrip ring antenna is proposed. By performing a characteristic mode analysis (CMA) on the ring antenna, two modes are identified that can be used together to cover with their radiation the entire half space. Notably, to excite these modes, an electronically reconfigurable matching network is developed. Due to the inherent orthogonality of characteristic modes, isolation greater than 60 dB is achieved between the antenna's ports for our two selected modes of operation.

articleTitle: Improving Wireless Power Transfer Efficiency Using Fractal Metamaterial for Wearable Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a wearable wireless power transfer (WPT) system that utilizes fractal antennas integrated with a fractal metamaterial (MTM) layer. Simulations are carried out using ANSYS HFSS. The effects of changing the distance between transmitter and receiver antennas and the position of the MTM surface are studied in a layered model of human body tissues. Simulation results show improvement in multiband power transfer efficiency (PTE) with the use of an MTM surface. The self-similar structures in fractal metamaterial allow for a compact design and enhanced multiband performance. The effect of horizontal misalignment and lateral movements in the presence of MTM are reported.

articleTitle: Characterization of Concrete Curing Using a Microwave Harmonic Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The paper describes a process to use a microwave harmonic sensor, or frequency doubling reflectenna, to understand the evolution of water content during concrete curing. The harmonic sensor has a 3D form factor, is constructed from printed circuit board pieces, and operates at 1.2 GHz (receive) and 2.4 GHz (transmit). The system operates by interrogating a sensor that is embedded in the concrete under test using a wireless reader and correlating variation in signal strength received back from the sensor with the complex permittivity of the concrete. Empirical results from tests of sand-water mixtures, sand-ionic solution mixtures, and cement mortar mixtures are presented. The data demonstrate high sensitivity in signal strength versus moisture and ionic content for relatively low, realistic moisture conditions.

articleTitle: Single-Pixel Chaotic Cavity Bandwidth Control using Rotman Lens-Based Multiplexer/Demultiplexer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the integration of a microwave multiplexer/demultiplexer based on a Rotman Lens, with a cavity-backed metasurface antenna, for the first time, which represents a key step towards achieving efficient and cost-effective channel characterisation at microwave frequencies. Converting wideband signals into multiple sub-band signals and distributing their computations to parallel processing units can enable high-performance characterisation with low-order computational complexities.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Analysis of Moving Ideal or Matched Plane Wave Source with the FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: By using the Finite Difference Time Domain method, this work proposes an original analysis concerning electromagnetism with moving bodies. An ideal plane wave source is modeled with a plane of current sources, whereas a matched plane wave source is modeled with current sources and resistors matched to free space. Numerical full-wave simulations show that energy is not conserved for a moving ideal plane wave source, whereas it is conserved for a moving matched plane wave source. The energy is defined as the integration of the square of the amplitude of the electric field over the frequency spectrum. We show why the ideal source is not realistic and we describe the consequences of our analysis. We believe that the reported results are novel and important in the theory of electromagnetism.

articleTitle: A Near-Field 3-D Imaging Radar Using a Sparse Spotlight MIMO Array for Weapons Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A sparse aperture Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) array for radar imaging of targets in the near-field is proposed. The array configuration is chosen to be uniform in order to support high-speed imaging using the Fast Fourier Transform. The sparsity condition combined with a uniform array provides a narrow main beam at the cost of large grating lobes which severely degrade image quality. By focusing the array in the near-field, these grating lobe effects are shown to be suppressed. The drawback of placing targets too close to a sparse array is that elements on the edges of the array do not illuminate the target. To overcome this, the elements are oriented in a spotlight mode, such that each antenna maximally illuminates the target region. An <tex>$18\times 18$</tex> MIMO array for spotlight mode imaging at X-band is designed. The array elements are chosen to be U-slot patch antennas for their wide bandwidth and stable phase center over the entire band. The multi-static polarimetric scattering response of a handgun placed 2 m away is simulated and used to construct an image which is of high enough resolution and quality to correctly identify the target.

articleTitle: Compact Directional Button Antenna Based on Curved Metamaterial for On-Body Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: <tex>$A$</tex> compact directional button antenna based on curved Artificial Magnetic Conductor (AMC) is proposed to integrate easily into clothing for on-body wireless power transfer (WPT). The antenna is fed by the microstrip line, and a curved 3 × 3 AMC cells are adopted to reduce the horizontal size and reduce the spacing between the monopole and reflector. The monopole is loaded by two substrates, one is directly connected and has the same radius, while the other has a larger radius. An efficient design method is employed for the curved AMC cells such that the resulting radiation characteristics remain unaffected compared to those of the flat one. Finally, the influence of the human body is studied by using a human arm model.

articleTitle: On the Large-Scale Parallel Scalability of Advanced EFIE Formulations Suitable for Multiscale Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Many electromagnetic structures are multiscale and extremely complex, calling for scalable parallel solvers of Maxwell equations. We perform the first parallel scalability investigation with up to 5,120 cores of two EFIE formulations suitable for broadband and multiscale simulations. We show that formulations relying on sparse matrix factorizations do not scale well beyond hundreds of CPU cores. We develop a parallel implementation of the multiplicative Calderon preconditioner, and demonstrate excellent parallel scaling with up to 5,120 cores, with a speed up of up to <tex>$10.4\times$</tex> compared to an alternative approach.

articleTitle: Analysis of Moving Metallic or Dielectric Scattering Cylinders with the FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work proposes an original analysis of the illumination by electromagnetic plane waves of moving metallic cylinders and moving dielectric cylinders. Full-wave numerical investigations are carried out by using the Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) method. The implementation of motions is done by changing the positions of bodies at each cycle of the FDTD time loop. With this approach, time is implicitly absolute and Voigt-Lorentz transformations are not implemented. This technique is suitable for most problems in antennas and propagation domain, where non-relativistic speeds are considered. Configurations with multiple cylinders moving at different speeds are also studied. The numerical results are analyzed and discussed in detail, based on electromagnetic theory.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Regolith Antenna for Future Lunar Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel regolith (in-situ) -based substrate for a circularly polarized antenna. Fabrication of regolith substrate using regolith soil, cement, and water in a specific combination. Regolith substrate has been measured which has a low dielectric constant of 2.08 and a dissipation factor of 0.00527. The antenna works at a center frequency of 6.175 GHz. It uses two-stacked regolith substrates with each substrate having a size of 30 x 50 x 2 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. It has an RHCP single radiating patch with a corner truncation. The results show that the measured impedance bandwidth and axial ratio bandwidth are 794 MHz (12.8%) and 386 MHz (6.25%), respectively. The antenna has a gain of 6.3 dBic and a VSWR of 1.4 at 6.175 GHz. Regolith has great potential for an antenna substrate to support future telecommunication infrastructure in the lunar environment.

articleTitle: An Optically Transparent Antenna on Glasses for 2.4GHz WiFi
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The optically transparent antenna potential to release the antenna volume constraints in compact mobile devices such as smart glasses. The transparent conductors have a trade-off between optical and electrical properties. Antenna performance is to be maximized to a level where the optical properties are acceptable. This paper reports optically transparent antenna by fine metal mesh that provide us for better resistivity. The proposed antenna is a slot antenna formed between a transparent conductor and a metal form factor, shows a total efficiency better than -4.0dB at 2.4GHz WiFi band.

articleTitle: Phased Array Antenna-in-Package Design for True-Wideband mmWave 5G Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The phased array design for millimeter (mmwave) 5G communication need numerous concurrent features, such as wide bandwidth, high gain, dual-polarization, and wide beam scanning capability. However, due to mutual coupling and grating lobe issues, it is difficult to simultaneously attain a real wideband operation for all of the aforementioned parameters. Most published papers have only demonstrated wideband operation for one or two parameters. To achieve a true wideband performance, this work used a variety of design techniques, including stacked patch architecture, electromagnetic band gap (EBG) structures, and the rotation of components. In this paper, a 5 by 5 phased array is realized in a multilayered low-temperature co-firing ceramic (LTCC) substrate, along with its feeding network. The phased array's element is designed to be a dual linear polarized stacking patch antenna with notched corners to ensure the antenna's wide bandwidth. The orientation of the array element is adjusted 45 degrees for mutual coupling reduction. The proposed phased array achieved a bandwidth of 6 GHz (24 to 30 GHz). It also achieves a maximum gain of 17.5 dB and a beam steering capability from -50 to +50 degrees. The features of multilayered implementation, low dielectric loss, and excellent packaging properties ensure a compact and high-efficiency phased array design and qualify this design as an antenna-in-packaging (AiP) design.

articleTitle: Reduction in Cross-Polar Fields in a DRA: Higher Mode vs. Conduction Current Control Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work explores a connection between the ground plane (GP) conduction current and higher order HEM <tex>$21\delta$</tex> mode in a cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna in light of cross-polar radiation. Ground plane engineering has been proposed to synthesize these current components. The same structures have been deliberately excited for HEM <tex>$21\delta$</tex> mode. The impact of current synthesis on HEM <tex>$21\delta$</tex> mode and its radiation pattern is studied. Significant suppression of fields due to <tex>$\mathbf{HEM}_{216}$</tex> mode is obtained revealing the role of conduction current on higher order mode.

articleTitle: Multi-Band Wearable Metasurface Antenna for Wireless Body Area Network Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper investigates the performance of a metasurface (MTS) based multi-band wearable antenna. The antenna is designed on the flexible and stretchable polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) polymer substrate having a compact dimension of 100 × 100 × 0.3 mm<sup>3</sup>, This antenna resonates at 4.23 GHz, 5.76 GHz, 7.3 GHz, and 8.85 GHz. A simple effective technique has been utilized to achieve circular polarization. By using MTS, directive radiation pattern has been achieved. The simulated performance of the designed antenna is analyzed with respect to different antenna parameters, including reflection coefficient, radiation pattern, directivity, voltage standing wave ratio, and electric-field distribution. From the performance metrics, it can be said that the proposed antenna will essentially be exploited for the application of wireless body area network (WBAN) applications.

articleTitle: A Magnetoelectric Dipole Antenna Structure for Scalable Phased Array Applications (Invited)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper discusses an L-shaped magnetoelectric dipole structure in a metal cavity environment targeted for scalable phased array applications. The structure takes into manufacturability requirements consideration enabling its deployment in product-grade 5G solutions.

articleTitle: A Modified T Shaped Complex FIR-Circuit for Simultaneous Transmit and Receive System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In full-duplex systems, both the transmitter and receiver operate simultaneously at the same frequency band. Hence, simultaneous transmit and receive systems (STAR) are spectrally efficient. However, self-interference (SI) is a major challenge for STAR implementation, especially across large wide bandwidth. In this work, a self-interference cancellation circuit (SICC) with low profile and 1 GHz SI suppression is presented. The SICC consists of a complex multi-tap T shaped finite impulse response (FIR) that allows for wideband coupling suppression of 26 dB across 1 GHz of operational bandwidth.

articleTitle: Prediction of indoor radio propagation using deep neural network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Radio propagation prediction is important for improving the stability and reliability of wireless communication systems. However, propagation loss prediction models by multiple regression based on measured data have problems in setting appropriate parameters and function types. This paper evaluates a radio propagation model that applies machine learning for indoor environments. The proposed neural network has the input parameters of the environmental characteristics such as floor area, ceiling height, and materials, and a dropout layer that disables the network units randomly is inserted to improve generalization performance. The RMSE (root mean squared error) by the proposed model is less than 5 dB for both training and test data and the proposed model can predict the indoor propagation more accurately than conventional models.

articleTitle: Identification of Hearing Impaired People in Crowded Environments Using Wi-Fi Signals
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this article, Wi-Fi signals are used to find hearing-impaired people in a crowded environment with the help of different gestures namely “empty, one-hand right, one-hand left, two-hand right, and two-hand left”. The existing system for recognizing hearing-impaired people is based on cameras. This has some drawbacks, such as poor photo quality at night, privacy concerns, and the high cost of putting these systems into everyday life. The data collected from the Wi-Fi is represented in the form of channel state information (CSI) values. Five activities were performed by the subject namely empty, one-hand right, one-hand left, two-hand right, and two-hand left. Support vector machine (SVM) (Linear SVM), Ensemble (Subspace discriminant), and neural network pattern recognition were performed on collected CSI values. The simulation results showed that 94.7% of classification accuracy was achieved by neural network pattern recognition while classifying gesture data.

articleTitle: Design of T/R Module for Far-Field WPT Applications with Third Harmonic Receiver Tracking System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: An advanced T/R module architecture for farfield wireless power transfer (WPT) application is proposed in this paper. In order to eliminate the alignment mismatch and correspondingly to increase the overall efficiency, third harmonic receiver tracking feature is employed in the proposed T/R module. Here, the T/R module transmit the power at 2.45 GHz and receives the feedback power at 7.35 GHz for direction estimation and precise alignment between the T/R module and the power seeking node (PSN). To realize compact PCB of the T/R module, coplanar waveguide matching is incorporated. Proposed architecture is simulated in SystemVue software and the complete link budget analysis shows that the realized WPT system can be used for indoor applications up to 2 meters.

articleTitle: Radiation Efficiency on Platform Excitation Antenna with Lossy Media
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The platform excitation antenna has been proposed for mobile devices to improve the radiation efficiency of the small antenna installed on the devices. However, lossy media such as liquid crystal displays (LCD) is also installed on the devices and is expected to have a negative impact on platform excitation. This paper investigates the influence of lossy media such as LCD on the radiation efficiency of the platform excitation antenna.

articleTitle: 3D-RL MIMO Capacity Estimations Under Vegetation Blockage
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Multiplexing gains are one of the many promises for increasing throughput in multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) systems. In this sense, a rich scattered environment may be beneficial for the multiplexing capabilities of the MIMO channel. However, mm Wave frequency bands tend to have less effective multipath contributions than sub-6 GHz bands. In this work, an in-deep analysis of the multiplexing capabilities in a mm Wave vehicular-to-infrastructure (V2I) channel is performed. Metrics that may impact the channel capacity like received power and angle-of-arrival (AoA) Spread are fully analyzed as well.

articleTitle: Pixelated Metamaterial Determination Using Genetic Algorithm and HFSS/Matlab Integration
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A pixelated metamaterial was designed using a genetic algorithm (GA) to match the reflection coefficient to that of a Gap Ring Resonator structure. The significance of this is that a GA can be used to arbitrarily meet design a goal without one knowing the priori of the physical metamaterial structure. The pixel mapping was controlled by interfacing Matlab with HFSS. Using the full wave simulation power of HFSS, s-parameters were exported to feed into an optimization cost function. Completion of hundreds of simulations led to the final pixel mapping that closely matched the response of the Gap Ring resonator across a wide frequency range.

articleTitle: Welcome Message from the General Co-Chairs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: You are cordially invited to the 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting – AP-S/URSI 2023, from July 23–28, 2023, at the Oregon Convention Center and Hyatt Regency, in Portland, Oregon, USA, the City of Roses. This conference is cosponsored by the IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society (AP-S) and the US National Committee (USNC) for the International Union of Radio Science (URSI). It is intended to provide an international forum for the exchange of information on state-of-the-art research on antennas, propagation, electromagnetic engineering, and radio science.

articleTitle: Directional and Omnidirectional Sources for an Elliptical Microwave Imaging Setup
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Microwave imaging using an elliptical conducting enclosure provides a focused beam, higher signal intensity at the location of the object-under the-test (OUT), and better electrical shielding, as a result, the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) improves, reducing the necessary number of samples for a given image resolution. In this paper, we investigate the performance of omnidirectional and directional antennas used as sources in elliptical microwave imaging systems.

articleTitle: Microwave Imaging Using Quasi-Conformal Transformed Luneburg Lens
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a microwave imaging experiment using a Quasi-Conformal Transformation Optics Modified 3D Spherical Luneburg lens. The 3D modified Luneburg lens has a diameter of 60 mm and a maximum directivity of 17 dBi at 18 GHz. The single-frequency imaging experiment through full-wave simulation demonstrates the potential of using a Modified Luneburg Lens for imaging applications.

articleTitle: A Large Aperture Parabolic Cylinder Deployable Mesh Reflector Antenna for Next-Generation Satellite Synthetic Aperture Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The tensegrity synthetic aperture radar (TenSAR) antenna architecture is a unique next-generation high-aspect-ratio deployable reflector that promises to enable surface deformation and change (SDC) monitoring with low-Earth orbit (LEO) small satellites. We present the development of a novel C-band parabolic cylinder deployable mesh reflector with a 7 <tex>$\mathrm{m}\times 1.5\ \mathrm{m}$</tex> rectangular aperture as the first TenSAR antenna demonstration. Unique stowage and deployment mechanisms are implemented for the first time for this mesh deployable reflector. A lightweight <tex>$1\times 32$</tex> element linear patch array feed based on honeycomb substrate is designed to test the performance of the reflector. The measured reflector antenna achieved a measured gain of 42.06 dB at 5.357 GHz, with half-power beamwidths of <tex>$0.52^\circ$</tex> and <tex>$2.35^\circ$</tex> in E- and H-plane.

articleTitle: Maximizing Pencil-Beam Pattern Performance in Metasurface Antennas Through Full-Wave Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We propose a design and optimization scheme for metasurface antennas that decouples the antenna and the feeding structure to maximize the antenna performance. This approach uses 2.5D fast algorithms to simulate the large antenna, significantly decreasing the amount of time and complexity required compared to 3D full-wave simulations. The optimization process is designed to maximize the antenna efficiency within a pencil beam pattern mask with a predefined database of unit cells. We present numerical results of the 3D metasurface antenna model comparing our code with a commercial solver to demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Loop Antennas with Balanced, Unbalanced, and Quasi-Balanced Feeds
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Three different feeds are used to realize a loop antenna with wideband circular polarization. The loop is backed by the ground plane and analyzed using the moment method. It is found that the antennas with balanced and unbalanced feeds radiate left and right-hand circularly polarized waves with 3 dB axial ratio bandwidths of 13% and 3%, respectively. Subsequently, the balanced feed is transformed into a quasi-balanced one for impedance matching. It is found that the VSWR remains less than 2 in an axial ratio bandwidth of 11%.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Metamaterial Absorber for Terahertz Sensitivity Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study presents a design for a terahertz-range metamaterial absorber capable of sensing changes in the refractive index of the surrounding medium. Adjacent etched rectangular patches on the top of a Gallium Arsenide (GaAs) substrate with a permittivity of 12.94 are used in the design. The proposed design produces two successive absorption peaks with absorption efficiencies of 98.46% and 87.35% at two distinct resonant frequencies of 1.77 THz and 2.91 THz, respectively. In addition, the quality factor (Q-factor) is about better than 25 for both frequency bands. The proposed absorber is a good candidate for terahertz sensing applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of AOA Estimation Error in UWB Indoor Positioning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Angle of arrival (AOA) estimation is of great importance to ultra-wideband (UWB) indoor positioning. However, the thermal noise and antenna coupling will introduce nonlinear azimuth errors inevitably to angle estimation results in an UWB indoor positioning system. In this paper, the theoretical influence of thermal noise and antenna coupling on AOA estimation is analysed. Three simulations are conducted to evaluate the practical influence of signal-to-noise ratio, antenna amplitude coupling and antenna phase coupling on AOA estimation. The quantitative results are analyzed and will provide important references to UWB positioning applications.

articleTitle: Dual-Band GNSS L-Band Antenna with a lean Design for an Automotive Integration
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A dual-band circular polarized L-band antenna is presented which combines a small size, easy fabrication of only one antenna part and an exceptional low effort in additional circuitry. The antenna allows an operation in the L2 and L1 Band of GNSS services in typical automotive integration spaces. A cylinder-symmetric right-hand circular polarized radiation pattern is achieved for both frequency bands with a gain of more than 5 dB within the L1 band and around 1 dB in L2 band, keeping an AR around 3 dB for the acquisition of waves transmitted by GNSS satellites. The antenna consists of only one punch-bent panel which can be pressed into an ESD-protection cover.

articleTitle: Metamaterial Antennas for RADAR and SAR
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: RADAR and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) systems require broadband directive antennas. Directivity requires antennas to be large, which turns out to be impracticable in many applications. This work presents a combination of an array of Vivaldi antennas with a slot ring resonator metamaterial for SAR applications. As such, vertically and horizontally polarized Vivaldi antennas can be simultaneously used for transmission and reception, allowing the use of lower transmission power with higher temporal duration signal instead of emitting high power pulses for short instants. The prototype at 2.3 GHz band is etched on an FR4 substrate and is fabricated and measured, obtaining similar results between simulation and measurements. Measured results show that, at 2.3 GHz, the metamaterial correctly transforms a linear polarization into a circular one while the array gain obtains its maximum. The proposed array allows for a more compact and easy-to-use test platform, being a valuable solution for SAR systems.

articleTitle: Frequency-Reconfigurable Artificial Magnetic Conductor with Wide Tuning Range
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A concept of frequency-reconfigurable artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) based on open-stub-loaded varactors with wide tuning range is presented. The design consists of a square patch with two open-stub-loaded varactors connected to two edges of the patch along one direction. The working principle is based on the impedance transformation characteristics of the stubs, which is exploited to load varactors for attaining the frequency reconfigurability. By applying a variable bias voltage on the varactors, the AMC operation frequency can be tuned continuously from 3.36 to 4.98 GHz while maintaining a reflection amplitude better than −3 dB. To satisfy the miniaturization requirement of the design, a commercially available substrate material WavePro from Garlock Sealing Technologies with a high relative permittivity of 10 is used in this design. The AMC performance is analyzed and characterized based on reflection coefficient and phase tuning range of its unit cell in simulation.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Low Frequency Portion of Ultra-wideband Antennas through Lumped Components
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna elements typically provide great performance about the center frequency of their operation, but require overly large geometry to cover the low frequency edge of their bandwidth. Here, we have utilized a shunt inductor and series capacitor to enhance the low frequency resonance from the ultrawide bandwidth antenna element and its ground plane. This allows for effective coverage of all Long Term Evolution (LTE) bands from 600 MHz – 6 GHz in a 25×32×1.6 mm surface mountable antenna element, suitable for Internet of Thing (IoT) applications.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Path Loss Prediction with Satellite Maps
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In recent years, with development of the six generation (6G) communication, higher requirements have been placed on high accuracy and low complexity of channel modeling. Deep learning techniques applied to channel modeling are promising solutions because of the high nonlinear fitting capability and low computational complexity. In this paper, we propose a deep learning-based model to predict path loss with satellite images. The model is analyzed and validated by using millimeter wave channel measurement data at 26 GHz in a vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) scenario.

articleTitle: Additive Manufacture of a Compact 8×8 Element Waveguide Array at mm-Wave Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A compact 8×8 element waveguide array with complex internal structure is described. Designed for mm-wave applications at 78.5 GHz and realized using aluminium SLS additive manufacturing techniques, maximum dimensions are 26.4×26.4×13.0 mm (1.04” x 1.04” x 0.51”). Simulation and measurement data are presented.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Radiating System for High-Power Microwave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A dual-band high-power antenna system operating in L-band at 1.3GHz and S-band at 3GHz, in Megawatt pulsed regime, is presented. The design consists of a wide-band corrugated horn antenna with a metallic lens and a dual-band waveguide diplexer. The system demonstrates good performance in terms of matching, isolation, and radiation at both frequencies of operation.

articleTitle: Active-Isolation Improvement Based on Phase-Only Optimization Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel methodology based on the phase-only optimization technique is proposed to realize the high isolation in a shared-aperture millimeter-wave phased array antenna. It is hard to realize the high active isolation in shared-aperture due to the increase of the mutual coupling between elements and the surface wave effect. In order to enhance the realization and reduce the complexity of the hardware design, two active isolation models are proposed for a shared-aperture phased array. Based on the combined expression of the active isolation and the radiation characteristics, by extracting the common factor, a fast optimization of the active isolation and the radiation performance through the optimization of the phase excitations can be realized. By attaching an extra set of phases to the port, the array with a good active isolation can be accomplished in the designated scan region with a little degradation of the radiation performance. As an example, in a K/Ka dual-band dual-circular-polarized shared- aperture phased array antenna, more than 50 dB of the active isolation can be achieved in the scanning range of ±50°.

articleTitle: Flexion Effect on the Radiofrequency-Induced Heating for Modular External Fixation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper studies the influence of flexion on radiofrequency (RF) – induced heating for patients with modular external fixation under 1.5 Tesla (T) and 3T magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) systems. Four configurations of a modular external fixation are developed to suit different patients' postures. They are applied at the same position on the patient's body. Numerical simulations are performed with patients loaded at three imaging landmarks. RF-induced heating in terms of peak averaged specific absorption rate (SAR) over 1 gram (peak <tex>$text{SAR}_{\mathbf{1}\mathbf{g}})$</tex> near the device is evaluated. The variation of peak <tex>$\text{SAR}_{\mathbf{1}\mathbf{g}}$</tex> is up to 44% at 1.5T and 48% at 3T due to the flexion of modular external fixation. Therefore, it is recommended flexion impacts should be considered for the RF-induced heating of modular external fixation.

articleTitle: An Anomalous Refraction Metagrating for Normal to Oblique Mode Conversion Into a Dielectric Medium
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper we present a metasurface that is able to convert a normally incident wave from free space into an obliquely propagating wave inside a dielectric with high efficiency. The metagrating is simulated as four layers of periodic wire gratings on a dielectric substrate and is able to convert a normally incident wave at 18.9 GHz to symmetric oblique modes propagating in the <tex>$\pm 65.4^{\circ}$</tex> directions inside the dielectric with transmission coefficients of <tex>$2.9 \text{dB}$</tex> and <tex>$-3.7\text{dB}$</tex>. All other propagating modes at this frequency, including the specular reflection and normal transmission modes, have a magnitude less than <tex>$-15\mathbf{dB}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Design and Verification Methodologies of D-Band Antenna Modules for Security Imaging Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This research presents the design and verification methodologies of cavity-backed slot antenna (CBSA) modules for D-band security imaging applications. First, to realize low-loss feeding networks in the D-band spectrum, the microstrip transmission line (TL) and 3-D interconnection structures based on the multi-layer low-temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) process have been designed and characterized. Moreover, to achieve low-loss interconnection in local-oscillation (LO) & intermediate-frequency (IF) parts of transmitting (TX)/receiving (RX) modules, the transition structures between FR-4 PCB and LTCC have been realized by utilizing a flip-chip bonding process. Second, the CBSA with low-loss 3-D interconnection structures has been proposed for coupling mitigation between the indium phosphide (InP) chipset and antenna. Finally, the antenna modules have been integrated with InP TX/RX chipsets using bonding wires. The measured EIRP of the TX module and conversion gain of the RX module exhibit <tex>$3.3\sim 6.6\ \text{dBm}$</tex> and <tex>$15.0\sim 25.5\ \text{dB}$</tex> at <tex>$117\sim 145\ \text{GHz}$</tex>, respectively.

articleTitle: Deep Q-Learning Based Beamforming in the Presence of a Jammer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Upcoming protocols and next generation mmWave communication standards require effective beamforming capabilities to compensate for the path loss suffered by high frequencies carriers. In this paper we explore an alternative to conventional beamforming in the form of reinforcement learning based methods. Instead of using using a lookup table based approach we investigate a reward maximization policy and formulate the Q-learning and the deep Q-learning framework framework to carry out beamforming steering while avoiding a jammer signal.

articleTitle: Wideband Circularly Polarized Low Gain Turnstile Antenna for Cube-Sat Tracking Applications at UHF-Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work proposes a broadband circularly po-larized turnstile antenna for CubeSat tracking applications at the UHF band. Broadband performance of the antenna is achieved by coupling two sequentially rotated identical radiating elements and coupling between the downward bent legs of the radiating elements and the upward bent cross-shaped reflector. As a result, 33% impedance bandwidth is achieved along the frequency band 357 MHz to 500MHz. Furthermore, the proposed antenna also accomplishes 27% 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth along the frequency band 376 MHz to 495 MHz. Realized gain of the proposed structure is 4.5 dBic, and the cross-polarization level of 16 dB is achieved with the proposed structure.

articleTitle: A Graph Neural Network-Based Electric-Field Prediction Model for Exposure Assessments
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Grasping the electric-field (E-field) distribution is challenging yet important for monitoring the electromagnetic field (EMF) exposure level. In this paper, a graph neural network (GNN)-based prediction model is proposed to estimate the E-field distribution in a complex indoor environment. The model provides a good accuracy and has an appealing feature of being quite efficient.

articleTitle: Wideband Conformal Transmitarray Employing Tightly Coupled Huygens Element at E Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A new method to achieve wideband conformal transmitarrays is presented by employing tightly coupled Huygens element in this paper. The element is composed of five pairs of metallic strips which are printed on two sides of a dielectric substrate. The tightly coupled elements can achieve a high transmission and a nearly full phase coverage in a wide bandwidth from 71 to 87 GHz. To further analyze the element, equivalent circuit models are developed. Good agreement is achieved between circuit and full-wave simulations. A cylindrical conformal transmitarray at 78 GHz is designed, fabricated and measured. The measured results have good agreement with the simulated ones. The measured peak realized gain is 26.6 dBi with an aperture efficiency of 37.2%. The measured 3-dB gain bandwidth is 20.4% from 71 to 87 GHz, which can fully cover the E-band spectrum.

articleTitle: Improvements on Low-Loss Material Characterization Based on Wideband Radar Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Distinguishing benign materials from potential hazards is an essential step in speeding up the personnel screening process in airports. In our previous works [1], [2], we have introduced an automatic algorithm for characterizing lossless and lossy materials. This paper proposes a method for having a more accurate characterization algorithm by automatically tuning the algorithm parameters for lossless, low-loss, and lossy mediums. The approach is applied to a previously developed algorithm. Having the location of the body-worn object on the 2D reconstructed radar cross-section, we predict the nominal body contour, and find an approximate location for the front and back surface responses caused by the presence of the attached object. Next, we search for the more dominant response and tune the characterization algorithm's thresholds based on this feature. Tuning the algorithm parameters based on intensity of features seen on the image helps improve the characterization result for low-loss materials.

articleTitle: Enhanced Gain mm- Wave Ridge Gap Waveguide Antenna based on Two Partially Reflective Layers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper discusses a novel wideband partially reflective unit cell (PRUC) for improving the gain of mm-wave printed ridge gap waveguide slot antenna (PRGWSA). The proposed PRUC is composed of two different metal-dielectric layers spaced by an air-gap. Over the frequency range of around 60 GHz, the PRUC exhibits a positive reflection phase slope and a high reflectivity. An array of 4×4 PRUCs is placed at an optimum distance from the PRGWSA to enhance its gain. A gain enhancement of 12.6 dB is achieved compared to the antenna without the array of PRUCs. The proposed antenna operates between 55.4 to 66.6 GHz (18% bandwidth) with a 3-dB gain bandwidth ranging from 58.6 to 66.4 GHz (12.5%), and it shows high directive symmetrical radiation patterns.

articleTitle: A Wideband Cryogenic Phased Array Receiver for Radio Astronomy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Phased array receivers can dramatically increase the utility of existing large aperture radio telescopes. Here we present the design and measured performance of a cryogenic phased array receiver for the Parkes radio telescope. The receiver covers the 0.7GHz to 1.95GHz frequency range and exhibits noise performance equivalent to similar single pixel receivers but with a larger field of view.

articleTitle: 1-Bit Reconfigurable Phase Shifter for mm-Wave Antenna Beam-Steering Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A 1-bit reconfigurable phase shifter for 28 GHz mm-wave beam steering antennas is proposed. The design uses two beam-lead GaAs PIN diodes loaded on a microstrip transmission line in parallel, to provide two discrete phases for the transmitted signal. When the diodes are switched OFF, no shift in the phase of the transmitted signal is observed while a phase shift of ~90° is achieved when the diodes are switched ON. The total length of the phase shifter is <tex>$\sim\lambda /2$</tex>. The compact size, low cost, reduced complexity and easy adaptation in antenna and phased array technology makes it a suitable candidate for 5G mm-wave beam steering applications.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Dual-Band Switched-Beam Antenna for 24/28 GHz Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A reconfigurable switched-beam antenna using a frequency-selective surface (FSS) active cylindrical structure is proposed. The antenna was originally designed and manufactured for 2.4 GHz in [1]. The Harmonic dual-band operating characteristics in the S11 graph were observed in the 24/28 GHz band. The entire structure is validated by CST simulation Studio. The antenna is promising in 5G applications where multiple beams are needed simultaneously.

articleTitle: Improved Cortical Stimulation Efficiency Using 3D Rotating Fields in Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This investigation proposes using 3D rotating fields for coupling the coil with neurons as an alternative to conventional Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS) techniques. This method requires calculating the field components necessary to rotate the vector field in a two-dimensional plane at a given point of interest Our results indicate that this approach activates neurons in that plane efficiently. In addition, the study demonstrates that selective activation of neurons is possible by restricting the rotation of the vector field plane to a three-dimensional sphere using an external circuit that adjusts the amplitude and phase difference between the field components. Computer simulations of human head models with orthogonal coils were used to verify the suggested approach.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of Non-Stationary Vehicle-to-Vehicle Massive MIMO Channel Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) wireless communication, which makes use of large number of antenna arrays to improve the network's capacity and propagation characteristics, is regarded as a crucial technology for non-stationary vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) 5G wireless communications. In this paper, a real-time measurement campaign is conducted at 3.5 GHz to investigate the channel capacity and angular spread (AS) of angle of arrival in elevation and azimuth planes for the cross-polarized and co-polarized antenna arrays by using Bartlett algorithm in subway tunnel. Results reveal that at the shorter separating distance between transmitter (Tx) and receiver (Rx), the channel capacity improves with increasing AS and co-polarized antenna arrays have a larger channel capacity than cross-polarized antenna arrays. The results are quite useful for antenna design and polarization-based MIMO system analysis in V2V environment.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband Compact Planar Antenna for Wearable Microwave Medical Imaging Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel low-profile ultra-wideband antenna for wearable microwave medical imaging (MMI) applications. The proposed antenna has a monopole structure with two triangles and a few parallel slots cut at the bottom corners and top edge of the radiation patch, respectively, to achieve an optimized ultra-wide bandwidth and a smaller antenna size. The simulated and measured results show that the antenna prototype can realize a bandwidth of 93% from 0.9–3.0 GHz with a realized gain of 3.32 dBi. Furthermore, in order to verify the performance, we investigate the feasibility of classifying brain strokes between an intracranial haemorrhage stroke and an ischemic stroke with this antenna. The S parameter of the antenna varies significantly with the stroke types introduced (i.e., different dielectric constants), which demonstrates the applicability of the antenna for such use scenarios in MMI.

articleTitle: Wullenweber Antenna for Secondary Surveillance Radar - Part 2 -
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The Wullenweber antenna for the secondary surveillance radar is proposed and numerically analyzed. The unbalanced fed ultra low profile inverted L antenna is used as element antenna. Nine element phased array antenna mounted on the side of sixty-faced polygonal cylinder with its radius of 1,400 mm is studied at the design frequencies from 1.03 GHz to 1.09 GHz.

articleTitle: A Comparison of Image Reconstruction Versus Array Layout in a 24-Element 38-GHz Active Incoherent Millimeter-Wave Imaging System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We compare the image reconstruction quality of two array layouts in a 24-element 38-GHz active incoherent millimeter-wave (AIM) imaging system. Compared to traditional passive millimeter-wave imaging systems, AIM imaging uses the transmission of spatiotemporally incoherent signals, leading to better sensitivity and enabling image reconstruction at rates exceeding 650 fps. Fast imaging of conducting objects may lead to improvements in a number of applications including non-destructive evaluation. AIM image reconstruction quality, and thus the capability to diagnose defects, is highly dependent on the physical layout of the antennas. In this work we compare a traditional Y-shaped array with a uniform circular (O-array) layout with the same number of elements. The O-array has less redundancy and thus yields more spatial frequency samples, leading to improved image quality. We investigate imaging of a set of conducting objects to show improved spurious signal reduction in the O-array.

articleTitle: Comparative Investigation of Iterative Solutions of the All-Frequency Stable Formulation and Its Vector-Potential-Only Variation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: An all-frequency stable formulation has been proposed and applied to solve low-frequency and multiscale electromagnetic problems to avoid the low-frequency breakdown catastrophe of the traditional vector wave equation. Based on the potential representation of the fields, this formulation involves vector and scalar potentials, as well as an auxiliary potential to enforce the gauge condition. In this paper, such a formulation is first simplified to involve vector potential only. Their iterative solutions are then sought by using an incomplete LU preconditioner and an iterative solver. The iterative performance of both formulations are investigated in a comparative study.

articleTitle: A mmWave, SiGe, 2x2 Spiral Array Design Using Sequential Rotation with Dual Circular Polarization for 6G and B5G Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: With the evergrowing throughputs beyond-5G (B5G) and 6G technologies promise, higher frequency bands need to be explored in order to satisfy the required communication bandwidths. To achieve this, cutting-edge RFIC-process of 130 nm SiGe BiCMOS has enabled the manufacture of integrated circuits capable of reaching Terabit/s communications at frequencies well above 100GHz. In this paper, a 2x2 SiGe spiral antenna array with dual circular polarization is presented. With a bandwidth of 30GHz and a central frequency of 200GHz, it is designed to be a building block for a future, fully integrated “frontend on a chip” in SiGe that could enable future generations of wireless connectivity in the mmWave range.

articleTitle: Integrated Millimeter-Wave and Microwave Antennas for Smartphones
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: An innovative, simple, low-cost, and practical integration solution of a millimeter-wave (mmw) antenna module based on a thin (0.3 mm) flexible printed circuit (FPC) and an FR1 (i.e., 410–7125 MHz) microwave (mcw) antenna based on a metal frame of a handset is presented for smartphone applications. The thin FPC-based mmw antenna module consists of a <tex>$1\times 4$</tex> mmw antenna array covering 5G band n261. The metal carrier of the mmw antenna module is electrically connected to a metal-frame-based FR1 mcw antenna in a smartphone as an extension of the FR1 mcw antenna. The FR1 mcw antenna can support multiple LTE bands 12, 13, 17, 28, and 30, and the WLAN 2.4-GHz band.

articleTitle: Bistatic Scattering Analysis of Vegetation Using Fast Hybrid Method of Full Wave Simulations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Bistatic scattering analysis of vegetation is an important element in developing remote sensing applications for microwave measurements. Previously, we applied the hybrid method (HM) to full wave simulations of realistic vegetation geometries. However, HM was limited to solving a relatively small number of scatterers. To accelerate the solving of the Foldy-Lax multiple scattering equations, the fast hybrid method (FHM) was applied to solving a much larger number of corn plants in a vegetation field. The FHM procedure for scattering is described in this paper. A bistatic scattering analysis of 49 corn plants by FHM showed good agreement with FEKO. The CPU time and memory of the FHM required less than 190 seconds and 570 Mbytes, respectively, and the computation can be readily performed on a standard laptop.

articleTitle: Shared Aperture Based Antenna in Package Incorporated with Connected Slot and Patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A shared aperture antenna (SAA) system consisting of patch and connected slot antenna array (CSAA) is presented. The antenna system covers the sub 6GHz and millimeter wave (mm-wave) bands. Coaxial probe fed patch antenna and corporate fed four element CSAA are designed in a package environment obtaining a bandwidth of 200 MHz and 0.77 GHz in the two bands respectively. The designed patch antenna has a far-field gain of 2.2 dB and the CSAA has a gain of 7.73 dB respectively.

articleTitle: Ultra-Thin Planar Reflection-Less Lens Based on Miniaturized-Element Frequency Selective Surfaces for a 230 GHz Polarimetric Single-Aperture Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A 230 GHz low-mass, ultra-thin, planar, and reflection-less lens antenna based on miniaturized element frequency selective surfaces (MEFSS) is designed, fabricated, and tested. This lens is designed to provide a narrow beam (0.88°) and high gain (44 dBi) while having a very low reflection coefficient (−35 dB at resonance) measured at its feed. This antenna is a key component in a dual-polarized, and single-aperture radar designed for radar studies of traffic scenes in the 230 GHz band. The phase compensation for the lens is accomplished locally with phase delays through distributed 3-pole spatial filters that make use of only shunt elements. This lens includes three MEFSS-gold patterned layers and two layers of glass substrate. The lens has <tex>$\mathrm{F}/\mathrm{D}=1.4$</tex> and is fed by a dual-polarized horn whose half-power beamwidth covers the aperture of the lens. The fabricated 4″ lens is only 387um thick and weighs 7g which is 13 times lighter and 44 times thinner than an equivalent dielectric lens (the same size and F/D) without degradation in gain but much improvement in average reflection coefficient from 226–234 GHz(> 10dB).

articleTitle: Evaluation of Methods to Generate Spread Spectrum Time Domain Reflectometry
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Reflectometry is used extensively to measure electrical characteristics such as impedance, fault location and detection, and wire degradation due to aging. Reflectometry is often not used on energized systems due to interference, the potential for device damage, or poor SNR. These issues have been solved in wireless communication systems using pseudo-noise (PN) codes. Combining PN codes and reflectometry creates spread spectrum time domain reflectometry (SSTDR). SSTDR enables reflectometry measurements on energized systems. This paper explores the tradeoffs in methods to implement SSTDR systems. Analog circuits can be used for simplicity but come at the cost of size. ASIC design is utilized for smaller circuits with less flexibility and higher initial costs. FPGAs allow for greater flexibility but typically don't go above 600 MHz. Current research is underway to implement SSTDR with software-defined radios (SDR), which will have the advantages of flexibility as well as high frequency options.

articleTitle: Investigation of Direction Finding Algorithms for a Circular Ring Array of Various Aperture Sizes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work investigates the direction-finding performance of a ring of various radius sizes and compares the performance for both a periodic and a random assortment of sensors. The topologies are filled with isotropic radiators, and the overall distribution is generated as a random filling of the topology or a periodic filling along the perimeter. Last, the direction-finding capabilities of circular arrays of different size radii are simulated in this work using MATLAB with comparisons of the periodic and randomly distributed sensor arrays using three different direction finding algorithms.

articleTitle: Unidirectional Patch Antenna Without an Extended Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel unidirectional quasi-patch antenna is proposed whose top surface and the ground plane exhibit the same sizes. Eight metal screws are assembled on the antenna connected with the ground plane as chokes. By adding these screws, good unidirectional radiation is realized in the upper plane. A prototype is fabricated, assembled, and tested. Good impedance matching with a high front-to-back ratio (FTBR) is experimentally validated. The peak realized gain of the proposed antenna is 5.68 dBi in simulation and 4.05 dBi in the measurement. And the measured FTBR is beyond 18.5 dB at the center frequency of 2.045 GHz. The measured FTBR and realized gain demonstrate that the proposed antenna could be a good candidate for devices in the Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystem.

articleTitle: Fast Simulations of Reflectarray Antennas using Quasi-Periodic Surfaces (QUPES)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The simulation time of reflectarray antenna increases with increase in size of the array. In this paper we discuss about the simulation of a Ka-band reflectarray antenna using quasi-periodic surfaces (QUPES) by TICRA, which significantly reduces the simulation time when compared with Ansys HFSS. The far-field pattern measurement of the reflectarray antenna is compared with HFSS and QUPES and shows differences in the side lobe levels. When array sizes exceed 5000 elements simulation time can be reduced for initial analysis.

articleTitle: Characteristics of Terahertz Low Profile Generalized Luneburg Lens Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the characteristics of generalized Luneburg lens (GLL) Antenna in terahertz frequency band are studied. According to the definition of GLL, the focus of traditional Luneburg lens (TLL) is designed inside the lens, and subtracts the part of behind focus to reduce the profile. A 220GHz rectangular pyramidal horn is used as the feed. The simulation results of CST Microwave Studio show that although the gain of GLL antenna is lower than that of TLL antenna, the beam scanning angle of feed rectilinear off-focus is improved. We reasonably explain the above phenomena according to the geometric structure of the lens. Finally, the gain is improved by changing the feed beamwidth. This research can not only reduce the lens profile, but also improve the scanning angle.

articleTitle: Solution of the Discontinuous EFIE Using Higher-Order Mortar Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The mortar method has emerged as an alternative to Discontinuous Galerkin formulations as a means of ensuring solution continuity in adaptive refinement of the EFIE. This work describes the application of the mortar method for higher-order discontinuous solution spaces on nonconformal geometries. The mortar method for the EFIE is demonstrated for higher-order basis sets, and results are presented to demonstrate the accuracy of the method for canonical scattering geometries.

articleTitle: In-Plane Circularly-Polarized Light Enhancement using Surface Lattice Resonances
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We investigate the use of Surface Lattice Resonances (SLRs) and resonances to enhance circularly polarized light (CPL) on a plane. We first review the basic mechanisms of SLRs and highlight the challenges and opportunities that they offer for in-plane CPL magnification. A figure of merit is then proposed to evaluate the enhancing efficiency of arbitrary unit-cell arrangements. Guidance to optimize the lattices is given and applied to design hybrid gold-graphene metasurfaces with large CPL field enhancement. In-plane field amplification provides new venues to unlock several applications in fields such as spintronics and nonreciprocal on-chip photonics.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of an Ultra Wideband Millimeter-Wave Array with 20:1 (2 – 40 GHz) Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel ultra-wideband (UWB) array operating from L-band to 40 GHz is presented. The novelty of this design is the simplified fabrication using a hybrid approach that uses i) low-loss Rogers substrate for fabrication of the antenna elements and feed, and ii) 3D printed structure for high-precision assembly. Simulations showed a VSWR < 2.8 at broadside and scanning down to <tex>$45^{\circ}$</tex> in all planes across the 2 - 40 GHz band. These simulations will be validated through fabrication and measurement of a 15 × 15 array prototype, to be presented at the conference.

articleTitle: 26.5/39.5 GHz Millimeter-Wave Phased Arrays Utilizing Microstrip Patch Antenna Elements for 5G Wireless Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Two 26.5/39.5 GHz 4-element antenna arrays utilizing patch antenna elements are presented for mmWave 5G wireless communication applications. RT/duroid 5880LZ laminate is used as the substrate to provide sufficient bandwidth for two millimeter-wave bands as well as maintaining low mutual coupling effect between the adjacent elements. The resonance frequencies and bandwidths are set to be 26.5 and 39.5 GHz and 1.7 and 2.2 GHz, respectively. The element spacing is set to be 0.55λ0 that provides at least 22 dB of isolation between elements. The 26.5/39.5 GHz arrays show pure linearly-polarized radiation patterns with the gain of −12.8/12.4 dB and 27.5/21.4 dB of front-to-back ratio. The antenna arrays are utilized in a dual-beam concurrent mmWave beamforming receiver.

articleTitle: A Wearable mmWave Radar System for Continuous Cardiopulmonary Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A 60 GHz wearable radar system is introduced for the first time for the continuous monitoring of human respiratory patterns and cardiac waveforms, including the detection of the respiratory rate (RR) and heart rate (HR). Full-wave electromagnetic simulations are presented to investigate the performance of the radar antennas in close proximity to a human subject. A physical prototype was developed, and a measurement campaign shows high accuracy levels for RR and HR detection, with cardiac displacement waveforms being mapped successfully against a standard electrocardiogram (ECG).

articleTitle: Miniaturized Millimeter Wave Resonators with Self-Biased BaM Films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Miniaturized millimeter wave resonators that are based on the ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) of M-type barium hexagonal ferrite (BaFe<inf>12</inf>O<inf>19</inf>, BaM) films are proposed and simulated. The operating frequency can be up to 50 GHz without external biasing magnetic fields by virtue of the internal anisotropy field of BaM films. A novel strip line ridge structure is utilized to couple energy from transmission line to the ferromagnetic resonators. An equivalent circuit is used to optimize the design, and simulation results from full-wave simulator (HFSS) agree with circuit simulation results from ADS.

articleTitle: Development of MegaWatt Traveling Wave Antennas for Plasma Heating at the DIII-D
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present an overview of the development of two high power traveling wave antennas (TWAs) termed the “comb-line” and the “finline” for launching fast and slow waves in plasmas. The comb-line antenna which has been deployed at the DIII-D National Fusion Facility tokamak can couple megawatt (MW) level RF power into the tokamak plasma with <tex>$\sim$</tex> 2% reflected power and <tex>$\sim$</tex> 2% dissipated power per array element at its design frequency, 476 MHz. A prototype of the finline antenna which has been designed to launch lower hybrid slow waves at 4.6 GHz, has reflection coefficient below 10% with 1.8 dB insertion loss.

articleTitle: Effective Simulation of Broadband Absorbers Using MoM/SIE and 2D Periodic Green Functions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: For effective simulation of broadband absorbers using MoM/SIE we propose the use of a) higher order basis functions, b) optimal dynamic meshing throughout the frequency range, c) efficient evaluation of 2D periodic Green's functions combining Ewald, modified Cesaro and Shank transforms, and d) parallel run of simulations at each frequency, in reverse order, from the highest to the lowest one. The method is demonstrated on a pyramidal absorber of maximal electric dimension of 13.75 wavelengths in vacuum using 150 frequency points, and the ratio of stop and start frequency equals 150.

articleTitle: High Gain Shared Aperture Antenna for Simultaneous Operation in L-Band and Ka-Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present a shared aperture antenna operating at both of the sub-6 and millimeter-wave (mmWave) frequency bands. Our antenna has a wide range of applications in 5G and satellite communication systems, where largely separated frequency bands are needed. More in detail, a loop antenna operating at L-band (viz 1.7 GHz) and a patch antenna operating at Ka-band (viz 38 GHz) are placed concentrically on a single surface. Concentric placement facilitates the use of a lens which enhances the overall directivity. Simulation results show that the designed antenna along with the lens can provide very high gain beams (~20 dBi) at both 1.7 GHz and 38 GHz. The obtained gain can be enhanced further by modifying the collimating structure's dimensions.

articleTitle: A Series-fed Microstrip Patch Array for Airy Beam Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work presents a series-fed microstrip patch array for the airy beam generation. The travelling wave antenna array consists of 16 amplitude and phase tapered elements with an inter-element distance of half the operating wavelength to achieve the desired Airy beam generation. The proposed microstrip array is designed and simulated in a full wave EM simulator at 2.4 GHz to observe the airy beam generation in the near field region. The obtained simulated result is compared against the theoretical Airy profile to observe the correlation exhibiting a good correspondence.

articleTitle: 2X Faster Solution of Computational 2D Electrostatic Problems Using Artificial Neural Network and Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present direct solution of 2D physics problems through neural network optimization. We further demonstrate transfer learning to achieve a faster convergence. We consider 2D second order differential equation, specifically, Poisson equation, to show the concept. We obtain error convergence below 10<sup>−6</sup>, and for a same residual error, up to 1.8 times faster convergence is shown compared to FEM and 2.7 times faster convergence is shown through transfer learning.

articleTitle: Doubling the Convergence Speed of Planar Topology Optimization Using the Multigradient
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Metasurfaces and metalenses promise the potential to be transformative in the way we design optical and nanophotonic systems.
