Because high performance is essential in these areas, metasurface designers have sought out device parameterizations which can reach very high efficiencies. Topology Optimization (TO) has been one such method owing to the freeform structures it is capable of producing. Indeed, TO is notable that despite facilitating very high degrees-of-freedom, as a local, gradient-based optimization technique, it nevertheless converges quite quickly compared with global optimization methods. In this paper, we share our recent work on improving the convergence of TO for the specific class of planar, lithographically fabricated metasurfaces using the multigradient. The new method is shown to converge twice as fast as the conventional method for a representative supercell design problem. We believe this method has the potential to transform how nanophotonic TO is done, with potential applications extending well beyond planar devices.

articleTitle: Stabilization of the Integral Equation for Modelling Metasurfaces via Impedance Boundary Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Impedance Boundary Condition (IBC) is a widely used approximation in the analysis of metasurfaces, and it greatly simplifies the design process. However, for some ranges of impedance values of practical interest in metasurface applications, the Integral Equation formulation has shown instabilities. This contribution proposes a way to improve that shortcoming; the method is based on the property of the involved operators and the nature of the IBC approximation.

articleTitle: Design and Measurement of W-Band On-Chip Antennas for an Array IC on a Thick PCB Module
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, various conventional on-chip antennas for a 2D array system are fabricated and compared. In a 28- nm complementary metal oxide semiconductors (CMOS) process, bow-tie, dipole, and folded dipole antennas are implemented to be packaged modules on a thick printed circuit board (PCB). The effect of silicon thickness and PCB on radiation characteristics is analyzed. Measurements are performed on polyvinyl chloride (PVC) plastic chuck as a thick PCB module. Bow-tie, dipole, and folded dipole antennas achieve boresight gains of -3 dBi, -5.3 dBi, and <tex>$-6.4\text{dBi}$</tex> and 3-dB beamwidths of <tex>$\pm 30^{\circ}, \pm 40^{\circ}$</tex>, and <tex>$\pm 70^{\circ}$</tex> at 90 G Hz, respectively.

articleTitle: Edge-based Material Cell Meshing for Improved Accuracy of Laguerre-Fdtd Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The unconditionally stable Laguerre-FDTD method is suitable for simulating 3-D multi-scale structures. In this work, a new meshing scheme for treating material cell in Laguerre- FDTD method is proposed to improve the simulation accuracy. This scheme uses linear average calculation of effective material property at edges of a material cell. Numerical results show that the proposed algorithm achieves significant improvement in simulation accuracy over conventional meshing.

articleTitle: Mode Conversion of Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons Based on Boundary-Modulated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a boundary-modulated spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP) waveguide with in-band suppression is proposed. A mode conversion between the first two modes of SSPP can be achieved by modulating the boundary with a wavy shape. As a result, a notched band can be generated. Moreover, the bandwidth can be controlled by regulating the dimensions of the proposed boundary-modulated waveguide. The simulated passband is from 1 GHz to 6.8 GHz with a return loss higher than 20 dB. The maximum attenuation of the notched band can reach 20 dB at 4.2 GHz. This work provides a new idea for the design of notched-wideband (NWB) bandpass filter (BPF) based on SSPP.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Metasurface Antenna Based on a Single Control Signal
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: <tex>$A$</tex> doble-layer reconfigurable metasurface antenna controlled by varactor diodes is presented. The structure is composed by a sinusoidally modulated metasurface on top, which is backed by a uniform metasurface loaded with varactor diodes and designed to accurately control the phase propagation. Beam-scanning dictated by a single parameter is performed. Numerical results are reported, demonstrating the good performance in terms of beam shape and aperture field control.

articleTitle: Adjoint Optimization of Reflectarray Antennas in the Presence of Failures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Reflectarrays (RA) are frequently being deployed in place of traditional phased arrays due to their advantages of spatial feeding, high gain, and low power consumption. Compared with phased arrays, RA performance is more dependent on the unit cells comprising the array. Thus, it is important to understand the impact that both environmental and systematic failures have on individual unit cells and how these effects translate to reduced array performance. A primary technique to mitigate these failures and extend the lifetime of the array is to retune the remaining working elements to recover the lost performance. A variety of recovery techniques have been investigated and successfully applied to phased arrays using array factor analysis. However, more complex RAs composed of hundreds of elements may not accurately be represented with an array factor. To overcome these complications, we propose the use of adjoint optimization paired with full-wave simulations to efficiently retune RAs affected by random phase failures. We demonstrate an exemplary case that applies this approach to a 625-element offset fed reflector to recover 0.9 dB of 2.9 dB lost from a 24% element failure.

articleTitle: Refractive Index Sensing with Plasmons in 2D Metals
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we show that nano-engineered ultrathin two-dimensional (2D) metal films supporting infrared plasmonic resonances can enable highly responsive refractive index (RI) sensing. Our results reveal the strong dependence of the RI sensitivity on the 2D-metals' thickness. In particular, for a 1-nm-thick analyte layer, a RI sensitivity up to 110 nm/RIU (90 nm/RIU) is observed in atomically thin 2D-In (2D-Ga) nanoribbons exhibiting highly localized plasmonic resonances at mid-infrared wavelengths.

articleTitle: 28–38 GHz Phased Array 5G Antenna Design for Future Smartphone Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Broadband phased array antennas with wide-scan and smart beam-steering are desirable to meet the requirements of future cellular networks. This paper discusses the characteristics of a new beam-steerable phased array design having broad bandwidth for 5G communications. The discussion is focused on smartphones, due to their small size and complexity. The design procedure is straightforward and accomplished on a mainboard of future smart handheld devices. The introduced phased array design involves eight circular-dipole resonators with a <tex>$1\times 8$</tex> linear form. The resonators have small sizes with microstrip-line feedings. For -10 dB, the design represents 28–38 GHz covering multiple bands in the 5G spectra.

articleTitle: Parameter Identification for Symmetrical Prandtl-Ishlinskii Hysteresis Model Using Gauss-Newton Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The Prandtl-Ishlinskii (PI) hysteresis model has been used to describe nonlinear hysteretic behaviors. In this paper, the PI model is first simplified to accommodate the symmetrical behavior of ferromagnetic hysteresis. A parameter identification method is then developed to extract the parameters of the symmetrical PI model from experimental data. Based on the Gauss-Newton method, regularization technique, and line search method, the model parameters can be retrieved efficiently from the measured data. Numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Accurate Imaging Algorithm with Dual-Path Propagation Loss for Monostatic System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: An accurate image reconstruction algorithm is presented in this paper for a monostatic millimeter-wave imaging system. The proposed physical model treats the incident and scattered waves as spherical waves, and therefore incorporates the dual path propagation loss. The algorithm is derived from the more accurate mathematical model with proper consideration of wave propagation and scattering. Numerical data are used to verify the performances. And simulated results for the root mean square error (RMSE) and the structural similarity (SSIM) indicators confirm that the new algorithm is more accurate.

articleTitle: Transmission Phase Controllable Rasorber Using All-Metal Cross-Polarization Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a rasorber, which has a middle high-transmission window and a controllable transmission phase response. A cross-polarization converter acts as a reflecting ground and provides a large phase shifting range with a low insertion loss. A lossy layer with two kinds of resistor-loaded patterns is applied to achieve the dual-polarized absorption. The total 360° transmission phase variation required for the applications of phase compensation is achieved. Meanwhile, dual-polarized significant absorption properties can be obtained in both lower and higher frequency bands.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface for Arbitrary mm-Wave Polarization Using Parasitic Enhancing Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The design of a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) for mm-waves with arbitrary polarization is proposed. At mm-wave frequencies, the RF switches needed in the RIS suffer from low isolation, and therefore a parasitic enhancing structure (PES) is also proposed to improve switch performance. In the RIS element, a dual-port dual-polarized patch antenna is used for scattering. Both ports of the antenna are connected to independent phase-reconfigurable circuits based on diodes, with PES, and these can provide 180-degree phase shifts. Simulation results show that the RIS can operate effectively for two orthogonal polarized waves and therefore an arbitrarily polarized wave.

articleTitle: Active Phased Array Radar of 475-Element Yagi Antenna for Stratosphere-Troposphere Observations at University of Calcutta
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: University of Calcutta establishing a 475 element Yagi-Uda antenna array of active phased radar system operating at a frequency of 53 MHz. The radar is capable to measure the atmospheric winds in the Troposphere and lower Stratosphere with an altitude range of 20-22 km. The 475 element Yagi antenna has been designed and simulated using MATLAB software. The atmospheric winds are measured by using the radar and initially comparisons are made with Radiosonde wind measurements.

articleTitle: Single-layer Polarizing Reflectarray Unit Cell Designs Based on a PSO-driven Optimizer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a tool for generating unit cell designs for a single-layer reflectarray (RA) that also accomplishes linear-to-circular polarization conversion. Those designs are based on an optimizer driven by the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm with a fast analysis technique using a 2D method of moments (MoM) electromagnetic (EM) solver. Four sample unit cell designs were developed in this work with an acceptably efficient and accurate optimization process, providing a 1 GHz operating band centered at 20 GHz and a 90° phase step among all the designs.

articleTitle: Single Source Volume-Surface Integral Equations for Scattering on Nonuniform Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This contribution introduces a single source formulation for the scattering of time harmonic electromagnetic waves by a nonuniform, penetrable region. The method is constructed from the combination of volume-surface integral equations with the single source method. In contrast to an additive multi-trace formulation, a multi-trace single source formulation combines the equation in a multiplicative fashion. The single source method requires fewer unknowns. Additionally, it is well-conditioned.

articleTitle: Optically Transparent Antenna on Glass Lens for AR Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present an optically transparent antenna for Augment Reality (AR) smart glasses. It operates at 5GHz Wi-Fi band to maximize data rate transfer between Personal Computer (PC) / Mobile Phones to the AR glasses. The proposed antenna is made of sub-micron silver metallic mesh (Nanoweb), fabricated on a glass substrate with an optically clear adhesive and protection layer to avoid any damages to the antenna feature. The Nanoweb antenna has a 96% optically transparency with 4.4% haze that present minimal obstruction to the user's field of view, while enabling reliable Wi-Fi or sub-6 GHz 5G communications.

articleTitle: Concurrent Dual Polarization Dielectric Waveguide Interconnect using Inverse Designed Dual-Mode Surface Antenna Launcher
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present the design of a dual-mode metallic antenna coupler that can simultaneously couple two separate signals into orthogonal polarizations of a dual-polarization metal-coated dielectric waveguide. The coupler sits on the top surface of the waveguide and features two side-by-side excitation ports, which excite the E<inf>x</inf> polarization of the waveguide when driven differentially and the E<inf>y</inf> polarization when driven in common mode. Design is done using random coordinate ascent (RCA). Simulation results show that both modes can be operated simultaneously in the 88.6 – 94 GHz range, achieving 6% fractional bandwidth and a coupler-to-coupler channel insertion loss of 3dB per channel. Due to the symmetric design of the coupler, the interconnect has theoretically zero cross-coupling between the two polarization channels. The design is also amenable to fabrication via standard microfabrication techniques due to its single-plane surface coupling nature. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first realization of a concurrent dual-mode dielectric waveguide which leverages a single surface antenna for coupling into both modes simultaneously.

articleTitle: Embedded Aperture-Based FSS Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Frequency selective surfaces (FSSs) are two-dimensional periodic arrays of electrically conductive elements or apertures that have a specific electromagnetic reflection and/or transmission response. In this work, an aperture-based sensor design was proposed that is capable of sensing strain when embedded in a layered dielectric structure (i.e., an embedded sensor). An aperture approach was selected due to the potential for operation in reflection mode without a conductive backplane. The sensor was designed to operate within the K-band to improve the potential strain measurement resolution, as the unit cell dimensions are inversely related to the operating frequency and directly related to strain sensitivity. Simulation results for the small-scale strain range of 0-0.5% are presented, with a sensitivity of 20.4 MHz/O.1 % strain.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Circularly Polarized Micro-Array Synthesis Using Spherical Wave Expansion
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a compact dual-band Right-Hand Circularly Polarized (RHCP) antenna for Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) applications. The design is based on two concentric parasitic micro <tex>$(\boldsymbol{\mu})-\mathbf{arrays}$</tex>; each formed by three Inverted F-Antennas (IFA). For each <tex>$\boldsymbol{\mu}-\mathbf{array}$</tex>, only one IFA is driven, while the other elements are loaded with optimized parasitic loads. The parasitic load values are optimized using a Spherical Wave Expansion (SWE) approach. The proposed antenna configuration covers the GPS-L2 (1215 MHz - 1237 MHz), GPS-L1 (1563 MHz - 1587 MHz), and the GALILEO-E1 (1559 MHz - 1591 MHz) bands.

articleTitle: Towards Detection of Hirschsprung's Disease using Dielectric Properties: Feasibility in thin mice colon
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Hirschsprung disease is a congenital disability due to the defect in migration of colonic ganglion. Definitive diagnosis is based on the findings of histopathological evaluation of rectal biopsies which can be highly variable. Post-op perforations and bleeding are major complications of rectal biopsy. Difficulty in establishing a definitive diagnosis leads to severe complications. Research studies on the myoelectrical activity in Hirschsprung's disease have shown disorganized electrical activities and variations in spontaneous membrane activity in the affected colon. Electrical properties can be measured as complex permittivity using dielectric spectroscopy as an attempt to diagnose Hirschsprung's disease. Dielectric spectroscopy measurements on thin biological samples offer challenges due to the requirements of sample size and probe positioning. In this work, the feasibility of dielectric property measurement of thin colon of early postnatal mice using the coaxial probe method is investigated. Complex permittivity of colon tissue was calculated from simulated return loss using a previously published mathematical model and compared with measured results. The results showed very good agreement from 500 MHz to 8 GHz range and demonstrate the potential for using dielectric properties as a biomarker for Hirschsprung disease.

articleTitle: Efficient Analytical Skeleton Approximation for Compressing Electrically Large Integral Operators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we develop an efficient method to build a Skeleton Approximation to compress electrically large integral operators. By introducing auxiliary plates and analytically selecting a reduced set of auxiliary points, an accurate low-rank approximation can be generated in a time complexity of <tex>$O(kn)$</tex>, as compared to existing <tex>$D(n^{3})$</tex> or <tex>$O(k^{2}n)$</tex> methods, where <tex>$k$</tex> is the rank and <tex>$n$</tex> is the matrix size. Numerical experiments have demonstrated its accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Wideband MIMO Antenna with Orthogonal Polarization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate small diameter and low profile wideband orthogonal polarization MIMO antennas. A combination of a wideband Halo antenna with four parasitic elements and a sleeve antenna with an upper sleeve structure is proposed, and its antenna characteristics are confirmed using simulation analysis. The antenna is loaded with short elements on the opposite side of the gap between the Halo antenna and the parasitic element to improve the directivity deviation between the both polarizations. As a result, an orthogonally polarized omnidirectional antenna with a relative bandwidth of 10 % has been obtained with <tex>$\vert \mathbf{S}_{11}\vert, \vert \mathbf{S}_{22}\vert \leq-10\mathbf{dB}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Antenna Inverse Design Using Mu-Near-Zero Isorefractive (MNZIR) Materials
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Inverse design based on topology optimization relies on continuous interpolation between two materials, with the goal of finding an optimized structure to achieve a desired performance. This has worked well for two simple dielectrics, however, much of RF engineering makes use of very good conductors such as Copper. Unfortunately, from the inverse-design perspective, very good conductors are considered “extreme” as compared to traditional dielectrics due to their very large imaginary permittivity. In contrast, mu-near-zero isorefractive (MNZIR) materials possess a large real permittivity and a small real permeability. Both MNZIR and highly conductive materials exhibit similar behavior at their interfaces, meaning that they both display a reflection coefficient with near-unity magnitude and 180° phase. In inverse design, one needs to interpolate to intermediate values of material parameters. But the intermediate values of conductivity exhibit large losses, which is neither similar to a dielectric nor a good conductor. The intermediate losses potentially impede converging to the desired optimal performance. However, intermediate values of MNZIR are both lossless and can maintain a fixed refractive index, e.g., an index of unity. We use this concept to demonstrate the power of this interpolation to design an inverse-designed patch antenna on a PCB.

articleTitle: Multi-Beam Reflectarray for Future High Throughput Satellites
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a method to generate multiple spot beam coverage based on metasurfaces where the incident wavefront from a single feeder is manipulated to reflect multiple off-centred beams. The proposed method produces four steered beams to secure continuous connection for different gateways (GWs) at an operation frequency of 35 GHz. A sub-wavelength unit cell <tex>$(\lambda/8)$</tex> is adopted to reduce the phase quantization error and to have smooth phase distribution over the aperture.

articleTitle: Isolation Between Nested OAM (Orbital Angular Momentum) Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper studies the isolation provided dy OAM orthogonality, between local antennas placed in a nested setup. A high isolation of more than <tex>$60\text{dB}$</tex> was observed. This setup is especially useful in a full duplex system.

articleTitle: Miniature Footprint of Multi-Stage Self Interference Cancellation in a STAR Radio
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Simultaneous Transmit and Receive (STAR) radio architecture provides for increased data rate without excess spectrum use. A fundamental challenge in STAR radio is the suppression of high-power self-interference from the collocated antennas. For a practical STAR operation, it is required to pursue a multi-stage self-interference cancellation (SIC) strategy in a smaller footprint. To realize such a miniature high isolation STAR front-end module (FEM) operating at the Ku band, antenna coupling reduction is critical at the first cancellation stage. But this alone is not enough for practical STAR radios. Additional cancellation should be achieved through self-interference cancellation (SIC) circuits placed after the RF front end. However, for high-frequency Ku band operation (12-18GHz), isolation from passive circuitry is very difficult. In this paper, a custom-integrated five-layer high isolation RF STAR passive FEM has been proposed. The prototype is fabricated using LTCC technology to provide 70dB of isolation across 1GHz bandwidth by combining the antenna and SIC filter stage with a reduced form factor.

articleTitle: Design of Wideband Dual–Polarized Antenna with Comb–Shaped Patches
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a simple and effective design for widening the impedance bandwidth of a dual-polarized patch antenna. Firstly, a dual-polarized patch antenna fed by L-shaped probes is designed as the basic antenna, consisting of two layers of dielectric substrate. The reflection coefficients <tex>$\left(\left\vert\mathbf{S}_{11}\right\vert\right)$</tex> of the basic antenna are less than -10 dB in the 9.4 - 10.6 GHz (12%) frequency band. And then, two comb-shaped metal patches are printed above the L-shaped probes to form the proposed antenna. Compared with the basic antenna, the impedance bandwidth of the proposed antenna is obviously widened, which covers the frequency band from 9.2 GHz to 11.9 GHz (25.6%). Meanwhile, the isolation and radiated performances of the antenna are only slightly affected. Thanks to the simple and effective method, the structural complexity of the antenna is hardly increased.

articleTitle: On the Pressure Sensing of Biological Fluids Using Microwaves
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In vivo biological fluid pressures have been linked to many diseases. Elevated blood pressure is a major risk factor for heart disease that affects millions of people across the world. Non-invasive blood pressure monitoring techniques have been limited to extremities of the body, like limbs, and are unable to measure dynamic internal pressures observed in deeper internal anatomical spaces like cardiac chambers, principal veins, cranial cavity, etc. Novel methods to investigate the internal biological pressures non-invasively can unlock new therapies to treat a wide range of diseases. Microwave-based sensing for biomedical applications is an active research area with the potential to expand in sensing vital physiological indicators like pressure. This study is an experimental investigation into the role of pressure on the dielectric properties of water to broaden the biomedical applications of microwave-based sensing. An experimental setup consisting of a pressure chamber with water and a co-axial probe was built to measure the dielectric properties at pressures ranging from 0 to 240 mm of Hg over a frequency range of 0.5-20 GHz. A comparison of the measurements shows a small and significant change in dielectric properties with varying pressures revealing the challenges and a direction for future scientific research.

articleTitle: 5G Network Planning Optimization Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present a regression-based machine learning (ML) optimization process to minimize the required number of 5G base stations for good coverage (>-80dBm received power) in a large percentage of the urban area. Area coordinates, orientations and states result in a total of 46 variables. To collect the data needed for training the ML algorithm, a Design of Experiment (DoE) algorithm Modified Extensible Lattice Sequence (MELS) is chosen. Using the data generated by MELS DoE, FAST (Fit Automatically Selected by Training) is used as ML algorithm to generate the ML model. Optimum coverage of the area is achieved with five base stations with 93.8% coverage greater than -80dBm.

articleTitle: Negative Permittivity Property of Finite Male Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The periodic metasurface cells of Split Ring Resonator (SRR) and its complementary structure CSRR comply with Babinet's principle. However, the finite CSRR cells do not correspond to the SRR cells where an infinite metal ground exists. Thus, the property of the large metal ground of finite SRR is investigated and the related negative permittivity bound is discussed.

articleTitle: Improvements in Edge of Coverage Gain for S-Band Sat-Com Applications Using Electromagnetic Band Gap Based Feeds
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper reports a design of EBG-based feed for Multi-Beam Antenna arrays to improve Edge of Coverage Gain (EoC) for satellite communication applications in the S-band. A secondary analysis has been carried out to find an appropriate phase center reference for our EBG-based feeds. Comparisons have been made with conventional horn antenna feeds in terms of peak gain, coverage gain and beam-to-beam isolation. When conventional horn feeds are substituted with the proposed EBG-based feed for our existing reflector antenna, EoC gain was improved by at least 1.72 dB and maximum by 2.24 dB for a 200MHz bandwidth from 2.5 to 2.7 GHz. Side Lobe Levels better than −27.1 dB were obtained at 2.6 GHz. The EBG-based feeds have been designed with a single-layer Partially Reflective Screen and a fully metallic construction for high-power handling.

articleTitle: Derivation of Maxwell's Equations Using Field-Impulses
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Recently, new fundamental equations for electromagnetics have been presented using field-impulses as physical field-integrators. The field-impulses are physically real, causal and gauge-independent for aptly describing electromagnetics. This paper presents the derivation of Maxwell's (Faraday and Ampere) equations using field-impulses. The derivation assumes that the equations are not available in complete explicit form beforehand, and only makes references to some earlier key findings before Maxwell. It also exploits judiciously the definition and relation of field-impulses, the physical reality of their time/spatial derivatives and their mathematical (e.g. solenoidal) properties. Being the necessary and sufficient fundamental physical quantities, the field-impulses find usefulness in field derivation as well as many aspects of classical and quantum electromagnetics.

articleTitle: Performance of Printed Antennas on Stretchable and Non-Stretchable Textiles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Durability of a printed dipole antenna was investigated as a function of tensile strain on different substrates. Two textiles were compared: a thick weave industrial fabric, and a lightweight consumer fabric with stretch in one direction. Radiation patterns and return loss measurements confirmed that performances of the printed antennas were comparable to a commercial dipole antenna. The performance of each printed antenna was measured before, during, and after undergoing mechanical strain. After maximum strain, the heavier fabric performed most similarly pre-and post-stretch, while the stretchable material showed poor recovery. This work provides a foundation for comprehensive analysis of printed antennas for wearables.

articleTitle: Performance of Cooperative SM-Aided Multiple Access Scheme with DF Relaying Protocol
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Spatial modulation (SM) is a promising approach that has been introduced as an alternative to classical multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) spatial multiplexing techniques with the hardware complexity reduction of those in mind, and is envisioned as a component in future 5G and beyond systems. Cooperative communications, on the other hand, provides additional diversity gains and high data rates while improving coverage. Combining the advantages of SM and cooperative communications would then further improve efficiency, without inducing a significant complexity. In this paper, a novel SM cooperative system with decode-and-forward (DF) protocol is proposed to ensure a viable balance between the system performance metrics: the transmission data rate and average bit error rate (BER). The system architecture and the corresponding signal processing with optimal detector (OD) for the cooperative SM system are presented in the presence of a direct communication link and multiple transmit/receive antennas at both the source (S), and the destination (D). Code division multiple access (CDMA) technique is also incorporated in the proposed solution to address multiple access contexts arising from very high data rate communications and involvement of multiple relays, respectively.

articleTitle: An Approximate Model of Near Field RCS based on Physical Optics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article deals with the study of backscattering of large target in a close environment. Due to the large size of the target, it cannot be considered as illuminated by a single wave hence the classical far-field assumptions is not verified. Based on high-frequency approximations like Physical Optics (PO) and Incremental Length of Diffraction Coefficient (ILDC), a model is established to evaluate the response of a close target in term of Radar Cross Section (RCS). The model is established with an optimized subdivision technique to manage the near-field contributions and validated trough full-wave simulation.

articleTitle: Path Loss From the Perspective of Electromagnetic Information Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Electromagnetic information theory (EMIT) receives an extensive research and attention in recent years. It provides a new perspective for the basic research of wireless communication by combining electromagnetic algorithm and information theory limit. In this paper, path loss, a key wireless communication parameter, is presented from the perspective of electromagnetic information theory by means of the mode analysis method of dyadic Green's function and capacity-based information theory. This study fills the theoretical gaps of the EMIT in the existing work.

articleTitle: A Hybrid DT-CNN Method for Buried Objects Profiling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a deep learning-based framework for solving the inverse scattering (IS) problem in half-space medium is presented. First, the qualitative method of diffraction tomography (DT) is used to generate a low-resolution reconstruction image, using the scattered field data. Then, a multilayer real-valued convolutional neural network (CNN) is designed to enhance the resolution of the DT images. Using the initializing step, alleviates the learning procedure complexity and challenges. The preliminary reported results, reveal that the proposed network could obtain high quality reconstructions and performs better than conventional nonlinear inverse scattering methods in terms of both image quality and computational time.

articleTitle: A Luneburg Lens Inspired Bessel Beam Launcher
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a Bessel beam launcher uti-lizing a Luneburg lens inspired gradient index lens. The inherent spherical symmetry of the lens lends itself well to switched beam scanning and multi-beam synthesis. A point design is implemented and shown to generate both single and multiple non-diffracting beams over a field of view with a cone angle of at least 135°.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Angle-Selective Surface Based on 3-D Frequency-Selective Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a TE-polarized reconfigurable angle-selective surface is proposed, which is realized by a bilayer structure consisting of two identical frequency-selective layers. Each layer can provide a very broad stopband with a constant <tex>$\vert \mathrm{S}_{21}\vert$</tex> less than −10 dB for all incident angles. Based on the equivalent circuits model, by tuning the distance between the two layers, the incident waves from desired directions can be selected to transmit without much attenuation, while incident waves from other directions will be reflected with a transmission coefficient less than −20 dB. The selected passband can be tuned from 0° to 55° in the frequency range of 8 GHz to 11.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Advances of Computational Efficiency and Characterizations of Metamaterials: Tribute to Brilliant Contributions in Wave Interaction with Complex Media
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Many have used equivalent representation of metamaterials with isotropic or anisotropic media. Analyses were basically based on matching measured or calculated scattering parameters of metamaterial design with those of a material slab with, in general, 18 terms permittivity and permeability tensors were developed for the equivalent material representation. The objective is to provide better understanding of the propagation and scattering characteristics of the metamaterial designs, based on fundamental wave materials interaction, and to examine avenues for achieving advanced characteristics, e.g., broader band, enhanced absorbability, improved focus efficiency, etc. With the continued advances in metamaterials designs, many unintuitively and dimensionally multiscale configurations were reported and many hours if not days of computational time were required to develop these designs. This brings additional benefits of the equivalent material representation of complex, and intuitively difficult to explain metamaterial structures, and the use of fundamentally established concepts of wave interaction with complex media, to help improve computational efficiency in optimizing the characteristics, in addition to providing critically needed fundamental understanding of the achieved results. This is where we believe Professor Ishimaru's foundational work on wave propagation in random and complex mediums will play a key role.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of a Pin-Loaded Circularly Polarized Patch Antenna using Double Negative Metamaterial Superstrates
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the gain enhancement technique of a unique high-gain, single probe-fed, metallic pin loaded, circularly polarized patch antenna using Double Negative Metamaterial (DNG) superstrates. The gain is investigated for different dimensions <tex>$(2\times 2\ \text{to}\ 6\times 6)$</tex> of DNG metamaterial superstrates. The proposed antenna structure is comprised of rectangular shaped patch with eight metallic shorting pins and DNG superstrate. Good performance of the antenna is achieved with the <tex>$5\times 5$</tex> elements of the DNG superstrate when placed 11.60 mm above the patch. The right-hand CP gain of the antenna is improved from 10.2 dBic to 12.4 dBic by employing this superstrate. This structure achieves the 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth from 27.96 to 28.26 GHz.

articleTitle: A Comparison of the Bandwidth Coverage for Different Metasurface Reflector Shapes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the comparison of metasurface reflector structure performance based on four different shape: circle, octagon, hexagon and square structures that working at X-band frequencies RIS application. The simulation process of the metasurface reflector structure are carried out using the Computer Simulation Technology (CST) Microwave Studio software. The dielectric substrate used in the simulation is FR-4 substrate with the permittivity of 4.6. The shape structure is copper metal, is design on the top surface of the FR-4 substrate while at the bottom surface is a full copper ground plane. Although the square structure is known to have the best reflection performance, however based on this study, it proven that the octagon and hexagon structures have better performance in terms of reflection percentage which is more than 90% reflection and more than 30% of bandwidth coverage.

articleTitle: Factors Affecting the RF-Induced Heating for the Electrodes Partially Inserted Inside Human Body at 1.5T MRI
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Electrodes partially inserted into the human body for epilepsy treatment have metallic wires. There is a safety concern during the MRI due to the RF-induced heating. This study evaluated RF-induced heating for different types of partially inserted electrodes at 1.5T MRI. Based on the experimental results inside the ASTM phantom and in-vivo simulations, it is found that the RF-induced heating for the partially inserted electrodes is highly related to the contact size, spacing, length of the lead, patient's body, and clinically relevant trajectories.

articleTitle: High Performance Dual-Band Antenna Using Rogers Magneto-Dielectric Material for GNSS Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)

articleTitle: Three Dimensional Printable Prototype to Realize Uniformity in Aperture Phase Distribution
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Analysi <tex>$s$</tex> in phase uniformity have been challenging aspect in design of Meta-surface. The proposed prototype shows less phase variation of about 7.96°, in 6.25 mm (<tex>$0.25\lambda$</tex>) above the top surface of it. The phase uniformity is observed in 300° case which is positioned in <tex>$12.5\ \text{mm}(0.5\lambda)$</tex> above the aperture of horn source in design frequency of 12 GHz. The proposed 3D printable prototype is of <tex>$105\ \text{mm} \times 105\ \text{mm}\times 37.5\ \text{mm}(4.2\lambda\times 4.2\lambda\times 1.5\lambda)$</tex> in dimension. The antenna exhibits wibeband in nature from 10 to 15 GHz whereas Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR) are less than 2.5 across the operating Ku-band frequency range.

articleTitle: Packaged In-Phase/Out-of-Phase Printed Multi-Layer Power Dividers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Microstrip line (MSL) multi-layer structures have been widely used to miniaturize circuits, possibly by half at the cost of narrower bandwidth and high leakage at mm Wave frequency bands. Moreover, phase matching becomes challenging, as the phase linearity differs through different layers. Here, a novel design is presented for MSL multi-layer power dividers with equal power division but different phase outputs. The power is transferred from one layer to another through an elliptic slot on a thick conducting plate. Various slot and matching transformers shapes control the phase difference between the output ports and the input matching bandwidth. To suppress radiation losses and leakage, the structure is packaged by artificial magnetic conductors from the top and bottom. The realized power dividers achieve a phase difference from 0° to <tex>$180^{\circ}\pm 6^{\circ}$</tex> with a matching input level below -15 dB within 21.8% bandwidth at center frequency 29.75 GHz.

articleTitle: VO2-Based Switchable Transmit-Reflect-Array for THz Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work presents the design of a unit cell of Transmit-Reflect-Array with two independent operations in the THz band. The size of a unit cell is 0.136 mm, which is composed of six layers in total. The mode of operation completely relies on the states of graphene and VO<inf>2</inf> materials. The performance of reflectarray is analyzed when both VO<inf>2</inf> and graphene act as metallic layers. Nearly 360° phase shift in reflectarray operation was obtained regardless of the dimensions of transmitarray and more than 400° phase shift was obtained in transmission mode with the negligible effect of reflection patch element length. The proposed method can be used for manipulating the characteristics of the reflecting or transmitting beam independently for bidirectional THz communication applications.

articleTitle: Applying a Novel Testing Scheme for the Numerical Evaluation of the Magnetic Field Integral Equation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The numerical evaluation of the double surface integrals that arise in the method of moments has captured considerable attention in recent years. Although most of the literature has focused on the evaluation of the source integral, the development of efficient and accurate procedures for the evaluation of the test integral is also needed. In this work, an integration scheme using a hybrid source singularity subtraction-cancellation scheme is proposed to improve the accuracy and efficiency of test integral evaluation arising in the magnetic field integral equation.

articleTitle: Exploring the Potential of Wireless Controlled Unit-Cells in Metamaterials: A New Concept in Multiple Degree of Freedom
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a new paradigm on the development and engineering applications of Software Defined Materials (SDMs), particularly in beam-steering and frequency agile antennas. The SDMs are characterized by a sophisticated material platform and a programmable control network, which enables multiple functionalities, such as multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO), non-line-of-sight (NLoS) communications from reflecting intelligent surfaces (LIS), and frequency agility. The design of the SDMs is presented with both numerical and experimental data, and a novel control network and associated algorithms are introduced to enable the demonstration of multiple functionalities. This work provides a comprehensive overview of the capabilities of SDMs and their potential applications in the field of antenna design.

articleTitle: Input Impedance Stabilization of Finite Arrays of HIS-Backed Antenna Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: When designing a phased array antenna, typically a unit cell is first optimized with periodic boundary conditions and then patterned into a finite array. However, there can be notable differences between the input impedances of elements designed with periodic boundary conditions and the same elements placed in a more realistic finite array. This paper presents a simple framework for explaining the cause of the finite effects, as well as a technique for suppressing them through strategic placement of conductive vias. An example wide band, low-profile antenna element composed of a dipole and high-impedance surface (HIS) is designed to demonstrate the technique, which improves input impedance consistency between the infinite periodic and finite simulation methods without requiring global optimization or individual matching of each element.

articleTitle: Broadband CP Wearable Antenna for WBAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a compact and simple broadband wide-slot circularly polarized antenna array using a 2×2 artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) is presented for wireless body area network (WBAN) applications. An inverted L-shaped parasitic strip at the open end of a microstrip line extension with a modified slot is introduced improve the wideband CP wearable antenna. The antenna system was conformed over a human body model with optimum separation distance. The simulation results indicate that the antenna has an impedance bandwidth of 60% (3.1-5.74 GHz) and an axial ratio bandwidth of 24% (4.3-5.5 GHz). Furthermore, at the distance of 3 mm away from the human body, the antenna achieved a peak gain of 10.9 dBi and total efficiency of 84.8%. The compact size and high gain of the proposed design, along with its low specific absorption rate, make it a suitable candidate for off-body wearable applications.

articleTitle: A Novel Technology for Antenna RCS Reduction with Dielectric Material
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel technology is proposed for antenna RCS reduction by adding a non-lossy dielectric material outside the microstrip antenna. The effectiveness of this technology is verified with Multi-Level Fast Multipole Algorithm (MLFMA). The simulation results show that the maximum RCS is reduced by 23.39dB from 3GHz to 20GHz using fixed-angle sweep, and the maximum average RCS is reduced by 15.34dB from 3GHz to 20GHz using fixed-frequency sweep. This technology can also be applied to other strong scattering sources for RCS reduction.

articleTitle: Dynamic Radiation Pattern of a Two-Element Antenna Array with Spatial Amplitude Modulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We characterize the dynamic complex radiation pattern of a two-element antenna array employing spatial amplitude modulation. By altering the relative amplitude ratio between the two antennas over time, the array phase pattern changes dynamically as a function of time and angle, while the amplitude pattern remains largely constant over the majority of the modulation. We analyze the complex radiation pattern of a two-element array consisting of two microstrip patch antennas designed to resonate at 2.5 GHz through simulation, characterizing the patterns from a continuously dynamic amplitude ratio and that from a discrete set of amplitude ratios. By changing only the amplitude ratio of the antenna input signals, the effective radiated power is independent of the amplitude ratio. Experiments were conducted using a 2.5 GHz two-element array with discrete amplitude ratios, demonstrating the complex dynamic radiation pattern.

articleTitle: A Heat Dissipating Dual-Pol Antenna Array with AMC Fins for Sub-6GHz Massive MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-polarized antenna array (AA) with the artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) fins implemented on the heatsink on the antenna side to increase heat dissipation and reduce the size of the fifth-generation mobile network (5G) radio unit. The AMC fins on the heatsink, which are attached to the same side of antenna, are composed of periodically arranged λ/4-height (20 mm) aluminum rectangle fins for 3.7 GHz on the aluminum base. Vivaldi antenna elements are used to cover the broadband frequency range of 3.4-4.4 GHz within sub-6 GHz. Through thermal and far-field measurements, compared to the conventional heat dissipating AA, the cooling performance improvement of more than 50% at natural convection was verified due to the additional heat dissipation from the heatsink using AMC fins without degrading of the antenna performances.

articleTitle: Miniaturized On-PCB RF Filter Design Based on Electromagnetic Bandgap Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a new Electromagnetic Band-Gap (EBG) Structure based filter design. This on-PCB filter imitates the functionality of a discrete low-pass filter without any of the associated Bill of Materials (BOM) costs. The methodology of constructing the EBG filter is explained in detail, making use of classical filter theory including tapering and multiple elements that enable tradeoffs between roll-off, rejection, and pass-band ripple. Furthermore, techniques such as multi-layer modulation and diagonal vias are utilized to reduce the physical footprint of the design. This addresses the limitation of prior designs which caused them to be inefficient due to their excessive area requirements and unmanageable pass-band ripple. Modeling and simulation was done using Computer Simulation Technology (CST), with the filter exhibiting a pass-band from 6–7 GHz and a stop-band from 8.45-22 GHz.

articleTitle: Exceptional Point Perspective of Periodic Leaky-Wave Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Over the past decade, the issue of gain degradation at broadside in periodic leaky-wave antennas (P-LWAs) has been resolved, using a circuit modeling approach, by introducing proper asymmetry in the unit cell of the antenna structure. This paper provides a more fundamental and insightful perspective of the problem by showing, using a simple coupled-mode analysis, that the optimal level of structural asymmetry corresponds to an exceptional point of the coupling parameter between the two eigenmodes of the P-LWA. This contribution represents a key step towards the development of a full electromagnetic resolution of the broadside issue; the second and final step, which will involve a mapping between the complex temporal and spatial eigenfrequencies, will be also presented at the conference.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency Full-Metal Dual-Mode Cavity-Backed Slot Antenna Array with Filtering Response
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Dual-mode cavity-backed slot antenna array using simplified feeding network with high efficiency and filtering response is proposed. Two cavity modes TE<inf>101</inf> and TE<inf>011</inf> are combined to form an enhanced operating bandwidth. The rectangular slots with 45° rotation angle can operate at both the two orthogonal modes. Besides, as both the cavity modes TE<inf>101</inf> and TE<inf>011</inf> have purely-directional electric field distribution, all the radiation slots can be directly excited by the cavity modes without using extra structures. This simplified feeding network introduce a simple antenna's structure and a high efficiency. Finally, a 4x4 slot antenna array is designed and optimized. The simulation shows that the proposed antenna can achieve 3.2% bandwidth, 14.5 dBi peak gain, and 99% total efficiency.

articleTitle: An UWB Receiver Model for AOA Estimation Accuracy Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Ultra-wideband (UWB) angle of arrival (AOA) estimation technology is currently one of the most accurate indoor positioning methods. However, there are few UWB system model that can be used to evaluate the influence of receiver defects on AOA estimation accuracy. In this paper, an UWB receiver model is built for AOA estimation error analysis. The AOA estimation errors caused by the characteristics of analog-to-digital converter and imbalance of receiver channels are investigated using the UWB receiver model, which is of great significance to the UWB positioning system.

articleTitle: Metasurface-Based Low-Dispersive Leaky-Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this communication, we present a low-dispersive leaky-wave antenna consisting of a parallel-plate-waveguide structure loaded by a modulated metasurface and a dense medium. The low-dispersive leaky-wave mode is engineered by a proper design of the metasurface and the chosen permittivity of the dense medium. The dispersion analysis is based on the transverse resonance technique and validated through full-wave simulations. A dense medium with a prism shape and a relative permittivity of 12 is used to radiate a beam pointing at 28.3° in elevation in the Ks-band (27–33 GHz) with only 0.5° variation over a 20% relative bandwidth. The leaky-wave mode supported by the structure is efficiently launched by using a compact quasi-optical system. The full antenna dimensions are 225×175×57 mm<sup>3</sup> with an expected average gain of 27.5 dBi and total efficiency greater than 55%.

articleTitle: Polarization Rotator Surfaces: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A comprehensive literature review of the transmissive and reflective polarization rotators is presented. Several wideband and multiband transmissive and reflective designs are introduced. This review aims to cover the most important design strategies for both types. In the transmission type, two techniques will be presented to achieve multiband performance. Then the dual-polarized designs will be also visited. More details on the operating principle will be presented during the presentation with a detailed literature review.

articleTitle: Direct Imaging of Layered Media with SISO Data Using Reduced Order Models
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a direct nonlinear imaging scheme for layered media with single-input single-output (SISO) data. This scheme is based on the reduced order model (ROM) approach, which transforms the measured data into its corresponding single scattering component. To construct ROMs with only SISO data, we enrich the SISO data by adding auxiliary sensors and estimating their measurements with the assumption that the measurements for different sensors only differ in arrival time and amplitude. The feasibility of this scheme is validated with a 2D numerical example.

articleTitle: Wideband Hybrid AMC Antenna Reflector
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: An Archimedean spiral antenna reflector was designed using a hybrid Artificial Magnetic Conductor (AMC) to provide uni-directional antenna radiation over a 1–5 GHz Frequency range. The hybrid AMC reflector provides at least 3 dB of additional gain compared to the same antenna without a reflector. In addition to the strong gain performance, the AMC reflector reduces the PEC reflector <tex>$\lambda/\mathbf{4}$</tex> thickness dimension from 25 mm to 14 mm, and also provides improved antenna pattern symmetry at higher frequencies. The hybrid AMC reflector is comprised of a traditional PEC reflector, used to reflect higher frequencies, and a capacitive loaded AMC reflector, used to reflect lower frequencies.

articleTitle: A Compact and Wide Band Dual-Sense Circularly Polarized Flexible Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work presents a flexible, wide-band, dual-sense, circularly polarised antenna. The Coplanar Waveguide (CPW) is the excitation feeding mechanism utilised for the 36 mm × 25 mm antenna footstep. Using Rogers Ultralam 3850 substrate material ensures flexibility. Left-Hand Circular-Polarization (LHCP) and Right-Hand Circular-Polarization (RHCP) are achieved by stimulating a triangle-shaped monopole by an asymmetric CPW ground in the general sense of dilatation the breadth and lengthening of one ground plane, with respect to the second one. The antenna has an ISM-band resonance at 5.8 GHz, a wide -10 dB bandwidth of 3.24 GHz, a realized gain equals 2.4 dBi, boresight axial ratio (AR) equals 0.88 dB, and a wide 3 dB-AR bandwidth equals 4.11 GHz. These characteristics provide for flexibility in the antenna's design for CP-related wearable applications.

articleTitle: Advances in Novel Spacecraft and Reflector Antenna Technologies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Through his 50-year career in antennas, Prof. Yahya Rahmat-Samii has had a profound impact on the development of spacecraft antennas used for planetary exploration and Earth Science. This paper highlights key advances in spacecraft antenna technology resulting from the work of Prof. Rahmat-Samii and his former students.

articleTitle: Directed High-Energy Radio Wave Exposure Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a directed high-energy radio wave exposure detection sensor using radio frequency (RF) energy harvesting techniques. The sensor comprises a small dipole antenna and a tunable rectifier circuit. Reverse biasing the diode allows high levels of RF radiation to be detected by the sensor. We also demonstrate how the frequency-dependent nature of the rectifier can be alleviated. The proposed sensor performance is experimentally evaluated in the 5–10 GHz range.

articleTitle: RF Energy Harvesting Using Complex-Conjugate Rectennas Along Single-Wire Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Goubau Single-Wire Transmission Lines (SWTL) enable low-loss long-distance links using surface waves confined to a single conductor. Here, the concept of harvesting RF energy in the near-field of a high-power SWTL is proposed, showing up to 25 mW and 30 V DC output from a wire excited with under 30 dBm of 902 MHz signals. The leakage from the SWTL is harvested using a flexible single-layer rectenna array based on six complex-conjugate electrically-small antennas with series power summation between the elements. 15 mW of DC power could be harvested at 4 m distance from the transmitter in proximity of an SWTL, compared to under <tex>$150\ \mu\mathrm{W}$</tex> in space. It is shown that SWTLs could enable long-range low-loss hybrid wireless power transmission (WPT).

articleTitle: Design of Non-Local Refractive Metasurfaces based on Cascaded Meta-Atoms
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Phase-gradient metasurfaces have proven their ability to enable an unprecedented control over the reflected and transmitted field. However, their angular behavior has been generally neglected even though its proper engineering may introduce additional degrees of freedom to be exploited in practical applications. Here, we discuss the design and the potential applications of non-local refractive metasurfaces able showing a different behavior depending on the incidence angle of the impinging wave. By considering the relevant example of lenses for extending the scan range of phased arrays, it is also shown how the performance of such spatially-dispersive metasurfaces may overcome the one of conventional designs. Full-wave simulations are provided to confirm the innovative features and improved performance of these devices.

articleTitle: Hybrid PO Method in Beam Tracing for Wireless Channel Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Beam tracing (BT) method with Geometrical Optics (GO) theory are commonly used in wireless channel simulation. However, the GO method can only calculate the scattered field in the specular direction. In this paper, we make use of the phase information of the Physical Optics (PO) method in near field. The PO method is successfully embedded into the original BT and GO framework by regarding the illuminated region as a new transmitter. Due to the new paths brought by the hybrid PO method, it achieves a good improvement in the channel characteristics in comparison with the measured data.

articleTitle: Horizontally Polarized Cylindrical Inverted-F Antenna Array Enabled by Additive Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A modified planar inverted-F antenna (PIFA) is placed in a circular array to achieve horizontal polarization with omnidirectional patterns. The coupling between elements is exploited to excite an additional resonance which is tuned to achieve a 10-dB fractional bandwidth of about 38%. This effectively increases the bandwidth by a factor of 3 compared to the single-element PIFA. Since the PIFA array with integrated feed is designed for fabrication by additive manufacturing, the inclusion of dielectric matching layers is not required.

articleTitle: Human- and Machine Design: Resonant-Size Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Random-based global optimization algorithms have been widely used for antenna shape design, primarily in situations where a human-knowledge based solution is not available. In this contribution we study the behavior of random-based global optimization in situations where the design can be addressed with a standard human-based design approach and human-driven parameter tweaking via simulations. The present case study is a resonant patch-type antenna with probe feeding.

articleTitle: A Wideband Hybrid Metal and Dielectric Reflective Lens Antenna for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel wideband reflect lens antenna based on hybrid metal and dielectric is proposed in this paper. The reflective lens antenna consists of two parts, a reflective metal lens and a dielectric lens, both of which exhibit the same curved surface and are hyperboloid, so they can be integrated together without increasing the thickness. Compared with a single metal lens or dielectric lens, the combination of the two lenses can significantly reduce the thickness of the lens within a certain aperture range. Due to the unique nature of the hyperboloid, the focal diameter ratio <tex>$(\boldsymbol{f}/\mathbf{D})$</tex> of the lens antenna can be changed arbitrarily in theory (small <tex>$\boldsymbol{f}/\mathbf{D}$</tex> can be achieved), so the height of the entire antenna system can also be reduced. In order to verify the proposed theory, a reflective lens antenna with an <tex>$\boldsymbol{f}/\mathbf{D}$</tex> of 0.5 and a diameter of 100 mm is designed and tested. Both the metal and dielectric lens antennas are processed by 3D printing technology. The simulated results show that a 3dB gain bandwidth of 26-40GHz with a peak gain of 25.4dBi is realized. The proposed antenna features low cost, high gain, and wide bandwidth, which is very suitable for mm-Wave applications.

articleTitle: Diagnosis Method for Automotive Radar Cover using Fourier Optics and Tikhonov Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The paper presents a radar cover defect identification method applicable to curved surfaces. The method localizes the defects due to fabrication errors over the radar cover surface. Fourier Optics and Tikhonov regularization are utilized for field reconstruction. Next, phase correlation matching is introduced to visualize the local phasic deviations on the surface without encountering issues owing to the periodic nature of the phase. The presented method is validated using field measurement at 76.5 GHz. The radar cover topology under test is selected as a sector of a cylindrical surface. The dielectric square patch with a length of 0.7 λ0 is detected at a maximum 6.06 λ0 away from the reconstruction region center. The method confirms the accuracy of a maximum of 9.63% deviation for sparse defect localization.

articleTitle: Design of Graphene-Based Thermal Mitigation for Phase Array Antenna Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a simulation-based investigation of a phase array structure that utilizes the combination of graphene for high terminal conductivity, Teflon for efficient heat dissipation, and honeycomb aluminum for effective heat transfer. The simulation results indicate that this design improves the overall thermal management and heat dissipation performance of the phase array. This design is a potential solution for addressing power loss and heat transfer issues in phase arrays for satellite applications

articleTitle: A Shared Ground Economical Dielectric-Free Dual Polarized Antenna System for 5G Mobile Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A probe-fed dielectric-free antenna with wide impedance bandwidth is proposed in this paper. The conventional SMA (SubMiniature version A) connector could be used to realize this antenna. Here, the top plane is the radiating element with a modified cuboid. The ground plane is Copper with dimensions of 8mm <tex>$\mathrm{x}\ 8$</tex> mm. This dielectric-free antenna offers an impedance bandwidth of 12.2%. As the form factor is minimal, the antenna could be panel mounted with modern 5G mobile devices. The same radiator is extended for dual-polarized system with shared ground.

articleTitle: All-Dielectric Artificial Magnetic Conductor at Millimeter-Wave Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: An all-dielectric Artificial Magnetic Conductor (AMC) structure operating at the centre frequency of 77 GHz is proposed as an alternative to metallic-based AMCs. The AMC structure consists of an array of interconnected cylinders. Unit cell simulation results are presented, as well as a validation of the reflection properties with a Hertzian Dipole (HD) placed on top of a 10-unit cells AMC. A comparison is made with an HD alone and with an HD on top of a Perfect Magnetic Conductor (PMC).

articleTitle: DOA Using Blind Compressive Sensing in the Presence of Mutual Coupling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Compressive sensing reconstruction techniques have been used to estimate the arrivals of correlated or uncorrelated signals impinging on a uniformly or nonuniformly space linear or circular arrays. DOA is accomplished without the need for spatial smoothing or interpolation if the array geometry is known a priori. The presence of mutual coupling renders such an approach ineffective. This paper proposes using blind compressive sensing with deterministic measuring matrix to perform DOA even with incomplete information about array geometry and with mutual coupling. The approach used here requires large number of antennas but does lead to reliable DOA estimates unlike MUSIC or other high-resolution methods.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual-Element Cross Dipole
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A dual-element cross-dipole antenna is proposed as follow up to the dual-element dipole design. The design features a -10-dB impedance bandwidth of 34.3%, and 3 distinct axial ratio bandwidths. The realized gain is stable at 2 dBi throughout the - 10dB impedance bandwidth and exhibits a maximum front-to-back ratio of 0.17 dB across the three axial ratio dips.

articleTitle: Symmetric Reflector/Absorber with Reconfigurable Low-Pass Capability
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A reflector/absorber with a reconfigurable low-pass capability is proposed utilizing a multilayered structure enabled with PIN diodes. First, an equivalent circuit model is incrementally developed to analyze performance tradeoffs and inform design choices. Then, a simulation model is created using a simple series-RC lossy patch-type geometry that is positioned between two identical reconfigurable grids that are electronically controlled through PIN diodes. The proposed reflector/absorber can be used for advanced antenna applications, such as where reconfigurable radomes with multifunctional capabilities are needed.

articleTitle: AM Interrogation of Harmonic Transponders for Measuring Channel Loss
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, we demonstrate that the loss of an unknown channel can be found through remote, wireless interrogation of an embedded harmonic transponder. The approach exploits the transponder's nonlinearity, by using a tone modulated AM interrogation signal and measuring the change in the backscattered signal's carrier to sideband ratio. Our results demonstrate that the forward channel loss can be readily determined within ±1.5 dB, regardless of the propagation characteristics of the reverse channel.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Unit Cell of EBG Structure for Printed Gap Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A dual electromagnetic gap (EBG) is realized by a unit cell of three substrates sandwiched between two metal plates. The unit cell consists of two stacked dielectric substrates topped by an aired substrate below the top metallic plate. The unit cell consists of a large mushroom patch on the bottom grounded substrate etched on its top and connected to the lower metal plane by a conducting via. The intermediate substrate has four smaller mushroom patches of total size smaller or equal to the bottom patch, and each is connected to the lower patch by conducting vias. The total size of the one-unit cell is 1.8mm. The unit cell is designed to achieve two stop band gaps; one is for the lower band for 13–24 GHz and another for the upper band 34–44 GHz. Inserting a so-called printed ridge perturbing the periodicity creates propagating modes within the EBG bands, guiding the electromagnetic waves between the upper conductor and the ridge and suppressing them elsewhere. The simulated results are presented. They could have the potential to be used for various dual-band applications.

articleTitle: High-Isolation Design of Dual-Polarized Aperture Antenna for Compact 60-GHz AiP Solution
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-polarized cavity-backed aperture antenna for a compact 60-GHz antenna-in-packaging (AiP) solution. The dual-polarization design is realized by two separate feed ports that excite the same resonant cavity with two orthogonal modes. Through the orthogonal design of antenna feed ports, the proposed antenna may achieve a very high port isolation of 40 dB over the entire band. In addition to the wide impedance bandwidth., the proposed antenna exhibits promising radiation properties., including stable radiation patterns., a very low cross-polarization level., and a high radiation efficiency. With the co-located cavity-backed design., the proposed antenna is compact and easy to integrate with ICs in a very small AiP module., making it very suitable for 60-GHz MIMO radar and communication applications.

articleTitle: Full-Wave FDTD Modeling and Simulation of Nonlinear Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a numerical scheme for simulating a ferrite loaded nonlinear transmission line (NLTL). The numerical scheme is an extension of the well known finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method. The method couples Maxwell's equations with the nonlinear Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (LLG) equation for modeling the dynamics of ferrite material. Furthermore, the method discretizes the domain using the staggered Veegrid with the magnetization vectors (M-fields) located at cell centers; the usual FDTD electric field and magnetic field updates are unchanged. We then validate the method and model by comparing simulation results with an Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) high-power NLTL experiment.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporally Modulated Metasurface Antennas for Direct Signal Modulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel simplified transmitter based on the space-time-coding (STC) metasurface antenna. The STC metasurface antenna can periodically ON-OFF switch its unit cell to form an equivalent sinusoidal amplitude distribution along the length of the wave-guiding structure to realize high-gain leaky radiation. Moreover, the phase of the radiated wave in the main-beam direction can be changed by shifting the equivalent sinusoidal amplitude distribution formed by the spatiotemporal modulation.
