The digital information can be encoded into the phase property of the radiated electromagnetic waves. Therefore, the STC metasurface antenna can realize direct signal modulation without requiring digital-to-analog converters, mixers, and filters. Experiment results demonstrate that the STC metasurface antenna can directly generate the modulated waveforms with the Quadrature Phase Shift Keying (QPSK) modulation scheme.

articleTitle: A Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons-Based Dual Band Shared Aperture Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons (SSPP) based dual-band shared aperture antenna is proposed. A Ku-band SSPP antenna is designed on the top side of the metal plate while an N77-band antenna is mounted on the backside. The <tex>$\mathbf{4}\times \mathbf{1}$</tex> SSPP dielectric tapered rod antenna array is fed by a compact SSPP power distribution network. A low-loss waveguide-to-SSPP adapter is also implemented for testing. The N77-band slotted antenna is printed on a PCB and shares the radiation aperture with the SSPP antenna. The antenna is fabricated and measured. The measurement results agree well with the simulation.

articleTitle: Experimental Characterization of a Low-Profile 37-dBi Gain Transmitarray for Backhauling at E-Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A low-profile transmitarray operating at E-band (72–86 GHz) is discussed. The antenna thickness including the power divider and the radome is 58 mm. Furthermore, the flat-lens aperture is equal to 133.7 mm × 133.7 mm and the focal-to-aperture size ratio F/D is less than 0.3. The low profile has been obtained by using a specific quad-feed source. The antenna has been fabricated and characterized. In good agreement with the numerical simulations, a peak gain of 37.0 dBi and a 3-dB gain relative bandwidth larger than 17.7% have been achieved, respectively. The aperture efficiency is larger than 33%.

articleTitle: Multiple Scattering of Waves in Numerical Simulations with Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present this paper to pay tribute to Professor Akira Ishimaru for his contributions to Electromagnetic waves in Random Media for close to seven decades. Professor Ishimaru made seminal fundamental contributions to the inclusion of multiple scattering of waves. Among his famous works are three papers [1]–[3]. Paper 1 in 1982 in which the measurements show that the attenuation rate in dense media is significantly different from that of independent scattering, which is a result of dense media packing effects that the positions of the particles are not uniformly random but governed by pair distribution functions. Paper 2 in 1984 in which backscattering enhancement of random discrete scatterers is shown due to constructive interference of higher order multiple scattering effects. The experimental measurements show a very narrow angular width of the backscattering peak. The phenomenon is not explained by radiative transfer theory nor the ladder approximation in Bethe-Salpeter equation. Paper 3 in 1994 shows backscattering enhancement of rough surfaces in experiments for co-polarization and cross-polarization.

articleTitle: A Kirigami-Inspired Foldable Spherical Fully Dielectric Luneburg Lens Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A kirigami-inspired foldable spherical fully dielectric Luneburg lens antenna using additive manufacturing technology is presented for the first time. The proposed lens is discretized into multilayer spherical shells which are subdivided by several interlaced annular dielectric sheets with different notch densities. The existence of the flexible notches and the different notch densities in different layers realize the structural foldability and the gradient distribution of the Luneburg lens, respectively. The foldable Luneburg lens in the unfolded state is fed by a horn antenna and the measured results reveal that the proposed antenna with different feed incidence angles has the reflection coefficients better than -10 dB in the entire Ku band, gains varying between 15.2 and 18.7 dBi, and symmetric radiation patterns with narrow beamwidths.

articleTitle: A Wideband Low-Profile Reflectarray with Decoupled LHCP/RHCP Beams
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband low-profile dual-circularly-polarized (DCP) reflectarray (RA) with decoupled left/right-handed circularly-polarized (LHCP/RHCP) beams. The RA unit is of two degrees of design freedom, offering decoupled LHCP/RHCP phase compensation for independent modulation of the DCP reflection phases. A low-profile RA is designed and simulated, with asymmetrical DCP beams of <tex>$(\varphi=120^{\circ},\theta=10^{\circ})$</tex> and <tex>$(\varphi=135^{\circ}, \theta=-30^{\circ})$</tex> for LHCP and RHCP excitations, respectively. The designed RA exhibits a wide axial ratio (AR) bandwidth (BW) of over 40% (AR < 2 dB), with sidelobe levels and cross-polarizations both under -15 dB. The overlapped 1-dB gain and AR < 2 dB BW is 17.1 % and 13% under LHCP and RHCP input, respectively, with maximum aperture efficiency of 36.8% and 31.2%. The proposed DCP RA is of wideband, high gain, low profile, pure chirality, with decoupled LHCP/RHCP beams.

articleTitle: Stability and Tolerance Analysis of Non-Foster Matched Electrically-Small Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The tolerances inherent in commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) components can affect system stability and performance, and the consequences are especially severe in an active non-Foster antenna system. This work presents a Monte-Carlo-based analysis framework that can provide information on the effects of tolerances on case-specific designs, which is essential information needed for building stable and robust non-Foster systems. Two examples are presented in this paper to demonstrate the concepts.

articleTitle: A Surface Integral Equation Based T-Matrix Formulation for Penetrable Obstacles and Scatterers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, a novel T-matrix formulation to estimate electromagnetic scattering from penetrable dielectric objects and scatterers is proposed. The method is based on the well-known PMCHWT formulation used for modeling dielectric objects. Numerical results demonstrate good agreement of the proposed technique as compared against commercial solvers.

articleTitle: Bi-Directional Stretchable Capacitors for Self-Tuning MRI Receive Coils
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Over the past several years, stretchable electronics have received significant research attention due to their wide range of applications in wearable sensors for electrophysiological monitoring. Among the various sensor types, capacitive devices are most widely used due to their high durability, reusability, and low hysteresis. This work introduces a new capacitive sensor design from annular interdigital geometry with a bi-directional stretch anisotropy that depends on the opening angle of its annular rings. Numerical analysis, electrostatic, and non-linear material stretching simulations are presented. It is demonstrated that the capacitance of the sensor remains stable at an annular ring angle of 180° with stretching in any direction. This type of design can be useful in applications where capacitance and/or resonance frequency stability is of importance. To this goal, we demonstrate a stretchable radio-frequency coil for magnetic resonance imaging using the proposed capacitor to maintain a stable resonance frequency with stretching.

articleTitle: Gap Waveguide Cruciform Couplers Nolen Matrix for Multi-Beam Antenna at 38 GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The design of a Nolen Matrix using cruciform directional couplers on Gap Waveguide (GW) technology at 38 GHz is presented. The matrix is utilized to feed a ridge GW slot array antenna. The simulation results shows that GW technology is suitable for this application at high frequency bands in a multilayer design.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Design Approach of 3D Printed Pixelated Lens MIMO Antenna for CubeSat
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A Machine Learning (ML) synthesis approach is proposed and presented to design a high gain 3D printed pixel lens MIMO antenna for CubeSat at V-band. A realized gain of 12 dBi and an fractional bandwidth of 11.59% (59.3-66.6 GHz) with S11<-20 dB are obtained. Simulated and ML performance results indicate that the ML-based synthesis approach required only a few seconds to predict results with a low error rate, whereas the classic optimization approach, such as GA in HFSS, required 48 hours of continuous iteration to solve the optimization problem.

articleTitle: Characterization of Space-Time Coding Metasurface Enabled Communication Systems from An Electromagnetic Information Perspective
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel metasurface-enabled communication system utilizing the far scattering pattern directly as the information modulation has attracted great attention recently. In such a system, the coding metasurface is directly controlled by the source digits, and the far-field is directly measured by the receiver to decode and realize information transmission. Furthermore, the metasurface can be controlled periodically in the time domain to achieve a scattering pattern distribution in both frequency and spacial domain, thus increasing the flexibility and capacity of the communication system. In this paper, the communication mechanisms and capacity of such space-time coding metasurface (STCM) enabled communication system is analyzed. The scattering far field of STCM is evaluated with a physical optics approximation. And based on the statistics of the scattering far-field, the capacity of the system is obtained from Shannon information theory. Various communication mechanisms considering both the observation frequency and direction are analyzed. And the mechanism of joint observation and frequency division observation are also discussed. The conclusion shows that in four lobes, the communication capability is larger, and the joint-frequency observation capacity is higher than single-frequency observation. Also, the frequency division observation mechanism can be well implemented in the STCM based communication system.

articleTitle: DOA Estimation for Curved Antenna Arrays Using CRLB Analysis and SDR
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) analysis for estimation of the direction of arrival (DOA) for curved receiving antenna arrays is presented. Software defined radio (SDR) measurements are used to validate the results. First the CRLB for curved arrays is derived. Then the method is applied to case studies using three different arrays for DOA estimation. The arrays with four antennas with different curvatures are fabricated and SDR is used to validate the results. It is found that the performance depends on the DOA, with the curved array providing benefits for certain directions of arrival. The proposed method can help designers of arrays for DOA estimation to improve the performance.

articleTitle: Phased-Array Antennas for K/Ka-Band Satellite Communication - Prototyping Scalable Apertures Composed of 8x8 Modules
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A receive phased-array antenna with 256 dual-polarized active antenna elements is realized and demonstrated. The antenna is composed of four sub-arrays with 8x8 antenna elements referred to as antenna modules. A module of size 8x8 is typically quite common for such approaches and various types have been reported in the literature. Yet, the combination of such modules to realize scalable apertures is not so frequently addressed. This paper presents a full-sized phased array for satellite reception in the K-band along with gain pattern and G/T measurements. It demonstrates the scalability by combining four modules so to form a phased-array antenna with 256 dual-polarized active antenna elements.

articleTitle: Design Guidelines for Fishnet Frequency Selective Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, practical guidelines for the design of connected, fishnet-like, frequency selective surfaces are proposed. An equivalent circuit analysis and accurate full-wave numerical simulations are simultaneously exploited to comprehensively evaluate an exemplificative radar absorbing structure based on a resistive frequency selective surface. The FSS unit-cell shape, consisting of a resistive patch connected to the adjacent cells in a fishnet-like structure, is carefully evaluated. In particular, the FSS impedance parameters are monitored as the patch connections are geometrically varied. Indeed, an optimized FSS behavior can be achieved by acting on this parameter, developing practical guidelines for the realization of this type of fishnet configurations. As a result, the structure can achieve significant broadband performance within the 7–12 GHz band with absorption values better than -10 dB. This study may be helpful to address some practical problems from the FSS optimized design perspective.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Scheme for Solving Volume-Surface Integral Equations with Generalized Media
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a broadband foldable reflectarray (FRA) antenna mounted onto a 3U CubeSat frame is presented. The Ku-band reflectarray is linearly polarized and is fed with a pair of wideband Vivaldi antennas that produce a symmetric illuminating radiation pattern. This high-gain antenna incorporates a stowage and deployment mechanism for both the reflectarray and the Vivaldi feed antenna elements. The bandwidth of the reflectarray is maximized through optimized reference phase mapping with multi-resonant elements. The measured gain for the two-element Vivaldi array feed is 10.3 dBi at 15.2 GHz, and measured results for the fabricated reflectarray mounted on a CubeSat frame show a maximum gain of 24.7 dBi at 15.2 GHz with a 4°3-dB beamwidth. The reflectarray achieves a measured realized gain of greater than 20 dBi from 11.7 GHz to 16.2 GHz.

articleTitle: Modeling and Optimization of the Steering Range of a Phased Array Antenna for Neuromodulation Applications in the Near-Field Region
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents modeling and optimization of the steering range of a microstrip planar phased array antenna to steer the unidirectional near-field focused beam towards a certain direction. This antenna can be implemented in headstage-based neural stimulation system and wireless recording system for optogenetic neuromodulation applications. The proposed phased-array antenna consists of sixteen elements that are designed to provide a uniform power transmission over the <tex>$\mathbf{27}\ \mathbf{cm} \times \mathbf{23}\ \mathbf{cm} \times \mathbf{16}\ \mathbf{cm}$</tex> rat behavioral cage area. The proposed transmitter (TX) antenna implements a near-field-based wireless power transmission system operating at 2.4 GHz frequency. The phased array antenna steers the beam from -30° to 60° in the elevation plane by feeding the individual elements with different phases using four 4-bit phase shifters. A design analysis of the beam-steering approach of the phased array antenna is presented and the corresponding simulation and measurement results are included in this paper.

articleTitle: Impulse Radiating Antennas with Four and Six Arms Excited with Differentiated Gaussian Pulses
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present results of numerical analysis of impulse radiating antennas with four and six feeding arms, with and without resistive matching networks. The antennas are excited using differentiated Gaussian pulses of different durations. The analysis of radiated pulses show that for certain short-pulse excitations, resistive matching networks can be omitted, and that using six arms instead of four can be advantageous.

articleTitle: 3-D Scattering Center Determination Algorithm for Detecting Primary Radar Cross-Section Contributing Regions on a Radar Target
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel algorithm for determining the 3-D scattering centers of a target that cause an increase in radar observability or radar cross-section (RCS) of the platform. The scattering centers on a given platform are calculated using the current density induced on the surface for the given direction of illumination and frequency of operation. The current density may be computed using a full-wave or an approximate electromagnetic solver. For a given point on the surface of the scatterer, the relative RCS contribution is computed by evaluating the radiation integral within a specific neighborhood. This RCS contribution value is then assigned to the corresponding point on the surface of the target, forming a color map of RCS contributions on the 3-D model of the scatterer. This approach can be further used as feedback mechanism to reduce the RCS in an iterative manner.

articleTitle: Maximizing the Radiated Power of Patch Antenna using Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A characteristic mode analysis (CMA) based optimization method is presented to maximize a rectangular patch's radiated power. The conventional narrowband microstrip antenna was designed on an FR-4 substrate resonating at 2.86 GHz, but its radiated power was maximum at 2.96 GHz. The single characteristic mode participated in antenna's characterization, which showed resonance at 2.96 GHz. Characteristic modes were controlled to shift the frequency of the radiated power where matching occurs or return loss is minimal. It is demonstrated that reactive loading influences the modal resonance of the antenna. Reactive loading using slits tends to optimize the antenna's modal significance and modal weighting coefficient (MWC). The optimization of MWC acted as an indicator to maximize the radiated power of the antenna.

articleTitle: Efficient Numerical Analysis for Few-Atom Cavity Quantum Electrodynamics Using the Coupling Matrix Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Numerical analysis of few-atom cavity quantum electrodynamics (QED) is challenging due to the exponentially scaling size of the Hilbert space when multiple quantized electromagnetic modes are considered. To overcome this, we propose an approach based on coupling matrix transformations that allows adjustment of the coupling structures of QED Hamiltonians so that they are more compatible with tensor network algorithms such as matrix product states. We present the relevant Hamiltonians along with the coupling matrix transformation scheme and present few-atom cavity QED simulations in the time domain that is able to characterize the interactions between atoms efficiently.

articleTitle: A Novel Optimization Technique for Designing Frequency Reconfigurable Pixelated Planar Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel method incorporating joint perturbation sensitivity analysis is proposed in this paper to design frequency reconfigurable planar antennas with a pixelated surface. Using our method, an antenna design having two switched working frequency bands and omnidirectional radiation patterns, is optimized. The simulation results verify its efficacy and potential computation efficiency.

articleTitle: Patch-Based Perfectly Matched Layer Scheme in Three-Dimensional Unstructured Meshes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The realization of a perfectly matched layer (PML) has been a numerical challenge in 3-D unstructured meshes in time domain. In this paper, we develop an efficient patch-based PML scheme to truncate 3-D unstructured meshes with the same ease as that in a rectangular grid. No projections and transformations between irregular meshes and Cartesian coordinates are needed. As a result, the PML can be placed conformal to the object under study and be shaped in an arbitrary way. Numerical experiments have demonstrated the validity and accuracy of the proposed new method.

articleTitle: Directional Metasurface Using Transistor-Loaded Circularly Polarized Antenna Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper discusses the RF design of a compact metasurface that enables directional propagation characteristics. It allows for circularly-polarized waves to penetrate through its volume in one direction of propagation whereas it absorbs them in the reverse one. Directionality is achieved by combining two transistors with two circularly-polarized patch antennas in each unit cell of the metasurface. A compact multi-layer integration scheme is proposed and is demonstrated through electromagnetic (EM) simulations at S-band. The proposed metasurface configuration exhibits directional characteristics with the following performance metrics. BW in the forward direction: 3.4-3.7 GHz, maximum Gain in the forward direction: 29 dB, isolation in the reversed direction> 50 dB.

articleTitle: HF Direction-of-Arrival Estimation Using Helicopter-Integrated Single-Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A helicopter-mounted antenna is designed for high frequency (HF) direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimations using the rotating main rotor-blade. Different from traditional direction finding (DF) arrays, a single helicopter-based antenna is developed. Different from conventional single DF antennas requiring directional radiation patterns, the proposed antenna uses blade modulation with phase diversity of nondirectional radiation patterns. Stable reflection coefficients and radiation patterns are obtained based on the characteristic mode (CM) analysis when the main rotor-blade rotates from 0° to 75°. The metallic helicopter structure is used as a main radiator, where a combination of pure CMs is excited by feeding one of the front landing gears based on CM surface current distributions without adding additional metallic structures. Radiation pattern diversity is demonstrated by calculating correlation coefficients of amplitude and phase of complex radiation patterns. The HF DF performance of the helicopter-based single antenna is validated by Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) values and multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Linarly-Polarized UnitCell at Ka-band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a linearly-polarized reconfigurable Huygens' metasurface unit-cell for flat lens antennas design in Ka-band (27.28-29.145 GHz). This structure consists of a symmetric copper double layer unit including two I-shape patches etched on the one substrate. To control the transmission phase, two varactor diodes are integrated on the two radiating elements printed on the top and bottom layers. The size of the proposed unit cell is 3×7×1.5 mm<sup>3</sup> (0.28λ0×0.65λ0×0.14λ0 at 28GHz, where λ<inf>0</inf> is the wavelength in free space). The simulated results show a wideband transmission phase shift tunability up to 300° by integrating varactors is achieved within a fractional bandwidth varies between 9.6% and 18.18%.

articleTitle: On the Sensitivity of RCS to Manufacturing Defects in as-built Camera Boxes with Voids
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A recently introduced benchmark structure is used to investigate the sensitivity of electromagnetic scattering to manufacturing imperfections in metallic structures with voids. Three versions of the cobra-in-a-camera-box benchmark are modeled: one exactly according to the benchmark specification and others with minor/major geometric perturbations in the vicinity of the aperture. Simulation results show that even minor perturbations can impact the scattered far fields significantly, the effect varies with frequency and look angle, and the largest effects are at higher frequencies and at void-aware look angles.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Microstructure Designs for Future Software Defined Materials
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Tunable microstructures are fundamental for the development of Software Defined Materials (SDMs). The concept to obtain reconfigurability within a SDM is demonstrated. Additionally, several concepts to perform reconfigurability with microstructures are reviewed and a novel tunable omega <tex>$(\Omega)$</tex> structured metamaterial design is validated numerically and experimentally. It can achieve tunable absorption or transmittance. The omega structured element has improved characteris-tics compared to the more conventional microstructure designs. Tunability is accomplished through varactor diodes which allow reconfiguration from an absorption rate of 0.75 to a transmission rate of 0.65.

articleTitle: Solving the Inverse Scattering Obstacle Problem via NIE Model and Contrast Source Inversion Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The new integral equation model has been recently introduced in literature to alleviate the non-linearity and complexity of the inverse scattering problem. It consists of a smart rewriting of the scattering equations and is usually used for quantitative inversion of unknown targets. On the other hand, in this contribution, the idea underlying a new method for inverse obstacle problem, which aims to retrieve just the shape and size of the unknown targets, is presented. The method takes advantages from the new integral equation model and from some interesting properties of the auxiliary function which is involved in this model and encodes the investigated target properties.

articleTitle: Low Complexity Direction Finding with an 8:1 Bandwidth Amplitude-Only Spiral Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A four-arm, cavity-backed spiral antenna is designed for operation without a mode forming or beamforming network, to facilitate low-cost, low-complexity direction finding. An application of the multiple signal classification (MUSIC) is demonstrated in the amplitude-only regime for the spiral. Good direction finding performance is obtained for 8:1 bandwidth (1–8 GHz). This multi-octave DF capability is demonstrated in a monopulse like manner, without any knowledge of the incident signal's frequency of operation, achieving less than one degree of error in a very low noise scenario. Additional studies show up to 87% improvement in performance by transitioning to a configuration where the frequency of operation is known.

articleTitle: A Wideband Reflectarray Antenna Unit with Double-Loop Phase Delay Lines for Satellite Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In order to enhance the bandwidth of reflectarray antennas, this paper proposes a wideband double-loop phase delay line which can be used as the antenna unit. The linear phase change of the double-loop phase delay line unit can be achieved over 360°, and a smoother linear phase response can be obtained at the center frequency of 8.5 GHz. Also, the amplitude of reflection coefficient in the 7–10 GHz band is within 2.0 dB. The simulation results verify the good performance of the phase delay line unit and it could be very useful in satellite communication systems.

articleTitle: Towards Real-Time Monitoring of Thermal Ablation Lesions in Liver Using Microwave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Minimally invasive ablative therapies have been used extensively to treat hepatic tumors in patients where surgical resections are not needed. Besides electroporation, ablation therapies induce extreme temperatures, i.e., hypothermia or hyperthermia, to cause irreversible damage to the tissue cells. The lesion volume created as a result depends on the temperature gradient in the tissue. Accurate and sensitive temperature monitoring is critical to optimize the treatment and reduce the risk of complications and extrahepatic injury. This study presents an approach to assess the tissue temperatures non-invasively using microwave imaging (MWI). A cross-section of a liver phantom is used for microwave imaging electromagnetic simulation at 915 MHz. Dielectric properties of porcine liver tissue at 915 MHz and varying temperatures are gathered from the literature. Point sources placed around the phantom model act as transmitters and receivers. Distorted Born Iterative Method (DBIM) was used to reconstruct the relative permittivity that is mapped to the temperature field and compared. The mapped temperature field from the reconstructed dielectric parameters resembles the temperature field used to create the phantom model demonstrating the feasibility of using MWI for the non-invasive assessment of liver tissue temperatures for ablative therapies

articleTitle: Characterization of Dielectric Materials Using Transmission Losses at W- and D-Bands for 6G
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Dielectric constant and tangent loss of several dielectric materials are characterized at 75~170 GHz from non-destructively measured transmission losses with different incident angles (0°~60° with a step of 5°), polarizations (TE and TM) and thicknesses. The transmission losses are calculated from randomly selected dielectric properties using the transmission line model (TLM) and are then compared with the measured transmission loss. The best fitted dielectric properties are obtained using the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm. Multiple transmission loss data at a single frequency allows the dielectric parameters to be extracted in spite of a measurement tolerance. Dielectric materials of plastic, fused silica, glass ceramic, glass, and alumina are successfully characterized.

articleTitle: Wideband All-Dielectric Reflector at 100 GHz for 6G Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Power-efficient systems are required for 6G communications. Part of a window real-state can be used as placement of a reflecting metasurface, which can provide coverage to users in scenarios, where there are no line-of-sight links. In this contribution, we propose a wideband all-dielectric metasurface at 100 GHz that consists of alumina posts on plastic and does not depend on the angle of incidence. The design has been manufactured and measured, with good agreement between measurements and simulations.

articleTitle: Dynamic Controlling of Transmission Characteristics of Spoof Plasmonic Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) supported by periodic unit cells formed by metallic stubs loaded with PIN diodes are proposed. Dispersion properties of SSPP with a diode in both on and off states are analyzed. A SSPP waveguide constructed by the proposed unit cells is designed and simulated. As a result, dynamic control of two different transmission characteristics, such as band-pass and band-stop features, can be realized by using the two different states of the PIN diodes. The simulated passband with a return loss higher than 10 <tex>$\text{dB}$</tex> ranges from 3.01 to 10.16 GHz, while the stopband with a rejection level better than -20 <tex>$\text{dB}$</tex> is from 3.94 to 5.88 GHz. The simulation results verify the feasibility of the proposed strategy based on PIN diodes and pave the way for the development of reconfigurable spoof plasmonic metamaterials.

articleTitle: Multi-Resolution Multi-Physics Imaging of Free-Space Targets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The joint inversion of electromagnetic (EM) and acoustic (AC) scattered data is addressed for the multi-physics (MP) imaging of unknown targets in free-space. The regularization properties yielded by a data-fusion approach are enhanced by integrating it with a multi-resolution (MR) strategy aimed at adaptively increasing the pixel density and exploiting progressively-acquired information on the imaged domain. An illustrative example is shown to preliminarily verify the effectiveness of the proposed MR-MP method.

articleTitle: Connected FORA Array Antenna Grouping for Cost Efficiency: Study on Microwave Breast Hyperthermia
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In microwave hyperthermia (MH) cancer treatment application, antenna arrays selectively heat cancerous cells to a temperature higher than the body's normal temperature. The administered heating relies on the optimal antenna feeds that maximize the specific absorption rate (SAR) inside the tumor. This paper investigates the heat-focusing performance of grouping the phase and/or amplitude of vertically aligned antenna elements, using 2D PSO optimization. The numerical MH system includes a three-dimensional MRI breast model and a connected array as the MH applicator. The array's structure is curved and it consists of 3 layers and 39 elements (<tex>$3\times 13$</tex>), which are capacitively coupled fractal octagonal rings (FORA). The results show that the phase parameters need to be individually optimized for superior focusing. Grouped antennas' amplitude optimization provides comparable performance to the individual antenna amplitude optimization. To conclude, using the sub-arrays approach in relation to the amplitude of the antenna array can significantly decrease the number of freedom in the system and the RF background cost, without compromising on performance.

articleTitle: An understanding of terms in Diversity Equity and Inclusion (DE&I) initiatives: Perspectives from the IEEE AP-S DE&I Committee
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We describe here below the Diversity Equity and Inclusion (DE&I) Committee as well as the initiatives and their significance. We also introduce the different papers of the special session.

articleTitle: Antenna Array Analysis on Real Quantum Computing Processors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work the effect of noise on the computation of the array factor of phased arrays through realistic quantum computers is addressed. Furthermore, numerical results are presented in relation to physical parameters of superconducting qubits, to analyze the impact of noise when the quantum Fourier transform is applied within the quantum computing framework.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Enhancement of a Luneburg Lens Amplitude-Only Direction-Finding Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A 5-element cylindrical Luneburg lens antenna, operating at 27.5 GHz, is proposed for a receive-only application. The array is poised to be integrated with amplitude-only receivers, for the purpose of determining the angle-of-arrival of a single signal received by the array. A conventional methodology for performing this task is shown as a baseline with machine-learning solution introduced for comparison. The peak improvement of the machine-learning technique shows an accuracy increase of up to 41%. In situations with reduced signal-to-noise ratio, the performance of the neural network solution outperforms the conventional method, demonstrating an improvement of 30%.

articleTitle: The Advanced Short Backfire Antenna as an Element for Space-Based Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Metasurfaces have been used to greatly enhance the performance capabilities of well-known antennas. One example of this improvement in performance is the Advanced Short Backfire Antenna (A-SBFA), in which the metallic inner rim-wall of a short-backfire antenna is lined with an anisotropic impedance metasurface. A hexagonal A-SBFA has been shown to produce greater than 90% aperture efficiency at both the GPS L1 (1.575 GHz) and L2 (1.227 GHz) bands [1], while circular A-SBFAs are capable of greater than 100% dual-band aperture efficiency at a range of aperture sizes [2]. The A-SBFA technology is therefore an excellent candidate for service as an array element on next-generation Medium Earth Orbit (MEO) GPS satellite buses. In this report, we outline the development path that led to the current A-SBFA technology. We further describe studies which should be conducted to bring the A-SBFA to a higher level of technology readiness as a phased array element.

articleTitle: Decoupling of Wideband Closely-Spaced Patch Antennas for MIMO Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A simple decoupling technique based on a single-layer substrate is proposed for wideband closely-spaced patch antennas. By combining the coplanar decoupling structure (CDS) and defected ground structure (DGS), the strong coupling between wideband closely-spaced patch antennas can be significantly suppressed across the operating band without an additional substrate layer. To validate the feasibility of the proposed decoupling schemes, two decoupled wideband antenna prototypes with microstrip and probe gap-coupled feeding are designed, simulated, and measured at ISM and X band, respectively. Experimental results show that the H-plane decoupled prototype achieves over 15 dB isolation across a wide matched bandwidth of 18.4% with an edge-to-edge separation of 0.038 <tex>$\lambda_{0}$</tex> and the E-plane decoupled prototype achieves beyond 20 dB isolation across a wide matched bandwidth of 22.2% with an edge-to-edge separation of 0.033 <tex>$\lambda_{0}$</tex>. Featuring a compact appearance, wideband operation, and strong-coupling suppression, the proposed decoupling technique is promising in wideband multiple-input and multiple-out (MIMO) applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of Offset, Shaped Reflectors Exactly Implementing the Abbe Sine Condition
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Dual shaped reflectors have often been designed to produce maximum gain with minimum spillover and this has led to a reputation that maximum gain is the only application of shaping. However, the basic theory of how to shape reflectors can be used to implement many other aperture illuminations. The design presented and analyzed here implements the Abbe sine condition which eliminates coma aberration, producing reflectors with a very wide field of view. This contrasts with the maximum gain case which has a very small field of view, demonstrating the wide applicability of shaping theory.

articleTitle: Comparison of Intermodulation Distortion Performance in Linear and Circular Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work analyzes how the intermodulation distortion (intermods) across array elements combines in the beam-former for uniform linear and circular arrays. It is shown that while intermods in a linear array manifest as an equivalent incident planewave signal at an apparent angle, this equivalence does not occur for circular arrays. Monte Carlo simulations indicate that on average the gain of intermods is higher for uniform circular arrays than linear array, but linear arrays are more likely to be exposed to stressing cases where the intermod gain is close to that of the main beam.

articleTitle: Design of A Reconfigurable-Polarization Slot-Ring Phased Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a reconfigurable-polarization slotring phased array antenna with narrow strip ground plane has been proposed for C-band applications. This antenna operates from 5.42 to 7.87 GHz, achieving 37% fractional bandwidth, and 7.6 dBi gain. The microstrip line is placed diagonally and is within the perimeter of a single antenna element which makes the antenna scalable. A <tex>$2\times 2$</tex> array has been constructed with <tex>$0.5\lambda_{0}$</tex> element spacing. The array is fed from the center of each element through a coaxial line. This array is capable of vertical, horizontal or circular polarization by properly feeding each port of the antenna element. In addition, this array is shown to be able to scan to ±30 degrees.

articleTitle: Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Perspective via the Women in Engineering Column of the IEEE Antennas and Propagation Magazine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The Women in Engineering column of the IEEE Antennas and Propagation Magazine started in 2019 and collected, over the years, several different opinions anxsd experiences of researchers and scientists within the antennas and propagation community. In this paper, a review of all these contributions is reported, analyzing how opportunities for progress in diversity, equity and inclusion can be pursued and applied.

articleTitle: Full Minimum Feature Size Enforcement Toward Freeform Optical Metasurfaces at Wafer-Scale
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Optical metasurfaces are an exciting area of research and development because they have demonstrated massive size and weight reduction when compared with conventional optical systems. At the same time, high-volume lithographic processes, which are necessary for bringing such systems out of the research lab and into general use, constrain the feature sizes which can be produced. This reality is especially important for the design of devices operating in the optical regime. In this paper, we share our recent work which provides a concrete set of criteria for checking the satisfaction of a minimum feature size (MFS) rule, and from this derive a method for MFS enforcement on lithographic masks for both filled and void regions. Using this method we are able to demonstrate a performance horizon associated with the MFS relative to the operating wavelength, bounding the performance achievable through device optimization.

articleTitle: Single Layer Reflectarray Independently Controlling at 15GHz / 30GHz for Dual Polarization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: For obtaining a multi band reflectarray with multi-beams, a reflectarray realizing multiple dual-polarization beams at a lower band (15GHz), in addition to ordinary dual-polarization beams at a higher band (30GHz). In this report, we have designed reflectarray elements considering we propose now-element that can control independently in dual band by the domain classification in the unit cell. Usefulness of the elements is verified by the reduction partion from the design reflectarray.

articleTitle: Multiband Bow-tie Dipole Absorber for RF Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel Four-band electromagnetic energy harvesting absorber, specifically designed to absorb energy at the GSM-1800, Wi-Fi (5.2 GHZ and 5.8 GHz), and Wimax (3.5 GHz) frequency bands, respectively. The unit cell of the absorber is made up of a novel three-arms bow-tie dipole with channeling traces and a resistive load. The simulation results demonstrate good absorption capabilities.

articleTitle: Multicommodity Network Flow for Indoor Progation Loss Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Channel models are an essential tool for some communication systems. Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer, SWIPT is a widely studied topic in areas like wireless sensor networks and internet of things applications, the utilization of a prediction model in this situation can bring many benefits. Therefore, this paper proposes a propagation loss model based on Multicommodity Network Flow (MCNF) for industrial indoor environments, focused on Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer Applications. We analyze the frequencies of 2.4GHz. The proposed model showed higher adherence to the measured values than the other indoor propagation models, mainly for short and higher transmission powers.

Author Keywords: Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT)

articleTitle: Optimizing Mutual Coupling Measurements for Active Phased Array Radar Calibration
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents experimental results of a radar calibration for an all-digital phased array using mutual coupling (MC) measurements. Three signal processing techniques are applied to the measurements to improve the Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) of distant couplings. A calibration procedure based on the far-field radiation patterns of truncated near-field measurements is used to quantify the effectiveness of the calibration. Root Mean Square Errors (RMSE) for magnitude and phase are estimated between the weights derived from radiation patterns and those from MC measurements. Results show improved SNR in the couplings as well as higher accuracy in the derived calibration weights when match filtering techniques are used in the MC measurements.

articleTitle: A Ku-Band Deployable Broadband Reflectarray for CubeSat Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a broadband foldable reflectarray (FRA) antenna mounted onto a 3U CubeSat frame is presented. The Ku-band reflectarray is linearly polarized and is fed with a pair of wideband Vivaldi antennas that produce a symmetric illu-minating radiation pattern. This high-gain antenna incorporates a stowage and deployment mechanism for both the reflectarray and the Vivaldi feed antenna elements. The bandwidth of the reflectarray is maximized through optimized reference phase mapping with multi-resonant elements. The measured gain for the two-element Vivaldi array feed is 10.3 dBi at 15.2 GHz, and measured results for the fabricated reflectarray mounted on a CubeSat frame show a maximum gain of 24.7 dBi at 15.2 GHz with a 4°3-dB beamwidth. The reflectarray achieves a measured realized gain of greater than 20 dBi from 11.7 GHz to 16.2 GHz.

articleTitle: A C-Band Dual-Pol Compact Reflector Antenna with a Square Waveguide Feed
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A C-band center-fed compact reflector antenna with dual linear polarization over a bandwidth of 25% is presented. To achieve this bandwidth, the feed uses a square waveguide, a polycarbonate neck, and a hat sub-reflector. The gain of the antenna is between 29 dBi and 32 dBi over the frequency range of 5-6.4 GHz. The main objective of the presented work is to extend the operating bandwidth of the high-gain antenna while keeping the structure of the feed as simple as possible. Measured antenna patterns, gain vs. frequency, cross-polarization vs. frequency, and S-parameters of the feed are presented.

articleTitle: Application of Vector Radiative Transfer Theory for Real-time Chaff Cloud Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we apply the vector radiative transfer method for real-time chaff cloud simulation. The chaff cloud created by an aircraft, called the chaff corridor, is analyzed. In order to consider the time flow, the orientation distribution of the chaff clouds is modeled by referring to the actual experimental results. As a result of analyzing the chaff clouds, the vertically polarized radar cross-section changed according to the change in the orientation distribution of the chaff cloud. The computation time was measured as an average of 0.583 seconds for the 3.1 million chaffs.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Accelerated Antenna Radiation Pattern Prediction for Undersampled Near-Field to Far-Field Transformation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a deep learning model based on U-Net architecture to estimate antenna radiation pattern and accelerate antenna characterization. This process is ordinarily time-consuming and expensive due to the need for an anechoic chamber and precision motion stages scanning through the antenna's 2D/3D near-field space. Significant developments in using deep neural network learning exhibit a non-linear relationship between high- and low-resolution datasets (e.g., images). In this work, we propose to build such a neural network to reconstruct the antenna radiation pattern from undersampled near-field data to accelerate pattern acquisition.

articleTitle: A Novel Minkowski Fractal Antenna with Double U-Slots for Ka-band Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel Minkowski fractal antenna with double U-slots is proposed for Ka-band satellite communications. A second-order Minkowski fractal is used to reduce the patch size. The double U -slots can create two resonant frequencies at 29.37 G Hz and 37.54 G Hz, respectively. The simulated results by the well-known CST software validate that the proposed antenna is capable of covering the frequency bands of 29.07 ~29.66 GHz and 37.08 ~37.92 GHz, respectively. The proposed antenna can achieve a gain of 7.0 dBi within the operating band and is applicable to Ka dual-band satellite communication. Also, its size is reduced by more than 28 % compared with the traditional double- U -slot antenna without the fractal structure.

articleTitle: Improving Genetic Algorithm Performance Using Artificial Intelligence for the First Population
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The design of UWB antennas is a complex process that involves many design parameters and constraints, such as the physical layout of the antenna, the frequency range, and the radiation pattern. The genetic Algorithm (GA) is a powerful optimization technique that can be used to solve these complex problems. However, the performance of GA is highly dependent on the initialization of the first population, which is commonly generated randomly. In this paper, we propose using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to generate the first population of GA and demonstrate an improvement of 9.5% in the performance of the optimization process.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Circular Patch Antenna with a Small Frequency Ratio
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A dual-band circular microstrip patch antenna, exciting the dominant TM<inf>11</inf>-mode and broadside higher-order TM<inf>12</inf>-mode with a frequency ratio of 1.17, is presented. The patch is loaded with two symmetric arc slits inspired by the surface current distribution of the TM12 mode. This will facilitate elongating the current path in the patch's periphery and reduce the frequency ratio. The unwanted sidelobes in the E-plane radiation pattern of the TM12 mode are consequently eliminated. In addition to the frequency-ratio reduction benefits, the antenna shows stable peak gain of ~8 dBi and a front-to-back ratio of at least ~18 dB in both bands. The results have been validated by prototyping and testing the antenna in practice.

articleTitle: Strategies for Gain Enhancement of Shared Aperture Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: It is desirable to improve the gain of existing aperture antennas because it can allow designers to reduce system size while maintaining the same level of performance. Some effective techniques include implementation of GRadient INdex (GRIN) lenses and metasurfaces. GRIN lenses have spatially varying material parameters, while metasurfaces can be used to create a phase gradient that alters the properties of an incoming wave. GRIN lenses and metasurfaces can be designed using sophisticated multi-objective optimization techniques to assure that they meet performance goals.

articleTitle: Experimental Validation of a Microwave Scanner for Brain Stroke Monitoring in Realistic Head Models
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work addresses brain stroke evolution assessment in mimicked clinical conditions using a low-complexity microwave imaging (MWI) scanner and realistic anthropomorphic head models. In particular, the MWI prototype employs a wearable 22-element flexible-antenna array, keeping a simple architecture and demanding low-computing power. It allows a real-time follow-up of the stroke-affected areas, providing 3-D maps of the dielectric variation through a differential linear imaging approach based on the Truncated Singular Value Decomposition (TSVD), the distorted Born approximation, and artifact removal procedure. The system includes a digital twin that emulates high-fidelity scenarios via EM full-wave simulations performed in an in-house Finite Element Method (FEM) solver. Finally, the assessment examines the system's monitoring capabilities involving custom-made and lifelike phantoms representing a dynamic stroke evolution.

articleTitle: An Evaluation and Modeling of Scattering Parameters of an Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) as a Function of Incident and Reflected Angles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Recently, reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) has attracted continuous attention in wireless communications. As the normal incidence condition of electromagnetic waves cannot always be satisfied in practical applications, the angular sensitivity of the incident and reflected waves on the performance of such RIS needs to be assessed and modeled. In this work, the impact of incident angles on the scattering parameters has been assessed through an RIS. The unit cell of the proposed RIS consists of a square spilt-ring-resonator which is designed on an FR-4 dielectric substrate with a ground plane at the back. Two horn antennas operating in the X-band are used as a transmitter and receiver antennas for assessing the scattering parameters. For different incident angles, simulation results show that the lowest insertion loss of −32 dB at 10 GHz has been achieved when the incident and reflected angles are 15° and 16.5° respectively. The proposed work is the first step to develop a theoretical model to determine the optimum receiver position for arbitrary incident angles as the main challenge in designing RISs is to obtain their electromagnetic (EM) responses, which is time-consuming and computationally prohibitive.

articleTitle: Integrate Fabry–Perot Resonator into Dielectric Resonator Antenna for Microwave and Mm-wave Operations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a design of a dual-band cylinder dielectric resonator antenna (CDRA) along with a Fabry-Perot resonator antenna (FPRA) for both sub-6 GHz and mm-wave 5G applications is presented. The proposed antenna generates two different operating resonances. The (FPRA) is realized by sticking the adhesive copper tape on the surfaces of the elliptical groove in the (DR), forming a pair of parallel plates and the ground plane. The FPRA is excited by an L-probe, which widens the bandwidth of the FPRA. At the same time, the CDR exited by a vertical conducting strip on its sidewall. The first resonance results from the CDR at 2.45 GHz with a realized gain of 6.7 dBi. On the other hand, the FPRA resonates at 28 GHz, achieving a realized gain of 11.9 dBi.

articleTitle: Realistic Colon Phantoms for Microwave Colonoscopy Validation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Colon phantoms that replicate a real colon dielectric properties, shape, and texture are required to verify a microwave colonoscopy system. The realism and accuracy of the phantom are quantified in this study using a method based on the antenna bandwidth variation.

articleTitle: 3D Phased Array Architecture for Field-of-View Enhancement in Satcom COTM Terminals
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In recent years, satellite communication (satcom) has attracted a lot of attention as key solution for mitigating the digital divide. In Communications On-the-Move (COTM) terminals, the antenna is subjected to a continuous movement, having to continuously adjust the radiated beam pattern in the satellite direction. In this paper, a satcom phased array with Field-of-View (FoV) improvement for mobility applications is presented exploiting a 3D configuration of the antenna elements.

articleTitle: Multi-Trace Multi-Screen Methods for Mixed Transmission/Scattering Problems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this contribution a novel fast-converging integral equation method is introduced that can be used to solve the mixed transmission/scattering problems by composite structures including multiple domains and metallic coatings that can contain junctions. This is achieved by combining the global multi-trace method with the quotient space discretisation of the multi-screen boundary integral equation. The method is illustrated by means of a sufficiently general geometry, the discretisation is discussed, and an effective Calderon multiplicative preconditioner is introduced. Numerical results corroborate the correctness and efficiency of the method.

articleTitle: A Simple Defected Ground Structure to Reduce Backside Radiation for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a defected ground structure (DGS)-based microstrip patch antenna for applications in the Industrial, Scientific, and Medical (ISM) band. The resonant frequency of the antenna is 2.33 GHz. The −10 dB impedance bandwidth of the antenna is 20 MHz (2.32-2.34 GHz), which satisfies the bandwidth requirement for most applications in the ISM band. The front-to-back ratio improves from 12 dB to 18 dB after incorporating the proposed DGS design without varying the overall gain. In addition, the proposed design has a reduced specific absorption rate from 1.54 W /kg to 0.53 W /kg, as averaged over 1 gm of tissue. This simple and low-profile antenna with the DGS is therefore suitable for biomedical, wearable devices, on-body sensors, and microwave imaging applications.

articleTitle: Silicon Carbide Slot Dielectric Resonator Antenna for High Temperature and Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) has a higher breakdown field and larger band gap compared to silicon, making it an attractive material for devices operating at high power and high temperatures. In this paper, we present the design and simulation of a slot fed rectangular dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) on a silicon carbide (4H-SiC) substrate. The antenna operates between 27 GHz – 33 GHz with a return loss of at least 10 dB. The maximum realized gain at 30 GHz is 5.5 dBi with a total efficiency of 97%.

articleTitle: Wideband Dual-Polarized 3D Printed Quad-Ridge Horn for mmWave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A design for manufacturing in stereolithography (SLA) with copper plating of a dual-polarized quad-ridge horn operating from Ka- through W-band is presented. The proposed horn has exponentially tapered ridges and sidewalls. Antenna is optimized to maintain nominal impedance match below 2.5:1 and consistent quality radiation patterns over the operating band. Phase-matched orthomode-transducer with custom single and double ridge waveguides is also designed and monolithically integrated with the horn. The computational studies are validated through an SLA 3D-printed and copper platted prototype.

articleTitle: The Detrimental Effects Experienced by a 5G mmWave 1×4 Antenna Array when Integrated into a Smartphone
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The detrimental effects experienced by a 5G mmWave antenna array (1×4) when integrated into an actual smartphone remain a challenge to the 5G mmWave antenna engineers. These effects include frequency shifting, impedance mismatching, mitigated gain/efficiency, and, worst of all, radiation pattern deformation. A small-size (26 mm x 5 mm x 1.524 mm) lx4 antenna array working across the 5G NR (new radio) bands n257/n258/n261 (24.25-29.5 GHz) was used as a study case. Two scenarios were studied, namely, without an open window on the frame, and with an open window on the frame. From the simulated results, one can see that the detrimental effect on the radiation pattern is the main concern when the smartphone frame is fully intact.

articleTitle: Measured and Modeled Outdoor Indoor Coverage at 28 GHz into High Thermal Efficiency Buildings
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: 28 GHz outdoor-indoor coverage into modern office buildings with high thermal efficiency windows is found to be severely limited due to 46 dB median penetration loss at normal incidence and additional 15 dB median oblique incidence loss. The study is based on measurements of path gain over 280 outdoor-indoor links, at ranges up to 100 m. A simple theoretical path gain model is extended to include building penetration through multiple sides of the building as well as a reflection from another building. The theoretical model accounts for the building orientation relative to the source, resulting in 4.9 dB RMSE relative to data, as compared to 5.7 dB RMSE from a linear fit and 14.7 dB RMSE for the 3GPP recommended model. Only coarse description of the buildings is required: building orientation and exterior wall composition, without any interior details. Coverage range for SNR>-8 dB from an outdoor base to a terminal just inside a high-efficiency building is under 35 m.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Imaging of Rough Dielectric Surface Profiles using a Single-Frequency Reverse Time Migration Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: An electromagnetic imaging scheme, which makes use of a single-frequency reverse time migration (RTM) technique to reconstruct two-dimensional (2D) rough surface profiles from the scattered field data, is formulated and implemented. The unknown surface profile, which is expressed as a one-dimensional height function, is the interface between two dielectric media. It is assumed that the profile is illuminated from one side and the scattered fields are “measured” along a line on this same side. RTM is used to construct a cross-correlation imaging functional that is numerically evaluated to yield an image of the investigation domain. The maxima of this functional yields an accurate reconstruction of the rough dielectric surface profile.

articleTitle: The Pyramid Cell and its Associated Scalar and Vector Bases for FEM and MoM Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Curl- and divergence-conforming vector bases for the pyramid have been recently obtained using a multiplicative constructive technique, that is by multiplying the lowest order vector functions by polynomial sets complete up to a given order. So far the technique has been successfully employed to obtain hierarchical bases of arbitrarily high order, which will be illustrated at the conference, and is now used to produce interpolatory vector bases. This presentation briefly summarizes the theoretical results produced up to now and the difficulties that still have to be overcome in order to obtain the interpolatory bases as well. Preliminary results will be presented at the conference.

articleTitle: Mechanical Phase Shifter with Continuous Beam Scanning Across Broadside
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper extends and consolidates previous work related with an all-metallic, low loss mechanical phase shifter implemented in gap-waveguide technology. The phase shifter is developed for Ka-band, to be used as part of a ground terminal for satellite-on-the-move communications. The device is formed by three levels. Levels 0 and 2 remain fixed whereas level 1 is rotatory. The rotation of level 1 does not increase the volume of the device in any case, and allows for the device to introduce a progressive phase shift between consecutive channels. This progressive phase shift provides beam steering capabilities to any array. Thanks to the arc-shaped and inverted-arc-shaped phase shifting waveguides, the device is able to provide continuous beam steering across the broadside point.

articleTitle: Dual-Band, Ultra-Thin MM-Wave Antenna with Shared Aperture on Flexible Substrate
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A low-profile, flexible dual-band stacked patch antenna for millimeter wave mobile communication with a capacitive feed and parasitic elements to enhance the bandwidth has been introduced. This antenna operates at frequencies of 27.8-29 GHz and 37.5-38.7 GHz and has a thickness of only 270 um. The effects of the parasitic elements on the antenna's return loss and gain were studied, and results indicate that the single element patch antenna maintained a consistent boresight radiation pattern with a maximum gain of 6.82 dBi for the lower band and 6.22 dBi for the upper band. A 4x1 array antenna is also investigated which has 12.04 dBi of gain with <tex>$\pm 45^{\circ}$</tex> of scan angle for the lower band and 12.84 dBi of gain with <tex>$\pm 30^{\circ}$</tex> scan angle for the upper band. Total efficiency of the antenna is found to be 86% for the lower band and 71% for the upper band.

articleTitle: Design of a Novel Sub-THz Dielectric Resonator Antenna Fed by Substrate Integrated Image Guide (SIIG) Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) design with an <tex>$\text{HEM}_{11\delta}$</tex> mode fed by a substrate integrated image guide (SIIG) operating at Sub-THz frequency bands. The proposed antenna operates over the wideband frequency range of 156–177 GHz and covers −10 dB impedance bandwidth of 21 GHz. In addition, the average gain of the proposed DRA is 7.35 dBi in the broadside direction, with a peak gain of 8.5 dBi at 163 GHz. The designed antenna can be applied in Sub-THz wireless communication applications with competitive performance and low-cost fabrication technology.

articleTitle: 3D Tracking of Small Moving Targets in Cluttered Environment from the Isolines Processing of Millimeter-wave Radar Images
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we report a three-dimensional tracking technique of small moving metallic targets in a cluttered environment using millimeter-wave Frequency-Modulated Continuous-Wave radars. Trajectories are determined from the estimation of the Direction of Arrival of signal backscattered from targets illuminated by the steerable radar beam. The electromagnetic clutter is mitigated thanks to an original image processing technique based on isolines, that is, lines in the radar images along which the echo level is the same. Our targeted application is the indoor detection at short range (up to 1.5 meters for a single radar) of tagged flying insects for behavioral studies.

articleTitle: Data Collection in Ducting Conditions for Emitter Localization with a Single Receiver
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We employ a prototype vertical antenna array collection system to collect overwater radio frequency (RF) signals in varied evaporative ducting conditions. Atmospheric modeling influenced site selection and scheduling, and results confirm the presence of evaporation ducts in the expected regions. The envisioned use of the data is for algorithmic testing of overwater emitter ranging from a single passive receiver platform. <sup>1</sup><sup>1</sup>This research was, in part, funded by the U.S. Government. The views and conclusions contained in this document are those of the authors and should not be interpreted as representing the official policies, either expressed or implied, of the U.S. Government. Approved for Public Release, Distribution Unlimited.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Tunable Programmable Reflective Metasurface Unit Based on Minkowski Fractal Geometry
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a miniaturized tunable programmable reflective metasurface unit based on Minkowski fractal geometry. Simulations are conducted to optimize the patch size <tex>$L$</tex> and scaling factor <tex>$S$</tex> of Minkowski fractal geometry in order to fully exploit its intrinsic miniaturization capability. Four voltage-controlled varactor diodes are then added to adjust the unit's resonant property, thus making the unit tunable. Simulation results show that the proposed unit can realize the phases of <tex>$0^{\circ}, 90^{\circ}, 180^{\circ}$</tex>, and 270° with a uniform difference of 90° at around 5.25 GHz while the dimension of the unit cell is only about <tex>$0.35\lambda\times 0.35\lambda$</tex>, where <tex>$\lambda$</tex> is the free-space wavelength. The compactness of the unit allows a smaller interelement spacing with a wide-angle scanning capability, so it is very suitable for designing reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) used in beamforming and beam-steering applications.

articleTitle: LoRa-based Privacy-Aware and Contactless Surveillance in Next-generation Smart Homes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: There are many security and surveillance applications in which camera-based or invasive human activity recognition is not permissible due to privacy, insecurity, and discomfort issues. Moreover, vision-based surveillance systems have a few key technical challenges that limit their practicality such as bad illumination, obstacles, and occlusion. In such cases, we require a more reliable system which can work in challenging situations such as in darkness, long-range, through walls or obstacles, a rainy and smoky environment where vision-based systems do not deliver good results. Only high-energy and long-range wireless sensors which can identify targets through obstacles, walls, worst climate or surrounding conditions can serve the purpose. In this paper, we propose to use the LoRa transceiver to identify different persons from their walking patterns through bricks and a concrete wall where people other than the target person are moving freely. Moreover, we employed three different deep-learning models to evaluate the efficacy of the proposed system. Our highly accurate 99% results encourage the use of contactless LoRa sensors in many privacy-critical applications such as healthcare, security, and surveillance, where short-range and low-energy signals have limited utilisation.

articleTitle: Propagation Modeling for Indoor Wireless Channels in High-Speed Train
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Wireless train communication network (WTCN) is very important to enhance the intelligence level of high-speed trains. In this paper, we study the indoor wireless channels in high-speed trains (HSTs). A propagation model considering the specific interior layout of HSTs is proposed. Compared with other classical models, the numerical results shows that the proposed model is more consistent with the measurements.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Flat-Top Beams Based on Pencil Beam Widening
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a pencil to flat-top beam transform based on polynomial shaping of given symmetrical excitation. The polynomials are constructed by imposing an arbitrary order of flatness at the beam peak. The shaping is illustrated with the synthesis of second-kind Chebyshev flat-top beams with specified sidelobe level. Compared to other flat-top beamforming techniques utilizing second-kind Chebyshev pencil beams, the proposed transform brings flatter beams for the same sidelobe level.

articleTitle: Learning From Noise: An Unsupervised GPR Data Denoising Scheme based on Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Denoising ground-penetrating radar (GPR) B-scans is of great importance for identifying the target response. Existing supervised deep learning techniques developed for this purpose require generating a large set of noise-free B-scans as labels, which requires high computational cost (i.e., days/weeks of the execution of forward solvers). To tackle this issue, this study proposes a generative adversarial network (GAN)-based unsupervised learning scheme for denoising B-scans. In particular, GAN estimates the noise patterns in B-scans and then the estimated patterns are removed from noisy B-scans to obtain the denoised B-scans. The proposed GAN uses a patchwise contrastive loss and a small set of noise-only images. The test results on real measured B-scans demonstrate the proposed unsupervised scheme's higher denoising accuracy and generalization capability compared to existing supervised deep learning techniques.

articleTitle: Multi-Trace Formulation of Internally Combined Volume-Surface Integral Equations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this contribution, volume-surface integral equations (VSIE) are incorporated into the global multi-trace method. This extends multi-trace modelling to scattering on composite structures, that also have parts with non-homogeneous properties. It is shown, the volume-surface integral equations modeling these regions can be integrated in the framework of the multi-trace formulation.
