Due to the nature of the multi-trace method, the interior of the non-homogeneous regions only interacts internally with its boundary. There are no interactions between a region and the interior of another region. Further, the block structure of the multi-trace method is retained, which allows the use Calderon preconditioning.

articleTitle: On-Chip 60 GHz Coplanar Folded Slot Antenna with Air Cavity and Reflector
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A 60 GHz coplanar folded slot antenna (CFSA) using a silicon-on-insulator substrate, an air cavity, and a back reflector is proposed. The proposed CFSA has a center frequency operating at 60 GHz with a −10 dB impedance bandwidth of 3.3% (58.9-60.9 GHz). The presence of air cavities and reflectors serves to improve efficiency and realized gain. The cross-sectional area of the air cavity occupies only 16% of that of the antenna unit cell. At 60 GHz, the peak gain of the proposed CFSA antenna is calculated to be 5.8 dBi with a directivity of 6.0 dBi. The efficiency of the proposed antenna is simulated to be 95%.

articleTitle: Analyzing Wideband Computational Time Delay for Phased Arrays After Direct Carrier Sampling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: New technologies are providing unprecedentedly high sample rates for converting multiple analog streams into digital formats for real time digital signal processing. High-speed analog conversion allows digital implementations of transformations that were previously only practical with analog circuits. With new capabilities in digital signal processing architectures comes new engineering trade-offs to explore. This paper examines the computational implementation of wideband time delay inside the field programmable gate array portion of a GHz sample rate system-on-chip device using a polyphase FIR filter architecture to interpolate high speed data in real time. Since the quality of the time delay operator is a key performance metric of phased array technologies used in radar, communications, remote sensing, and radio astronomy, innovations to the implementation of the time delay operator can benefit all of these technologies.

articleTitle: Polarimetric Terahertz Transmission Imaging of Crystal Quartz Sample
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper investigates polarimetric terahertz time domain transmission imaging aiming at enhancing the detection of different regions on the same sample. Here, x-cut quartz crystal adjacent to quartz glass are utilized to compose a sample that hypothetically mimics breast tumor of cancerous and healthy regions, respectively. The obtained images establish a potential advantage of polarimetric terahertz imaging for future use in imaging excised breast cancer tumors.

articleTitle: 5G Multilayer Slot Array Antenna Fed by Integrated Substrate Groove Gap Waveguide for 26 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a 5G multilayer slot array antenna in the 26 GHz band, fed by an integrated substrate groove gap waveguide (ISGGW). In contrast to previous works, we chose to populate the ISGGW and the intermediate “cavity” layers with a printed “Mushroom” type unit cell in order to appropriately guide the electromagnetic wave. The design allows for a multi-layered architecture, that is supported by the configuration of parallel Artificial Magnetic Conductors (AMC) and Perfect Electric Conductor (PEC) structures at the intermediate, in-contact, surfaces of the layers. The presence of parallel AMC and PEC surfaces avoids any electromagnetic leakage among them, regardless of any air gap existence. Unwanted air gaps between the layers of a multilayer structure can be caused by surface roughness and imperfect flat surface presence. The multiple stacked layers of the proposed structure are robust to such gaps underlining the work's significance. The impedance bandwidth <tex>$(\mathrm{S}_{11} < -10\ \text{dB})$</tex> of 7.4% covers the frequency range from 25.13 GHz to 27.05 GHz, the realized gain varies between 8–12 dB, and the efficiency ranges between 50% and 80% over the operating band.

articleTitle: Novel 3D-Printed Flat, Cylindrical Lens for Beam Focusing and Higher Gain of Horn Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A COTS K-band gain horn with advertised gain of 20dBi at center frequency (<tex>$\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{c}}$</tex>) and boresight is compared to a longer gain horn of the same series, with a gain of 25dBi. It is desired to achieve the gain of the longer horn using lensing techniques as applied to the shorter horn to create a total device of smaller form factor capable of demonstrating the higher gain. A Luneburg-like lens was designed to fill a cylindrical form factor and was then optimized using Computer Simulation Technology (CST) software to produce the desired beam shape for the goal gain. The lens was realized using a low-loss photocurable resin on a digital light processing (DLP) driven stereolithography (SLA) 3D printer. The 20dBi horn was then characterized in a far field anechoic chamber against a K-band rectangular reference horn, both with and without the cylindrical lens. A total of 6dB of gain increase was achieved with the lensed aperture at f<inf>c</inf>, exceeding larger version of the horn by 1dB.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Coaxial Metasurface Radar Absorber Using Varactor Diode Tuning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Metasurfaces can be used as radar absorbers. However, passive metasurfaces are intrinsically limited in their bandwidth-to-thickness ratio. Thus, it is difficult to design a metasurface which is both thin and wideband. To overcome such limitation, we design a reconfigurable metasurface using varactor diodes. Their bias-dependent variable capacitance offer a range of resonance frequencies that can cover most of the VHF-UHF range. Such behavior is here highlighted on a coaxial metasurface by simulation. Reconfigurability is intended to serve as a preliminary step towards time-modulated metasurfaces.

articleTitle: Broadband Metamaterial Design Using Carbon Fiber and Resistive Sheet Materials
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to compare experimental and simulated results of different broadband metamaterial absorber approaches. One such approach, which used a custom patterned fabricated board with resistive sheets, showed promising results in achieving broadband characteristics. In addition, quasi-isotropic carbon fiber patterns have been designed using genetic programming and simulated results have been obtained. We fabricate these carbon fiber designs and compare the measured results with the simulations, as well as compare with the resistive sheet design.

articleTitle: Electro-Mechanical Beam Steering Modeling to Enhance the Scanning Range of UWB Vivaldi Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a simulation based far-field radiation beam steering model to increase the scanning range of a <tex>$1\times 4$</tex> Vivaldi antenna array operating at <tex>$5.8-18+GHz$</tex>. Along with the electrical beam steering method where phase difference is provided between the array elements, a novel mechanical tilting of the array elements is introduced. Different mechanical tilting is implemented by tilting the array elements along the elevation plane while maintaining a <tex>$15^{\circ}$</tex> tilt angle difference. The introduction of electro-mechanical steering increases the scanning range by 4.3 times while maintaining a unidirectional radiation pattern and 15.4 <tex>$dBi$</tex> gain. Based on the simulated results, the electro-mechanical beam steering model when implemented on the proposed <tex>$1\times 4$</tex> Vivaldi antenna array is capable of achieving a <tex>$\pm 52^{\circ}$</tex> scanning range along the elevation plane with a 4.8 dB scanning loss.

articleTitle: Metasurface Tiles on Conformable Origami Platforms for Adaptive and Sparse Computational Microwave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article presents a computational imaging technique by making an interesting connection between two design methodologies namely, origami based shape morphing platforms and metasurfaces. Reconfigurable origami platforms mounted with cavity-backed metasurface antennas have been employed to demonstrate stand-off sparse computational imaging at mi-crowave frequencies (17 - 27 GHz). We use these apertures to perform diffraction-limited RF image reconstructions of 2D and 3D stand-off targets. Such modular, low-cost, conformable aperture find application in remote sensing, stand-off security imagers at checkpoints, automotive radars, and biomedical imaging. We also demonstrate scene adaptive imaging where different origami morphology helps to improve different aspects of imaging metrics like signal-to-noise ratio, cross-range resolution, spatial diversity, and field-of-view.

articleTitle: Over-the-Air Noise Figure Measurement in a Reverberation Chamber for Low-Noise Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Measuring the noise figure (NF) of highly-integrated wireless devices can be a challenging task. This paper shows that the reverberation-chamber-noise-figure (RCN) method can be used to determine this characteristic of a device with an NF below 4 dB at sub-GHz frequencies. This is a significantly lower NF and operating frequency as compared to the device used for the original RCN method. The lower NF is measured using the simplified RCN method, which has an improved uncertainty over the original RCN method. To accommodate for the operating frequency below 1 GHz, a larger reverberation chamber is used. An uncertainty analysis shows that the NF could be estimated within 0.52 dB uncertainty and the gain within 0.91 dB.

articleTitle: A 4-Unit High-Isolation Broadband MIMO Antenna Used for Mobile Phone of 5G Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a 4-unit multi-branch high-isolation wideband MIMO antenna used for the mobile phone of 5G communication, and it consists of 4 identical units located at the four corners of the smartphone. Each unit is composed of 2 U-shaped branches and metallized vias. The antenna uses a multi-branch resonance technology to expand the bandwidth, and applies a reasonable distribution of decoupling branches to improve the isolation. The final design has a return loss of less than −6 dB in the band of 3.3 – 5 GHz, and the isolation is better than 14 dB. The antenna has good omnidirectional radiation and gain, which can fully meet the requirements for mobile phone antennas.

articleTitle: Efficient Design of Thinner Broadband MRAM Using Novel Formulation of Cost Function
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Modern military and civic applications require broadband microwave radar absorbing material (RAM). Such a RAM is multilayer and invariably increases the surface thickness of platforms (viz., aircraft, ship, vehicle) and thereby increases the overall body weight. So, all RAM design methods do some kind of optimization of layer parameters. In this paper, we study the effect of commonly used cost function formulations on obtaining global optima. We also explore formulation for thinner design of RAM and propose a new cost function. Our proposed formulation effectively works as a two-step optimizer and is able to provide thinner results without increasing the complexity of the algorithm employed for optimization.

articleTitle: Understanding Aperture Efficiency for Reflector Antennas Using the Poynting Streamline Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In most analysis methods, the reflector antennas are usually modeled and understood as transmitters, while the receiving characteristics are approximated using the Geometrical Optics (GO) methods. The Poynting streamline method based on full-wave analysis uses the streamlines of Poynting vectors to represent the trajectory of field energy near the receiving antenna. Through the analysis of a horn antenna feed and a planar array feed, the aperture efficiency of the reflector antenna can be intuitively visualized by comparing the geometry of the effective area to the physical shape of the reflector antenna.

articleTitle: Field Experiment of a Circularly Polarized Underwater Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A half sheath dipole antenna (HSDA) has been investigated as one of practical antennas for various underwater applications such as wireless communication systems. However, a wireless communication system using HSDAs may suffer from poor connectivity when antennas are perpendicularly arranged because HSDAs are linearly polarized antennas with high cross polar discrimination (XPD). To overcome this problem, we propose a quadrature feed circularly polarized half sheath antenna (Q-HSA) consisting of two vertically crossing HSDAs, which ideally shows 0-dB XPD. A Q-HSA and a HSDA are designed at the frequency of 100 kHz and are prototyped to measure their characteristics at real sea. Measured results show that the Q-HSA outperforms the HSDA because the variation of the received power by the Q-HSA while rotating, up to 4 dB, is extremely lower than that of the HSDA. We believe the proposed Q-HSAs expand the communicable area of underwater wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: A Statistical Analysis of Feature Transformation for Efficient Localisation in Urban Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we perform a transformation-based statistical analysis with an eye to designing a robust and efficient localisation scheme. To this end, we evaluate the coefficient of determination (COD) also denoted as <tex>$R^{2}$</tex> on simulated electromagnetic wave propagation models in an urban environment. Our transformation-based statistical models show that two measurable network parameters, namely the received power (RP) and the time of arrival (ToA), present a strong correlation with a mobile user's given location. By transforming the network parameters we were able to achieve COD of 0.577 for the RP and 0.549 for ToA using the Modulus transformation. We believe that by exploiting the high correlation of parameter transformation, there is potential to design fast and robust machine learning localisation schemes through which the future location of a mobile user can be accurately and reliably predicted.

articleTitle: Towards a Self-Adaptive Frequency Normalization Scheme for the Low-Frequency Stabilized Magnetic Field Integral Equation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Low-frequency preconditioned boundary integral equations based on quasi-Helmholtz decompositions are widely used to obtain the radiated or scattered fields by a finite structure over a wide frequency range. Specifically, for perfectly electrically conducting (PEC) structures, the conformingly discretized magnetic field integral equation (MFIE) plays a crucial role. However, a careful analysis and, potentially, ad-hoc adaptions are necessary for each excitation to ensure that all fields are obtained accurately. To avoid such cumbersome analyses, we propose an excitation agnostic and self-adaptive frequency normalization scheme. To this end, the appropriate scaling factors are derived based on the norms of the right-hand side (RHS) components without requiring any ad-hoc adaptions or any a-priori knowledge about the excitation. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach to obtain accurate fields.

articleTitle: Propagation Modeling for RIS-Enabled Channels Based on Ray-Tracing and the Equivalence Principle
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We propose a method to model wave propagation in realistic reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-enabled communication channels. Based on full-wave simulation and the equivalence principle, an RIS is equivalent to a surface current source with electric and magnetic current densities. Next, this equivalent source is integrated into ray-tracing to derive the RIS propagation model. This method combines the accuracy of full-wave analysis with the efficiency of ray-tracing, and provides a rigorous way to analyze realistic RIS-enabled channels. A case study of modeling a simple scenario demonstrates that the accuracy of this method is comparable with full-wave analysis across the near-field and far-field regions of the RIS.

articleTitle: Radiation Characteristics and Performance Evaluation of A Non-Uniform Slots SIW Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Radiation characteristics and performance evaluation of a slotted array substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) antenna with non-uniform slots are presented by varying the length of slots on the SIW surface. The slotted array SIW antenna is designed with non-uniform slots and intended to work at the operating frequency of 2.4 GHz, while the dielectric substrate used is an FR4 epoxy material with the thickness of 1.6 mm. Performance evaluation of the proposed SIW antenna radiation characteristics is carried out by comparing the simulation and measurement results. It was found that the proposed non-uniform slots SIW antenna could achieve the measured bandwidth of 92 MHz from the frequency of 2.323 GHz to 2.415 GHz which was comparable to the simulation result while maintaining the gain and radiation patterns.

articleTitle: A Hybrid MSL/SIW-Based Feeding Network for Broadband mm-Wave Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A Broadband series-fed linearly polarized antenna Array is presented for millimeter-wave applications. Three-dimensional hybrid MSL/SIW T-Juctions with a wide range of coupling ratios and unequal amplitude are used to build the power network with equal power distribution. For validation, four linearly polarized (LP) tapered slot antenna element arranged serially in vertical position to the feeding networks. The elements are flared in opposite directions to achieve equal phase at adjacent elements. Simulated results show that the impedance bandwidth of about 53% over the entire 23-39.7 GHz range and a maximum gain of 18.2 dBi.

articleTitle: Estimation of High-Altitude Electromagnetic Pulse Coupling onto Power Generation Facility Equipment
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A systematic approach is presented to evaluate the effects of high-altitude electromagnetic pulse (HEMP) signals on the equipment located inside a power generation facility. The technique is based on a combination of practical measurement and simulation efforts in characterizing the radio wave propagation behavior and the device immunity profile. Of particular interest in this work is the estimation of the vulnerability level of equipment that is connected to long cables. As an example application, a detailed study is put forth for one common class of facility equipment, with its frequency- and time-domain HEMP coupling properties investigated as a function of terminal loading condition and cable attachment configuration. Overall, the proposed method can be generalized and applied to other electronic components and systems found in the facility environment.

articleTitle: Array of Coaxial Periodic Leaky Wave Antennas in Parallel Configuration for Restricted Volume Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper studies a unique approach to combine coaxial periodic leaky wave (CPLW) antennas in parallel array configuration for restricted volume application. An improved gain and mitigated stopband attenuation are observed when up to four 200 mm long CPLW semi-rigid cables are simultaneously fed, forming a narrow beam pattern suitable for use in a confined volume due to the reduced size. The proposed antenna array exhibits a gain of greater than 10 dB from 8.0 to 10.5 GHz. The sidelobe levels are less than −10 dB at broadside frequency 9.8 GHz. The beam width of the CPLWA array is approximately 9° with a scanning range of greater than 25° over the operated frequency band. The array of CPLW antenna called parallel CPLWA array is discussed, fabricated and measured showing good agreement with simulations.

articleTitle: Intensity-only OMP-based Direction Estimation for Hybrid Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Future wireless networks are envisioned to benefit from adaptive electromagnetic wave propagation by leveraging reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) that programmably redirect signals toward intended users. This reconfigurable wireless environment is only possible when the directions of the transmitters and the receivers with respect to RISs are known. This information can be efficiently retrieved using hybrid reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (HRISs) that can sense a portion of the incident signal. However, HRIS structures are most beneficial when the integrated sensing circuitry can be implemented in a simple and low-cost manner. In this paper, we propose and numerically demonstrate a process to only use the intensity of the sampled incident signal to detect the angles of arrivals (AoA) on the HRIS. Toward this goal, we deploy an orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) algorithm which can robustly recover data from sparsely sensed samples-a condition also applicable to HRISs. The proposed estimation approach will reduce the complexity of the sensing components of HRISs and will bring them one step closer to real-world applications.

articleTitle: Point-of-Care Microwave Scanner for Monitoring Breast Cancer Treatment: An Initial Stability Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Microwave imaging has been proposed for monitoring breast health and cancer treatment. Consistency of the images collected from volunteers over time is crucial, as this enables detecting changes in the breast for monitoring applications. In this paper, the stability of the permittivity reconstruction for left and right breasts of a healthy volunteer during successive scans and at three different time points is examined.

articleTitle: Genetic Algorithm Based Optimization for Concentric Circular Antenna Array Design
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the implementation of the Genetic Algorithm to optimize the design of a large-scale sparse receiving array for innovative bistatic radar systems aimed at space debris detection. The optimization procedure is employed to find a preliminary configuration for a thinned array that exhibits maximum side lobe level suppression and simultaneously reduces the number of active elements. The results obtained through the exploited strategy are compared with those of the basic configuration with uniformly fed elements and those resulting from the use of tapering with traditional windowing techniques. The proposed thinned array configuration shows a peak directivity of 33.5 dBi and a Side Lobe Level (SLL) of -31.5 dB in the principal planes, with a 19 % reduction of the number of elements, meeting the specifications required by the application scenario.

articleTitle: Experimental Test of Employing Probe Signal Derivatives in Near-Field Antenna Measurements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We report the results of a first experimental test employing both the probe signal and a probe signal spatial derivative in spherical near-field antenna measurements – with the aim of reducing the number of sampling points and potentially the measurement time.

articleTitle: Design & EM Simulation of a Continuous-Dielectric Luneburg Lens Antenna Using COMSOL-PyAEDT
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a new approach of the design and electromagnetic (EM) simulation of a graded-index (GRIN) Luneburg lens antenna is shown and discussed. Two FEM-based commercial EM software packages, COMSOL and HFSS, were utilized to design, simulate, and predict the EM performances of the lens antenna. MATLAB scripting language was utilized to interact with the COMSOL solver and design and generate the lens' inhomogeneous permittivity profile, and python-based scripting language, PyAEDT, was used to control HFSS solver and simulate the EM performance of the designed lens. Full wave electromagnetic simulation results of an example Luneburg lens antenna (60mm diameter) with WR28 waveguide source are presented along with the detail description of the simulation approach.

articleTitle: Dual Circularly Polarized Metasurface Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes the design and numerical validation of a low-profile dual-polarized antenna where two opposite circular polarizations are obtained by exciting the same modulated metasurface either with a radially outward traveling surface wave (SW) or with an inward traveling SW. The outward traveling SW is launched from a vertical pin located at the center of the radiating aperture, as in conventional MTS antennas, while the inward traveling SW is excited from the aperture edge, through an underlying parallel plate waveguide. The MTS is characterized by a modulation designed to achieve broadside radiation and by an anisotropy providing a different circular polarization depending on the traveling direction of the SW. The modulation index is designed to equalize the efficiency of the beams radiated in the two polarizations. A practical two-port feeding structure has also been designed and numerically analyzed.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of the Lander's UHF Antenna for the Mars Sample Return Campaign
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an investigation of the Radio-Frequency (RF) performance of the UHF antenna employed on the Sample Retrieval Lander (SRL) for the planned Mars Sample Return campaign. The antenna would be used for the radio communication with the orbital spacecraft and its operation is impacted by the presence of the lander deck, instruments located in close proximity, solar panels, and the Martian terrain. To evaluate the degradation of antenna radiation pattern, numerical analyses have been carried out in Ansys HFSS using the Finite-Element Method (FEM). The study was validated by repeating the simulation using a hybrid technique that employs the Integral Equation (IE) method.

articleTitle: Deployable L-Band Bowtie Antenna Array for Satellite Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A stowable and deployable 4×4 bowtie array at L-band is presented. The 16 bowtie antennas are fabricated using standard FR-4. The bowtie array uses flexible copper-clad kapton with supporting narrow aluminum channels to replace the conventional rigid ground plane. A size reduction of about 85% is achieved when the antenna is stowed. The measured gain, excluding the losses of the feed network, is between 16 dBi and 19.5 dBi over the frequency band of interest from 1.2 GHz to 1.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Dual Polarized Omnidirectional 5G/6G mmWave Tx/Rx Frontend Module
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: An omnidirectional 5G mmWave frontend module is proposed. The frontend module covers 5G frequencies from 24.25 GHz up to 29.5 GHz (n258, n257, and n261 3GPP bands). Dual linear polarization is supported. 24 beamformer ICs feed a phased array antenna with <tex>$2\times 96$</tex> elements. The concept is modular – a sub-module is used as a base. Several PCB sub-modules are stacked to create the complete frontend. The proposed design consists of four sub-modules and achieves 360° scanning performance in azimuth, ± 45° in elevation and an EIRP of about 50 dBm.

articleTitle: CLASI Florida Preliminary Drone Measurements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Expanding upon our previous experiment in Monterey, California, the Coastal Land-Air-Sea Interaction (CLASI) group seeks to explore and characterize additional coastal boundary locations. Extending our range in height from our previous experiment, this experiment takes us to the coastal boundary of Florida, specifically around Topsail Hill Preserve State Park in Santa Rosa Beach. Our drone was deployed throughout the month of February to observe and record how electromagnetic (EM) signals travel in different types of environments spanning from standard to ducting conditions. Our goal for this experiment is to further investigate duct estimation and analyze sea surface roughness using our two-channel drone-based software defined radio receiver system. With this extended height, our drone profiles will have more null and peaks, allowing us to better compare theoretical models of sea surface roughness such as Miller-Brown and Ament.

articleTitle: Deep Feature Learning for Microwave Mammography with Convolutional Autoencoders
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel system relying on an unsupervised approach to categorize breast impressions obtained using low-frequency electromagnetic fields (LFEMF). We designed a miniaturized metasurface as the receiver, and an electrically small antenna as the transmitter, both operating at 200 MHz, to create two-dimensional impressions, referred to as LFEMF mammograms. Leveraging the integration of our designed metasurface and applied scanning techniques, we achieved images with resolutions less than <tex>$\lambda/150$</tex>. Our deep learning algorithm, trained on mammogram impressions in an unsupervised manner where no human labeling is involved, clusters images to their twelve subcategories with an adjusted rand score (ARS) of 91.18%.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Fast Method for Designing Hybrid Phase-Shifting Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, we present a semi-numerical approach that enables the efficient design of hybrid phase-shifting surfaces (PSSs) with significantly reduced computational cost. Traditional design approaches of PSSs with <tex>$N$</tex> number of layers that have <tex>$M$</tex> different variations of conductive patches, must utilize <tex>$M^{N}$</tex> full-wave simulations. Our approach achieves a great reduction of this computational effort only requiring <tex>$N\times M$</tex> full-wave simulations by decomposing a PSS into <tex>$N$</tex> number of cascaded networks, and utilizing the multiplication property of ABCD parameters. To validate the accuracy of our method, a hybrid PSS is designed to steer the beam of a circularly polarized holographic metasurface antenna (HMA) that operates at 30 GHz. Comparisons between our analytical results and full-wave simulations for our beam steerable antenna demonstrate an angular error of less than 1°.

articleTitle: A Mammography System based on Low-Frequency Electromagnetic Fields
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, we introduce a breast cancer detection system based on a metasurface antenna with miniaturized unitcells. The operating frequency of the system is 200 MHz, allowing for sufficient penetration into the female breast tissues, while providing impressions with good resolution. Leveraging the designed metasurface film and working in the near-field region of the transmitter antenna, we were able to detect very small abnormalities in female breast models.

articleTitle: Wearable Flexible Body-Adaptable Frequency Reconfigurable Filter for Muscle Contraction Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a wearable and flexible Radio Frequency (RF) filter that is designed to act as a sensor to monitor muscular contractions. The Coplanar Waveguide (CPW) fed filter incorporates logarithmically scaled spiral defected ground structures (DGSs) etched from the ground planes in addition to U -slot capacitors etched from the feeding line. The filter is fabricated on top of a Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) substrate and is sandwiched between a Room Temperature Vulcanizing (RTV) silicon substrate. When the filter is at rest, it displays a dual bandstop operation at 2.5 GHz and 3.36 GHz and a dual bandpass operation at 1.62 GHz and 2.27 GHz. When stretched, these four frequencies change in an ascending order in a gradual fashion correlated with the intensity of the exerted muscular contraction on the stretchable filter. This flexible filter constitutes the front-end of the sensor, and it is accompanied by a flexible back-end circuit that extracts the reflection and transmission coefficients of the filter and derives their associated voltages. Each of these associated voltages that are extracted from the flexible back-end circuits indicates a specific level of muscle contraction.

articleTitle: An Array of Millimeter-Wave Groove Gap Waveguide Elements with Phase Shifting and Polarization Reconfigurability
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper discusses the design of an array of groove gap waveguide elements that achieves polarization reconfigurability over the span of frequencies between 28 and 32 GHz. The proposed array is composed of two vertically and two horizontally placed groove gap waveguide elements. Each element is able to act as a phase shifter by altering the pin configurations along the two sides of the groove. More specifically, at 30 GHz, each element produces a phase shift that spans between -96° and -49° with a phase step of almost 10°. In addition, polarization reconfigurability is achieved by exciting the corresponding waveguide elements through a single-pole-double-throw (SPDT) switch.

articleTitle: Joint Estimation of Mutual Coupling and Direction of Arrival for 2D Sparse Arrays using CMA-ES
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: 2D sparse arrays have better performance than uniformly-spaced arrays with the same number of elements when applied in direction of arrival (DOA) estimation problems. In practice, when these elements are closely spaced, mutual coupling effects distort the commonly assumed spatial model and compromise the standard DOA techniques. If the exact mutual coupling matrix (MCM) is not known a priori, the MCM and DOAs must be jointly estimated. This results in a difficult, nonlinear optimization problem. Nature inspired algorithms have been shown to be effective in complex electromagnetic optimization problems including 1D sparse array problems for DOA estimation. In this paper, covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES) is used to jointly compensate for mutual coupling and estimate direction of arrival for 2D sparse arrays. Results for a nested sparse array configuration are presented.

articleTitle: High Gain Meander Line Antenna for 2.4 GHz Bluetooth Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a highly directive meander line antenna is proposed to be utilized in the unlicensed Bluetooth band. The main goal of the proposed structure is to achieve low profile, and high gain in the Bluetooth band. Moreover, the antenna should be of low cost to be suitable for commercial use. The proposed structure is simulated using HFSS and CST to verify the obtained results. The maximum calculated gain of the antenna is 9.95 dBi (9.79 dBi) along the end-fire direction as simulated by HFSS (CST). The antenna demonstrated high radiation efficiency which is around 96% over its working bandwidth ranging from 2.395 GHz – 2.5 GHz (2.4 GHz – 2.48 GHz), according to HFSS (CST). The antenna also demonstrated its high polarization purity with maximum cross polarization level of −24 dB.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Frequency Selective Surface with Reconfigurable Properties
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-band frequency selective surface (FSS) with reconfigurable properties unit cell for the millimeter wave frequency band. The proposed unit cell is composed of patches printed on a dielectric substrate with no metallic screen on the back side, where a PIN diode is embedded between the two patches. The unit cell transmits or reflects the incident waves by switching the diode to ON and OFF states. The maximum reflection is achieved at the OFF state of the diode in the frequency band of 4.70 to 7.75 GHz and the maximum transmission is obtained in the same frequency band when the diode is ON state. In contrast, the maximum transmission is achieved at OFF state of the diode in the frequency band of 25.80 to 30.40 GHz and the maximum reflection is obtained in the same frequency band when the diode is ON. The multiple functionalities with high values of transmission and reflection make this FSS a good candidate for mm-wave applications.

articleTitle: Multi-Band CubeSat Antenna and Design Considerations for Space Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a slot-based multi-band CubeSat antenna is designed for CubeSat applications operating at the UHF band. The proposed antenna design consists of a frequency reconfigurable (FR) slot-based antenna fabricated on a FR-4 substrate. The frequency range covered by the FR antenna is 300-450MHz. A single varactor diode is used to sweep the frequency of the design. The proposed meandered loop-slot antenna design is small in size and has planar geometry with overall substrate dimensions of <tex>$\mathbf{100}\times \mathbf{100}\ \mathbf{mm}^{2}$</tex>. The proposed antenna with frequency reconfigurability is ideally suited for small satellite applications in the UHF band, especially CubeSats.

articleTitle: Analytical Design of Perfectly Matched Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work presents a novel formulation that locally controls electromagnetic fields with reflectionless metamaterials. From discretized spatial distributions of phase progression and power flow direction, material parameters of homogeneous, magnetically-anisotropic unit cells are analytically derived. The proposed formulation allows arbitrary electromagnetic field transformations while totally suppressing internal (intercell) and external (with the background medium) reflections.

articleTitle: A Distributed-Memory Implementation of Schur-Complement PCA Preconditioner for Ill-Conditioned Problems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper describes our first effort toward an implementation of Schur-complement principal component analysis (PCA) preconditioner for distributed-memory computing platforms. A distributed binary tree structure for binary hierarchical matrix partitioning is proposed. This implementation targets performance portability by leveraging the abstractions provided by Kokkos and Kokkos Kernels. We evaluate the implementation via an ill-conditioned problem with an iterative solver in terms of effectiveness and efficiency.

articleTitle: A Flexible Measurement Setup for Far-Field Characterization of Reflectarrays Above 200 GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Experimental verification of the far-field radiation characteristic of reflectarrays (RAs) in the upper millimeter-wave range is challenging due to the required alignment precision given the small array dimensions. In this work, a measurement setup allowing flexible adjustment of incidence angle and distance between feed antenna and RA is presented. By means of an RA demonstrator operating at 245 GHz, the influence of alignment errors and parasitic effects, such as undesired reflections and clutter, is investigated. The resulting measured radiation pattern recorded in both principal planes exhibits excellent agreement with full-wave simulations of the corresponding RA design.

articleTitle: Automated Design of a Broadside-Radiating Linearly Polarized Isotropic Metasurface Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present the automated design of a broadside-radiating metasurface antenna. The design is carried out by employing a continuous isotropic Impedance Boundary Condition through an optimization procedure based on the equivalent surface current only. A modified gradient-descent optimization algorithm is applied to minimize an objective function that incorporates both realizability and far field requirements. The antenna is then implemented by a suitable arrangement of circular unit cells, selected from a database of precomputed shapes. This procedure is applied to the design of a broadside-radiating, linearly polarized circular metasurface antenna working at 23 GHz, with size <tex>$\approx 12\lambda$</tex>. The obtained design is then validated with commercial software simulations.

articleTitle: A High-Efficiency Underwater Dipole Antenna With Spherical Electrodes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Development of high-efficiency antennas and effective use of radio frequency (RF) waves propagating along the boundary of two media are crucial to utilize RF waves in seawater which has high attenuation coefficient. In this paper, we propose an antenna with spherical electrodes based on a half-sheath dipole antenna consists of two cylindrical electrodes exposed to seawater and an insulator sheath at inner half of the antenna. A theoretical study indicates that spherical electrodes minimize a loss in seawater around the electrodes and improve the transmission factor between two antennas. The effectiveness of our proposed antenna is verified by an experiment in real sea using antenna prototypes designed at 100 kHz.

articleTitle: Polarization Analysis of Reflectarray Unit Elements Using Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Polarization analysis for reflection waves from a circularly polarized (CP) reflectarray unit element is studied in detail in this work. Characteristic mode analysis is adopted to analyze the wave excitation and reflection waves. It's found that the polarization of the reflected waves depends on the polarization of the incident waves, and a CP reflection wave or a linearly polarized (LP) reflection wave can be achieved with a properly oriented LP incident wave. Moreover, it is also found that when a CP wave is incident on a CP element, it has LP reflection waves at the CP frequency of the unit element.

articleTitle: Double-Choke Antenna Radiation Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper discusses the benefit of adding a second choke to a choke antenna. An analytical model that obtains the antenna far-field radiation components is developed. This model proves the advantage in using a second choke which introduces further phase delay in the formed complex currents. Therefore, the desired half power beamwidth (HPBW) or radiation maxima direction can be achieved with smaller antenna size. Analytical model validation is conducted using finite element method solver Ansys HFSS. Finally, the processing time of the analytical model and FEM simulation is shown and compared in CPU time.

articleTitle: Performance Characteristics of SIW-Based BPF with Square-Shaped CSRR Incorporation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, performance characteristics of band-pass filter (BPF) developed based on substrate-integrated-waveguide (SIW) with complimentary-split ring-resonator (CSSR) incorporation is presented. An array of 12 square-shaped CSRRs configured in 2 columns by 6 rows is incorporated into the SIW surface of BPF to attain an optimal desirable passband performance. Some attempts to investigate the coupling characteristic are carried out by controlling the distance between CSRRs in the column, as well as between the array of CSRR in the row. Based on the optimal value of coupling coefficient, configuration of the proposed SIW-based BPF is then realized and experimentally characterized. The measured result of scattering (S) parameters shows that the realized BPF has the 3-dB working bandwidth of 1.52 GHz ranges from the frequency of 2.36 GHz to 3.88 GHz, or its fractional bandwidth of 50.23%. This result is comparable to the simulated one, whereby the value of coupling coefficient in this configuration is 0.28.

articleTitle: Channel Measurement and Analysis at Emergency Frequency Band in Primeval Forest
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, fixed-point channel measurements for emergency communication scene in the primeval forest were conducted at emergency communication frequency band. We estimate and model channel characteristics based on the measured data within 100 m by taking 5 m as the step fixed point in the primeval forest. The emergency frequency band is 380 MHz and the corresponding bandwidth is 20 MHz. Based on the measured data, we obtain the power delay profile (PDP) of different distance. Finally, multipath components (MPCs) and large-scale fading characteristics at different distances are analyzed which contributes to make primeval forest emergency communication more reliable.

articleTitle: Fidelity Evaluation of the Phase-Encoded Linear Sampling Method and Backprojection Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The phase-encoded linear sampling method (PE-LSM) is a qualitative inverse scattering technique that can create high-fidelity target images from synthetic-aperture data acquisitions. Unlike conventional backprojection approaches, it does not rely on isotropic point scatterer models, and thus has the potential for avoiding imaging artifacts in wide-angle scenarios. In this paper, we evaluate the relative imaging performance of the PE-LSM and a backprojection implementation using simulated synthetic aperture radar data.

articleTitle: Reflector Antenna for Lunar Crater Radio Telescope
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: An ultra-long wavelength Lunar Crater Radio Telescope (LCRT) for observing early universe in 4.7-47 MHz range using a reflector antenna is under development at the NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. The LCRT consists of a 350 m diameter reflector antenna and receiver to be deployed inside a crater on the far side of the moon. Once deployed, LCRT will be one of the largest filled telescopes in the Solar System alongside 305m Arecibo and 500m FAST telescopes. The telescope. This paper discusses the structural limitations and its implications on the RF performance inside the lunar crater.

articleTitle: Quaternion-Neural-Networks-Based Decoder for RIS-Aided Polarization-Space Modulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Contemporary communications systems use large arrays in order to exploit the spatial domain requiring multiple radio-frequency (RF) chains leading to prohibitive cost and power. Spatial degrees of freedom are also achieved by utilizing the polarization states of an electromagnetic wave. To this end, we propose a polarization-state modulation system based on carrier wave reflections from a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS), where a sequence of data bits is mapped to polarization states. We consider a system with an upper millimeter-wave or low-THz RF source so that the channel model is line-of-sight-dominant. The data symbol constellation consists of sixteen quaternion-valued symbols, of which two correspond to linear and the remaining twelve represent elliptical polarizations. Our numerical experiments indicate that the RIS is capable of directing signal power toward the location of the receiver. The bit error rate performance of our rudimentary demodulator, although worse than OFDM-BPSK, is improved using a quaternion neural network.

articleTitle: AMC-Loaded Millimeter-Wave CPW-Fed Monopole Antenna for 5G Wearable Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a new millimeter-wave (mmWave) co-planar waveguide (CPW) fed monopole antenna backed by artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) is presented. A novel AMC unit cell has been designed and a 2×2 array is used below the antenna to increase the gain and achieve low specific absorption rate (SAR) values below 1.6 W/Kg. Novelty of AMC unit cell lies in the fact that single or dual band operation of the unit cell can be achieved by only adjusting the inner patch size without changing the outer dimensions of the unit cell. Presented AMC unit cell has zero reflection phase at 28GHz for single band operation. Proposed design has been designed using semi-flexible substrate making it suitable for 5G mmWave wearable applications.

articleTitle: 3D-Printed Multi-Section Dielectric Resonator Antenna with Symmetric Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article presents a 3D-printed multi-section dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) with a symmetrical radiation pattern operating at 5.8 GHz, based on the inclusion of a high-dielectric cylindrical section that surrounds a standard cylindrical DRA to achieve symmetry. The antenna is manufactured using low-cost 3D printing and low-loss dielectric filaments. The antenna achieves a highly symmetrical radiation pattern in both E-plane and H-plane, and a maximum gain of around 13 dB.

articleTitle: Traveling and Standing Wave Recognition Based on PE Basis Functions and Standing Wave Ratio
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In the development of adaptive mesh refinement methods for electromagnetic scattering problems, it is crucial to determine accurately the regions that need a denser discretization. For complex objects, such regions are usually identified manually, based on physical understandings and user experiences. From a physical perspective, regions with strong standing waves need smaller elements to capture the fast amplitude and phase variation of the induced currents, while traveling waves can be modeled accurately by the phase-extracted basis functions (PEBFs) defined on a coarse mesh due to their slowly-varying amplitude and traveling-wave phase distribution. In this paper, a standing and traveling wave recognition technique is described based on the use of PEBFs and the standing wave ratio of the induced current.

articleTitle: Next Generation Antenna Design Synthesis Framework Using k-Nearest Neighbours Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: The state-of-the-art antenna design synthesis and optimization techniques cannot reduce the requirement of high computational resources and domain expertise. Therefore, we suggest a new framework using a machine learning model (k-nearest neighbors algorithm) with the ability to design an antenna with user-defined requirements. To demonstrate the workings of the proposed framework, two specific coplanar waveguide-fed patch antenna designs were developed based on user-defined requirements with almost 100% accuracy and a run time less than 5 seconds.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Spherical Dielectric Resonator Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work presents a new design technique to realize a microstrip resonator fed spherical dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) and <tex>$2\times 2$</tex> array at 36 GHz. The dielectric resonators can be placed on thin planar circuit board or on-chip. Vertical metallic walls around radiators eliminate the otherwise high sidelobes known for the spherical DRA. In the array, the metallic walls also contribute to a reduction of mutual coupling. Simulations, verified by measurements, show significant reduction of sidelobes and mutual coupling, while the impedance bandwidth of the in-phase fed <tex>$2\times 2$</tex> array reduces from 7.3% to 3.5%.

articleTitle: Concentric Circular Array Analysis to Overcome Divergence of Vortex Waves for 70 GHz Frequency Link
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) of waves, also known as vortex, offers a promising way to enhance communication link capacity and diversity. One of the advantages of vortex modal communication is that one can use different signal information within a fixed frequency band. There is no need to expand the frequency bandwidth, change the polarization, or wait for a time to transfer two-way communication. However, there is still work to be done before vortex communication can be considered as a potential for the next wireless network. One major issue when generating and receiving vortex high modes is the limitation of signal power level in comparison with normal waves. In this study we propose using different concentric circular array formations to overcome low power amounts for OAM modes. Through the use of a higher directive vortex mode, it is possible to increase the link budget and deal with the physical phenomena of divergence patterns. Different modes of 0, 1, and 2 are considered when tapering the array elements. The achieved directivity values were 23, 20, and 18 dB for 0, 10, and 16° angles. Helix antenna as the basic element is suggested in theory for a 70 GHz backhaul communication link.

articleTitle: Metamaterial Phase-Shifter Utilizing a Compliant Mechanism Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A new metamaterial unit-cell design for reflectarray antennas (RA) that integrates an electromechanical reconfigurable metamaterial technology with a rugged compliant mechanism topology is presented. The proposed unit-cell design uses a compliant mechanism that achieves motion through a custom single-leaf spring compliant revolute iris to guide two shorting pins along the bottom surface of a circular patch element. The proposed design is actuated by a stepper motor for ease of control implementation and is safely positioned below the ground plane to shield against incident electric fields and minimize electromagnetic interference. The performance of the unit-cell in a full reflectarray configuration has been approximated through simulations, showing its potential for beam steering and high-power operation.

articleTitle: On a Time Domain Calderón Preconditioned CFIE Discretized with Convolution Quadratures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Several standard integral equations in the time domain suffer from at least one of the following limitations: 1) conditioning breakdowns, 2) internal resonances, or 3) DC-instabilities. The standard time domain combined field integral equation (CFIE) being no exception, is plagued by the large time step and dense discretization breakdowns. Calderón preconditioning strategies are commonly proposed to address these issues in the frequency domain but, to this day, they were not available for convolution quadrature CFIEs. This work will fill this gap proposing a new Calderón approach leading to a well-conditioned and resonant-free convolution quadrature discretized equation.

articleTitle: Contactless Fall Detection Using RFID Wall and AI
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Fall detection (FD) in elderly people is crucial for preventing serious injuries that could lead to prolonged dependence and even death in severe cases. The world health organization reports that 50% of elderly people fall annually, underscoring the need for early FD to prevent hospitalized or dying in accidents. Contactless FD systems have developed as a viable alternative to wearable sensor-based systems for detecting falls amid concern to security and privacy. This paper proposes a contactless FD system that leverages a passive UHF RFID tag array to measure the received signal strength indicator (RSSI) and utilizes deep learning (DL) to accurately predict fall activity by observing RSSI fluctuations. The system can effectively differentiate between standing and falling activities by training the DL-based classifiers on features extracted from raw data. Our proposed contactless system is capable of detecting indoor falling activity with an accuracy of 95%, which demonstrates the efficacy of the approach.

articleTitle: A Sliding Feeding Mechanism for a Bi-Stable Reconfigurable Quadrifilar Helix Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper discusses the integration of a sliding feeding mechanism designed specifically to ensure the reconfiguration of a bi-stable Quadrifilar Helix Antenna (QHA). The feeding mechanism is integrated within the ground plane of the QHA and slides with the changes in its topology. The QHA modifies its structure and deployment stages in a bi-stable fashion to radiate at 1 GHz. In one configuration, the QHA exhibits almost monopole-like radiation with linear polarization for terrestrial point-to-point communication. While in another configuration, the QHA exhibits circular polarization with a directional pattern making it suitable for satellite communications. The antenna is proposed to be deployed in areas that lack infrastructure and necessitate no power or actuation to ensure reconfiguration.

articleTitle: Noise Immune Antenna (NIA) - A Novel Approach to Mitigate Desense for On-Board Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Conventional de-sense mitigation techniques mainly tackle aggressor and coupling path to the antenna. However, very little work has been done to realize antennas with minimal reverse fields. This paper highlights a novel noise immune antenna design that can meet wireless specifications while being immune to noise leading to cost reduction by effectively removing shield can.

articleTitle: Wideband Circularly Polarized Modular Active Phased Array for Vehicular Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband circular polarized patch element in X- and Ku-bands for vehicular satellite communication. A 2x2 array of the element is designed and fabricated with overlapped 10-dB impedance and 3-dB axial ratio band of 10.7–13 GHz. The 2x2 array enables modular design of larger arrays. Each 2x2 array is controlled by an 8-channel beamformer integrated circuit mounted on an interposer. The interposer circuit simplifies routing of dc and digital lines on the surface of larger arrays.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Navigational Radar Antenna with Radiating Horn Aperture Fed by a Gap Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A navigational radar antenna comprising <tex>$4\ \mathrm{x}\ 32$</tex> radiating elements fed by a ridge gap waveguide is presented. The antenna is designed at a millimeter-wave frequency band with a grid of horns making the aperture. The proposed structure has no electrical contact between the layers. There are a total of three metal layers, each separated by a small gap. A set of four horns forms an antenna unit cell which is fed by a single cavity-backed slot. The top metal layer is a radiating layer comprising a grid of 32 horn-based unit cells. The E-plane sectoral horn is used as a radiator and is optimized to reduce mutual coupling between adjacent horn elements. A cavity layer is added in the middle to increase the impedance bandwidth of the antenna. The complex distribution network based on the ridge gap waveguide lies at the bottom which feeds the array corporately. Circular Artificial Magnetic Conductor (AMC) pins are designed that confines the input power within the prescribed path. 3dB power dividers are designed with equal amplitudes and phases at all output ports. The proposed antenna array has a relative impedance bandwidth of 13.7<sup>%</sup> with an input reflection coefficient better than -10dB from the 65 GHz to 65.9 GHz frequency range.

articleTitle: Self-Diplexing Implantable Antenna with Independently Controllable Bands
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a self-diplexing implantable antenna is proposed for head implants. The proposed antenna operates at 915 MHz (Port 1 = ON) and 1420 MHz (Port 2 = ON) with independently controllable bands. This antenna is optimized by implanting it in a realistic human head model (implant depth = 4 mm). It maintains a compact size (7.13 mm × 8.9 mm × 0.13 mm) due to multiple slots and shorting pins. Moreover, an isolation level (31.4 dB) between both ports of the antenna is achieved using an ultra-thin substrate and a series of vias. It has a stable radiation pattern at both frequency bands and has good gains of -18.94 dBi (at 915 MHz) and -17.06 dBi (at 1420 MHz). Due to high isolation, good impedance matching, acceptable gains and independently controllable bands, this antenna is suitable for head implants.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface for the Doppler Shift
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: We propose a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) to create the Doppler frequency shift (DS), which is one of the important issues in fast-moving wireless communication systems. Especially the DS is a crucial factor for the 5G system, which requires high data rates and low latency even in high-mobility communication environments. The proposed RIS consists of a metasurface unit cell combined with varactor diodes connected to an external DC bias circuit. We can modulate the phase of reflected waves from the RIS and derive the desired DS according to real-time varying varactor capacitance. Using the proposed RIS, we can test the DS impact on wireless communication qualities on high-speed vehicles or trains more easily without over-the-air (OTA) experiments. The experimental result agrees well with the simulation data, showing the validity and usefulness of our RIS.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approach to Determine the Characteristics of a Longitudinally Slotted Waveguide Immersed into a High Dielectric
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work the performance of a longitudinally slotted waveguide (LSWG) immersed into a high dielectric surroundings was determined using machine learning (ML) regression analysis. By varying the key parameters, slot length and the offset distance of the waveguide a total of 124 samples were generated for the ML algorithm. Here, we used 4 different types of ML regression analysis to predict the resonance frequency of the LSWG. The decision tree regressor and random forest regressor performs the best with the r2 values of 0.9982 and 0.9880 respectively. Two other regressor, linear regression and ridge regression models only produced an r2 score of 0.5462 and 0.5474 respectively. These ML algorithms mitigate the computational time and tedious work need to done with the Electromagnetic (EM) simulator. Moreover, decision tree regression, and random forest regression can predict the resonance frequency which is closest to the EM simulator.

articleTitle: Secure Non-Coherent Links Using Commercial Software-Defined Radios
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A low probability of detection (LPD) communication network is proposed using commercial software-defined radios (SDRs) for transmission and reception. The network utilizes code-division multiple access (CDMA) to simultaneously transmit signals over a shared bandwidth. Four transmitters are used to send unique 20-bit binary sequences to a receiver non-coherently. Each sequence uses Direct Sequence Spread Spectrum (DSSS) to extend the signal's spectrum by a factor of 635 to bury the desired signals below the RF noise floor. The receiver was able to acquire, align, and despread all four signals in real time.

articleTitle: Increasing the Bandwidth of Reflectarray Antennas Using the Frequency Pulling Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, a frequency pulling technique (FPT) is used to increase the bandwidth of traditional reflectarray antennas (RAs). Specifically, the bandwidth of a rectangular patch unit cell is doubled by simultaneously feeding it at two slightly asymmetric points. The required phase shift for each unit cell of our reflectarray is achieved using meandered microstrip lines below the patch elements. Our results illustrate that our proposed RA achieves a fractional gain bandwidth of 30%, which is approximately two times greater than the 16% fractional bandwidth of the traditional RA with single-point fed patches.

articleTitle: 2D Scanning by Subwavelength Superoscillatory Focused Beams for Wireless Power Delivery
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: Miniature implantable medical neurostimulation devices offer new therapy options to patients with otherwise untreatable neurological or psychiatric disorders. However, powering such devices, which may be implanted deep in the brain, remains a major challenge. We demonstrate an energy focusing approach for wireless power transmission purposes, envisioned to be deployed in wearable head-mounted devices. A 2D focusing technique is introduced within a A× λ─size cavity at 1 GHz that utilizes the principle of superoscillations. This mode of power transmission enables reaching deep inside the cavity while allowing for arbitrarily steering of the focal point. Through meticulous analysis, the 2D-focused waveform's full width at the half-maximum (FWHM) is determined as 0.38λ.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of QCTO Approaches for Luneburg Lens Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A performance comparison of two quasi-conformal transformation optics (QCTO) design approaches for a flattened Luneburg lens antenna is presented. Two different sets of boundary conditions are applied in the QCTO transformation and we observe notably differing permittivity distributions, directivity, and beamwidth from the design. One result exhibits a higher maximum permittivity requirement but improved directivity and beamwidth. One case is studied here (a planar cut of the 2D circular lens at 144°), the two designs require maximum permittivity of 3.7 and 8.86 and 2 dBi difference in directivity.

articleTitle: Gain Improvement of 6×26 Slotted Array Waveguide Antenna by Grid Cavity Located on Radiator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a design for gain improvement of the 6×26 slotted array waveguide antenna. The proposed antenna was equipped with the grid cavity and 4 cylinder poles located on the radiator. The proposed antenna had a broad bandwidth of 3.7% based on the −10 dB reflection coefficients. Due to the grid cavity and 4 cylinder poles, the first sidelobe level is improved by about 2.8 dB compared with the conventional antenna. Antenna gain was obtained at about 31 dBi, which improved 2.33 dBi compared with the conventional antenna.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electromagnetic Decoupling of an Isolation Barrier Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a machine learning technique is used to analyze the decoupling performance of an isolation barrier that prevents electromagnetic interference between cables in nuclear power plants. To train the machine learning model, the mode-matching method is also employed to generate a training dataset including the decoupling capability corresponding to design parameters. After confirming that the deep neural network model is well-trained, we utilize the resulting model to predict the decoupling capability of an isolation barrier in the variation of design parameters. We conclude that the machine learning model can be possibly used to obtain information on precautions against electromagnetic coupling problems in cabling applications in nuclear power plants.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Metasurface for Functional and Anatomical 1.5 T MRI
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, a dual-band passive metasurface, excited by an RF coil and able to homogenize the magnetic field distribution for 1.5 T magnetic resonance imaging is presented. In particular, the metasurface is composed by a 5×5 passive array, covering a 15 cm x 15 cm area. Each unit-cell consists of two concentric spiral coils resonating at different Larmor frequencies: the internal coil at 64 MHz and the external one at 17 MHz, respectively. The two frequencies have been chosen to simultaneously combine the anatomical (<sup>1</sup>H, 64 MHz) and functional <sup>23</sup>Na, 17 MHz) imaging for 1.5 T MRI scanners within the same hardware system. To validate the theoretical approach, we performed preliminary numerical full-wave simulations with and without the metasurface presence. Specifically, we compared the magnetic field distributions in terms of uniformity within the Field of View for the two configurations and at different distances from the radiating system. A superior magnetic field uniformity and, thus, a high signal-to-noise ratio, has been observed in the presence of the metasurface for both the frequencies. Therefore, these preliminary results demonstrated the possibility to use the proposed system for both anatomical and functional 1.5 T MRI.

articleTitle: Optimizing $\mathcal{H}$-Matrix Solvers' Admissability Criteria via Rapid Spectrum Estimation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A recently introduced iterative random sampling algorithm is adopted to maximize the total compression of hierarchically partitioned impedance matrices by rapidly finding optimal admissibility criteria parameters (cluster-to-cluster distance measure, cluster-size measure, and admissibility constant) to set the block partition. Because the algorithm can estimate ranks accurately only for sufficiently incoherent matrix blocks, its rank estimates are penalized for blocks with relatively large size-to-distance ratios. The algorithm is tested on the PRIME aircraft model from the Austin RCS Benchmark Suite.

articleTitle: Particle Swarm Optimizer Utilization for Dual-Band Inset-Fed Microstrip Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper discusses the utilization of particle swarm optimizer (PSO) for the design of dual-band inset-fed microstrip antenna. The antenna is designed to work at the frequency of 3.3 GHz WiMAX and 5 GHz WLAN systems. The inset-fed line is applied in the structure of rectangular patch to improve its reflection coefficient. The simulated PSO configuration provides the S<inf>11</inf> values of −26.98 dB at the frequency of 3.3 GHz and −16.06 dB at the frequency of 5.6 GHz, while the measured one achieves the S<inf>11</inf> values of −13.22 dB and −12.65 dB at the frequencies of 3.3 GHz and 5.6 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: A Method to Reduce the Back Radiation of the Dual-Polarized Antenna With Vertical Fins
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: A dual-polarized crossed dipole antenna with high front-to-back ratio is introduced in this paper. The antenna is composed of two orthogonally placed trapezoidal dipoles printed on the bottom side of a substrate. To realize high front-to-back ratio, vertical fins are employed and integrated onto the flat rectangular ground plane. Simulation results demonstrate that the antenna with modified ground-plane has an impedance bandwidth from 674 to 795 MHz (16.4%) and an improved front-to-back ratio of about 20 dB over the entire operating band.

articleTitle: Field Evaluation of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface with Varying Surface Size
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper addresses a system-level demand to validate the effectiveness of the physical dimension variation of reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) in typical indoor scenarios. To this aim, the varying surface size of RIS operating in millimeter wave spectrum has been tested with a beamforming capability to boost up the received signal power. In a non-line-of-sight (NLOS) environment where the measured signal power is very low to achieve meaningful throughput performance, we observed the <tex>$\mathbf{7}\sim \mathbf{8} \mathbf{dB}$</tex> increase of the received signal power by enabling a beamforming feature by means of our liquid crystal based RIS prototype. Consequently, observed signal quality becomes a medium level for proper 5G communications. We also evaluated that the enlarged physical dimension of RIS contributes <tex>$\mathbf{13}.\mathbf{5}\sim \mathbf{15} \mathbf{dB}$</tex> increase to the received signal power, which comes from the surface area increase by 22.5 times, and hence the throughput performance reached nearly twice compared with that measured in the case of NLOS. All the experimental results have been verified along with the theoretic analysis with a small amount of skew resulting from small-scale fading generally observed in an indoor environment.

articleTitle: Wideband Design of a Single-Layer Dual-Band Multi-Ring Microstrip Antenna Fed by an L-Probe with Separated L-shaped Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents wideband design of a single-layer dual-band multi-ring microstrip antenna (MR-MSA) fed by an L-Probe with separated L-shaped elements. The proposed antenna consists of an inner square split ring patch for a higher band, two outer separated L-shaped patches for a lower band, and a feeding L-shaped probe (L-Probe) to excite the radiating patches. The radiating patches and the L-Probe are arranged on a thick single-layer dielectric substrate with a thickness of approximately 0.1 wavelengths to obtain dual-band and wideband operation. The two design frequencies of the proposed antenna are about 9 GHz and 12.5 GHz. In order to achieve dual-band and wideband characteristics at the two design frequencies, dimensions of the proposed antenna are tuned by using ANSYS HFSS. It is confirmed by the numerical simulation that fractional bandwidths below −10 dB reflection are 10.1% for the lower band and 16.9% for the higher band, respectively. Stable unidirectional radiation pattern characteristics for the lower and higher bands are also confirmed by the simulation.
